articles.title: WhatsApp para Mac estrena controles de actualización: elige entre versiones diarias o semanales
articles.text:
WhatsApp ha modificado la gestión de su aplicación para Mac, permitiendo a los usuarios elegir la frecuencia y el tipo de actualizaciones que desean recibir. A partir de ahora, quienes utilicen WhatsApp en Mac pueden optar entre recibir compilaciones diarias (con acceso inmediato a nuevas funciones y correcciones) o versiones semanales más estables, todo desde una nueva sección de configuración.
Esta función, que se está desplegando de forma gradual en la beta, marca un avance en el control del usuario sobre la experiencia de mensajería y la estabilidad de la aplicación, en un contexto donde la flexibilidad tecnológica es cada vez más valorada.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con WABetaInfo, la novedad es especialmente relevante tras la suspensión del programa beta a través de TestFlight, que era la vía tradicional para probar nuevas funciones en Mac. WhatsApp ha adaptado su estrategia, permitiendo la descarga directa de versiones beta desde sus servidores y sumando ahora herramientas para que cada usuario decida cuándo y cómo actualizar.
¿Qué cambia con los nuevos controles de actualización?
La principal novedad es la incorporación de una sección dedicada a las actualizaciones dentro del menú de configuración de WhatsApp para Mac. Desde allí, los usuarios pueden:
PUBLICIDAD
- Consultar la versión actual instalada.
- Buscar manualmente nuevas versiones en cualquier momento.
- Elegir entre dos modos de actualización: “Última versión” (diaria) o “Versión semanal estable”.
Este sistema permite alternar entre opciones sin necesidad de reinstalar la aplicación, aportando una experiencia más personalizada y adaptada a las necesidades de cada usuario.
¿En qué consiste la opción “Última versión”?
Seleccionar la opción “Última versión” significa recibir compilaciones diarias de WhatsApp para Mac. Cada día, la aplicación puede instalar nuevas correcciones de errores, pequeñas mejoras o pruebas de funciones experimentales. Es la opción preferida para quienes desean estar siempre a la vanguardia y acceder antes que nadie a novedades.
PUBLICIDAD
El punto a considerar es que, al tratarse de trabajo en curso, estas versiones pueden contener errores menores o cambios inesperados. Por eso, es recomendable para usuarios que disfrutan de probar nuevas funciones y no dependen de la total estabilidad de la aplicación para cuestiones laborales o reuniones importantes.
¿Qué ventajas tiene la “Versión semanal estable”?
La alternativa es la actualización semanal, que agrupa todas las correcciones y mejoras de las versiones diarias en una sola compilación, distribuida generalmente antes del fin de semana. Esta opción prioriza la estabilidad y la confiabilidad, evitando sorpresas a mitad de semana y garantizando una experiencia más predecible.
PUBLICIDAD
Es la modalidad más recomendable para quienes usan WhatsApp en Mac por trabajo, o prefieren evitar cambios inesperados y posibles fallos en su flujo diario de comunicación. La versión semanal suele estar mejor testeada y es menos probable que incluya errores disruptivos.
¿Qué opción conviene a cada perfil de usuario?
Ambas alternativas ofrecen las mismas funciones base, pero difieren en el ritmo de entrega y la exposición a nuevas características. Los usuarios curiosos, beta testers o entusiastas de las novedades tecnológicas pueden sacar provecho de la actualización diaria. Quienes buscan máxima fiabilidad y previsibilidad, encontrarán en la versión semanal una mejor opción.
PUBLICIDAD
Cabe destacar que la función aún se está desplegando de forma progresiva entre los usuarios beta de Mac. Si la nueva sección no aparece en la configuración, es cuestión de semanas para que llegue a más cuentas, según el cronograma de WhatsApp.
Cómo acceder y aprovechar los nuevos controles
Para probar los nuevos controles de actualización, es necesario instalar la versión beta más reciente de WhatsApp para Mac desde los canales oficiales de la compañía. En la configuración, dentro de la sección de “Actualizaciones de la aplicación”, se puede alternar entre los modos diario y semanal, así como buscar manualmente nuevas versiones en cualquier momento.
PUBLICIDAD
La decisión de WhatsApp de brindar mayor control sobre las actualizaciones responde a una demanda creciente de los usuarios por personalizar su experiencia digital. En un entorno donde la estabilidad y la innovación deben convivir, ofrecer un menú de opciones para administrar el software es un paso lógico y bien recibido.
Con estos nuevos controles, WhatsApp para Mac se posiciona como una de las aplicaciones de mensajería más flexibles y adaptables, permitiendo que cada usuario elija el equilibrio entre novedad y estabilidad que mejor se ajuste a sus necesidades cotidianas.

articles.title: Le robot de piscine Sora 70 affine sa filtration avec un accessoire à 59,90 €
articles.text:
Le robot de piscine Sora 70 affine sa filtration avec un accessoire à 59,90 €
Trois microns sous le panier
Beatbot commercialise un nouveau panier filtrant double pour son robot de piscine Sora 70. Vendu 59,90 €, il associe un panier de 400 microns à un filtre textile de 3 microns pour capturer les particules les plus fines.
Beatbot Panier filtrant double ultra-fin
Le Beatbot Sora 70 peut désormais s’attaquer plus efficacement aux poussières fines, aux algues et aux particules que son filtre d’origine peine à retenir. Le fabricant commercialise un panier filtrant double ultra-fin, proposé séparément au prix de 59,90 €.
Cet accessoire de 6 l repose sur deux niveaux de filtration. Le panier extérieur retient les débris jusqu’à 400 microns et peut être utilisé seul, notamment lorsque la piscine contient beaucoup de feuilles ou de déchets volumineux. Un filtre intérieur en tissu vient ensuite s’y insérer pour descendre jusqu’à 3 microns.
Cette finesse supplémentaire répond à l’une des principales limites relevées lors de notre test du Sora 70. Le panier fourni avec le robot filtre jusqu’à 150 microns, ce qui suffit pour l’entretien courant, mais laisse passer certaines particules très légères. Nous avions notamment pu voir de petits débris ressortir par l’évacuation.
Beatbot Sora 70
Un résultat convaincant sur les cendres
Nous avons pu tester ce nouveau filtre après les incendies de juillet 2026 en Gironde, alors que des cendres s’étaient déposées dans notre piscine durant l’évacuation du secteur. Après un cycle de trois heures, le filtre textile avait récupéré une quantité importante de particules fines, avec un résultat nettement plus convaincant que le panier standard.
Le nettoyage de l’accessoire demande en revanche davantage de temps. Un simple jet d’eau n’a pas suffi à retirer tous les résidus incrustés dans le tissu. Beatbot annonce une durée de vie de 40 cycles, soit environ 150 heures de fonctionnement, avant remplacement.
Le fabricant recommande par ailleurs de réserver ce filtre au nettoyage du fond. Il ne doit pas être utilisé pour la surface, probablement parce que la maille très serrée réduit la circulation de l’eau et la puissance disponible pour rabattre les débris flottants.
Une option utile, mais pas fournie
Le prix de 59,90 € reste relativement raisonnable pour un accessoire capable d’améliorer sensiblement la filtration. On regrette toutefois qu’un second filtre plus fin ne soit pas proposé directement avec le Sora 70, vendu 1499 €. À ce tarif, offrir le choix entre un panier standard et un filtre ultrafin n’aurait rien eu d’extravagant.
Beatbot prévoit également un accessoire équivalent pour le Sora 30, avec une conception adaptée à ce modèle. Il faudra toutefois faire preuve de patience, les livraisons pour cet accessoires n'auront lieu qu'à partir du mois de septembre 2026.

articles.title: Palantir verdoppelt Umsatz: Firmenchef schießt gegen OpenAI
articles.text:
Das Geschäft der für ihre Zusammenarbeit mit US-Sicherheitsbehörden bekannten Datenanalyse-Firma Palantir ist im vergangenen Quartal rasant gewachsen. Das KI-Unternehmen konnte den Umsatz im Jahresvergleich mit einem Plus von 93 Prozent fast verdoppeln. Mit Erlösen von knapp 1,94 Milliarden US-Dollar übertraf Palantir deutlich die Erwartungen der Analysten, die im Schnitt eher mit 1,8 Milliarden Dollar gerechnet hatten. Allein binnen drei Monaten wuchs der Umsatz um rund ein Fünftel.
Palantir ist auf die Auswertung großer Datenmengen spezialisiert und liefert unter anderem Software, mit der Geheimdienst- und Militärinformationen analysiert werden.
Palantir-Chef teilt gegen KI-Vorreiter aus
Firmenchef Alex Karp nutzt den geschäftlichen Rückenwind, um Palantir als Gegengewicht zu den führenden KI-Entwicklern wie OpenAI und Anthropic zu positionieren. Palantir ist laut Karp ein wichtiger Mittelsmann, um bei der Anwendung deren KI-Software die volle Kontrolle über die eigenen Daten zu behalten – und bei Bedarf auch zwischen Anbietern Künstlicher Intelligenz wechseln zu können.
Die großen KI-Labore bestreiten stets, Kundendaten zum Training ihrer KI-Modelle zu nutzen. In einer Videokonferenz mit Analysten sagte Karp aber dennoch, Unternehmen zahlten Geld dafür, damit ihr Wissen in KI-Modelle eingebracht werde, so dass damit ein konkurrierendes Geschäft aufgebaut werden könne.
Die Palantir-Aktie stieg im nachbörslichen Handel um rund 14 Prozent. Das Unternehmen hob die Umsatzprognose für das gesamte Jahr an und übertraf mit der Vorhersage für das laufende Quartal die Markterwartungen.
Hohe Nachfrage in den USA
Das aktuelle Wachstum kommt vor allem aus dem US-Geschäft. Die Erlöse im Heimatmarkt waren im vergangenen Vierteljahr mit 1,57 Milliarden Dollar mehr als doppelt so hoch wie ein Jahr zuvor. Das Geschäft mit Regierungsbehörden wuchs um 90 Prozent auf 809 Millionen Dollar. Software von Palantir wird unter anderem vom Heimatschutzministerium und vom Pentagon eingesetzt – Medienberichten zufolge auch im Iran-Krieg. Das Geschäft mit Unternehmen in den USA stieg um 149 Prozent auf 764 Millionen Dollar.

articles.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Faces 30% Price Increase in South Korea
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Faces 30% Price Increase in South Korea
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 50 series is rumored to see a price increase of about 20-30%, depending on the model, due to rapidly rising costs of GDDR7 memory from NVIDIA's VRAM suppliers. According to ZDNet Korea, South Korean importers and distributors have already informed the supply chain about this price hike, which could reach up to 30%. NVIDIA provides its add-in board partners with GDDR7 memory as a kit that includes both the GPU die and GDDR7, so any price increase from memory manufacturers affects AIBs and, ultimately, consumers.
Currently, each 2 GB GDDR7 memory module costs in the low 20s in USD. This spot pricing for GDDR7 means NVIDIA needs 16 of these modules for its flagship GeForce RTX 5090 GPU. This results in at least $320 being spent on GDDR7 memory for the flagship model, before adding the cost of the GPU die, research and development, and the margins for AIB partners. The situation remains challenging even in South Korea, the world's hub of DRAM production. Despite being home to SK hynix and Samsung, no one is exempt from these price increases, which are expected to continue.

articles.title: Snap CEO sidesteps Specs preorder questions on Q2 earnings call | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Snap CEO Evan Spiegel sidestepped investors’ questions about preorder demand for the company’s long-awaited Specs smart glasses during Monday’s earnings call, just weeks before the device’s September launch event.
“What we’re hearing from folks is really that they want to try Specs,” Spiegel told investors. “It’s obviously a high consideration purchase at $2,195. Obviously, developers and folks who are familiar with the platform really understand it and understand the technical leaps we’ve made with this generation. I think for the broader public and consumers, it’s going to be really important for folks to go hands-on. Our upcoming launch event will be an important sort of starting point for that consumer-oriented journey.”
The company unveiled Specs in June after spending more than a decade developing the device. The wearable’s $2,195 price tag is significantly higher than most Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses, which start at around $350, but lower than Apple’s Vision Pro, which starts at $3,500.
Investors also pressed Spiegel on why he believes Snap’s strategy is financially viable for a company of its size, why it chose to go it alone rather than partner with another company, and what gives him confidence that the company can compete with Apple, Meta, and Alphabet.
Spiegel responded that Snap believes the long-term opportunity to develop the next computing platform is “enormous.”
“I think what some folks maybe don’t understand yet, especially because Specs are so new and we’re really the first mover in this category, is how difficult the product is to execute from a technical perspective,” Spiegel said. “When we started innovating in the social space, we were a late entrant. So, most of the apps at the time, whether it was Facebook or Instagram or Twitter, were already in existence, and we had to really innovate to continue to grow. What’s so unique about this opportunity for us is really that we’re a first mover, and that really plays to our strengths as an innovator.”
When asked about product-market fit, Spiegel said it will likely be closer to the end of the decade before the company sees mass-market consumer adoption.
“I think things, for example, like weight and cost are going to have to come down to see you know unit volumes really meaningfully pick up.” But we do have, I think, a real advantage here in that developers have been building on the Specs platform now for several years.”

articles.title: ChatGPT statt Google? So verändert KI die Suche nach Restaurants und Arztpraxen
articles.text:
ChatGPT statt Google? So verändert KI die Suche nach Restaurants und Geschäften
Im Rahmen des „Consumer Search Behaviors Report 2026“ hat der Dienstleister, der andere Unternehmen dabei unterstützt, ihre Standort-, Marken- und Produktinformationen zentral zu verwalten und über Suchmaschinen und KI-Dienste auffindbar zu machen, das Suchverhalten von Verbraucher:innen untersucht. Wenig überraschend: 84 Prozent der Befragten verwenden entsprechende Anwendungen nach eigenen Angaben heute häufiger als noch vor einem Jahr. Und die KI wird immer öfter zum Einstiegspunkt in die Suche, allerdings bislang, ohne klassische Suchmaschinen zu verdrängen.
77 Prozent der Befragten suchen weiterhin über herkömmliche Suchmaschinen nach Unternehmen in ihrer Nähe. KI-Tools folgen mit 41 Prozent auf dem zweiten Platz. Soziale Netzwerke erreichen 39 Prozent. Was die Ergebnisse zeigen, ist also, dass Unternehmen, die im Netz auffindbar sein wollen, die klassische Websuche weiterhin bedienen müssen, aber eben auch auf die neuen Kanäle hin optimieren müssen.
Gleichzeitig gebe es, so Yext, ein erhebliches Potenzial bei all jenen, die KI-Tools noch nicht für die lokale Suche einsetzen. 48 Prozent dieser Gruppe können sich vorstellen, innerhalb der kommenden sechs Monate erstmals einen solchen Dienst einzusetzen. Weltweit kam die Yext-Erhebung auf einen Anteil von knapp 43 Prozent, die im vergangenen Monat ein KI-Tool zur Suche nach lokalen Unternehmen verwendet hatten.
KI-Empfehlungen bringen Unternehmen neue Kundschaft
Dass es sich für lokale Unternehmen lohnt, in solchen KI-Antworten vorzukommen, ist naheliegend. 27 Prozent der deutschen Verbraucher:innen haben nach eigenen Angaben innerhalb der vergangenen sechs Monate ein zuvor nicht besuchtes lokales Unternehmen aufgrund einer KI-Empfehlung kontaktiert oder aufgesucht. Vor allem gilt das für die Gastronomie. Fast jede:r Zweite, der aufgrund einer KI-Empfehlung aktiv wurde (48 Prozent), suchte ein Restaurant oder einen anderen gastronomischen Betrieb auf. Im Einzelhandel lag der Anteil bei 44 Prozent, bei Gesundheitsdienstleistungen wie Arztpraxen und Apotheken waren es 37 Prozent.
Für lokale Unternehmen entsteht dadurch eine zusätzliche Aufgabe, weil sie zusätzlich darauf achten müssen, welche Informationen KI-Systeme über sie ausgeben und im Rahmen welcher Fragestellungen sie dort vorkommen. Eine hier veraltete Angabe kann im Sinne der Kundenkommunikation schaden, etwa bei Standorten, Öffnungszeiten oder angebotenen Leistungen.
Die Herausforderung besteht vor allem darin, dass Unternehmen ihre Darstellung in Chatbots meist nicht so unmittelbar kontrollieren können wie das etwa bei den Google-Einträgen der Fall ist. Denn KI-Anbieter beziehen ihre Informationen aus unterschiedlichen Quellen – unter anderem aus Unternehmenswebsites, Verzeichnissen, Bewertungsportalen und klassischen Suchergebnissen. Zudem unterscheiden sich die verwendeten Quellen je nach Plattform. Im weltweiten Yext-Bericht lag ChatGPT unter den genutzten KI-Angeboten vorn, gefolgt von Google Gemini, Meta AI und Microsoft Copilot.
Nutzer vertrauen der KI eingeschränkt
Interessant ist aber auch eine weitere Einschätzung vieler Verbraucher:innen. Demnach ist das Vertrauen in die KI-Antworten vergleichsweise hoch. Immerhin 79 Prozent der deutschen Befragten vertrauen den Aussagen zum Teil, wobei sich allerdings nur elf Prozent auf die Technologie komplett verlassen. Jede:r Zweite (51 Prozent) der deutschen KI-Nutzer:innen gibt an, das Vertrauen habe im Vergleich zum Vorjahr zugenommen. 19 Prozent sind dagegen skeptischer geworden.
Insofern übernehmen auch nur vier Prozent eine KI-Empfehlung, ohne weitere Informationen einzuholen. 96 Prozent prüfen die Antwort zumindest auf einem weiteren Weg. Am wichtigsten sind hier klassische Suchmaschinen (50 Prozent), die Websites der Anbieter (48 Prozent) sowie die durch die KI angegebenen Quellen (33 Prozent).
Die KI übernimmt somit häufig die Vorauswahl, wird aber noch nicht zur alleinigen Entscheidungsinstanz. Statt eines geradlinigen Wechsels von Google zu ChatGPT oder Gemini entsteht eine hybride Such-Journey, bei der die Kund:innen in einem Chatbot beginnen und dann zur Suchmaschine oder Unternehmenswebsite wechseln. Relevant bleiben aber auch weiterhin Bewertungen von Unternehmen: Laut einer weiteren US-Erhebung des Local-Marketing-Anbieters Brightlocal lesen 97 Prozent der Befragten Bewertungen lokaler Unternehmen.
Zweigleisigkeit bei Unternehmensauftritten
Laut der Yext-Studie geht es also um das Gesamtbild, das sich aus guten und vor allem aktuellen Bewertungen ergibt. Für lokale Unternehmen reicht es demnach nicht, über Jahre eine große Zahl positiver Bewertungen zu sammeln. Sie benötigen einen kontinuierlichen Strom neuer Rezensionen. Ein Profil mit vielen älteren Bewertungen kann bei potenziellen Kund:innen weniger Vertrauen wecken als ein kleineres Profil, auf dem regelmäßig neue Erfahrungen veröffentlicht werden.
Die Ergebnisse sind ein deutlicher Hinweis darauf, dass Chatbots in der Customer Journey lokaler Unternehmen angekommen sind. Sie passen zu der Entwicklung, dass Google seine eigene Suche zunehmend dialogorientiert gestaltet, und auch andere Untersuchungen stellen eine wachsende Bedeutung von KI bei Empfehlungen und Kaufentscheidungen fest.
Auch wenn andere Untersuchungen je nach Fragestellung zu etwas niedrigeren Werten kommen, offenbart sich der Trend hin zu einer Zweigleisigkeit. Für Unternehmen – egal welcher Größe und Branche – steht damit ein Punkt mehr auf der Agenda im Online-Marketing. Es wird zukünftig um die Verbindung der Kanäle gehen. Denn KI-Systeme liefern Vorschläge, die anschließend über Websites, Suchmaschinen, Quellen und Bewertungen geprüft werden. Unternehmen müssen deshalb dafür sorgen, dass ihre Informationen auf allen relevanten Oberflächen korrekt, aktuell und widerspruchsfrei sind.

articles.title: Beltone Venture Capital exits BirdNest investment with 3.5x return
articles.text:
Beltone Venture Capital exits BirdNest investment with 3.5x return
- Egypt-based Beltone Venture Capital has completed a partial exit from Egyptian proptech BirdNest, generating a 3.5x return on invested capital and an 80% internal rate of return (IRR) over a two-year investment period.
- The transaction covered both Beltone Venture Capital's direct investment and its indirect stake through its joint fund with UAE-based Citadel International Holdings, while the firm retained a strategic stake in BirdNest.
- According to Ali Mokhtar, CEO and Managing Partner of Beltone Venture Capital, the partial exit reflects the firm's disciplined investment strategy while allowing it to return capital to investors and continue supporting BirdNest's next growth phase.
- Founded in 2019 by Mostafa Elnahawy, BirdNest offers a technology-powered marketplace for curated boutique hotels and holiday homes centred on art, wellness, and local experiences.
Press release:
Beltone Venture Capital has announced the successful partial exit from BirdNest, delivering a 3.5x return on invested capital and an 80% internal rate of return (IRR) over a two-year holding period.
The partial exit was executed across Beltone Venture Capital's direct stake and its indirect stake through the joint fund with UAE-based Citadel International Holdings, while Beltone Venture Capital continues to retain a strategic stake in BirdNest, reinforcing its confidence in the company's long-term growth potential.
Commenting on the milestone, Ali Mokhtar, CEO & Managing Partner of Beltone Venture Capital, said: "This outcome reflects the discipline of Beltone Venture Capital's investment approach from rigorous underwriting and active portfolio support to disciplined capital realization. This partial exit enables us to return capital to our investors while retaining a strategic stake in BirdNest. We remain committed to supporting the company's next phase of growth through Beltone's financial ecosystem and capabilities."
Mostafa Elnahawy, Co-Founder & CEO of BirdNest, added: “This milestone reflects the strength of BirdNest’s business model and the dedication of our team, partners, and investors. Over the past two years, we have achieved more than 10x growth in U.S. dollar revenue while reaching profitability. As we enter our next phase, we remain focused on creating sustainable long-term value and redefining hospitality through technology and exceptional guest experiences.”

articles.title: How IT Consulting Optimizes Everyday Technology Decisions - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Complexity of Technology in Business
In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, businesses face an ever-growing array of technology choices. From cloud computing and cybersecurity to software integration and data analytics, technology decisions have become increasingly complex and critical to operational success. While many companies strive to manage these decisions internally, the specialized knowledge required often exceeds the capacity of in-house teams. This is where IT consulting emerges as a vital asset, offering expert guidance to optimize technology choices that align with business goals.
According to a recent survey, 70% of organizations reported that they struggle to keep up with the pace of technology change, highlighting a significant challenge for businesses striving to stay competitive. This statistic underscores the urgency for companies to seek external expertise to navigate the complex technology landscape effectively.
Moreover, the rapid advancement of technologies means that what is cutting-edge today may become obsolete tomorrow. This pace of change necessitates continuous learning and adaptation, which can strain internal resources. IT consultants not only bring current knowledge but also anticipate future trends, enabling businesses to make proactive, rather than reactive, technology decisions. This foresight is essential in maintaining a competitive edge and avoiding costly missteps.
The Role of IT Consulting in Everyday Technology Decisions
IT consulting firms specialize in analyzing a company’s current IT environment and future needs to recommend the most suitable technology solutions. These consultants bring a wealth of experience across various industries, enabling them to identify pitfalls and opportunities that may not be apparent to internal teams. By leveraging their expertise, businesses can make informed decisions about technology investments, implementation, and management.
An excellent example of this expertise can be found through Protek’s IT professionals. Their IT professionals provide comprehensive assessments that help organizations understand the implications of adopting new technologies, ensuring alignment with business objectives and compliance requirements.
Beyond initial technology selection, IT consultants play a crucial role in the ongoing management and optimization of IT systems. They assist with change management, staff training, and establishing governance frameworks that ensure technologies continue to deliver value over time. This ongoing support helps organizations adapt to shifting business needs and evolving technological landscapes without disruption.
Furthermore, IT consulting can help bridge the gap between technical teams and business leadership. Consultants often act as translators, converting complex technical jargon into understandable insights that inform strategic decision-making. This communication facilitates better collaboration across departments, aligning technology initiatives with broader business goals.
Streamlining IT Strategy with Proven Methodologies
Adopting a structured methodology is crucial for effective IT consulting engagements. Frameworks that emphasize assessment, planning, implementation, and review allow consultants to deliver consistent and measurable results.
Prototype IT’s methodology exemplifies this approach by employing a methodology designed to tailor IT solutions precisely to their clients’ operational and strategic needs.
The structured nature of such methodologies helps businesses avoid common pitfalls, such as underestimating resource requirements or overlooking security vulnerabilities. Research shows that 63% of IT projects exceed their budget or timeline due to poor planning and management. Utilizing a proven IT consulting methodology can significantly reduce these risks, leading to more successful project outcomes.
In addition, these methodologies often incorporate best practices for risk assessment and mitigation, ensuring that potential challenges are identified early and addressed proactively. This approach not only safeguards project timelines and budgets but also enhances the overall quality and effectiveness of technology implementations.
By following a disciplined process, IT consulting firms can also facilitate better stakeholder engagement and transparency throughout the project lifecycle. Regular progress reviews and clear communication channels help maintain alignment and build trust, which are critical factors in the success of any technology initiative.
Enhancing Cybersecurity and Risk Management
One of the most critical aspects of everyday technology decisions is cybersecurity. With cyberattacks increasing in frequency and sophistication, organizations must prioritize robust security measures. IT consultants evaluate current security postures and recommend enhancements that protect sensitive data and ensure regulatory compliance.
Data from Cybersecurity Ventures predicts that global cybercrime costs will reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, underscoring the urgency of effective security strategies. This staggering figure highlights the growing financial risks associated with inadequate cybersecurity.
IT consultants help organizations adopt a multi-layered defense strategy, incorporating technologies such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, encryption, and endpoint protection. They also assist in developing comprehensive security policies and incident response plans, which are vital for minimizing damage in the event of a breach.
Moreover, consultants stay abreast of evolving regulatory requirements, such as GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA, ensuring that businesses maintain compliance and avoid costly penalties. By integrating cybersecurity into the broader IT strategy, consultants help businesses mitigate risks and foster trust with customers and partners.
Regular security assessments and penetration testing conducted by IT consultants can uncover vulnerabilities before malicious actors exploit them. This proactive stance is essential in today’s threat landscape, where attackers continuously develop new tactics.
Cost Efficiency and ROI Through Expert Advice
Making informed technology decisions can lead to significant cost savings and improved return on investment (ROI). IT consultants analyze the total cost of ownership (TCO) for various technology options, factoring in acquisition, maintenance, training, and potential downtime costs. This comprehensive perspective enables businesses to prioritize investments that deliver the greatest value.
Studies indicate that companies engaging IT consultants are 30% more likely to complete technology projects on time and within budget. This increased efficiency not only reduces unnecessary expenditures but also accelerates the realization of business benefits from new technologies.
Additionally, IT consulting can help organizations identify opportunities to consolidate systems, eliminate redundancies, and leverage cloud services to reduce infrastructure costs. For example, migrating to cloud platforms often results in lower upfront capital expenses and more flexible scalability, which can be optimized with expert guidance.
Consultants also assist in negotiating vendor contracts and service-level agreements (SLAs), ensuring that businesses receive favorable terms and reliable support. This expertise helps prevent hidden costs and service disruptions that can impact operations.
By focusing on strategic investments aligned with business priorities, IT consulting maximizes ROI and ensures that technology expenditures contribute directly to organizational growth and efficiency.
Facilitating Digital Transformation and Innovation
Beyond immediate technology decisions, IT consulting plays a strategic role in digital transformation initiatives. Consultants help organizations adopt emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which can drive innovation and competitive advantage.
By aligning technology adoption with business vision, IT consultants ensure that digital transformation efforts are purposeful and sustainable rather than reactive and fragmented. This foresight is essential in a business environment where 87% of executives believe digital transformation is a priority but only 40% feel their organization is fully prepared to execute it.
IT consultants guide companies through the complex process of integrating new technologies with existing systems, minimizing disruption while maximizing benefits. They also help establish metrics to measure the impact of digital initiatives, enabling continuous improvement and accountability.
Furthermore, consultants facilitate cultural change within organizations, encouraging innovation mindsets and agility. This human element is often overlooked but is critical for successful digital transformation, as technology alone cannot drive change without engaged and adaptable people.
By fostering innovation ecosystems, IT consulting supports businesses in exploring new business models, enhancing customer experiences, and creating data-driven decision-making capabilities that position them for long-term success.
Conclusion
In an era marked by technological complexity and rapid change, IT consulting stands out as a critical enabler of sound technology decision-making. By leveraging the expertise of specialized professionals like and adopting structured approaches exemplified by, businesses can optimize their technology investments, enhance cybersecurity, improve operational efficiency, and drive innovation.
The impact of these contributions is measurable: from reducing project overruns to mitigating cyber risks and accelerating digital transformation, IT consulting offers tangible benefits that empower organizations to thrive in a competitive marketplace. As technology continues to evolve, partnering with trusted IT consultants is not just a strategic advantage-it is a necessity for sustainable business success.
Through comprehensive assessments, proven methodologies, and a focus on both technology and people, IT consulting transforms complex technology landscapes into clear, manageable pathways that support business growth and resilience. This holistic approach ensures that technology decisions are not only optimized for today’s challenges but also future-proofed for tomorrow’s opportunities.

articles.title: Torrent of states repeal data center tax exemptions, and it could increase costs by upwards of 7%
articles.text:
A torrent of states are repealing data center tax exemptions — but it could increase costs by upwards of 7%
New data center projects could be hit by a big increase in costs
- Multiple US states are repealing or enacting moratoriums on sales tax exemptions for data centers
- Estimates on lost tax revenue are far below the billions of dollars some states have missed out on
- Ongoing data center constructions may not be subject, but costs are expected to increase for new or planned projects
In a blow to US firms trying to expand AI compute capacity by building more data centers, multiple states are now repealing tax exemptions for equipment costs.
According to exclusive The Information reporting, the estimated costs could rise by upwards of 7%, as the exemptions previously allowed data centers to be kitted out with equipment without having to pay sales tax.
But as soon as Ohio Governor Mike DeWine revealed that the lost tax revenue amounted to $1.6 billion, instead of the projected $136 million, other states have started following suit.
States repeal data center tax exemptions
Ohio repealed its tax exemptions for data centers in June 2026, and since July, Illinois and Arizona have both paused their own exemptions. Illinois’ program has been paused indefinitely, and Arizona has enacted a 3-year moratorium.
A further nine states are also considering halting their own exemptions, and a further 28 states have introduced bills to limit the effects of their own exemptions.
Per Avalra data, the sales tax in Ohio sits at almost 6%, with Illinois just over the same figure. These sales taxes will immediately increase the costs of new data center projects, but some projects already under way could be subject to indefinite exemptions.
Are data center costs already unsustainable?
The costs of data center construction have already been rising due to the sudden expansion in capacity. Electricity costs have skyrocketed as more data centers join grids without suitable additions in energy sources.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
In an attempt to combat this, President Donald Trump has rolled back regulations on fossil-fuel burning power stations, with multiple data centers being built with on-site natural gas turbine electricity generation. This has caused a string of issues with local residents complaining of sickness caused by infra-sound, and deafening noise levels similar to that of an international airport.
Funding and incentives for renewable wind and solar sources have also been scrapped by Trump, which ironically are some of the cheapest energy sources in the US. This has compounded consumer electricity price rises, acting as a catalyst for data center opposition in the US. AI companies have been urged by the UN to disclose the full environmental damage of the technology.
Additionally, a study by Nikkei has found that numerous big tech firms looking to expand data center capacity have almost $1.65 trillion in ‘hidden’ debt, where contracts are signed between subsidiary companies and data center operators. This means the debt does not appear on the company’s balance sheet, and will only show up as annotations in quarterly financial statements.
This hidden debt at big tech companies has exploded eightfold in the last four years, alongside the visible balance sheet debt for big tech companies which stands at $1.35 trillion. Many businesses are still struggling to justify the ROI on adopting AI technologies, especially as token costs increase.
Sales exemptions are an attractive benefit for data center construction projects, and states that keep or enact sales exemptions will likely see an explosion in new project applications.

articles.title: In a troubling sign, Nvidia RTX 50 series prices jump up to 30% in South Korea — TSMC wafer hikes and $20 GDDR7 modules push RTX 5090 past $5,100
articles.text:
In a troubling sign, Nvidia RTX 50 series prices jump up to 30% in South Korea — TSMC wafer hikes and $20 GDDR7 modules push RTX 5090 past $5,100
Yet another blow for gamers.
GPU prices are set to increase in South Korea starting this month, specifically Nvidia’s desktop GeForce RTX 50 series. According to a recent report, the price increase is primarily due to the recent increase in price for advanced process wafers from TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company), along with the rising price for GDDR7 memory. Perhaps most troubling is that, due to global market dynamics, pricing doesn't exist in a vacuum for any single region, suggesting that price hikes could be in store for other areas in the future.
For context, TSMC recently asked its customers to prepare for price increases across its advanced chipmaking portfolio. This hike was extended beyond the newer 3nm process to include 7nm and other legacy products. ZDnet Korea’s report additionally cites market research firm TrendForce, claiming that GDDR7 2GB modules used in the RTX 50 series GPUs have increased to $20 per unit. As fabrication and memory costs have increased, Nvidia has raised the prices of the RTX 50 series GPU packages it sells to board partners. These board partners, thus, have little choice but to pass those higher costs on to consumers.
Multiple officials from domestic importers and distributors in the region have reportedly confirmed the price rise and have announced that major graphics card manufacturers plan to raise the prices of RTX 50 series models by up to 30% starting this month.
According to a manufacturing company official, "Major manufacturers have temporarily suspended shipments ahead of the August price hike, and to my knowledge, few companies have secured inventory prior to the price increase." Similarly, a local distributor said, "One manufacturer with a low domestic market share is considering a price increase of about 20% compared to existing levels, and other manufacturers are also preparing for price increases of up to around 30%."
High-end graphics cards with larger GDDR7 memory configurations are expected to see the biggest increase in production costs, leading to higher retail prices. According to Danawa, a South Korean price comparison website, the cheapest RTX 5060 Ti 8GB model now sells for around 700,000 won (about $490), up roughly 100,000 won (about $70). Meanwhile, the lowest-priced RTX 5070 model is listed at around 1.1 million won (about $770), an increase of approximately 200,000 won (about $140).
The flagship RTX 5090 has seen the biggest price hike. Depending on the model and manufacturer, it is currently selling for up to 7.3 million won (around $5,112), an increase of as much as 1.5 million won (around $1,050) compared to last month.

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta el BlackBerry Curve 8520 en 2026 y qué funciones aún sirven
articles.text:
El BlackBerry Curve 8520 es uno de los modelos más recordados de la marca, por lo que aún es posible encontrar dispositivos en el mercado de segunda mano que sean funcionales, a pesar de haber sido descatalogado.
Este modelo incluyó varias mejoras en su lanzamiento en 2009 y se convirtió en un pilar clave de la compañía durante esa etapa en la que BlackBerry fue uno de los referentes de los teléfonos inteligentes.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál es el precio actual del BlackBerry Curve 8520
En plataformas como eBay, el Curve 8520 aparece en tres categorías distintas: equipos usados o reacondicionados, unidades nuevas de colección y teléfonos para repuestos.
Los dispositivos usados o reacondicionados suelen encontrarse en un rango de $30 USD a $60 USD, según el desgaste físico, si incluyen cargador, caja original o si están desbloqueados para cualquier operadora.
PUBLICIDAD
La categoría más codiciada entre los coleccionistas es la de equipos completamente nuevos, sellados y en caja original, denominados en la jerga de los entusiastas como New Old Stock (NOS). Estas unidades, muy difíciles de encontrar, pueden alcanzar precios entre $100 USD y $200 USD.
El atractivo principal de estos teléfonos reside en que nunca fueron activados ni usados, lo que los convierte en piezas de colección. Por debajo de estos valores se ubican los equipos para repuestos: teléfonos que no encienden o presentan fallos graves suelen ofertarse por menos de $20 USD.
PUBLICIDAD
Los anuncios en internet suelen detallar el estado del equipo: modelos usados muestran signos de desgaste en la carcasa y teclado, y algunos conservan accesorios originales como cargador, auriculares o la caja.
Los reacondicionados pueden haber recibido carcasas nuevas o baterías de reemplazo, pero su funcionamiento depende en gran medida del uso previo. Los dispositivos nuevos, sellados, son cada vez más escasos y su precio refleja la rareza.
PUBLICIDAD
Al momento de adquirir uno de estos teléfonos, es fundamental verificar si está desbloqueado para cualquier operadora y si la red 2G sigue activa en el país de residencia. La mayoría de los vendedores advierten que, debido al apagado de los servidores de BlackBerry OS en enero de 2022, muchas de sus funciones originales han dejado de estar disponibles.
Qué funciones siguen vigentes en el BlackBerry Curve 8520
El BlackBerry Curve 8520 puede funcionar para llamadas y mensajes SMS, siempre que la red 2G esté activa en la región. Sin embargo, la mayoría de las funciones de internet, correo electrónico y redes sociales han quedado inoperantes tras el cierre de los servidores de BlackBerry.
PUBLICIDAD
Esto limita el uso del dispositivo a funciones básicas, aunque el reproductor multimedia, la radio FM y la cámara de 2 megapíxeles siguen operativas de forma local.
El teclado QWERTY, uno de los sellos de identidad del modelo, permite escribir mensajes de texto con rapidez y precisión, lo que aún resulta atractivo para quienes buscan una experiencia diferente a la de los teléfonos actuales de pantalla táctil. La salida para auriculares de 3,5 mm y los botones físicos para controlar la música, ubicados en la parte superior del equipo, también continúan siendo funcionales.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál fue el impacto del Curve 8520 en el mercado de smartphones
El BlackBerry Curve 8520 fue presentado en septiembre de 2009, con el objetivo de captar consumidores que no habían probado antes un smartphone de la marca. Su estrategia se basó en ofrecer un equipo más accesible que las líneas prémium, como la Bold, y dotado de elementos que lo acercaban a los jóvenes: teclas multimedia, colores llamativos y un precio contenido gracias a acuerdos con operadoras.
La principal innovación del modelo fue el reemplazo del clásico trackball por un trackpad óptico táctil, más resistente al uso intensivo y al polvo. El teclado físico, ideal para chatear a través de BlackBerry Messenger (BBM), y la conectividad Wi-Fi complementaban la propuesta, aunque la ausencia de 3G marcó una diferencia frente a otros smartphones del momento.
PUBLICIDAD
Su popularidad fue tal que dominó el mercado en países como Sudáfrica y España durante varios años, superando a los teléfonos táctiles en segmentos clave.
Durante el auge de la serie Curve, BlackBerry alcanzó en septiembre de 2011 los 85 millones de suscriptores activos a nivel mundial. En su mejor momento, la compañía llegó a vender más de 50 millones de dispositivos en un solo año y dominó aproximadamente el 20% del mercado global de smartphones, superando el 50% en Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Michael Dell's son and a SpaceX alum want to put battery storage in every backyard
articles.text:
In brief: As energy demands from AI, electric vehicles, and other technologies mount, the tech sector's interest in battery storage has grown sharply in recent years. In the latest example, the son of Dell's founder has teamed up with a SpaceX alumnus to break into the fast-growing home battery storage market.
Home battery storage, which can lower electric bills by feeding power back to the grid, is gaining popularity across the US, particularly in warmer regions. A startup led by Zach Dell shows how the industry is expanding options for grid operators.
Although local battery storage has historically been tied to home solar power, the technology is increasingly showing up in homes with or without solar panels. Installing an air-conditioning-compressor-sized battery near a home's electric meter lets homeowners store energy when it's cheap, usually during the day, and helps stabilize the grid during peak hours.
Dell's company, Base Power, installs about 100 39-kWh home batteries a day and expects to double that pace by the end of 2026. So far, it has installed roughly 550 megawatt-hours, on par with a large utility-scale storage project.
The company is helping drive a broader trend. Partly encouraged by state policy in Texas, California, Arizona, and Hawaii, US homeowners installed a record 673 megawatts of storage in the first quarter of this year, according to the Energy Information Administration.
The American Clean Power Association and Wood Mackenzie report that of the 3.3 gigawatts of power capacity and 8.4 gigawatt-hours of total energy storage the US installed during the quarter, home batteries accounted for 1.3 gigawatt-hours.
The end of federal tax incentives for residential solar and battery installations has made both technologies less economically attractive, but individual states are finding their own ways to compensate homeowners who install batteries. Hawaii, for instance, pays $400 per kilowatt of installed capacity, while California offers recurring payments for contributions to the grid.
Base offers batteries that can power homes for 36 to 72 hours during outages and lower energy bills when connected to the grid. In regions with battery network policies, Base can enter agreements with local authorities; where those policies don't exist, it can double as a home backup battery retailer and an electric grid operator.
Early financial backer Antonio Gracias and co-founder Justin Lopas, both with SpaceX ties, believe Base and similar operations can help the US energy grid power a return to domestic manufacturing. Many also see them as a way to help meet the massive energy demands of AI data centers.

Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Lenovo Googlebook 15 Renders Appear Months Ahead of Launch
In mid-May, Google announced that it is working on bringing its new Googlebook devices to the masses, with a promise to introduce a new operating system featuring integrated Gemini AI across the board. As the company collaborates with multiple OEMs, including Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, we have received the first leak of the Lenovo Googlebook 15 model. This model is set to offer a 15-inch experience of Google's upcoming "Aluminium" operating system. Thanks to a leak by Digital Citizen, we can see the first renderings of the Lenovo Googlebook 15, showcasing a sandblasted aluminium casing in a 15-inch body. The device features the traditional Lenovo bezel and overall design, housed in a medium-thickness body.
On the keyboard front, Lenovo has included a small "G" button with the Google icon, reminiscent of the Windows key on standard Windows-based laptops. Two speakers flank the keyboard, and the left side of the unit includes an HDMI port, a USB-C or Thunderbolt port, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack. On the right, there is another USB-C port, a USB Type-A port, and a slot similar to an SD card reader. Specifications such as display resolution, refresh rate, and details about the processor powering this PC are currently unknown, but we expect to learn more when Googlebooks officially launch. Scheduled for release in the fall of this year, we are still months away from the official debut.Interestingly, Intel announced that it has been collaborating with Google on these models, with Intel Core processors at the heart of the platform. Google is likely to pair these laptops with Intel's latest Core Series 300 "Wildcat Lake" processors, which the company recently launched. This means that Googlebooks will feature an x86 platform based on Intel processors, with six CPU cores consisting of two "Cougar Cove" P-cores and four LPE "Darkmont" cores. Google has set strict requirements for its OEM partners, including specifications for CPU, memory, keyboard layout, and storage configurations for its upcoming devices. Since launch partners will also include Qualcomm and MediaTek, we can expect to see Arm-powered Googlebooks as well.

articles.title: Why India pays highway builders even when roads stay empty
articles.text:
Why India pays highway builders even when roads stay empty
India’s Hybrid Annuity Model protects highway developers from traffic risk by guaranteeing scheduled payments. But growing land acquisition and financing delays are exposing new weaknesses.
Intuitively, a toll road company should want traffic. More cars, more tolls, more revenue, it seems like the whole point of building the road. But a large share of India's national highways today are built under a model where the private company that constructs the road gets paid on a schedule that has nothing to do with how many vehicles ever use it, and the government, not the developer, absorbs the risk of an empty highway.
What the government actually built to fix a broken system
This is the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in January 2016 and issued as a circular by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways the following month. It was a direct response to a wave of failed projects under the earlier Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) toll model. CRISIL Ratings estimated in 2015 that roughly 7,500 km of highway projects, 5,100 km under construction and 2,400 km already operational, awarded mostly between fiscals 2010 and 2012 on a BOT basis, were at high risk, with about half the under-construction stretch unlikely to be completed because of cost overruns and weak sponsors. Private developers had taken on toll revenue risk they could not reliably manage.
HAM restructured that risk entirely. Under the model, as confirmed in an official Press Information Bureau release dated 21 November 2019, the government funds 40% of the project cost directly during construction, paid out in milestone-linked installments tied to physical progress. The remaining 60% is raised by the private developer through debt and equity, and recovered afterward through semi-annual annuity payments from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), spread across the operations period, along with separately calculated interest and maintenance payments. Critically, per the same PIB release: "Toll fee collection from the highways projects developed under the hybrid annuity model is the responsibility of the Government/Authority," not the developer.
Those annuities are not fixed in nominal terms. They are indexed to inflation, and the interest component floats with the average one-year marginal cost of lending rate of the top five scheduled commercial banks plus 125 basis points. What is fixed is the developer's exposure to traffic, which is zero.
Why this actually works, structurally
The Asian Development Bank's working paper on HAM is explicit about what this changes. In its analysis, the authority assumes the full risks associated with traffic forecast and revenue leakage, and its risk matrix classifies both revenue forecast and revenue collection under HAM as government-borne. The developer's annuity payments arrive on schedule whether the highway carries heavy daily traffic or sits comparatively empty. The developer's job is to build the road well and maintain it, full stop. Whether commuters actually choose to drive on it, and how much toll revenue that generates, becomes the government's problem to manage, not a variable that threatens the company's return on investment.
This isn't a small, experimental corner of India's highway programme either. According to CareEdge Ratings' analysis of HAM projects awarded between fiscal years 2016 and 2023, 306 HAM projects were awarded to 62 different sponsors, spanning a combined 12,700 km of highway, with a total bid project cost of Rs 3.35 lakh crore. Of the projects awarded before 2020, representing over Rs 1 lakh crore in project cost, CareEdge found in September 2023 that 88% had reached operational status, with only 12% delayed.
Where the model shows real strain
That 88% figure covers the oldest and simplest cohort, and the picture for everything awarded since has deteriorated sharply. In a February 2025 update covering 374 HAM projects awarded between 2015 and 2024, spanning roughly 16,000 km and over Rs 4.03 lakh crore in bid project cost, CareEdge found that only 42% of the sample cost had been commissioned as of September 2024, with 45% still under construction and 13% yet to receive an appointed date. Among the under-construction projects, 55% with an aggregate bid project cost of Rs 1 lakh crore were running more than six months late, up from roughly 33% in June 2023.
The causes are split. India Ratings and Research (part of Fitch Group) flagged in May 2024 that newer sponsors, many of whom had moved from EPC contracting to HAM for the first time after technical and financial qualification norms were relaxed, were struggling to secure funding as banks tightened capital requirements. Small and medium developers, the agency noted, had largely managed to execute their projects. For financially strong and medium sponsors, the binding constraint was different: land acquisition. More than 110 projects worth over Rs 1 trillion were awaiting an appointed date, mostly on right-of-way issues. Ind-Ra nonetheless held its FY25 outlook for both annuity projects and toll-collecting assets at stable.
Why this matters beyond highways
HAM is a clean illustration of how infrastructure financing can be deliberately restructured to make projects investable again once a previous risk-allocation model has failed. The BOT-toll model asked private companies to bet on traffic forecasts, a bet that had already stranded thousands of kilometres of road. HAM keeps developers focused on what they can actually control, building and maintaining quality infrastructure, while shifting the genuinely unpredictable variable, how many people choose to drive on a given stretch of road, back to the government, whose job it arguably always was to manage.
What the model could not fix is everything upstream of the contract. Land that has not been acquired and lenders who will not lend are not risks the annuity structure was designed to absorb, and they are where the delays now sit. Sometimes the smartest fix for a broken system isn't a completely new idea. It's simply moving the risk to whoever is actually positioned to carry it, and then discovering which risks nobody had allocated at all.

articles.title: Managed IT And Cybersecurity For Everyday Operational Resilience - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Understanding Operational Resilience in Today’s Business Landscape
In an increasingly digital world, operational resilience has become a critical focus for businesses of all sizes. Operational resilience refers to an organization’s ability to continue delivering essential services despite disruptions, whether due to cyberattacks, system failures, or natural disasters. For businesses reliant on technology, integrating managed IT and cybersecurity solutions is essential to maintaining continuity and minimizing downtime.
The complexity of modern IT environments, combined with the growing sophistication of cyber threats, means businesses can no longer afford to treat resilience as a secondary concern. Instead, it must be woven into daily operations. The ability to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions separates thriving organizations from those vulnerable to operational collapse.
According to a report by IBM, the average cost of a data breach in 2023 reached $4.45 million, highlighting the significant financial impact cybersecurity incidents can cause globally. This figure includes direct costs such as remediation and legal fees, as well as indirect costs like reputational damage and customer churn. Such high stakes emphasize the need for comprehensive strategies that protect IT infrastructure while ensuring smooth operations.
Operational resilience encompasses not only technology but also people and processes. It requires a holistic approach aligning IT capabilities with business objectives, ensuring critical functions continue under various stress scenarios. This mindset encourages proactive risk management, continuous improvement, and adaptive planning-cornerstones of a resilient enterprise.
The Role of Managed IT Services in Strengthening Resilience
Managed IT services have emerged as a cornerstone for businesses aiming to enhance their operational resilience. By partnering with a managed services provider in Richmond, organizations gain access to expert support, proactive maintenance, and tailored IT solutions that address both current and evolving challenges.
Outsourcing IT management allows businesses to leverage specialized knowledge and advanced tools without the burden of managing complex systems internally. This model enables continuous monitoring, faster issue resolution, and strategic IT planning, all contributing to reduced downtime and improved system reliability. Managed service providers (MSPs) provide scalability and flexibility, adapting services as business needs change and new technologies emerge.
Recent data shows that companies using managed IT services experience 50% fewer IT-related disruptions annually compared to those managing IT in-house. This efficiency translates into cost savings and stronger operational stability. Additionally, MSPs often provide 24/7 support, ensuring rapid responses to incidents and reducing the risk of prolonged outages.
Beyond technical support, MSPs help organizations implement best practices such as patch management, data backups, and disaster recovery planning. These proactive measures are vital for maintaining uptime and safeguarding data integrity. Moreover, MSPs assist with compliance requirements, helping businesses navigate complex regulatory landscapes.
Cybersecurity: A Pillar of Operational Continuity
Cybersecurity is no longer just an IT concern but a fundamental business imperative. Effective cybersecurity safeguards sensitive data, protects intellectual property, and ensures compliance with regulatory requirements. A comprehensive cybersecurity strategy includes threat detection, incident response, and employee training to mitigate risks from both external and internal sources.
Engaging with experts in cybersecurity by Nuvodia provides businesses with advanced, tailored protection that adapts to the changing threat landscape. These services encompass vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, continuous monitoring, and rapid threat neutralization. Cybersecurity specialists use cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify anomalies and predict potential attacks before they cause damage.
Data from Cybersecurity Ventures predicts that global cybercrime costs will reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, illustrating the escalating risk businesses face without robust defenses. This staggering figure underscores the urgency of investing in cybersecurity to protect operational continuity.
In addition to technology, cybersecurity requires a strong focus on human factors. Social engineering attacks, phishing, and insider threats remain prevalent, making employee awareness and training essential components of any defense strategy. Regular drills, clear policies, and a culture of security mindfulness help reduce vulnerabilities caused by human error.
Integration of Managed IT and Cybersecurity for Holistic Resilience
The convergence of managed IT and cybersecurity services offers a holistic approach to operational resilience. Managed service providers not only maintain IT infrastructure but also embed cybersecurity protocols within their service delivery. This integration ensures security is built into everyday IT operations rather than treated as an afterthought.
By aligning IT management with cybersecurity, businesses can detect threats early, respond swiftly, and maintain compliance with industry standards such as ISO 27001 or NIST frameworks. This proactive stance mitigates risks before they escalate into full-scale incidents, reducing potential downtime and reputational damage.
Moreover, integrating these services facilitates centralized visibility and control over IT assets and security posture. Unified dashboards and reporting tools empower decision-makers with real-time insights, enabling faster, data-driven responses to emerging threats or operational challenges.
This integrated approach also supports business continuity planning and disaster recovery. Coordinating IT management and cybersecurity efforts enables organizations to develop comprehensive playbooks addressing various disruption scenarios, ensuring rapid recovery and minimal operational impact.
Practical Steps to Enhance Everyday Operational Resilience
Improving operational resilience is a continuous journey involving multiple layers of defense and preparation. Here are key practical steps businesses can take:
- Conduct Regular Risk Assessments: Identifying vulnerabilities in IT systems and business processes helps prioritize investments in technology and security measures. Risk assessments should be updated frequently to account for new threats and changing business conditions.
- Partner with Experienced Providers: Working with trusted managed service and cybersecurity experts delivers access to cutting-edge technologies and best practices. Providers with industry-specific knowledge can tailor solutions to unique operational needs.
- Implement Continuous Monitoring: Real-time visibility into network activity allows faster detection of anomalies and potential breaches. Utilizing automated alerts and AI-driven analytics enhances threat identification capabilities.
- Develop Incident Response Plans: Preparing for various disruption scenarios ensures teams can act decisively and minimize impact. Incident response plans should include clear roles, communication protocols, and escalation procedures.
- Invest in Employee Training: Human error remains a leading cause of security breaches; ongoing education empowers staff to recognize and avoid threats. Simulated phishing campaigns and security awareness workshops reinforce learning.
- Leverage Cloud and Hybrid Solutions: Cloud platforms offer scalable and resilient infrastructure options that support disaster recovery and business continuity efforts. Hybrid models provide flexibility by combining on-premises and cloud resources.
- Regularly Update and Patch Systems: Keeping software and hardware up to date reduces exposure to known vulnerabilities. Automated patch management tools help streamline this critical task.
- Test Backup and Recovery Processes: Regular drills and validation of backup data ensure recovery systems function correctly when needed.
The Business Case for Operational Resilience through Managed IT and Cybersecurity
Operational resilience directly impacts customer trust, regulatory compliance, and financial performance. Businesses that invest in managed IT and cybersecurity not only protect themselves from disruptions but also gain competitive advantages by demonstrating reliability and security.
According to a survey by Deloitte, 79% of organizations view operational resilience as a top priority for their digital transformation initiatives. This shift reflects growing recognition that resilience underpins long-term success in a volatile business environment.
Furthermore, resilient IT infrastructures enable faster recovery times after incidents, preserving revenue streams and maintaining stakeholder confidence. The cost of proactive resilience measures often pales in comparison to losses incurred from prolonged outages or data breaches. For example, downtime costs can range from $5,600 to $9,000 per minute depending on industry and scale.
Companies that prioritize resilience also benefit from improved operational efficiency. Streamlined IT management and robust security reduce the frequency and severity of disruptions, freeing resources to focus on innovation and growth. Additionally, regulatory bodies increasingly require evidence of resilience capabilities, making investments in these areas essential for compliance.
Future Trends in Operational Resilience
Looking ahead, operational resilience will continue to evolve in response to technological advancements and emerging threats. Artificial intelligence and machine learning will play larger roles in predictive analytics, enabling organizations to anticipate and mitigate risks more effectively.
The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing introduces new complexities, expanding the attack surface and challenging traditional security models. Managed IT and cybersecurity providers will need to develop specialized solutions to address these trends.
Moreover, regulatory frameworks are expected to become more stringent, with governments mandating higher standards for resilience and data protection. Businesses that proactively adapt to these changes will be better positioned to thrive in the future landscape.
Sustainability considerations are also intersecting with operational resilience. Energy-efficient data centers, green IT practices, and sustainable supply chains contribute to long-term viability and risk reduction.
Conclusion
In today’s complex threat landscape, operational resilience is essential for business continuity and growth. Managed IT and cybersecurity services form the backbone of resilient operations, providing expert support, advanced protection, and strategic insights. By partnering with specialized providers, businesses can create robust defenses against disruptions, safeguard critical assets, and ensure uninterrupted service delivery.
Embracing integrated IT management and cybersecurity is not just a technical decision but a strategic imperative that safeguards the future of any organization. As cyber threats evolve and operational risks multiply, the time to invest in resilience is now. Organizations that prioritize operational resilience will not only survive but thrive, turning challenges into opportunities for sustained success.

articles.title: Des écrans toujours plus grands chez Mercedes, mais avec une particularité que vous allez adorer
articles.text:
Présentée en 2021, la Mercedes EQS a littéralement redéfini la place des écrans dans nos voitures. Avec l’option Hyperscreen, la limousine électrique présentait une planche de bord spectaculaire composée de trois dalles placées derrière un plateau en verre. Moderne pour certains et indigeste pour d’autres, cette disposition a inspiré les concurrents qui n’hésitent plus à tartiner leurs habitacles d’afficheurs.
Le mea-culpa inattendu du patron de Mercedes
L’idée est la même : recouvrir l’intérieur d’écrans pour épurer le tout et supprimer des boutons. De quoi faire de belles économies, même si les automobilistes ont du mal à s’y retrouver. Ola Källenius, le PDG de la marque à l’étoile, concède ainsi que les constructeurs sont peut-être allés trop loin dans le processus. Les commandes physiques reviendront, mais les écrans poursuivront leur domination.
« Un enfant de cinq ans peut utiliser l’interface »
Au sujet de l’interface, Källenius explique dans une interview accordée à Autocar que « chaque année, [il] passe des heures à en discuter avec [ses] ingénieurs et [ils] plaisantent en disant qu’elle doit être si simple qu’un enfant de cinq ans ou un membre du conseil d’administration de Mercedes puisse l’utiliser ». Le patron salue également l’avancée des commandes vocales permettant de contourner les écrans.
La fin du tout-tactile : quand la technologie oublie le client
Même si les systèmes embarqués sont de plus en plus performants grâce à l’intelligence artificielle, Källenius admet que, « parfois, on s’emballe un peu et on développe la technologie pour le simple plaisir de la technologie, en oubliant quelque peu le client. C’est pourquoi, à partir de maintenant, nous réintroduirons les boutons les plus pertinents ». Les choses avancent déjà peu à peu sur la dernière CLA.
Le grand retour des boutons physiques dans l’habitacle
La petite berline possédait à son lancement des pavés tactiles sur son volant pour régler le régulateur de vitesse ainsi que le volume du multimédia. Les derniers modèles sont désormais revenus à des roulettes physiques bien plus commodes à l’usage. Cette dynamique devrait donc se poursuivre, avec un retour des commandes en dur pour contrôler la ventilation ou les aides à la conduite, par exemple.
Des écrans géants toujours plus grands, mais…
Källenius le confirme à demi-mot après avoir été interrogé sur la taille des écrans : « je ne sais pas si nous avons atteint un sommet en termes d’écrans, mais nous sommes au bas de l’échelle en termes de boutons ». Cela suggère donc que si les touches physiques vont repeupler les habitacles, la course aux écrans n’est pas prête de s’arrêter. Préparons-nous à voir des afficheurs toujours plus gros dans nos véhicules.

articles.title: Le MacBook Air vous fait de l'oeil pour la rentrée ? Dépêchez-vous, les stocks s'épuisent
articles.text:
La course aux centres de données d’intelligence artificielle aspire depuis des mois la production mondiale de puces mémoire, et les fabricants d’ordinateurs passent après. Apple, longtemps protégé par sa force de frappe commerciale, avait tenu. C’est terminé : son portable vedette manque un peu partout, en pleine période d’achats de rentrée.
Jusqu’à six semaines d’attente pour l’ordinateur préféré des étudiants
Sur la boutique en ligne d’Apple, les délais de livraison du MacBook Air s’étirent désormais de 4 à 6 semaines. Toutes les configurations de base glissent vers la fin août, et les versions personnalisées, mémoire gonflée en tête, filent vers début septembre. La France n’est pas mieux lotie : les dates y dérivent aussi vers la fin du mois, voire la rentrée, suivant la configuration choisie. En magasin, les revendeurs décriraient des arrivages plus maigres que jamais.
Cette ruée survient de surcroît après une douche froide tarifaire. Le 25 juin, Apple a relevé les prix de quatorze produits : l’Air est passé à 1 399 euros chez nous. Même plus cher, il part donc plus vite qu’Apple ne peut le fabriquer. Le Mac mini et le Mac Studio avaient ouvert le bal ces derniers mois ; avec le modèle le plus vendu de la gamme, la pénurie change simplement d’échelle. Tim Cook a prévenu fin juillet que les contraintes s’aggraveraient nettement sur l’iPhone, le Mac et l’iPad d’ici septembre, la demande ayant été sous-estimée.
Apple pousse déjà ses clients vers le MacBook Pro
À l’origine du manque, toujours le même siphon : Samsung, SK Hynix et Micron réservent leurs lignes de production à la mémoire haute performance des centres de données d’IA. Les puces destinées à nos ordinateurs passent après, comme un client au comptoir derrière un car de touristes. Résultat, la DRAM classique a presque doublé en un an (+98 % au premier trimestre), et les analystes attendent encore 58 à 63 % de hausse. Personne, chez les fabricants, ne promet d’accalmie avant 2027, voire 2028.
Lire aussi : Mémoire vive : l’espoir d’une baisse de prix avant 2030 vient de mourir
Apple s’adapte sans le crier sur les toits. Sa promotion de rentrée, d’ordinaire lancée fin juin, n’est arrivée qu’à la mi-juillet, faute de stocks. Ses supports marketing mettent surtout en avant, pour la première fois, le MacBook Pro 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme. L’Air n’y est proposé que « sous réserve de disponibilité », précision inhabituelle chez la firme. Cette bascule préparerait aussi le terrain, puisqu’un MacBook Pro M6 est attendu à l’automne, tandis que le prochain Air ne viendrait pas avant l’an prochain. La marque chercherait même de la mémoire chez des fournisseurs chinois pour ses appareils vendus sur place.
Pour la rentrée, la stratégie se résume en quelques gestes. Commander tout de suite en visant une livraison fin août, plutôt qu’espérer un miracle en boutique. Se rabattre sur le 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme, le seul qu’Apple livre sans sourciller, ou traquer chez les revendeurs les derniers exemplaires à l’ancien tarif et le (ô combien oublié) reconditionné. Et fuir les configurations mémoire sur mesure, les plus mal servies. Changer de crémerie n’aidera pas davantage : la pénurie frappe tout autant les PC sous Windows.
L’ordinateur à tout faire de la rentrée se guette désormais comme une console en rupture : si un Air traîne encore au prix de juin quelque part, ne le laissez pas filer.

articles.title: Mantener satélites en órbita terrestre muy baja es muy problemático, pero esta compañía española quiere convertir el problema en solución
articles.text:
La startup española Kreios Space se está preparando para hacer historia con el lanzamiento del primer satélite en órbita terrestre muy baja (VLEO) impulsado por propulsión eléctrica atmosférica. Este tipo de propulsión está ideada precisamente para que los satélites puedan operar en órbitas muy bajas, donde las imágenes de la Tierra son más nítidas, las mediciones más precisas y las comunicaciones mucho más optimizadas. Todo suena muy bien, pero mantener un vehículo a esa altitud es muy costoso por muchos motivos. Para solucionarlo, se deben buscar opciones novedosas, como la que propone Kreios Space. Por eso es tan interesante lo que están a punto de hacer.
Kongsberg NanoAvionics entra en escena. Kreios Space ha seleccionado a la compañía Kongsberg NanoAvionics, uno de los principales fabricantes europeos de plataformas satelitales, para participar en la primera demostración de su tecnología de propulsión en órbita terrestre muy baja. En principio se ha seleccionado el bus de microsatélite MP42 de NanoAvionics, con un peso aproximado de 200 kg en su configuración final incluyendo la carga útil. Con esta primera misión se validará el rendimiento del propulsor de Kreios a altitudes de entre 150 y 300 km. Además, se realizarán mediciones del entorno y se capturarán imágenes en el rango espectral del visible y el infrarrojo cercano.
NanoAvionics se encargará de proporcionar y adaptar la plataforma satelital, integrar la carga útil y llevar a cabo las primeras operaciones de la misión. Después, Kreios Space asumirá el control operativo.
VLEO, una órbita interesante, pero complicada. Muchas agencias espaciales están interesadas en enviar sus satélites a VLEO por todo lo que hemos visto. El problema es que, a altitudes tan bajas, existen muchos retos por superar. Para empezar, la atmósfera terrestre va perdiendo densidad a medida que ascendemos. A una altura tan baja, aún queda bastante atmósfera residual, por lo que se genera cierta fricción con los satélites. Esta, poco a poco, va frenándolos, hasta el punto de que pueden desorbitarse y caer. Esto puede ocurrir también a mayor altitud. De hecho, le está pasando al telescopio espacial Swift. Por eso se ha enviado una nave a rescatarlo. No obstante, ha sido un proceso más lento, que se ha agravado por la actividad solar. En VLEO puede ocurrir mucho más deprisa, sin necesidad de inclemencias solares. Para evitar que esto ocurra, se requiere un impulso constante que no es viable con los combustibles habituales.
Por otro lado, el oxígeno atómico a esas alturas es muy corrosivo, por lo que puede alterar los materiales de los satélites.
Muchas agencias espaciales interesadas. Ya hay muchas agencias y compañías espaciales interesadas en VLEO. Es, por ejemplo, el caso de China, donde se ha creado una alianza industrial nacional centrada en órbitas terrestres muy bajas. Kreios Space también quiere su trozo de pastel. Por eso, ha ideado un método para impulsar los satélites capaz de enfrentarse a la fricción de la atmósfera residual y el resto de hándicaps mencionados.
La solución de Kreios Space. Hace tiempo que se ha estudiado como solución a los problemas de VLEO el uso de propulsión eléctrica atmosférica. No obstante, de momento nadie la ha usado. Kreios Space podría ser la primera compañía en lograrlo si sus planes siguen según lo previsto. Este método de propulsión consiste, básicamente, en convertir el problema en solución, ya que ese aire de la atmósfera residual, cargado de oxígeno corrosivo, es el que se usa como combustible.
Se emplea una especie de embudo que recoge las moléculas de oxígeno y nitrógeno de la atmósfera a medida que el satélite avanza. Estas se introducen en una cámara en la que, gracias a una corriente eléctrica, se ionizan y se convierten en plasma. El mismo sistema eléctrico acelera los iones que componen ese plasma, de modo que se genera un empuje capaz de compensar la resistencia ejercida por la atmósfera. Es un win win.
Aún no hay fecha. De momento no hay fecha para el lanzamiento, pero, con su acuerdo con Kongsberg NanoAvionics, la compañía española demuestra que no se han dormido en los laureles. Su proyecto sigue adelante y, si no cambian las cosas, puede suponer un gran hito para la carrera espacial española.
