articles.title: L'Audi A2 e-tron est bien partie pour devenir la voiture électrique la plus sobre de sa catégorie
articles.text:
Audi s’apprête à ressusciter un modèle assez particulier à l’automne 2026 : l’A2 e-tron. La petite compacte au look si disruptif va faire son retour avec une motorisation 100 % électrique. Avant de révéler le design définitif, la marque aux anneaux fait parler de son futur modèle d’entrée de gamme par le biais de ses caractéristiques techniques.
Dans un communiqué publié ce 4 août 2026, on en apprend plus sur le travail effectué pour arriver à une efficience record pour le constructeur : 12,8 kWh/100 km. Un paramètre qui était déjà « la marque de fabrique » de la première A2 dans les années 2000.
L’aérodynamique au service de la consommation
Au-delà de 100 km/h, la résistance de l’air représente plus de la moitié de l’énergie consommée par un véhicule, souligne Audi. Le constructeur a ainsi concentré ses efforts sur ce paramètre et cela passe notamment par l’aérodynamique. La carrosserie de l’A2 e-tron adopte une face avant arrondie, une ligne de toit continue et une partie arrière profilée, complétées par des rideaux d’air et des dispositifs limitant les turbulences autour des passages de roues. Une prise d’air de refroidissement reste fermée en usage normal et ne s’ouvre qu’en cas de forte sollicitation du groupe motopropulseur ou de températures élevées, notamment pendant la recharge.
Il en résulte un coefficient de traînée (Cx) de 0,24, présenté comme le meilleur de la « gamme compacte » Audi. D’après les données annoncées, ce seul paramètre permettrait de réduire la consommation WLTP de 0,9 kWh/100 km par rapport à une configuration équivalente.
Une chaîne de traction revue sur trois points
Audi met en avant trois évolutions sur le groupe motopropulseur, dont le moteur synchrone à excitation permanente est la figure de proue :
- L’électronique de puissance passe à des semi-conducteurs en carbure de silicium, en remplacement du silicium classique. Une fréquence de commutation variable réduirait les pertes jusqu’à 20 watts et des techniques de modulation alternatives limiteraient les pertes de commutation jusqu’à 33 % par rapport aux méthodes conventionnelles.
- Le moteur électrique utilise des tôles de 0,2 mm d’épaisseur (contre 0,3 mm auparavant) pour réduire les pertes, tandis que le bobinage du stator passe d’un couplage dit en étoile à un couplage en triangle, déplaçant le point de fonctionnement vers des régimes plus efficients.
- La transmission bénéficie d’une huile à faible friction, quatre fois moins visqueuse que la précédente, avec un gain d’autonomie allant jusqu’à 12 km par temps froid.
L’ensemble de ces optimisations représenterait un gain d’efficience allant jusqu’à 10 % sur la chaîne de traction.
Trois capacités de batterie dès le lancement
La version 190 ch reçoit une batterie de 62 kWh (bruts) à cellules lithium-fer-phosphate (LFP), avec une architecture « cell-to-pack » où les cellules sont intégrées directement au boîtier plutôt qu’en modules. Cette chimie a pour avantages de ne pas nécessiter de matériaux « terres rares », de mieux résister au vieillissement, et de tolérer des charges répétées à 100 % sans dégradation accélérée.
L’A2 e-tron gère aussi la recharge bidirectionnelle : la fonction Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) permet d’alimenter des appareils externes, tandis que la fonction Vehicle-to-Home (V2H) permet d’utiliser le véhicule comme unité de stockage pour le domicile.
Pour le reste du catalogue, l’A2 e-tron sera aussi proposée avec deux autres capacités de batterie de 52 kWh (LFP) et 84 kWh (NMC). Pour l’heure, la marque ne précise pas encore l’autonomie WLTP associée à chaque version, ni la puissance de recharge en courant continu.
Comment se situe l’A2 e-tron face à ses concurrentes directes ?
Replacée dans son segment, la promesse de 12,8 kWh/100 km d’Audi se distingue nettement des chiffres WLTP publiés par les compactes électriques déjà commercialisées. Sur des gammes de batterie comparables, la plupart des rivales se situent plutôt entre 13,9 et 17,6 kWh/100 km selon les configurations.
L’écart entre l’A2 e-tron et ses concurrentes directes représenterait donc environ 1 à 5 kWh/100 km, soit une différence notable de 30 à 50 km sur l’autonomie en condition réelle.
Caractéristiques techniques Audi A2 e-tron
| Caractéristique | Donnée | 
|---|---|
| Puissance (version 62 kWh) | 190 ch | 
| Consommation WLTP (provisoire) | 12,8 kWh/100 km | 
| Coefficient de traînée (Cx) | 0,24 | 
| Chimie de batterie | LFP, cell-to-pack | 
| Capacités de batterie (brut) | 52 / 62 / 84 kWh | 
| Autonomie (WLTP) | non communiquée | 
| Puissance de charge rapide (DC) | non communiquée | 
| Commercialisation | automne 2026 |

articles.title: TSMC Targets 100,000 N2 Wafers per Month by the End of 2026
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
TSMC Targets 100,000 N2 Wafers per Month by the End of 2026
If readers recall, a few days ago we reported that TSMC has achieved a milestone of about 20,000 wafers per month on the company's latest 2 nm N2 node. However, the company is now rapidly scaling its high-volume manufacturing, aiming to produce about 100,000 N2 wafers per month by the end of 2026. This gives the company about four months to increase its manufacturing output fivefold. While that might seem impossible, TSMC has been rapidly scaling its manufacturing output over the years, and the latest N2 node is no exception. Currently, the N2 node accounts for only 3% of TSMC's revenue, while the 3 nm node holds 30%, and the 5 nm node secures the top spot at 33%. Even with projected growth in N3 and N5 consumption, increasing revenue fivefold would mean the N2 node would represent more than 10% of the company's overall revenue share.
Meanwhile, the demand for its 3 nm N3 family of nodes is still strong. Reportedly, TSMC's customers, including NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, and many others, have pushed the total monthly wafer output of the N3 node to 180,000 units, exceeding the company's internal targets. While TSMC hoped to achieve this number in the fourth quarter of 2026, demand has pushed production capacity to its limits, prompting TSMC to consider additional expansion plans for this node.This doesn't mean the N2 node is underperforming. Recently, the company confirmed that the N2 node has four times the number of tape-outs compared to its previous leading-edge 3 nm N3 node. With GAAFET technology, TSMC's N2 delivers up to a 15% performance increase at the same power level or up to a 30% power reduction at the same speed. This has led to four times the number of customers doing tape-outs, including AMD with its EPYC "Venice" server CPUs, Apple with its A20 Pro chips for the iPhone 18 Pro series, and many others. Even though the N2 ramp currently accounts for a small portion of revenue and wafer output, the majority of the business is gradually heading in that direction.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima just teamed up with boutique Japanese audio brand km5 to make a Death Stranding-themed orange CD player and despite owning a km5 player already, I must have it
articles.text:
No shade Sony, but Hideo Kojima is celebrating his love of physical discs with a new limited edition version of my favorite mini CD player
My new baby?
- km5 is collaborating with Kojima Productions on a limited edition CD player
- The Cp1 features Bluetooth 5.3, a 3.5mm headphone jack and more
- It's inspired by Death Stranding 2: On the Beach and comes in neon orange
Sony might be planning to wind down its production of PlayStation game discs, but physical media still has plenty of fans. Among them is auteur game director Hideo Kojima, whose studio Kojima Productions just announced a new collaboration with boutique Japanese audio brand km5 to celebrate that fact.
You can now buy an official Death Stranding 2: On the Beach version of km5's Cp1, a compact CD player that looks like a minimalist picture frame. It features wireless Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity so you can hook it up to one of the best Bluetooth speakers, or your wireless earbuds, in addition to a 3.5mm headphone jack if you'd prefer a more retro vibe.
It's got all the expected controls (a Bluetooth pairing button, play/pause, stop, fast forward, and rewind) in a row of clicky tactile buttons, and even a built-in battery which supports roughly eight hours of playtime, so you can take it on the go. And unlike retro players with nasty AA-type batteries, charging here is via USB Type-C. There's also a little LED display, which shows the current track number, and a little sleeve that you can use to display album art.
The Death Stranding 2 edition is, naturally, translucent neon orange and is designed to look like the BB Pod from the game — that's the glowing jar that contains the adorable baby that you use to detect invisible enemies. It's got a few little decals to really drive home the look, including little text warnings like 'ensure lock is tight', and comes nestled in special packaging alongside a card insert inspired by the series.
It looks like a lovely collectible and I already know that it's a capable little CD player, having used its big brother, the Cp2, for a few years now — the only real difference between the two models being the addition of a small speaker on the Cp2. I picked it up in Tokyo before the brand was more readily available worldwide, wanting a cute CD player that would be compact enough to fit on my shelf next to my extensive (and dare I say, pretty impressive) J-pop collection.
I normally have mine hooked up to my beefy JBL Boombox 4 (in a setup that TechRadar audio expert Matt Bolton once described as "insanity") blasting tunes as I work — right now Ano's single Kill Love. While the fidelity is obviously not quite as good as lossless streaming, there's simply nothing quite like the properly exploring a beautifully made physical album or the tactile sensation of popping in a new disc.
If you want to get your hands on this limited edition CD player, you can grab it online via the km5 website for $199 / £175 / AU$315, excluding shipping and any customs duties. That makes it about $40 / £40 / AU$60 more than the standard model. You might want to make haste though, as I expect it to sell out fast.

articles.title: Drone flyover reveals rapid progress at Elon Musk’s new ATCF chip fab — Texas site prepares for all-in-one logic, memory, and packaging facility
articles.text:
Drone flyover reveals rapid progress at Elon Musk’s new ATCF chip fab — Texas site prepares for all-in-one logic, memory, and packaging facility
Eyes in the sky confirm that ground work has 'hit another gear.'
Drone flyovers of Elon Musk’s new Advanced Technology Chip Fab (ATCF) in Texas have been shared on social media. The videos and photos come courtesy of flight instructor and drone videographer Joe Tegtmeyer (@JoeTegtmeyer), who regularly documents the progress of Giga Texas and Starbase projects. Considering that the fab was only announced on March 21 this year, groundwork has been brisk, and in a follow-up post, Tegtmeyer states progress has “hit another gear.”
In the above post, the all-things-space enthusiast notes that the ATCF already appears to be very well defined. “GeoPiers are at work on the part of the foundation that has had gravel mix placed on the top soil and more work grading on the south end,” he explains.
A few days later, there was an update with progress clearly accelerating, according to Tegtmeyer. As well as commenting on the shape of the facility becoming ever clearer and construction materials continuing to be stockpiled, there are other important signs of progress. Specifically, “4 new permits were filed in the past few days for the large trailer complex that houses the general contractors and the temporary Tesla offices for the new facility,” noted the enthusiast. “[It is] a great sign that things are progressing rapidly behind the scenes to fit out the facility when construction progresses far enough to allow for equipment installation.”
Importantly, Tegtmeyer reminds his followers that the ATCF is not the Terafab that will be built ~ 100 miles or so to the East in Grimes County, Texas. Rather, the ATCF is the equally vital but “smaller development facility that is the first part of the overall AI Chip development program.”
The ATCF is a joint Tesla–SpaceX facility, and is a keystone for the Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI accelerator chips to come. It is expected that chips from the ATCF will combine logic, memory, and advanced packaging under one roof. Projects spawned from here are destined to support Tesla cars and Robotaxis, Optimus robots, and upcoming Earth-orbiting AI data centers.
That’s distinct from the much larger, multi-phase, vertically integrated, 1TW/year Terafab megaproject, which will see collabs between Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, and Intel. It has massive AI computer production ambitions to feed terrestrial and space-based AI systems. We are still awaiting evidence that the Terafab has moved beyond the pre-construction phase.
If there were any doubt about the seriousness of Musk's semiconductor design and fabrication ambitions in these and other progress reports, ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet recently confirmed talks with Musk had taken place about building one of the largest chip manufacturing operations ever attempted. SpaceX has also already filed for a $55 billion facility in Grimes County, Texas, with potential expansion costs reaching $119 billion, and phase one potentially beginning before the end of the year. Meanwhile, it is good to see the rapid progress of the smaller ATCF.

articles.title: Lenovo ThinkStation P4: Professionelle Workstation für CAD, 3D und KI
articles.text:
Welche Workstation für CAD, 3D und lokale KI? Warum Lenovo ThinkStations die richtige Wahl sind
Ein 3D-Modell, das beim Drehen ruckelt. Eine Simulation, die erst nach der Mittagspause fertig ist. Ein Rendering, das den Rechner blockiert, während eigentlich schon die nächste Korrekturschleife ansteht.
Solche Momente kennt fast jedes Team, das mit großen Dateien, visuellen Projekten oder datenintensiven Anwendungen arbeitet. Oft beginnt hier die Auseinandersetzung mit der Frage, ob der Arbeitsplatz noch der Richtige ist. Für E-Mails, Browser, Office-Tools, Cloud-Dienste und Videocalls reicht ein Business-PC meist aus. Dafür braucht es nichts Spezielles, sondern ein stabiles, sicheres und gut verwaltbares System.
Nur bleibt es in vielen Unternehmen nicht dabei: Architekten arbeiten mit BIM-Modellen, Produktteams prüfen Varianten in 3D, Kreativteams rendern Visuals und KI-Funktionen wandern in Anwendungen. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 ist für solche CAD-, 3D- und KI-Workloads konzipiert.
CAD, BIM und 3D: Wenn der Rechner zum Flaschenhals wird
Der Unterschied zwischen einem guten Business-PC und einer Workstation zeigt sich, wenn die Arbeit ins Stocken gerät.
Wenn ein Team mehr Zeit mit Warten als mit Ausprobieren verbringt. Wenn Varianten nicht spontan getestet werden, weil die Berechnung zu lange dauert. Oder wenn kreative und technische Entscheidungen davon abhängen, ob gerade genug Rechenleistung verfügbar ist.
Einmal ist das nervig. Jeden Tag ist es ein Produktivitätsproblem. Bei Workstations müssen Prozessor, Grafikkarte, Arbeitsspeicher, Storage, Kühlung, Netzteil und Erweiterbarkeit auch unter Dauerlast zusammenspielen. Die leistungsstarke Lenovo ThinkStation P4 kombiniert Prozessoren der AMD Ryzen PRO 9000-Serie, eine professionelle NVIDIA RTX PRO Grafikkarte und bis zu 256 GB DDR5-Speicher. Für professionelle Anwendungen von Anbietern wie Autodesk, ANSYS, Dassault, PTC und Siemens liegen ISV-Zertifizierungen vor.
Rendering, Simulation und lokale KI: Warum lokale Leistung wichtiger wird
Lenovo ist ein globales Technologieunternehmen mit einem Umsatz von 83 Milliarden US-Dollar und entwickelt intelligente Technologien für Kunden in 180 Märkten. Das Portfolio reicht von PCs, Workstations, Smartphones und Tablets über Server, Speicher, Edge Computing und High Performance Computing bis hin zu Software, Lösungen und Services.
Ob ein Workflow in die Cloud passt, hängt von verschiedenen Faktoren ab. Große Projektdateien, sensible Daten, Latenzen oder laufende Nutzungskosten können es sinnvoll machen, mehr Leistung direkt am Arbeitsplatz bereitzustellen.
Bei Rendering, Simulation und lokaler KI-Inferenz zählt, wie schnell Ergebnisse verfügbar sind. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 lässt sich dafür mit einer NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition konfigurieren und erreicht dank der GPU eine KI-Rechenleistung von bis zu 4.000 TOPS. Für leistungsstärkere CPU-Optionen bis 170 Watt steht Flüssigkühlung zur Verfügung, um die Leistung auch unter anhaltender Last stabil zu halten. Damit auch die leistungsstärkste Grafikkarte jederzeit ausreichend versorgt ist, bietet Lenovo passende Netzteile mit 500, 750 oder 1.100 Watt an – je nach CPU- und GPU-Konfiguration.
Für IT-Teams heißt das: Manche Arbeitsplätze kommen mit klassischen Standard-PCs aus, andere wiederum benötigen deutlich mehr Leistung. Dank ihrer vielfältigen Konfigurationsmöglichkeiten lässt sich die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 an unterschiedliche professionelle Anforderungen und Einsatzszenarien anpassen.
Lenovo ThinkStation P4: Skalierbarer Einstieg in professionelle Workstation-Leistung
Bei Workstations denken viele sofort an große Tower, hochspezialisierte Fachabteilungen und sehr hohe Budgets. Das gibt es natürlich. Aber es ist nur ein Teil der Wahrheit.
In vielen Unternehmen liegt der Bedarf dazwischen: Mehr Leistung als ein Business-PC, aber kein überdimensioniertes High-End-System. Die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 bietet hier eine skalierbare Plattform für CAD, BIM, 3D, Rendering und lokale KI.
Spannend wird diese Mitte, wenn Workstation-Leistung für ganze Teams planbar werden muss und damit über den Bedarf einzelner Experten hinausgeht. Dann geht es weniger um das leistungsfähigste System – und mehr um eine Plattform, die genug Reserven bietet, sich sauber verwalten lässt und im Lebenszyklus wirtschaftlich bleibt.
Dann wird die Frage nach dem Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis entscheidend. Nicht die teuerste Workstation ist automatisch die beste Wahl, sondern die, die zum tatsächlichen Workflow passt.
Mit Lenovo ThinkStations skalierbar planen
Workloads wachsen selten ordentlich nach Plan. Projekte werden größer, Dateien schwerer, Visualisierungen detaillierter. KI-Funktionen ziehen in bestehende Anwendungen ein.
Für wachsende Workloads unterstützt die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 bis zu 48 TB Storage. PCIe Gen 5 und vier Erweiterungssteckplätze schaffen Reserven; Lenovo ThinkShield ergänzt die Plattform um Sicherheitsfunktionen auf Hardware- und Firmware-Ebene.
Lenovo deckt darüber hinaus die gesamte Bandbreite mit verschiedenen ThinkStation-Modellen ab – von kompakteren oder preisbewussteren Systemen wie der ThinkStation P3 über leistungsstärkere Modelle wie ThinkStation P5, P7 und P8 bis hin zur ThinkStation PX für besonders anspruchsvolle Workloads.
Seit Juni 2026 ergänzt die Lenovo ThinkStation P4 das Portfolio. Sie richtet sich an Fachleute in Architektur, Ingenieurwesen, Design und Content-Erstellung, die regelmäßig mit CAD, BIM, 3D, Rendering, Simulation oder lokaler KI-Inferenz arbeiten – besonders dort, wo Business-PCs an Grenzen stoßen, aber keine High-End-Workstation nötig ist.

articles.title: Design Arena creators raise $7.9 million to bring taste to AI models | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As co-founder Grace Li tells it, her company started a few weeks before graduation in 2025, with a handful of college friends trying to make their AI game engine work. The models could make functional games, but none of the games were fun — which raised the interesting question, how can you tell if a game will be fun?
There was no substitute for human judgment, they decided, and soon they were brainstorming ways to get honest human feedback at scale. The result became Design Arena, an AI tool now used by 5.3 million people around the world. As it turned out, there were lots of AI companies looking for scalable user feedback — and many of them were willing to pay for it.
“It was the missing bottleneck for a lot of these models to make improvements in the design space,” Li says. “About a week later, we closed our first major deal with a frontier lab, and the rest is kind of history.”
On Monday, the company behind Design Arena — dubbed Intelligence — announced a $7.9 million seed round led by Index Ventures with participation from Conviction (Sarah Guo and Mike Vernal), A*, Valkyrie, and others.
For non-enterprise users, using Design Arena is a lot like using a sophisticated model router. There’s a ChatGPT-style window for prompts, with separate dropdowns for websites, images, and a dozen other visual formats. Once you put in the request, format, and style, you’ll be presented with a series of “A vs. B” choices until you’ve ranked the handful of outputs from best to worst.
It’s a useful service, but the real value of the platform comes from the enterprise side, where participating models can treat it as a source of endless instant feedback for their media-generating models. The users tend to be indifferent to which models they’re ranking — as Li puts it, they just want the best output they can get — so their rankings can give critical input to what users really want.
For frontier labs, that’s a service worth paying for, Li says, adding the site is currently generating $60 million in ARR, solidifying its position as a key source of human-led evaluation data for the AI industry.
Crucially, users have to log in to get their output, so Intelligence can also track how those tastes change across different continents and over time. (Li notes that web dashboards in Asia tend to have a more maximalist design style.) These measures are an important complement to automated benchmarks, which can operate at a greater scale but are often subject to being gamed or otherwise manipulated, as the Hugging Face breach demonstrated in dramatic fashion last week.
That’s not to say that crowdsourced human feedback will be an automatic winning market. Less than a year after launching, Yupp shuttered its doors earlier this year after raising $33 million from a16z crypto’s Chris Dixon. It too nabbed some frontier models as customers and had, it said, over 1.3 million users, but still couldn’t build a sustainable long-term business.
Even so, other startups based on human evaluation seem to be thriving. LM Arena, which takes a similar approach to text-based responses, raised $150 million in a Series A in January, just four months after formally launching its paid product.

articles.title: Renesas Tackles Memory Bottleneck with MRDIMM Update - EE Times
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence data centers, cloud infrastructure, and accelerated compute workloads are the driving factors behind the development of Renesas Electronics’ latest DDR5 multiplexed rank dual in‑line memory module (MRDIMM) chipset.
“As AI training, AI inference, cloud computing, and HPC workloads continue to scale, processors are becoming increasingly limited by the rate at which data can be delivered from memory,” Allen Youssefi, director of product management for Renesas’s memory interface division, told EE Times in a briefing.
Renesas’s Gen 3 DDR5 MRDIMM chipset solutions deliver server-class speeds—up to 16,000 megatransfers per second (MT/s) and 25% higher memory bandwidth than the company’s Gen 2 chipsets. Youssefi said that because the latest iteration uses existing DDR5 infrastructure, server platforms can extract more performance without disruptive architectural changes.
Youssefi said this allows for scaling bandwidth without breaking the platform model that server OEMs already rely on. “MRDIMM uses the same DDR5 ecosystem and keeps the same standard mechanical and electrical interfaces,” he said. “The deployment largely becomes a platform validation exercise rather than a major redesign or hardware swap.”
Memory continues to be the primary bottleneck in AI and HPC systems, Youssefi said, as bandwidth improvements have not kept the same pace as the growth in compute capability. “Memory is becoming the constraint here rather than the compute capability itself.”
The impact of the memory bottleneck is compounded as data centers move from a training-centric AI cycle to the inference era. “These applications come with massive models, massive parameters, and data that require that memory,” Youssefi said.
During inference, latency directly affects the user experience, whether the task is unlocking a device, choosing a driver in a ride-hailing app, or serving real-time enterprise workloads. He said having these services available faster comes with infrastructure requirements. “That infrastructure depends on CPUs, GPUs, compute engines, machine learning models, and deep learning models that support inference.”
The transition to more inference-heavy AI comes at a time when performance per watt is a critical metric for data centers, which Youssefi said is another selling point of Renesas’s MRDIMM chipsets.
MRDIMM improves performance per watt by delivering much higher memory bandwidth with lower latency without requiring DRAM chips to run at higher speeds, he said. Because the DRAM does not have to be overclocked, the system can do more useful work at roughly the same memory power, Youssefi said.
Renesas’s release echoes that emphasis, saying Gen 3 was designed with system-level power efficiency in mind as customers balance higher bandwidth against thermal and power constraints. For semiconductor engineers, that combination of higher bandwidth and controlled power draw is likely the key design point, especially in AI servers where memory is often the limiting subsystem.
Renesas’s Gen 3 DDR5 MRDIMM chipset is a platform, not a single chip pair. Youssefi said the company’s portfolio is uniquely positioned to complete memory interface stack by MRCD, MDB, PMICs, SPD hubs, and temperature sensors.
Renesas is not the only company tackling the memory bottleneck with DIMM technology. Rambus recently announced its DDR5 9600 Server RDIMM chipset built around its new Rambus 6th Generation Registering Clock Driver (RCD06). The chipset is claimed to deliver a 20% increase in bandwidth over the previous generation, enabling RDIMMs operating at up to 9,600 MT/s.
Like Renesas, Rambus is looking to improve bandwidth and capacity to support agentic AI, HPC, and other data-intensive workloads.
Youssefi said this kind of incremental but architectural bandwidth gain may prove more valuable than a wholesale platform redesign if AI and HPC demand continues to rise as expected. “Memory bandwidth has become one of the most important constraints in AI, HPC, and cloud computing environments.”

articles.title: Box-office : Spider-Man détrône Avengers Endgame et signe un démarrage historique
articles.text:
Box-office : Spider-Man détrône Avengers Endgame et signe un démarrage historique
Tout simplement énorme. Le film Spider-Man : Brand New Day vient de faire un lancement colossal au box-office américain et mondial, générant déjà presque un milliard de dollars et battant le record d'Avengers : Endgame.
Oubliez Batman et Superman : Spider-Man est bel et bien le super-héros le plus populaire au monde, et ce week-end l'a une nouvelle fois prouvé. Le tout nouveau film Spider-Man : Brand New Day vient en effet de réaliser un démarrage hallucinant dans les salles de cinéma mondiales, totalisant déjà près d'un milliard de dollars en à peine cinq jours. On fait le point.
Spidey plus fort que les Avengers
Commençons par les États-Unis, où la dernière aventure de l'homme-araignée a enregistré 360 millions de dollars lors de ses trois premiers jours d'exploitation, plus les avant-premières du jeudi soir. Ce score colossal est tout simplement le meilleur démarrage de tous les temps en Amérique du Nord, juste devantAvengers : Endgame et ses 357,1 millions.
Le film offre de fait son plus gros lancement au studio Sony et à la franchise Spider-Man, battant largement le précédent record de Spider-Man : No Way Home (260,1 millions), et bien sûr les scores de Spider-Man 3 (151,1 millions), Spider-Man : Across the Spider-Verse (120,6 millions), Homecoming (117 millions), Far From Home (92,5 millions) et du tout premier Spider-Man (114,8 millions).
Comme si ça ne suffisait pas, ce plébiscite américain atteint une autre dimension à l'international où le film ajoute pas moins de 572 millions grâce à 73 500 écrans venus de 66 pays. Si vous êtes forts en calcul mental, vous comprendrez donc que Spider-Man : Brand New Day enregistre un cumul monde de 932 milllions de dollars... en seulement cinq petits jours dans les salles obscures. Historique, on vous dit.
À ce rythme, Spider-Man : Brand New Day devrait dépasser la barre du milliard d'ici mardi, et vise une fin de carrière parmi les plus massives de l'Histoire, au-delà des 2 milliards de dollars. Il devrait ainsi détrôner Star Wars VII (2,07 milliards), Titanic (2,264 milliards), Ne Zha 2 (2,270 milliards) et Avatar 2 (2,334 milliards), et peut même rêver d'aller chercher Avengers : Endgame (2,8 milliards) et Avatar (2,9 milliards). Bien sûr, tout cela ne prend pas en compte l'inflation.
Le reste du box-office ne se porte pas si mal que ça, puisque L'Odyssée glane encore 51 millions de dollars pour porter son cumul US près des 400 millions, et son total monde pas loin du milliard. Le film de Christopher Nolan devrait passer cette barre symbolique d'ici ce week-end et devenir le plus gros succès en salles du réalisateur en fin de carrière, passant devant The Dark Knight Rises (1,082 milliard).
On notera également le joli maintien de Toy Story 5, qui s'accroche à la troisième place pour sa septième semaine d'exploitation. Le film deviendra le plus gros succès de la franchise Pixar d'ici ce week-end. De l'autre côté, le remake live action de Vaiana coule un peu plus, et aura du mal à dépasser les 300 millions dans le monde. Le bide du film Disney est confirmé.

articles.title: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the foldable phone for people who never thought they’d want one
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a shot in the arm for the foldables market. Samsung has adapted familiar elements to make a phone that's ready to fit your lifestyle with its practical size, excellent screens, and plenty of software and performance potential. It’s still costly, and the lack of some features seems extra disappointing given the price, but what’s here gels together in a wonderfully cohesive way.
Pros
- +Easily pocketable design that can still open into a tablet-sized device
- +Attractive displays
- +Fun and useful software/AI tools
Cons
- -Expensive
- -No telephoto camera
Why you can trust TechRadar
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8: Two-minute review
It’s high praise that one of my biggest problems with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is that I wish it had a different name.
The fact that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has taken up the mantle of the Galaxy Z Fold 7 and all previous Galaxy Z Fold models is a little confusing. But titles aside, what Samsung has actually done here with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 — that is, build a new kind of foldable for a new kind of audience — deserves recognition, and I'm glad the South Korean giant has once again moved the category forward in a meaningful way.
Ideal Galaxy Z Fold 8 users are those focused on mobile entertainment and exploring new ideas with a pair of screens that Samsung has shaped specifically for watching video and reading, respectively.
While the phone is still technically capable, with an excellent chipset, plenty of memory, and strong battery and charging specs, it’s being sold more on its everyday use cases — and convincingly so.
In one way, it’s going to be hard to judge how good the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is until we get the long-rumored foldable iPhone, which is going to be the second (and perhaps more important) passport-style foldable to hit Western markets. But what I can say right now, looking at the Galaxy Z Fold 8 itself and the wider foldable phone and Android phone markets, is that this mid-sized foldable may herald a new generation of folding phones. I just wish it wasn’t so expensive.
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Price and availability
- From $1,899 in the US
- From £1,699 in the UK
- From $2,699 in Australia
Starting at $1,899 /£1,699 / AU$2,699, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is currently in its pre-order phase; it'll hit shelves on August 7.
These prices put the phone in between the Galaxy Z Flip 8 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra in terms of cost, and it's cheaper than the Galaxy Z Fold 7, which retailed for $1,999.99 / £1,799 / AU$2,899 at launch.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Samsung releasing a cheaper book-style foldable is absolutely a good thing, but the small price difference between the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra makes the former seem a little too keenly-priced.
That said, excluding the Huawei Pura X — which is hard to get in the West and requires some fiddling to get working with familiar Google services — and the as-yet-unnannounced iPhone Ultra, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the only representative of this size of foldable you can easily buy right now.
Hopefully future discounts will make this phone more affordable, but right now, it seems like Samsung’s charging a little uniqueness tax on top of what the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is truly worth.

Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Specs
These are the key specs of the Galaxy Z Fold 8:

| OS: | Android 17 with One UI 9 | 
| Cameras: | 50MP wide (f/1.8), 50MP ultra-wide (f/1.9) | 
| Selfie Cameras: | 10MP (f/2.2) inner, 10MP (f/2.2) outer | 
| Battery: | 4,800mAh | 
| Charging: | 45W wired, 20W wireless | 
| Colors: | Lavender, Graphite, Cream, Mint (Samsung Store exclusive) | 
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Design
- Compact and light for a “big” folding phone
- Outer and inner screens equally useful
When open, the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s 7.6-inch screen resembles a typical foldable phone, with a few exceptions.
It’s easier to handle, with its 201g weight making it lighter than any other book-style foldable, while the phone's 4.5mm thickness also contributes to it feeling like a small tablet. The minimal crease, while not as invisible as the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s, is barely a distraction unless you happen to catch the light in a particular way, and it's only noticeable to the touch when you’re trying to look for it.
With its slightly rectangular open shape, the Z Fold 8 is much more similar in size and form to an iPad (specifically, the iPad mini) or ereader than most foldables, which tend towards a square shape. And while being square can have its advantages, I have really fallen for the Z Fold 8’s design during my testing time.
While working on this review, I often turned the Z Fold 8 vertically for a physical document-style view of my work. You get almost double the number of lines in Google Docs with the keyboard open as you do with the Fold 8 in its regular orientation, while the keyboard remains split for easier typing. As a result, the Z Fold 8 is now my favorite device without a physical keyboard to write on, even though Samsung considers the Z Fold 8 Ultra to be the top choice for anyone wanting to get serious work done.
However, I also found myself less inclined to open the Z Fold 8 than I have been with other book-style foldables. The phone's outer 5.5-inch screen is perfect for one-handed use of fully-sized apps, which isn't a given even on standard bar-shaped phones today.
To alleviate any (understandable) durability concerns about folding phones, Samsung has rated the Galaxy Z Fold 8 as IP48 for dust and water resistance, which means it's as well-protected against water as any other flagship phone.
The '4' in that designation means no foreign objects above 1mm in size will worm their way into the Galaxy Z Fold 8's inner components, though other foldables — namely the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold and the Honor Magic V6 — offer superior IP68 dust protection.
There’s also Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 on the display and Victus 2 on the back to avoid scratches or serious cracks, plus a Flex Titanium layer under the main display, which makes the most vulnerable part of the Z Fold 8 tougher.
Rounding off these impressive design credentials is a quartet of appealing color options: the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is available in Lavender (pictured in this review), Graphite, Cream, and the Samsung Store-exclusive Pistachio.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Displays
- High-quality screens inside and out
- Display brightness could still be higher
The Galaxy Z Fold 8's 7.6-inch main display and 5.5-inch cover display have been crafted by Samsung to help you enjoy whatever kind of content you’re into.
The phone's outer screen has a video-friendly 16:10 aspect ratio, while its inner panel uses a more spacious, practical 4:3 ratio that's best suited to reading (though this inner panel is also better suited to widescreen video than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's square-shaped equivalent). We've compared the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's screen sizes elsewhere on TechRadar so you can visualize the difference between the two.
Both screens are detailed and colorful, which is no great surprise — Samsung is one of the best, if not the best, mobile display manufacturers in the world.
That said, despite a high brightness rating of 3,000 nits, the Galaxy Z Fold 8's screen readability can be a problem when using the phone in direct sunlight, even with the Extra brightness setting enabled.
Still, the low-reflection coating on the phone's inside screen makes some difference. It’s not as effective as the one you get on the Galaxy S26 Ultra or Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 definitely softens reflections better than most standard phones, making it easier to see what's on screen.
- Display score: 4 / 5
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Software
- The latest Galaxy AI features with foldable-specific upgrades
- A mix of fun features, like My FanCam, and practical ones, like Multi-Window
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 runs on One UI 9, which is based on Android 17. It’s quite different from other Android skins, which hew closer to Google’s original design, but it’s still one of the best options around in terms of adaptation to foldable phones.
Several of Samsung’s software features have been adapted for the Z Fold 8 series, specifically, including Now Nudge. These small, discreet but helpful prompts suggest what app or action you might want to use next depending on what’s on screen, and offer to open a split-screen view on your behalf.
For AI fans, Samsung has expanded task automation for select apps, assuming you’re in the US, UK, or South Korea, where this feature is currently enabled. These automations don’t work all that fast, but assuming your prompt is understood correctly, the Z Fold 8’s AI will work through your request until you decide to take back control, or when it alerts you when it’s time to intervene to finalize a booking or order.
My FanCam, meanwhile, lets you create a motion-tracked video of a particular subject from any video (from your photo gallery, YouTube, or anywhere else). I have not made a fancam before, so I don’t know how well this sort of software — which is popular among K-pop fans — works elsewhere, but Samsung’s version is relatively effective, albeit with some major limitations.
Making a My FanCam clip is easy: just open the AI tools menu with the video you want to use in the Gallery app, tap the relevant icon, then tap your subject. After some processing time, depending on the size of the original clip, you have your tracked footage. But after trying the feature with a number of videos, two problems appeared.
First, the subject needs to be large enough in the frame. Even if you have high-resolution 4K footage, you need to crop in before My FanCam will detect them. Similarly, they need to be well-lit — I tried to use a clip of a dance troupe moving around in dramatic stage lighting, and My FanCam simply would not work.
Since there is no manual tracking option you can use, you are at the mercy of Samsung’s algorithms as to whether your footage is compatible.
As for multitasking, although it’s not as much of a focus on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 as it is on the Z Fold 8 Ultra, I still appreciate Samsung’s updates to its Multi-Window system, which lets you use two or more apps at once. The Z Fold 8 and its sibling now let you use three apps side-by-side vertically or horizontally, as well as via the older splitting method, which sees one app taking up half the screen and the other two taking a quarter each.
Multi-Window is still not as versatile as the windowed system you now find on many tablets and rival foldables, but if you’re cross-referencing without wanting to make too many edits to what you’re looking at, it certainly avoids the need to open your laptop from time to time, which makes the Galaxy Z Fold 8 a valuable productivity companion.
- Software score: 4 / 5
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Cameras
- No telephoto camera at this price feels unfair
- But cameras that *are* present perform well
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has the undistinguished position of having the highest relative price per camera of any Samsung phone. Unlike the Z Fold 8 Ultra, there’s no telephoto camera to speak of here, although at least the cameras you do get are of good quality. Specifically, there are 50MP main and ultra-wide lenses on the back, plus 10MP selfie cameras embedded in the phone's cover and inner displays.
Samsung’s camera processing has made an important step forward in recent years, going from exaggerated colors to more natural ones, matching the vibe of other flagship smartphone cameras. That’s why, even in the intense sunlight that was slowly melting me during my photo trip to Beckenham Place Park, we still get attractive-looking trees, grass, sky and brickwork.

Samsung’s 50MP main camera offers 2x in-sensor zoom for a little extra reach when you need it without compromising on image quality. The Camera app also offers presets for 4x and 10x (the latter is the maximum available digital zoom), although the image quality deteriorates, as you’d expect.

For selfies, the 10MP cameras on the inside and outside of the phone are identical, and therefore equally competent. You’re also free to open the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and switch the preview to the outer screen for hi-res or ultra-wide selfies — perhaps one of the most underrated abilities of foldable phones.
Portrait mode on Samsung phones is a particular strength, as it can cut accurately around glasses where other phones struggle. These examples show that the Z Fold 8 hasn’t missed out on this ability.
Video maxes out at 8K/30fps, or 4K/60fps if you need your extra frames. Samsung’s videography party trick from the Galaxy S26 series — Super Steady video with Horizontal Lock — has also made it to the Z Fold 8 series.
This feature levels out shaky footage at the expense of some resolution. It does a fantastic job, though, as you can see in these samples of me running along a path (the first is the original footage, the second is the edited footage).
Overall, while it would be nice if Samsung had given the Z Fold 8 a telephoto camera, what’s here works well. And since this phone is designed to appeal to a more casual user, there’s a reasonable chance that anyone interested in the Z Fold 8 won’t mind the compromise.
- Camera score: 3 / 5
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Performance
- Top-performing chipset with plenty of memory, even by default
- Great for games, even with below-par benchmark scores
The Z Fold 8 contains the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset, which is the best version of the best silicon currently available in an Android phone. The scores I got in my own benchmarking tests are a little lower than I would have anticipated, but they're impressive nonetheless, and prove that the Z Fold 8 is absolutely a performance powerhouse.
Indeed, this top-end chipset proved its worth while I tested several games on the Galaxy Z Fold 8. Destiny Rising, set to its highest graphical setting and 60fps, ran perfectly smoothly. Similarly, Asphalt Legends at its full high quality/120fps settings proved no challenge for the Z Fold 8.
Under the hood, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 features 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage by default, but you can spec the device up to 512GB if you wish. There’s also a 1TB model, which gets a RAM bump to 16GB, though whether this upgrade is worth the money will depend entirely on how intensively you use your phone.

Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 review: Battery
- The phone can last a surprisingly long time if you use the inner screen sparingly
- Charging isn’t the fastest, but it's definitely quick enough when you need it
Despite being smaller than last year’s Galaxy Z Fold 7, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 packs a larger-capacity battery — specifically 4,800mAh versus 4,400mAh. That’s thanks to Samsung finally adopting industry-leading silicon-carbon battery technology, which boasts higher energy density than the lithium-ion technology used by Samsung (and indeed most other Western phone manufacturers) in its previous batteries.
Samsung’s battery estimate claims you can get 26 hours of video playback from a single charge of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 — and I’m inclined to believe that, if you stick to the cover screen. In my light to moderate mixed usage of the phone during testing, switching between screens, enabling the always-on display and leaving the phone off charge overnight, I would get between a day and a day and a half between plug-ins.
Samsung is using its best 45W wired and 20W wireless charging options on the Z Fold 8 series, which, while slower than some rival devices, is still an upgrade on previous Z Folds. Using a compatible third-party charger, I was able to fill the Z Fold 8 to 43% in 15 minutes, and to 100% in 1 hour and 5 minutes.
In other words, you wouldn’t want to forget to charge this phone overnight, given the below-average battery life, but if you do, it won’t take long to get a usable amount of charge in an emergency.
- Battery score: 3 / 5
Should you buy the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8?
Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Not as costly as some foldables, but still expensive. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | Perfectly sized whether open or closed, plus strong protection against common sources of damage. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Displays | All your content looks great inside and out, with low-reflection tech to help in bright light. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Software | Whether you're focused on productivity or entertainment, the Z Fold 8 has features to help. | 4.5 / 5 |

Buy it if...
Traditional folding phones or flip phones haven’t appealed to you yet
Sitting between the two sizes of foldable phones we've become familiar with, the Z Fold 8 is fully functional whether you’ve got it open or closed. 
You like the idea of a small phone combined with a mini tablet
When closed, no phone on the market is as small and as usable as the Galaxy Z Fold 8. And when it’s open, it’s like you’ve pulled an iPad mini or a Kindle out of nowhere.
You want the best software available on a foldable
Samsung has been making folding phones the longest out of any brand, and that shows in how well its software adapts and works with the Z Fold 8’s hardware. And that’s not even mentioning the Galaxy AI tools that few other phones can match up to.
Don't buy it if...
You want a complete, well-priced phone experience
For the price of the Z Fold 8, you could instead buy a fully-specced Galaxy S26 Ultra or similar flagship phone, which will more than make up for its lack of hinge with other features.
Battery life is a deal-breaker
Battery life isn’t too bad on the Z Fold 8, but only in terms of other foldable phones. Stick to a regular-shaped phone if you want the best possible endurance.
The camera limitations will bother you
Spending well over 1,500 of your local currency on a phone that lacks a telephoto camera is a big ask, even if such a compromise becomes the standard for this size of foldable phone.

This is currently our best flip-style foldable pick, and it might be the better device for you if you're looking for a foldable that can go the distance with its battery, and don’t mind only having a standard-sized phone screen when you open it up.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
Considering the minimal price difference, you might be better off saving a little extra money and getting the full-fat fold experience with more screen space, a telephoto camera, and a longer-lasting battery. The Z Fold 8 Ultra isn't as well-suited to video, though.

articles.title: Cómo ver Las Guerreras K-pop en Español Latino en Android y iPhone de forma legal y sin virus
articles.text:
Para quienes buscan ver Las Guerreras K-pop en sus celulares Android o iPhone, la alternativa más segura y libre de riesgos informáticos sigue siendo la aplicación oficial de Netflix.
El interés por acceder a contenidos de cine y televisión en español latino ha impulsado la aparición de muchas opciones en línea, pero no todas garantizan la protección de los usuarios ni de sus dispositivos.
PUBLICIDAD
Según el Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (INCIBE), instalar aplicaciones fuera de las tiendas oficiales puede exponer los teléfonos a amenazas como el robo de información personal, la pérdida de archivos o la manipulación remota del dispositivo.
Por esta razón, la única vía segura para ver Las Guerreras K-pop sin virus es utilizar la app oficial de Netflix disponible en Google Play y App Store. Esta plataforma cuenta con controles de calidad y seguridad que no están presentes en sitios o aplicaciones de procedencia dudosa.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué elegir la app de Netflix para ver Las Guerreras K-pop en español latino
Netflix es una opción útil para acceder a estrenos internacionales, incluida la película Las Guerreras K-pop, en español latino y otros idiomas. A través de su aplicación, disponible tanto para Android como para iPhone, los usuarios pueden ver contenidos de manera legal, con garantía de calidad y sin interrupciones por publicidad invasiva o riesgos técnicos.
Una de las mayores ventajas de usar Netflix reside en que la app pasa por rigurosos controles de seguridad antes de estar disponible para su descarga. Esto protege a los usuarios de virus, troyanos y aplicaciones fraudulentas que suelen camuflarse como servicios streaming gratuitos.
PUBLICIDAD
El sistema de actualizaciones automáticas, además, permite que tanto el contenido como la propia aplicación se mantengan protegidos frente a vulnerabilidades recién detectadas.
Qué riesgos hay al instalar aplicaciones piratas para ver películas
El uso de aplicaciones no oficiales o tiendas alternativas puede acarrear consecuencias graves. El INCIBE advierte que una app maliciosa puede acceder a datos personales, desde fotografías y contactos hasta contraseñas bancarias y mensajes privados.
PUBLICIDAD
En casos de infección por ransomware, los archivos personales quedan bloqueados y se exige un pago para recuperarlos. Otro de los riesgos descritos por el instituto es la instalación de keyloggers, programas que registran pulsaciones en la pantalla y pueden capturar contraseñas o códigos de seguridad.
Además, algunas aplicaciones solicitan permisos excesivos, como leer los SMS recibidos, lo que facilita la interceptación de códigos de autenticación y la confirmación de transacciones sin el consentimiento del usuario.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son las ventajas de utilizar aplicaciones legales de streaming
Optar por aplicaciones legales como Netflix o plataformas reconocidas garantiza que el usuario accede a contenidos verificados, libres de malware y en calidad óptima.
Las tiendas oficiales, como Google Play o App Store, implementan sistemas automáticos y revisiones humanas para identificar y eliminar aplicaciones dañinas antes de que lleguen a los usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, al recurrir a servicios legales el usuario puede gestionar los permisos de la aplicación, acceder a soporte técnico y contar con actualizaciones periódicas que incluyen mejoras de seguridad.
El INCIBE sugiere leer las valoraciones de otros usuarios y expertos antes de instalar cualquier app, lo que ayuda a identificar posibles inconvenientes.
Qué medidas de protección sugieren los expertos para ver películas en el celular
El INCIBE sugiere descargar siempre las aplicaciones desde las tiendas oficiales. Google Play y App Store implementan políticas estrictas contra el malware y eliminan rápidamente las aplicaciones peligrosas para los usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
Los expertos aconsejan mantener el sistema operativo actualizado y utilizar soluciones antivirus confiables para detectar amenazas, sumado a realizar copias de seguridad periódicas. En caso de infección, daño o robo del dispositivo, disponer de un respaldo permite recuperar información.
Los organismos de ciberseguridad sugieren consultar fuentes confiables y expertos antes de instalar nuevas aplicaciones, sobre todo si prometen acceso gratuito a contenidos exclusivos.

articles.title: Lexar lists 32GB DDR5 memory with homegrown Chinese chips — 3,999 Yuan ($592) price undercuts hopes for cheaper CXMT-powered RAM
articles.text:
Lexar lists 32GB DDR5 memory with homegrown Chinese chips — 3,999 Yuan ($592) price undercuts hopes for cheaper CXMT-powered RAM
High-speed DDR5 with Chinese DRAM.
Storage and memory manufacturer Lexar has listed a new 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-7200 CL38 memory kit in China with a price tag of 3,999 yuan (roughly $592). Part of the second-generation Thor RGB series, the kit features a sandblasted aluminum heat spreader, thermal pads, and eight LEDs that support a variety of RGB lighting effects. It is rated for 38-48-48-86 timings at 1.40V and supports both Intel XMP 3.0 and AMD EXPO profiles.
Lexar says the modules use carefully selected domestically produced DRAM, although it does not specify the actual manufacturer. While there is no confirmation, the company may be using DRAM chips made by CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies). Lexar has also published a compatibility list covering 43 motherboards, including 30 Asus models and 13 MSI models across Intel Z890, Intel B860, and AMD B850 platforms. The compatibility list also includes supported boards for a faster 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-7600 CL38 memory kit.
Interestingly, none of AMD's X870 or previous-generation motherboards appear on the list. That said, the kit should work on most DDR5 boards that Lexar hasn't tested, but the absence of AMD's flagship consumer chipset from the compatibility list is a bit odd. Notably, major motherboard manufacturers, including MSI and Gigabyte, have already started optimizing their motherboards to support CXMT memory ICs.
A few months ago, Corsair began adopting CXMT DDR5 chips in select memory kits, including its popular Vengeance lineup. Likewise, major PC manufacturers such as HP and Dell have started qualifying CXMT DRAM, while Acer and Asus have reportedly asked their Chinese manufacturing partners to source locally made memory chips.
The arrival of CXMT-made DDR5 chips earlier this year raised hopes that a new DRAM supplier could ease supply constraints and eventually lower memory prices. So far, there seems to be little evidence of that happening. At around $592, Lexar's new DDR5-7200 kit is priced in line or only slightly below many comparable 32GB DDR5-7200 kits currently available in the U.S. Similar kits from brands such as G.Skill, Corsair, and Kingston are currently selling anywhere from $585 to $700.

articles.title: La stratégie futée de David Ellison pour sauver la fusion Paramount-Warner : le bras de fer est lancé
articles.text:
Bloquée en pleine débâcle judiciaire, la fusion à 111 milliards de dollars entre Paramount et Warner Bros. Discovery se joue désormais devant un tribunal fédéral. Et pour sauver son deal, David Ellison prépare une contre-offensive tous azimuts… Quitte à jouer gros.
Après une longue traque, le patron de Paramount a réussi à imposer son offre hostile sur Warner Bros. Discovery, qui s'était pourtant entendue avec Netflix. Mais cette fusion ne fait pas l’unanimité. Une coalition de 12 États américains, menée par la Californie a porté plainte à la mi-juillet pour bloquer l’opération, jugée trop dangereuse pour la concurrence. L’acquisition est suspendue depuis, et se dirige tout droit vers un procès ô combien explosif, dont les enjeux ont été révélés par une vaste enquête du Wall Street Journal.
Chaque semaine compte
Car le P.-D. G de Paramount, David Ellison, préfère aller jusqu’au tribunal plutôt que de négocier. Un pari potentiellement très coûteux : si l’accord n’est pas finalisé d’ici au 30 septembre, la firme devra verser 650 millions de dollars par trimestre à Warner, soit environ 7 millions par jour. Pire encore, passé juin 2027 sans deal définitif, la facture grimpera à 7 milliards de dollars de pénalité de rupture.
C’est tout l’enjeu du bras de fer qui se joue actuellement sur le calendrier du procès. Paramount exige que celui-ci début le 4 novembre, quand les procureurs généraux des États plaignants poussent pour le 5 avril, soit 5 mois plus tard. Une décision du juge est attendue dans les prochains jours et elle constituera déjà un bon indicateur de vers qui la balance penche.
- moodRemboursement sous 30 jours
- devices2 connexions simultanées
- live_tvQualité vidéo : Full HD
- downloadLecture hors ligne disponible
- escalator_warningEspace enfant disponible
Concessions et pression politique
En interne chez Paramount, plusieurs dirigeants estiment que la plainte est en réalité motivée par des divergences politiques : le père de David Ellison, Larry Ellison, est un proche de Donald Trump, tandis que tous les États impliqués sont à majorité démocrate. Selon l’un des avocats de l’entreprise, l’objectif inavoué de la procédure serait d’empêcher la famille Ellison de mettre la main sur CNN, chaîne régulièrement ciblée par le président.
Dans ce contexte, Paramount entend convaincre certains États de la coalition de se retirer, et a recruté l’avocate Beth Wilkinson, artisane de la victoire de Microsoft face aux autorités dans le rachat d’Activision Blizzard, pour y parvenir. Ellison envisage même, en dernier recours, de délocaliser une partie de ses activités hors de Californie. Cette option ne réglerait rien sur le plan juridique, mais sonnerait comme un désaveu cinglant envers l’État qui l’attaque.
Signe qu’il continue d’y croire, le patron ne relâche pas la pression sur l’intégration des deux groupes, qui se poursuit en coulisses. Dans un mémo adressé à ses équipes, il n’a d’ailleurs laissé planer aucun doute sur sa détermination : l’accord a été validé dans 65 juridictions à travers le monde, un gage, selon lui, qu'il ne pose aucun problème de concurrence.

articles.title: Henry Cavill annonce que Mike Flanagan écrit la série Warhammer 40,000, mais garde son rôle secret
articles.text:
Quand on parle de l’adaptation de l’univers Warhammer 40,000 en film et série, Henry Cavill, immense passionné, n’est jamais très loin. Dans une publication Instagram datant du 3 août 2026, il a pris la parole pour commenter les rumeurs et les informations partagées ces derniers jours. Son objectif est simple : confirmer une bonne fois pour toutes les points discutés précédemment.
Comme découvert dans les derniers résultats financiers de Games Workshop, Mike Flanagan est bien de la partie. « Nous travaillons déjà avec lui sur la création, et nous faisons des progrès considérables au niveau de l’histoire. Comme les fans s’en doutent, c’est un sacré morceau, mais le talent extraordinaire de Mike nous aide à lui donner forme », indique le comédien. Il confirme aussi le deal avec United Artists, qu’Henry Cavill connaît bien grâce à Highlander.
Que jouera Henry Cavill dans l’adaptation live action de Warhammer 40,000 ? Secret défense
Henry Cavill en profite pour confirmer la mise en chantier d’un autre projet : une série d’animation centrée sur la Deathwatch et qui sera un dérivé de la deuxième saison de l’anthologie Secret Level. Dans l’univers de Warhammer 40,000, la Deathwatch est une unité de l’Imperium spécialisée dans l’élimination des menaces extraterrestres. Dave Wilson reprendra du service et est adoubé par Henry Cavill : « Il pilote le projet et nous appuyons son travail colossal pour garantir la cohérence avec le plan d’ensemble de l’univers. »
Enfin, Henry Cavill a abordé son cas personnel, puisqu’il ne fait pas que chapeauter cette constellation de projets. Outre sa casquette de producteur, il enfilera son costume plus habituel d’acteur dans la série écrite par Mike Flanagan et à destination de la plateforme Amazon Prime Video. Et si certains fans en doutaient, ce sera toujours le cas. Il confie à ce sujet : « Petit point important : vous avez été plusieurs à me demander si j’allais toujours tenir le rôle principal dans la série TV en prise de vues réelles — soyez rassurés, ce sera tout à fait le cas ! En revanche, l’identité de ce personnage restera un secret pour le moment ! »
Henry Cavill refuse de donner davantage de précision, sans doute par crainte de spoiler tout ou partie de l’histoire. En donnant le nom du personnage qu’il incarnera, il serait sans doute facile de deviner certains événements que couvrira la série. C’est aussi une forme de teasing qui amène de la spéculation, sachant que le champ des possibles est immense avec un univers comme Warhammer 40,000. L’évidence pointerait vers le chapitre des Ultramarines — les soldats les plus connus et déjà adaptés (récemment dans l’excellent jeu vidéo Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 — mais nous ne sommes pas à l’abri d’une surprise.

Celular com Snapdragon: 11 modelos com chip da Qualcomm para comprar em 2026
Encontre o melhor celular com processador Snapdragon para comprar no Brasil; chips são conhecidos pelo bom desempenho do segmento básico ao avançado
Celulares com Snapdragon são frequentemente buscados por consumidores que desejam desempenho alto, 5G estável e boa eficiência energética em 2026. O melhor modelo depende de detalhes do processador, como CPU, litografia e velocidade de cada núcleo.
Para além do chip da Qualcomm, o smartphone deve ter componentes que atendam a outras necessidades de uso, como tela OLED, bateria de longa duração, câmeras avançadas e uma boa política de atualizações.
Este guia reúne 11 celulares Snapdragon para comprar em 2026, do topo de linha ao intermediário barato. Compare os modelos, veja os pontos fortes e escolha o smartphone ideal para jogos, fotos, produtividade ou custo-benefício.
O Galaxy S26 Ultra traz o processador Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy de 3 nanômetros, com 12 GB ou 16 GB de RAM e armazenamento de até 1 TB. O chip usa uma arquitetura com núcleos customizados Oryon Gen 3 (dois principais de até 4,74 GHz e seis de desempenho até 3,6 GHz), GPU Adreno 840 e NPU Hexagon para IA no dispositivo.
Nos testes do Tecnoblog, o smartphone se saiu bem em jogos, multitarefa, edição de vídeo e inteligência artificial.
O conjunto traseiro traz lente principal de 200 MP com OIS. Outro destaque vai para a tela: painel AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,9 polegadas, 120 Hz, com filtro de privacidade nativo via hardware.
O Motorola Signature traz o processador Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 (3 nm), com até 16 GB de RAM e 1 TB de armazenamento. O chipset tem CPU octa-core Oryon V3 Phoenix (2×3,8 GHz e 6×3,32 GHz), GPU Adreno 840 e NPU Hexagon, para os recursos de processamento de imagem do Moto AI.
Apesar de não usar a versão Elite do chip da Qualcomm, o celular demonstrou alto desempenho em nossa análise prática, rodando jogos como Genshin Impact sem travamentos com gráficos em qualidade máxima.
O conjunto fotográfico traseiro é triplo com sensores da Sony de 50 MP (principal com OIS, ultrawide e telefoto periscópica). A tela é um painel AMOLED LTPO de 6,8 polegadas com taxa de atualização de 165 Hz, que entrega boa fluidez, contrastes intensos e cores vivas.
O Galaxy S25 Ultra e os demais celulares da linha S25 (base, Plus e S25 Edge) usam o processador Snapdragon 8 Elite (3 nm). No Ultra, a CPU Oryon tem dois núcleos de 4,47 GHz e seis de 3,53 GHz, combinada à GPU Adreno 830, que traz ganho de frequência em relação à versão padrão do chip.
Trata-se de um ótimo smartphone para quem deseja alto desempenho sem pagar o preço do topo de linha atual.
O celular traz câmera principal de 200 MP com OIS, ultrawide de 50 MP, lente teleobjetiva de 10 MP e periscópica de 50 MP. A tela de 6,8 polegadas tem vidro antirreflexo Gorilla Armor. A bateria é de 5.000 mAh com carregamento de 45 W, com estrutura em titânio e certificação IP68.
O Galaxy Z Fold 8 traz o processador Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 (3 nm), versões com até 16 GB de RAM e até 1 TB de armazenamento interno. Esse chip tem dois núcleos de 4,74 GHz e seis de 3,62 GHz, além de uma GPU Adreno 840 para execução de múltiplas tarefas e NPU Hexagon da Qualcomm.
A tela principal é um painel AMOLED de 7,6 polegadas com taxa de atualização adaptativa de até 120 Hz; a secundária tem 5,5 polegadas e a mesma tecnologia . As câmeras traseiras incluem apenas dois sensores de 50 MP (principal e ultra-angular), com câmera frontal de 10 MP em cada uma das telas.
A compra faz sentido para quem valoriza produtividade acima de câmeras e preço. O custo costuma ser alto, mas a experiência de tela dobrável ainda é única entre celulares Android premium.
O Galaxy Z Fold 7 continua relevante em 2026 para quem quer celular dobrável premium pagando menos que no modelo mais novo.
O aparelho é movido pelo processador Snapdragon 8 Elite (3 nm), combinado a 12 GB ou 16 GB de RAM. São oito núcleos de processamento (dois de 4,32 GHz e seis de 3,53 GHz), além de uma GPU Adreno 830. O conjunto se traduz em alto desempenho, garantindo fluidez em multitarefa, jogos e modo DeX.
Enquanto a tela principal tem 8 polegadas, a secundária tem 6,5″, ambas com 120 Hz de taxa de atualização e tecnologia LTPO AMOLED 2X. O conjunto de câmeras traseiras traz o sensor principal de 200 MP, mas a estrutura do celular tem certificação IP48 para resistência contra água.
O Realme GT 7 Pro também traz o processador Snapdragon 8 Elite, até 16 GB de RAM e máximo de 1 TB de armazenamento. A CPU Oryon trabalha com oito núcleos (2x 4,32 GHz e 6x 3,53 GHz Oryon V2 Phoenix), além de uma GPU Adreno 830 para o máximo de performance gráfica.
A bateria é de silício-carbono com 6.500 mAh de capacidade e carregamento com fio de 120 W. A tela AMOLED LTPO de 6,78 polegadas tem taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de pico de 6.500 nits. O conjunto traseiro possui câmeras com OIS e modo de fotografia subaquática respaldado por certificações IP68 e IP69.
O Motorola Edge 70 Fusion vem equipado com o processador Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 (4 nm), acompanhado de 8 GB de RAM. O chipset utiliza arquitetura octa-core (núcleos Cortex-A720 e Cortex-A520), GPU Adreno 810 e NPU Hexagon para aceleração de tarefas de IA do sistema.
Ele é recomendado para quem não precisa de câmeras topo de linha, mas quer aparelho bonito e rápido. O custo-benefício melhora quando o preço fica abaixo dos flagships antigos.
A tela é um painel AMOLED de 6,78 polegadas com taxa de atualização de 144 Hz e brilho de pico de 5.200 nits. A câmera principal traz 50 MP com estabilização óptica (OIS), e a bateria de silício-carbono tem 5.200 mAh de capacidade.
O Motorola Edge 70 é indicado para quem quer desempenho acima da média sem pagar por um smartphone premium.
O dispositivo utiliza o processador Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 (4 nm) e memória RAM de 12 GB. A CPU de oito núcleos opera a velocidades de até 2,8 GHz e a GPU é a Adreno 722, modelo superior ao do Edge 70 Fusion, o que indica maior potencial para alto desempenho gráfico.
A tela é pOLED de 6,7 polegadas com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e brilho máximo de 4.500 nits, além de três câmeras com 50 MP.
O Galaxy A36 é uma das escolhas mais equilibradas entre celulares baratos com Snapdragon em 2026. O Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 (4nm) entrega bom desempenho para uso diário, 5G, redes sociais, streaming e jogos leves.
O chip conta com oito núcleos (quatro Cortex-A78 a 2,4 GHz e quatro Cortex-A55 a 1,8 GHz) e GPU Adreno 710, focado no consumo energético e na execução de tarefas cotidianas.
A tela é um painel Super AMOLED de 6,7 polegadas FHD+ com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+. A câmera principal é de 50 MP com OIS e a Samsung oferece até seis anos de atualização do Android.
O Redmi Note 15 5G é recomendado para quem busca custo-benefício, tela grande e bom desempenho para tarefas do dia a dia. O processador Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 (4 nm) possui modem 5G integrado e utiliza oito núcleos, divididos entre Cortex-A78 e Cortex-A55 de até 2,4 GHz. A GPU Adreno 710 foca em equilibro entre desempenho e consumo de energia.
Em uso real, um Snapdragon intermediário atende bem WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube, bancos, GPS e até jogos populares. A presença de 5G garante maior vida útil para quem pretende ficar anos com o aparelho.
Antes de comprar, confira se a versão é global, tem NFC, bandas 5G brasileiras e carregador compatível. Esses detalhes fazem diferença na experiência e evitam limitações em pagamentos e conectividade.
O Poco M8 5G é a opção para quem quer celular barato com foco em desempenho básico. Ele deve atender estudantes, motoristas de app e usuários que priorizam bateria e conectividade.
O smartphone funciona com um processador Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 (4 nm) e 8 GB de RAM. A CPU tem 8 núcleos, divididos entre ARM Cortex-A78 de 2,4 GHz e Cortex-A55 de 1,8 GHz, além de uma GPU Adreno 710.
O aparelho traz tela AMOLED de 6,77 polegadas com taxa de 120 Hz e câmera principal de 50 MP. A bateria é de 5.520 mAh com recarga de 45 W, acompanhada de sensor infravermelho e certificação IP66.
Você deve se atentar aos seguintes aspectos para escolher o melhor celular com Snapdragon:
O melhor processador da Qualcomm em 2026 é o Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.
Ele lidera o mercado com os núcleos Oryon de maior frequência (até 4,74 GHz), a GPU Adreno 840 com memória de alta performance e suporte avançado para jogos e IA generativa local. É o chip que equipa os melhores celulares do ano, como o S26 Ultra.
O Samsung Galaxy A36 5G é o celular barato com melhor custo-benefício equipado com Snapdragon.
Esse modelo traz o Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, se destacando pela estabilidade no uso diário, tela Super AMOLED de 120 Hz e longevidade nas atualizações de software.
O Snapdragon costuma ser a escolha mais consistente para jogos e uso pesado, graças às GPUs Adreno e ao bom desempenho geral.
A linha de placas gráficas Adreno (exclusiva da Qualcomm) se destaca pelo gerenciamento térmico. Enquanto outros chips costumam sofrer mais com perda de desempenho por aquecimento (thermal throttling) em uso prolongado, o Snapdragon consegue manter altas velocidades por mais tempo.

articles.title: Telegram kurzzeitig aus dem App-Store geflogen: Das war der Grund
articles.text:
Telegram kurzzeitig aus dem App-Store geflogen: Das war der Grund
Apple hat die App des Messaging-Dienstes Telegram wegen Verbreitung von Kinderpornografie für kurze Zeit aus der Download-Plattform für seine iPhones entfernt. Die App wurde dem Konzern zufolge wieder zugelassen, nachdem Telegram die Inhalte entfernte und den Nutzer, der sie verbreitet hatte, von der Plattform verbannte.
In den vergangenen Jahren gab es verschiedene Kontroversen um Telegram. So wurde Gründer Pawel Durow 2024 in Frankreich wegen des Vorwurfs festgenommen, dass Telegram nicht ausreichend gegen den Missbrauch durch Kriminelle vorgehe. Die Behörden in Australien starteten ein Verfahren gegen Telegram wegen Vorwürfen, dass der Messaging-Dienst extremistische Beiträge nicht entdeckt und entfernt habe.
Telegrams Rolle im Ukraine-Konflikt
Telegram spielt zugleich eine wichtige Rolle unter anderem im Ukraine-Konflikt, weil beide Seiten über den Dienst Informationen zum Verlauf des russischen Angriffskrieges veröffentlichen. In Russland wurde Durow vergangene Woche auf eine Terroristen-Liste gesetzt.
Ein Grund dafür waren Behauptungen, dass Telegram von ukrainischen Geheimdiensten genutzt werde, um Kontakt zu Russen anzubahnen. Telegram ist in Russland zwar blockiert, aber kann über verschlüsselte VPN-Verbindungen genutzt werden, die den Aufenthaltsort der Nutzer verschleiern.

articles.title: Rusia tenía un problema llamado Boeing y Airbus. Su avión nacional acaba de dar el paso que llevaba años esperando
articles.text:
Durante años, hablar de aviación comercial en Rusia también fue hablar de Boeing y Airbus. Sus aviones han sostenido buena parte de la flota comercial del país, pero esa normalidad empezó a romperse cuando las sanciones occidentales complicaron el acceso a nuevos aparatos, repuestos y soporte técnico. Lo que antes era una dependencia asumida se convirtió en un problema industrial de primer orden: mantener una flota moderna sin poder contar con normalidad con los fabricantes que la habían hecho posible.
La respuesta rusa a ese problema tiene nombre propio, aunque su historia viene de lejos: MC-21. El programa realizó su primer vuelo en 2017, pero lo que acaba de ocurrir en Irkutsk pertenece a otra fase del proyecto. United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) y el Ministerio de Transporte ruso han comunicado que el primer MC-21-310 de serie, presentado con sistemas y componentes rusos en lugar de los importados, ya ha completado su primer vuelo, una prueba relevante porque traslada el foco desde el desarrollo prolongado del avión hacia su posible fabricación en serie.
El avión que Rusia necesitaba para dejar de mirar a Boeing y Airbus
La comparación con Boeing y Airbus no sale de la nada. El MC-21 es un avión de pasillo único y medio alcance, justo el tipo de aparato que usan las aerolíneas para cubrir gran parte de sus rutas domésticas y regionales. Puede llevar hasta 211 pasajeros, una cifra que lo sitúa en el mismo terreno comercial que las familias Boeing 737 MAX y Airbus A320neo, dos de las referencias mundiales en ese segmento. La diferencia, al menos por ahora, es que la ambición rusa mira primero hacia dentro: cubrir un mercado nacional que necesita alternativas propias.
El giro no se entiende sin mirar la historia del programa. El MC-21 avanzó durante años como un proyecto con cooperación internacional y componentes extranjeros, incluida una variante MC-21-300 equipada con motores Pratt & Whitney. Ese camino quedó en cuestión tras la invasión rusa de Ucrania y las sanciones occidentales, que empujaron a la industria aeronáutica rusa a sustituir sistemas importados por desarrollos nacionales. La versión que ahora concentra el futuro del proyecto es el MC-21-310, con motores rusos PD-14 y una cadena industrial mucho más cerrada dentro del país.
La prueba ha tenido lugar este lunes, 3 de agosto, en el aeródromo de la planta aeronáutica de Irkutsk, según han comunicado UAC y el Ministerio de Transporte ruso. El avión ha volado durante 1 hora y 23 minutos, ha alcanzado altitudes de hasta 6.000 metros y ha llegado a velocidades instrumentales de hasta 600 km/h. Durante el vuelo, los equipos han comprobado la estabilidad y el control del aparato en distintas configuraciones, además del funcionamiento de sus sistemas rusos de a bordo. El piloto de pruebas Roman Taskaev ha afirmado, en la valoración difundida por UAC, que la primera máquina de serie se ha comportado bien y ha completado el plan previsto.
El valor de esta prueba no está solo en que el avión haya despegado y aterrizado, sino en lo que UAC quiere presentar como una señal de madurez industrial. Vitaly Naryshkin, jefe de diseño del MC-21, ha señalado que la compañía está aprovechando el calendario de vuelos de certificación para ensayar procedimientos propios de las fases finales de producción. La lectura oficial es clara: cuanto más trabajo quede resuelto antes de recibir el certificado, menor debería ser la distancia entre la aprobación regulatoria y las primeras entregas a aerolíneas.
Si bajamos el avión a cifras, la ficha del fabricante habla de 42,25 metros de longitud, 35,90 metros de envergadura, 11,45 metros de altura, 85.000 kg de peso máximo al despegue y un alcance de 3.830 km en configuración de dos clases con 175 pasajeros. UAC también destaca una estructura con más del 30% de materiales compuestos y una cabina que, según su propia descripción, ofrece más anchura y espacio que otros aviones de su categoría.
El MC-21-310 ha dado el paso que Rusia llevaba años esperando, pero ese paso no resuelve por sí solo el problema que lo hizo más urgente. Un avión no cambia una industria únicamente por completar una prueba: necesita certificación, producción sostenida y una red capaz de mantenerlo operativo cuando empiece a volar con pasajeros. Lo ocurrido este lunes acerca el proyecto a ese objetivo, pero también deja claro que la parte más difícil aún no se mide en horas de vuelo, sino en aviones entregados.
