articles.title: Totgeglaubtes Geothermiekraftwerk: Dieses Startup rettet die Anlage mit einem Bohrloch
articles.text:
Dieses Startup rettet altes Geothermiekraftwerk – mit nur einem neuen Bohrloch
Im Juni 2024 erwarb ein junges Unternehmen namens Zanskar Geothermal ein Geothermiekraftwerk im US-Bundesstaat New Mexico, das zum damaligen Zeitpunkt zusehends an Leistung verlor. Das aus dem unterirdischen Reservoir kommende Wasser wurde von Tag zu Tag kälter, wodurch der Betrieb des Kraftwerks langsam unrentabel zu werden schien. Doch jetzt, nur zwei Jahre später, läuft das Kraftwerk dank eines neuen Bohrlochs wieder mit voller Kapazität.

articles.title: Xiaomi va a romper el mercado: su próximo móvil barato va a ser la recomendación del año
articles.text:
Si tenías pensado comprarte un móvil nuevo y tienes un presupuesto más bien bajo, tienes que esperar a que Xiaomi lance su próximo dispositivo. Hablamos del Redmi 17 5G, un smartphone que se acaba de filtrar al completo y que cuenta con una serie de especificaciones bastante sorprendentes. Echando un vistazo a su lista de características y al diseño, es fácil adelantar que Xiaomi tiene entre manos uno de los móviles más recomendables del año.
No para todo el mundo, por supuesto, pero sí para aquellos que quieren que cada euro invertido se destine a las mejores características posibles y, a su vez, la cifra final sea bastante baja. Y es que, aunque todavía no sabemos cuánto va a costar, echando un vistazo a sus características y los precios de las generaciones anteriores, podemos saber que estamos ante uno de esos dispositivos que se van a vender como pan caliente.
Y lo mejor es que no tienes que esperar para conocerlo: se ha filtrado TODO sobre este Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G. Su diseño, los colores disponibles, las dimensiones, la pantalla, el procesador e incluso la batería. Ya te lo adelantamos: vas a desear que se lance en España cuanto antes.
Así es el Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G: una bestia de la relación calidad-precio
Desde 91Mobiles han filtrado todo lo que nos interesa sobre este Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G, empezando por un diseño básico pero efectivo. El dispositivo tiene bordes planos, un módulo de cámara sencillo, una pantalla que podría estar un poco mejor aprovechada y estará disponible en 3 colores: naranja, azul y negro.
En la parte frontal encontramos una pantalla de 6,9 pulgadas en resolución HD+ que, además, ofrece una tasa de refresco adaptativa entre 120, 90 y 60 Hz, algo que no se suele ver mucho en dispositivos de este precio. Según la filtración, su brillo llega hasta los 825 nits de pico máximo.
Todo está comandado por un procesador Qualcomm Snapdragon 4 Gen 5, corre HyperOS 3 basado en Android 16, cuenta con una cámara principal trasera de 50 MP y una delantera de 8 MP.
Ahora bien, la mejor noticia está en su autonomía. Este Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G tiene una batería de 7.500 mAh en su interior con una carga de 45 W por cable, dos cifras que, teniendo en cuenta su bajo consumo energético, auguran varios días de uso por cada carga.
Para rematar la jugada, Xiaomi ha incluido certificación IP64 contra el agua y el polvo, NFC, jack 3,5 mm, doble SIM 5G y una protección Corning Gorilla Glass 7i para la pantalla.
¿Cuánto va a costar este Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G? La compañía todavía no lo ha anunciado de forma oficial, pero es de esperar que se presente en las próximas semanas y que su precio esté por debajo de los 200 euros cuando llegue oficialmente a España. En otras palabras: un muy buen móvil a tener en cuenta para este 2026.

articles.title: Outernet turns your saved posts into real-world adventures | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Danielle Egan and Athena Leong know how to have fun. Between the two of them, they’ve organized a citywide scavenger hunt in San Francisco and turned a viral prank into an exclusive NYC restaurant for a night. They even created an alternative to a running club for socializing, dubbed a “sit club,” where people just bring their chairs and relax. Now, with their new startup, Outernet, the co-founders want to help others add more fun to their lives, too.
The app’s name is inspired by the concept of using the internet as a tool to get you to go outside, hence “outernet.” It’s one of several apps that helps you save the things you see online — like local events, restaurants or bars to try, or other city landmarks — and turn them into a list of to-dos for exploring the world around you.
Outernet’s pitch is that instead of simply liking a post about something you’d like to see or do on social media, you should share it to its app, where it will track the activity or place you want to visit in an organized interface. (Invite codes to try the app for yourself are at the bottom of this post).
What makes Outernet different from others in the space, like Albo, Tabi, or Plotline, is who’s behind it: founders who have devoted much of their time to playfulness and having fun offline. Now, they want to bring that same spirit into their app.
“In my free time, I’m very passionate about getting people to go outside and do things,” explains Egan, whose offline persona is quite different from her former day job working in product BizOps at LinkedIn. “I just love capturing attention in unexpected ways and delivering delightful things.” She says the thesis behind the app is becoming the “motivation engine for IRL” — something that removes the friction between wanting to do something and actually going out to do it.
Outernet taps into an already common consumer behavior. As you scroll TikTok and Instagram, you’re often inspired by a creator’s post, so you’ll save it in the app as a reminder. But then you promptly forget about the idea as you continue to consume more content. Outernet solves this problem by keeping track of the things you want to do or places you want to visit, all in one place.
To save a post to the app, you’ll tap the share option from the source app, like TikTok or Instagram, then scroll through the list of places you can share to until you find Outernet. You can also paste social media URLs or website links directly into the app, or upload a photo of something you see, like a flyer.
To organize everything, Outernet leverages AI to pull relevant information, like the date, time, location, and details about the activity you want to try or the location of a place you’d like to visit. Events are saved to a chronological feed, which you can revisit whenever you’re looking for something to do. Other activities without a date, as well as places you’d like to visit, are organized into separate tabs within the app. You can also save events to your Apple or Google Calendar or view them in Outernet’s map.
The app can also send proactive reminders and nudges that encourage you to go do the things you’ve saved.
Then, as you explore places in the real world, you can “stamp” them as such, building what will eventually become a passport documenting your activities.
“We’re thinking of different ways of creating maybe some sort of like passport book where you can look at all the things [you’ve done] and maybe share that with friends and get some sort of sense of pride of that,” Egan says of future product plans. They’re also thinking of using traditional gamification techniques to encourage activity, like giving out stamps when you reach different milestones.
The idea for Outernet came out of the co-founders’ experience designing a citywide scavenger hunt in San Francisco, called “Pursuit,” which began three years ago and is now held annually. The monthlong game drew participation from about 1.5% of San Francisco’s population during its most recent run.
As the founders chatted with participants, they found that people didn’t get involved because they loved scavenger hunts or adventure games; they just wanted an excuse to go outside. This sparked an idea.
“We just realized that people really have an appetite for doing things, like going on adventures. This is the new trend,” notes Leong, whose background is in computer science and child development, before she landed a job in adventure game design.
“There are so many incredible community events, and being community organizers ourselves, we’re very plugged into that scene,” Egan adds. “What’s so hard is there are these boots on the ground — incredible community organizers who are hosting these amazing events, and they just don’t know how to reach people because marketing and grabbing people’s attention is such a different skill set. And that’s something that we are exceptional in. So we see ourselves as the conduit,” she says.
Outernet’s app has been on the market for roughly two months and is already profitable from its premium subscription ($6.99/mo or $39.99/year), which lets you save more items per day. It has around 18,000 users in total, and the team is experimenting rapidly with new ideas.
The founders are now having casual conversations with investors about their next steps, but finding the right fit is key.
“We want to bring on investors — if we do — [who are] people who are really aligned with us,” says Leong. “We’re whimsical, and we have to find investors that match.”
Outernet is invite-only and available on iOS, with an Android waitlist. TechCrunch readers can use the invite code “coffeewalk” to skip the waitlist.

GameSir, a global gaming peripheral brand renowned for combining high-performance engineering with innovative gaming technology, today announces the launch of the GameSir Tarantula 8K PC, a purpose-built wired esports controller designed for players seeking uncompromising speed, precision and customisation. Engineered exclusively for PC gaming, and available in a striking orange colorway, the Tarantula 8K PC delivers an ultra-fast 8000 Hz polling rate with just 0.25 ms response time, alongside GameSir's latest Gen-2 Mag-Res TMR stick technology, extensive programmable controls and an exceptionally lightweight 180 g design. Further enhancing control, the integrated six-axis gyroscope provides motion input for supported games, while GameSir Connect software allows players to fully customise button mapping, stick and trigger settings, macros, lighting effects and multiple controller profiles to suit individual play styles.
Despite its extensive feature set, the Tarantula 8K PC weighs just 180 g. By removing vibration motors and the internal battery, GameSir has created an exceptionally lightweight controller that reduces hand fatigue during extended gaming sessions while maintaining a solid, comfortable feel through laser-engraved textured grips.
Dynamic RGB lighting offers multiple visual modes including solid colour, breathing, rainbow and animated effects, allowing players to personalise their setup without compromising performance.
Additional features include a tactile D-pad, adjustable turbo functionality, onboard profile switching, trigger calibration, joystick dead zone adjustment and a 3.5 mm headset jack for wired audio.

articles.title: Everyday Efficiency Through Dependable Managed IT Services - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Need for Reliable IT Support in Business
In today’s fast-paced business environment, operational efficiency is paramount. Companies face the constant challenge of maintaining seamless technology infrastructures while managing costs and minimizing downtime. This is where dependable managed IT services become invaluable. By outsourcing IT management to specialized providers, businesses can focus on their core activities while ensuring their technology systems are robust, secure, and efficient.
The reliance on technology to drive daily operations has never been greater. According to a report by Statista, 84% of enterprises worldwide have adopted some form of managed IT services to enhance their operational capabilities. This trend indicates a growing recognition that in-house IT teams alone often cannot meet the demands of modern business environments without external support.
Moreover, the digital transformation accelerated by recent global events has made IT infrastructure more critical than ever. Companies that invest in reliable IT management experience not only increased productivity but also a significant edge over competitors who struggle with frequent outages and cyber threats. For many businesses, partnering with dependable managed IT services providers is no longer optional – it’s a strategic necessity.
Unlocking the Benefits of Managed IT Services
Managed IT services provide a comprehensive approach to handling a company’s technology needs. These services include network monitoring, cybersecurity, data backup, and help desk support. By partnering with experienced providers, businesses can leverage expert knowledge and advanced tools that might otherwise be cost-prohibitive.
One significant advantage is the proactive nature of managed services. Instead of waiting for problems to occur, service providers continuously monitor systems to identify and resolve issues before they impact operations. This approach dramatically reduces downtime, which can be costly. Gartner estimates that the average cost of IT downtime is $5,600 per minute, underscoring the importance of prevention.
For companies operating in specific regions, choosing a local provider can offer additional benefits. For example, Sacramento MSPs like GitsTel combine industry expertise with a deep understanding of local business needs, delivering tailored solutions that maximize efficiency and reliability. This localized approach often results in faster response times and more personalized service, ensuring that IT issues are resolved promptly and with minimal disruption.
Additionally, the scalability of managed IT services allows businesses to adapt quickly to changing demands. Whether expanding operations or downsizing, companies can adjust their IT resources without the need for significant capital investment. This flexibility not only supports growth but also helps maintain cost control.
Enhancing Security and Compliance
Cybersecurity remains a top concern for businesses of all sizes. The increasing complexity of cyber threats requires continuous vigilance and updated defenses. Managed IT service providers specialize in safeguarding company data through advanced security protocols, regular vulnerability assessments, and compliance management.
Data breaches can be devastating, both financially and reputationally. According to IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report, the average cost of a data breach in 2023 was $4.45 million, highlighting the high stakes involved in protecting sensitive information. By outsourcing security functions, businesses access specialized skills and technologies without the expense of maintaining an in-house security team. This is especially important as compliance requirements grow more stringent across industries. Organizations can reduce risk and ensure adherence to regulations by partnering with providers that offer comprehensive compliance solutions.
Those interested in advanced security services and infrastructure management can visit Gravity Systems. Their expertise ensures that businesses stay ahead of evolving threats while maintaining operational continuity. With cyberattacks becoming more sophisticated, having a trusted partner who can implement cutting-edge defense strategies is essential for safeguarding business assets.
Driving Cost Efficiency and Scalability
Beyond improving reliability and security, managed IT services also help businesses control costs. Predictable monthly fees eliminate unexpected expenses related to emergency repairs or system failures. Moreover, outsourcing IT functions frees internal staff to focus on strategic projects rather than routine maintenance.
Scalability is another critical benefit. As companies grow, their technology needs evolve. Managed IT providers can quickly adjust service levels, provisioning additional resources or scaling back as necessary. This flexibility supports business agility and helps organizations adapt to changing market conditions.
According to a study by CompTIA, 70% of small and medium-sized businesses cited cost savings as a primary reason for adopting managed IT services, highlighting the financial impact of these partnerships. Furthermore, businesses that utilize managed IT services report a 25% improvement in operational efficiency within the first year of implementation, demonstrating tangible benefits beyond cost savings.
Choosing the Right Managed IT Partner
Selecting the right managed IT service provider is crucial. Businesses should look for partners with a proven track record, industry certifications, and a customer-centric approach. The provider should offer transparent service level agreements (SLAs) and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.
Local providers often bring an added advantage through personalized service and faster response times. Companies should evaluate their unique IT needs and seek providers that offer tailored solutions aligned with their business goals. For instance, working with can ensure that the provider understands specific regional regulations and business practices, which is vital for compliance and operational success.
Additionally, businesses should consider providers that invest in the latest technologies and maintain a proactive stance toward emerging IT trends and threats. This foresight can help organizations maintain a competitive edge and avoid costly disruptions.
The Future of Managed IT Services
As technology continues to evolve, so too will the scope and capabilities of managed IT services. Emerging trends such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and automation are increasingly integrated into IT management practices, enabling faster issue detection and resolution. Cloud computing also remains a key focus area, with many businesses migrating critical workloads to cloud platforms for enhanced flexibility and disaster recovery.
Managed IT service providers are adapting by offering hybrid solutions that combine on-premises infrastructure with cloud services, ensuring optimal performance and security. Businesses that embrace these innovations through reliable managed IT partners position themselves for long-term success.
Furthermore, the rise of remote work has underscored the importance of dependable IT services. Ensuring secure and efficient remote access to company resources is now a baseline requirement. Managed service providers help organizations implement virtual private networks (VPNs), endpoint security, and collaboration tools that support a distributed workforce without compromising security or productivity.
Conclusion
Dependable managed IT services are essential for businesses striving to maintain everyday efficiency and competitiveness. By leveraging expert support, companies reduce downtime, enhance security, control costs, and scale effectively. Whether working with local specialists or exploring advanced solutions, organizations can build resilient IT infrastructures that support sustained success in an increasingly digital world.
In summary, the strategic partnership with managed IT service providers empowers businesses to focus on what they do best while leaving the complexities of IT management to trusted experts. As technology continues to advance and threats evolve, dependable managed IT services will remain a cornerstone of operational excellence and business resilience.

articles.title: Des images satellites dévoilent les opérations de remorquage du Starship 40 vers l'Australie
articles.text:
Rarement une opération de repêchage de Starship aura attiré autant d’attention. Depuis la survenue du treizième vol d’essai de la fusée géante dans la nuit du 24 au 25 juillet 2026, au cours duquel la bonne résistance de l’étage supérieur a été constatée, une manœuvre de récupération est en cours au large de l’Australie, là où l’engin a fini sa course.
Et le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que des internautes suivent ça de très près, en essayant de repérer les navires déployés sur zone et de les suivre avec leurs données de localisation. Depuis le 3 août, cependant, la situation s’est largement éclaircie avec la publication par CNN d’une série de photos prises grâce à des satellites d’observation de la Terre.
Ces images en haute résolution ont été fournies par la société Vantor, qui est spécialisée dans l’intelligence spatiale pour des applications de défense (et qui a récemment été au cœur de l’actualité via une controverse autour de Pokémon Go). On peut ainsi voir un à trois bateaux autour du Starship, selon les clichés, en train de le tracter ou de l’escorter.
Un Starship qui sera tracté jusqu’en Australie
Compte tenu de la zone maritime dans laquelle l’engin a amerri, toute cette petite armada va inévitablement mettre les voiles vers l’Australie dès que la sécurisation du véhicule pour le remorquage aura été effectuée. Ce sont en effet les côtes les plus proches, même si la structure a dérivé en mer durant des jours avant que SpaceX ne se décide à la repêcher.
Toute l’opération prendra encore quelques jours avant de rallier le port, car la manœuvre reste délicate. L’équipage doit en particulier prendre garde à ne pas aller trop vite, pour s’assurer que le Ship reste bien à flot malgré la houle. D’aucuns pensent avoir repéré des flotteurs au niveau des moteurs, afin justement d’éviter qu’ils prennent l’eau.
Il n’était pas prévu à l’origine de récupérer cet étage supérieur, mais dans la mesure où il s’est montré plus performant qu’attendu, décision a été prise de le rapatrier au pays pour l’ausculter physiquement, en complément de toute la télémétrie déjà collectée lors du vol et des observations à distance faites quand il était à la dérive.

articles.title: Windows 11 rame sur votre PC ? Microsoft prépare enfin la mise au régime que tout le monde attendait
articles.text:
Microsoft veut réduire la consommation de mémoire vive de Windows 11 d'ici à la fin de 2026. Une optimisation bienvenue alors que la flambée du prix de la RAM menace de prolonger la carrière des PC limités à 8 Go.
Huit gigaoctets de RAM vont-ils enfin cesser d'être synonymes de Windows 11 au ralenti ? Microsoft promet de réduire l'empreinte mémoire de son système d'exploitation afin de rendre les PC modestement équipés plus rapides et plus réactifs. Une priorité qui tombe à point nommé alors que la hausse du prix de la DRAM incite les fabricants, Microsoft le premier, à conserver des configurations de 8 Go sur leurs machines les moins chères.
Microsoft s'attaque aux frameworks de Windows 11
Le géant de Redmond ne compte pas se contenter d'un nettoyage superficiel de son OS qui s'apprête à fêter ses 5 ans. Dans son blog officiel, Microsoft explique avoir adopté un allocateur de mémoire plus efficace pour réduire la surcharge des applications et des composants du système. Microsoft poursuit également l'optimisation de WinUI 3, le framework désormais utilisé par une part croissante de l'interface de Windows 11, notamment les Widgets et la nouvelle fenêtre Exécuter.
Autre chantier sensible, l'entreprise cherche désormais à diminuer la consommation des composants Chromium et WebView2 intégrés au système. Ces briques permettent d'afficher des interfaces Web dans des applications natives, mais peuvent aussi multiplier les processus et alourdir l'utilisation de la mémoire. Pour atteindre son objectif, Microsoft agirait donc sur les fondations de Windows, son interface et ses technologies Web embarquées.
Aucun gain chiffré pour le moment
Microsoft ne précise toutefois ni la quantité de RAM qui sera économisée ni l'accélération attendue. L'entreprise promet seulement une expérience plus réactive sur les PC dotés de 8 Go ou davantage d'ici à la fin de l'année.
Une optimisation qui ressemble aussi à un léger coup de canif dans l'ambition Copilot+ PC de Microsoft. Alors que l'éditeur vante des machines taillées pour l'IA locale avec au moins 16 Go de RAM, il doit désormais consacrer ses efforts à maintenir à flot celles qui n'en embarquent que 8...

articles.title: 7 Books that change how you view time and your future
articles.text:
7 Books that change how you view time and your future
Discover seven thought-provoking books that transform how you think about time, aging, goals, and the future you are building.
Most people think of time as something they have plenty of, until suddenly they don't. Days turn into months, months into years, and before long, the future we imagined begins to feel much closer than expected.
The way we think about time shapes nearly every aspect of our lives. It influences our goals, priorities, relationships, careers, and sense of purpose. Yet many of us rarely stop to examine our assumptions about it. Some books have a remarkable ability to change our perspective on time. They make us rethink how we're spending our days, what we're postponing, and whether we're building a future that aligns with what truly matters.
7 Books that may permanently alter how you think about time
1. Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
This book begins with a startling observation: if you live to eighty years old, you'll have roughly four thousand weeks on Earth. Rather than encouraging readers to become more productive, Burkeman argues that accepting our limited time can lead to a more meaningful life. He challenges the idea that we can optimise our way out of life's constraints and instead encourages us to focus on what truly deserves our attention. Many readers finish this book with a completely different relationship to time, urgency, and ambition.
2. Die with Zero by Bill Perkins
Most financial advice focuses on accumulating wealth for the future. Bill Perkins asks a different question: What if you're saving so much for tomorrow that you're missing today? The book explores the idea that experiences have a "best-before date." Certain adventures, opportunities, and memories are more meaningful at specific stages of life. By emphasising the relationship between money, time, and experiences, the book encourages readers to think more carefully about when, not just whether, they pursue their goals.
3. When Breath Becomes Air by Paul Kalanithi
Few books make readers reflect on time more deeply than this memoir. After being diagnosed with terminal cancer at age thirty-six, Paul Kalanithi confronts questions about mortality, meaning, and purpose. His reflections reveal how easily people assume they have more time than they actually do. The book encourages readers to reconsider what they are postponing and whether they are investing their time in things that genuinely matter. Its insights linger long after the final page.
4. The Midnight Library by Matt Haig
Regret often distorts our view of both the past and the future. In The Midnight Library, Nora Seed explores alternate versions of her life based on different choices she could have made. Through these experiences, she learns that every life contains compromises, uncertainties, and unexpected challenges. The novel encourages readers to stop obsessing over roads not taken and focus instead on the possibilities still available to them. It's a powerful reminder that the future is shaped less by perfect choices and more by meaningful engagement with the present.
5. The Top Five Regrets of the Dying by Bronnie Ware
Based on conversations with people nearing the end of life, this book offers a unique perspective on how people view time when they know it is running out. Many of Ware's patients regretted not living more authentically, spending too much time working, and waiting too long to pursue what mattered to them.
The book invites readers to examine whether their current priorities align with the life they hope to look back on someday. Its lessons are simple but deeply impactful.
6. The Psychology of Time Travel by Kate Mascarenhas
This inventive novel uses time travel not merely as a plot device but as a way to explore memory, identity, and the human relationship with time itself. The story examines how knowledge of the future influences present decisions and how people cope with uncertainty, inevitability, and change. While fictional, the book raises fascinating questions about how we think about the future and the choices we make today.
7. Essentialism by Greg McKeown
One of the most important questions about time is not how much of it we have but how we choose to spend it. Greg McKeown argues that many people allow their schedules to become crowded with obligations that do little to advance their most important goals. As a result, their attention becomes scattered across countless priorities. The book encourages readers to focus on what is truly essential and eliminate what isn't. In doing so, it transforms how people think about both time and the future they are creating.
Lessons to carry forward
Time is the one resource that cannot be earned back, saved indefinitely, or replaced. Yet it is often treated as if there will always be more of it tomorrow. Whether it's the perspective-shifting ideas of Four Thousand Weeks, the experience-focused philosophy of Die with Zero, the mortality reflections of When Breath Becomes Air, the lessons on regret in The Midnight Library, the wisdom of The Top Five Regrets of the Dying, the imaginative questions raised by The Psychology of Time Travel, or the prioritization framework of Essentialism, these books challenge readers to think differently about time. Because changing how you view time often changes how you view your future, and ultimately, how you choose to live your life today.

articles.title: Chatbots, deepfakes, IA : l’Europe impose de nouvelles règles
articles.text:
Depuis le 2 août 2026, l’article 50 de l’AI Act est entré en vigueur. Le texte de la Commission européenne poursuit un objectif clair : permettre aux internautes de mieux différencier les contenus générés ou modifiés par l’IA des contenus authentiques. Mais ces nouvelles règles pourront-elles réellement être appliquées à l’heure où les outils d’intelligence artificielle sont omniprésents ?
Les contenus générés ou modifiés par l’IA devront être étiquetés comme tels
Les fournisseurs de systèmes d’IA devront mettre au point un système d’étiquetage pour marquer les contenus générés ou modifiés à l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle, que ce soit une vidéo, une image, un son ou un texte. Les deepfakes diffusés dans le cadre d’une activité professionnelle devront quant à eux être étiquetés comme tels. L’objectif est simple : permettre aux internautes de distinguer les contenus générés ou modifiés par l’intelligence artificielle des contenus réels.
Par ailleurs, les chatbots utilisés par certaines plateformes, comme les services publics ou les sites de commerce en ligne, devront être clairement signalés comme étant des systèmes d’intelligence artificielle. De ce fait, un internaute doit être capable de comprendre rapidement s’il interagit avec une IA ou un humain. Il faut dire que certaines plateformes maintiennent un flou à ce niveau en faisant passer une IA pour un véritable agent du service client.
Autre règle particulièrement importante : les textes d’intérêt public générés par l’IA devront être étiquetés comme tels. Ce point concerne seulement les textes publiés sans contrôle éditorial humain. Une personne qui utilise l’IA pour écrire un texte, mais qui le relit et approuve son contenu est exempte de cette règle. Les textes artistiques, satiriques ou de fiction échappent également à cette règle.
L’étiquetage des contenus générés par IA sera-t-il vraiment efficace ?
Plusieurs plateformes ont déjà mis en place un système d’étiquetage pour identifier les contenus générés ou modifiés à l’aide de l’IA. À titre d’exemple, Instagram propose les « notices sur l’IA ». De son côté, l’AI Act demande que les contenus générés par IA « soient marqués dans un format lisible par machine et identifiables comme ayant été générés ou manipulés par une IA », mais les technologies actuelles (filigranes numériques, métadonnées, systèmes de provenance) ont des limites. Les filigranes numériques peuvent par exemple être supprimés, tandis que les métadonnées associées aux fichiers peuvent disparaître lors d’une modification ou d’une republication.
Par ailleurs, où se situe la limite entre un contenu sensiblement modifié par l’IA et une simple retouche ? Les outils d’intelligence artificielle sont désormais omniprésents et se sont largement démocratisés auprès du grand public. À terme, le risque est donc de voir se multiplier les étiquetages « modifié à l’aide de l’IA » sur Internet. La Commission européenne et les plateformes concernées devront préciser certains aspects pratiques afin d’assurer une application cohérente de ces nouvelles règles.

articles.title: June launches with $20M to speed up enterprise software projects - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
June launches with $20M to speed up enterprise software projects
June.ai Technologies Inc., a startup that uses artificial intelligence to modernize enterprise software environments, launched today with $20 million in funding.
The pre-seed round was led by Time Ventures with participation from SV Angel, Vesey Ventures and other funds. They were joined by several prominent angel investors. The group included Michael Dell, VMware co-founder Diane Greene and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. Chief Executive George Kurtz.
June was launched last year by four former Salesforce Inc. executives. They joined the cloud giant in 2019 after it acquired their previous venture, an early AI startup called Bonobo AI Ltd. Time Ventures, the fund that led June’s round, is affiliated with Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff.
Changing the core applications that an enterprise uses to power its employees’ work can be a highly complicated task. The same applies to large-scale AI agent rollouts. As a result, companies often offload some of the work to professional service providers. That can significantly increase the cost of software projects.
June offers an AI platform that automates some of the work historically managed by professional service companies. According to the company, its AI can not only reduce the cost of software upgrades but also speed them up.
June identifies opportunities to make software upgrades by analyzing data from a company’s existing applications. For example, the platform can review employee activity in a support ticket processing system and spot inefficiencies. It also maps out business workflows that span multiple applications.
The information in an application doesn’t always provide a complete picture of the associated business process. When that’s the case, June rounds out the data with feedback from employees. The platform collects the information using a chatbot that asks questions in natural language.
Companies can use the data surfaced by June to inform their software development efforts. If the platform shows that a particular subsidiary struggles to keep up with support tickets, engineers could build an AI help desk agent to automate the work. June can also spot inefficiencies in other areas such as supply management and cybersecurity.
Once engineers identify a task that they wish to streamline with software upgrades, they can have June implement the necessary changes. The platform takes a natural language description of a business process update as input. It uses AI to implement the update and then runs tests to ensure that the code works as expected.
When June modifies a software system or rolls out a new one, it creates a simulated environment in which employees can familiarize themselves with the upgrade. The platform also generates training materials. A built-in support tool enables employees to request help from administrators if the training materials don’t cover all their questions.
According to June, its platform also automates a number of related tasks. It generates dashboards that track the return on investment of software changes. Another feature automatically spots technical issues that may slow down business workflows.
June’s platform could create more competition for so-called process mining platforms. Such tools use data from a company’s applications to identify business inefficiencies. Celonis SE, one of the biggest players in the process mining market, received a $13 billion valuation following its most recent funding round.

articles.title: eslint-rspack-plugin 5.0.0 Ships as a Pure ESM Package, Aligning with the Rstack Ecosystem
articles.text:
eslint-rspack-plugin, the plugin that runs ESLint checks during Rspack compilation, has released version 5.0.0, shipping as a pure ESM package and realigning the tool with the wider Rstack ecosystem.
The headline change in 5.0.0 is that eslint-rspack-plugin is now published as a pure ESM package, with its CommonJS build removed. The move mirrors Rspack 2.0, which republished its core packages as pure ESM and dropped their CommonJS builds to make module loading more consistent and better aligned with current Node.js practices. Because Node.js 20 and later can already load ESM modules using require(esm), most projects consuming the plugin through the JavaScript API should see little practical impact and need no code changes.
Functionally the plugin continues to run ESLint as part of the build and, in watch mode, re-runs ESLint only on the files Rspack has changed. It was originally forked from eslint-webpack-plugin, so its configuration surface feels familiar to webpack users. A typical setup registers the plugin in the Rspack config file.
Options carried into the 5.x line include caching, which is on by default to reduce execution time, a configType switch between the classic eslintrc format and ESLint's newer flat config, threads for running lint tasks across a thread pool, and lintAllFiles, which lints every matching file rather than only those in the dependency graph. That last option targets multi-environment Rsbuild and Rspack builds, where separate client and server passes would otherwise skip files:
The project README cautions that "you may find it more efficient to avoid using the eslint-rspack-plugin, as running ESLint during the build can lead to longer build times," recommending a separate lint command instead. The same guidance appears in @rsbuild/plugin-eslint, which wraps this plugin internally, and in the Rsbuild FAQ, which notes that Rsbuild does not run ESLint during builds by default "to protect compilation performance."
That caveat reflects a broader shift in the ecosystem. The Rstack team now ships Rslint, a TypeScript-first, ESLint-compatible linter written in Go and powered by typescript-go, which it claims delivers 20 to 40 times faster linting than traditional ESLint setups. For teams chasing build speed, running a fast standalone linter, whether ESLint through a dedicated script or an alternative such as Rslint, increasingly looks preferable to linting inside the bundler itself.
Developers upgrading from the 4.x line should test the pure ESM change against their toolchain and, where practical, adopt ESLint's flat config through configType: 'flat'. Migration context for the underlying ESM shift is documented in the Rspack 2.0 release notes.
eslint-rspack-plugin is open source under the MIT license and can be installed from npm.

articles.title: 150,000 Impacted by Madera Community Hospital Data Breach
articles.text:
Madera Community Hospital in California is notifying just over 150,000 individuals that their personal, financial, and medical information was compromised in a data breach.
A not-for-profit community healthcare provider serving Madera County and surrounding areas, Madera Community Hospital provides emergency services, surgical services, acute care, diagnostic imaging, and specialized medical programs.
The incident, the hospital says in an incident notice, occurred in May 2025, when hackers accessed its network for two days and likely exfiltrated certain files.
According to the hospital, after identifying files that were potentially exfiltrated in the attack, it engaged with experts and a data-review firm for analysis.
“We received the data-review results in April 2026 and have been working since then to ensure we have accurate contact information for notifying potentially impacted individuals,” Madera Community Hospital’s notice (PDF) reads.
The impacted data, it says, includes names, contact information, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, account credentials, financial account information, treatment and health insurance information, and limited biometric information.
“But not every person had each of those elements impacted, and we have not found any evidence that such information was shared or otherwise released publicly,” the hospital says.
In mid-July, the hospital started notifying the potentially impacted individuals of the data breach, and informed the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that 150,810 people were affected.
According to Madera Community Hospital, the extortion group that was responsible for the attack and demanded a ransom payment ultimately withdrew its demand, claiming it did not want to harm patients.
“We worked with third-party experts to address this event, perform an investigation into the unauthorized activity, and further secure our systems to protect information. We also notified law enforcement,” the hospital says.

articles.title: Mejor smartwatch por menos de 100 euros. Recomendaciones de relojes inteligentes baratos de los expertos de Xataka
articles.text:
El mercado de los smartwatch o relojes inteligentes ha ido creciendo con el paso de los años ofreciendo novedades y tecnologías y una amplia variedad de modelos. Y hoy en día no hace falta gastarse mucho dinero para tener algo de calidad, ya que por debajo de los 100 euros podemos encontrar modelos tan atractivos como el Amazfit Bip 6, nuestra recomendación por debajo de esta cifra.
El Amazfit Bip 6 es un smartwatch que se presenta con un diseño cuadrado bastante elegante, aunque también viene con muchas funciones centradas en el deporte, como es el caso de los más de 100 modos deportivos o los sensores de salud para llevar un seguimiento de las métricas a la hora de hacer deporte.
La pantalla es AMOLED y tiene una buena diagonal de 1,97 pulgadas, por lo que las notificaciones se ven especialmente bien. Es capaz de realizar y recibir llamadas Bluetooth, su autonomía es de hasta dos semanas dependiendo del uso que le demos y cuenta con GPS.
Los destacados
| MODELO |  | PERFECTO PARA TI | LO MEJOR | LO PEOR | PRECIO DESDE | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amazfit Bip 6 |  | Si buscas un smartwatch muy completo y cómodo de utilizar. | Tiene pantalla AMOLED, llamadas Bluetooth y GPS. | No tiene NFC. | 70€ | 
| Huawei Watch Fit 3 |  | Si tienes un móvil Huawei o buscas un reloj con una muy buena pantalla. | Es cómodo y elegante y la pantalla se ve de escándalo. | No tiene pagos móviles y su sistema operativo no es muy completo. | 89€ | 
| Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite |  | Si quieres un reloj que cueste poco dinero. | Tiene pantalla AMOLED y es muy económico. | Las prestaciones son menores que su competencia. | 42,99€ | 
| Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 |  | Si buscas un smartwatch con una muy buena relación calidad-precio. | Mejor que el anterior modelo, y añade llamadas Bluetooth. | La versión con NFC es más cara. | 91,98€ | 
| Amazfit Bip Max |  | Si quieres un reloj con una gran batería. | Tiene buena batería y medición constante de salud. | No tiene NFC. | 99,90€ | 
Por qué destacan
De entre todos los smartwatch que podemos encontrar por debajo de los 100 euros, nos quedamos con el Amazfit Bip 6 por todo lo que ofrece. A continuación, vamos a hacer un repaso de las principales características de estos dispositivos para que tengas claro qué criterio seguir a la hora de elegir un smartwatch.
Pantalla. A la hora de comprar un smartwatch conviene prestar especial atención a la pantalla. Lo mejor es que cuente con un panel AMOLED, y si tiene un brillo alto mucho mejor para así poder ver bien la pantalla en exteriores. Además, es recomendable que el panel ofrezca una buena tasa de refresco para que se vea fluida a la hora de navegar por los menús.
Diseño. Como podrás ver en nuestra selección de smartwatch por debajo de los 100 euros, en este rango de precio solemos encontrar, sobre todo, modelos con diseño cuadrado y no tanto redondos. Esto tiene una clara ventaja a la hora de leer notificaciones o leer el texto y las métricas que ofrecen algunas aplicaciones de salud.
Tamaño. De nada sirve que tengamos un buen smartwatch si no nos queda bien en la muñeca. Es por ello que debemos tener en cuenta que las marcas a veces ofrecen diferentes tamaños (generalmente de 42 y 46 milímetros aproximadamente). Es importante elegir bien para que el reloj nos quede bien estéticamente y sea lo más cómodo posible de llevar.
Funciones. Uno de los apartados más diferentes en cada reloj es el de las funciones. Lo habitual es que los smartwatch cuenten con muchos modos deportivos (varían entre cada modelo), pero además también cuentan con sensores de salud para medir la frecuencia cardiaca o el oxígeno en sangre. Dependiendo de lo que estemos buscando conviene elegir entre un modelo u otro.
Por otro lado, al tratarse de relojes más económicos, hay algunas funciones que no solemos ver en este rango de precio, como es el caso de la apnea de sueño que vemos en los smartwatch de Samsung y Apple. Los pagos a través de NFC es otro ejemplo, aunque esta ausencia también la vemos en modelos de gama media y gama alta.
Otras opciones a considerar
Aunque te hemos recomendado el Amazfit Bip 6 como el mejor smartwatch por debajo de los 100 euros, hay alternativas que conviene tener en mente. Aquí tienes las que nos parecen más destacables:
Huawei Watch Fit 3. El Huawei Watch Fit 3 no es un smartwatch muy reciente porque tenemos dos generaciones por delante, pero su relación calidad-precio es muy buena. El reloj es bastante cómodo y elegante, la pantalla se ve perfectamente a plena luz del día y su batería aguanta una semana sin ningún problema. Además, viene con una corona giratoria muy práctica que también se puede pulsar.
Cabe destacar que el Huawei Watch Fit 4 y el Huawei Watch Fit 5 suelen encontrarse por encima de los 100 euros, pero que pueden bajar de esta barrera a través de alguna oferta puntual.
Huawei Watch Fit 3
Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite. El Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite es el reloj perfecto para quienes busquen un precio muy ajustado. Uno de los puntos más destacables es que incorpora un panel AMOLED, pero además su batería dura prácticamente dos semanas y cuenta con llamadas Bluetooth.
Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite
Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6. Un peldaño por encima tenemos el Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6, un smartwatch que incorpora una pantalla AMOLED con diagonal de 2,07 pulgadas. Su autonomía teórica es de hasta 24 horas (varía según el uso), incluye una corona giratoria y viene con más de 150 modos deportivos. No incluye conectividad NFC, pero hay una versión un poco más cara que sí la incluye.
Amazfit Bip Max. El Amazfit Bip Max es otra alternativa muy atractiva por todo lo que ofrece. Por un lado tenemos un panel AMOLED de 2,07 pulgadas y por otro viene con mapas offline. Su autonomía teórica es de hasta 20 días, es compatible con la app Strava y viene con una función con planes de entrenamiento.
Configuraciones y extras
Además de todo lo que hemos comentado anteriormente, a la hora de comprar un smartwatch o reloj inteligente viene bien que tengamos en cuenta que puede llegar con distintas configuraciones:
Tamaño. Algunos relojes inteligentes, aunque sobre todo de gama alta, cuentan con varias configuraciones de tamaño para elegir el que más se ajuste a nuestra muñeca.
Correas. La mayor parte de smartwatch vienen con correas de silicona. No obstante, algunos modelos, como por ejemplo el Huawei Watch Fit 3, cuentan con versiones que incluyen correas de náilon. Estas últimas son más resistentes y el cierre suele ser de velcro, aunque se ensucian con más facilidad.
Preguntas frecuentes sobre el mejor smartwatch barato
¿Tiene GPS integrado o depende de la conexión con el teléfono móvil?
En este rango de precio hay modelos que incorporan GPS para registrar rutas de carrera o bicicleta sin la necesidad de llevar el móvil. Por el contrario, hay otros smartwatch que utilizan el GPS del móvil mediante Bluetooth, obligándonos a llevar el teléfono a la hora de realizar algunos deportes.
¿Cuánto tiempo dura la batería con un uso normal diario?
Los fabricantes suelen ofrecer autonomías teóricas bajo condiciones de uso muy concretas. En la práctica, la autonomía suele ser inferior. En cualquier caso, lo habitual es que este tipo de smartwatch ofrezcan una autonomía de entre 7 y 14 días de uso.
¿Permite responder llamadas directamente desde el propio reloj?
Algunos relojes incorporan micrófono y altavoz para realizar y contestar llamadas mediante la conexión por Bluetooth. En cambio, muchos otros modelos únicamente reciben la notificación visual de la llamada entrante para colgar o silenciar la llamada.
¿Qué funciones de salud y seguimiento del sueño ofrece?
Lo habitual es que este tipo de relojes cuenten con algunas funciones de salud, siendo las más comunes la de frecuencia cardíaca, nivel de oxígeno en sangre, los pasos diarios y la calidad de sueño. En cualquier caso, los resultados son orientativos.
¿Qué tipo de pantalla tiene y cómo se ve bajo la luz del sol?
Las pantallas AMOLED ofrecen colores mucho más vivos y un nivel de brillo más alto, lo que facilita que podamos ver bien la pantalla en exteriores. En cambio, las pantallas LCD son más económicas y suelen ofrecer un nivel de brillo más bajo.
¿Se pueden responder notificaciones de aplicaciones como WhatsApp?
La mayoría de relojes únicamente pueden leer las el texto de los mensajes de WhatsApp que recibamos. En cambio, otros además permiten responder a los mensajes.
¿Permite realizar pagos móviles en tiendas mediante tecnología NFC?
La función para realizar pagos móviles es poco habitual en relojes por debajo de 100 euros, salvo muy contadas excepciones.
Recomendación final
De entre todas las propuestas que podemos encontrar ahora mismo, nos quedamos con el Amazfit Bip 6 por todo lo que ofrece. Es un smartwatch que incorpora un buen panel, es capaz de realizar llamadas Bluetooth y viene con un buen surtido de modos deportivos.
Sin embargo, es posible que estés buscando un smartwatch con otro precio u otras características. En ese caso, el Huawei Watch Fit 3 es un reloj inteligente cómodo y elegante que incorpora una pantalla que se ve muy bien en interiores y exteriores y que, además, tiene una corona giratoria muy práctica.
Por otro lado, el Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite es otro reloj especialmente interesante por su precio y por el panel AMOLED que incorpora (sin dejar a un lado sus llamadas Bluetooth) y el Xiaomi Redmi Watch 6 también es una muy buena alternativa por su batería y por su pantalla.
Nota: algunos de los enlaces aquí publicados son de afiliados. A pesar de ello, ninguno de los artículos mencionados han sido propuestos ni por las marcas ni por las tiendas, siendo su introducción una decisión única del equipo de editores.

articles.title: DAS trop élevé : l’ANFR épingle ce smartphone Nothing et demande son retrait
articles.text:
DAS trop élevé : l’ANFR épingle ce smartphone Nothing et demande son retrait
L'ANFR demande le retrait du marché d'un smarphone très populaire de Nothing. Elle reproche au Phone (3a) son DAS trop élevé au regard des normes hexagonales.
L’Agence nationale des fréquences (ANFR) veille au grain. Comme elle le fait assez régulièrement, elle épingle des appareils qui ne respectent pas certaines normes propres au marché hexagonal. L’autorité a ainsi demandé, l’an dernier, le retrait de modèles signés Ulefone et Oukitel, en raison de leur DAS trop élevé. Ces marques à petit prix, vendues essentiellement sur des plateformes en ligne, ne sont pas les seules à commercialiser des terminaux au débit d’absorption spécifique (c’est-à-dire la quantité d’énergie électromagnétique absorbée par le corps humain lors de l’utilisation d’un téléphone portable) trop élevé au regard de la législation française.
Passons rapidement sur le cas des AGM Note N1, Doogee N55 Plus et Infinix Smart 9, modèles réservés effectivement aux plateformes en ligne, positionnés en entrée de gamme et vendus à tout petit prix, pour nous concentrer sur un fabricant ayant bien davantage pignon sur rue en France : Nothing. Le Phone (3a) du fabricant londonien, annoncé au printemps 2025 (et testé par Les Numériques dans la foulée), accuse un DAS “membre” (c’est-à-dire au contact de la peau, par exemple dans la paume de la main) de 4,32 W/kg, alors que la limite légale s’établit à 4 W/kg dans l’Hexagone.
Nothing Phone (4a) Pro
Que faire si vous êtes équipé ?
La publication de l’ANFR fait suite à sa “mise en demeure [de la marque]de prendre toutes les mesures appropriées pour mettre fin aux non-conformités constatées sur les équipements actuellement sur le marché ainsi que ceux déjà commercialisés”, par le biais d’une mise à jour corrective, destinée à diminuer la puissance d’émission.
L’ANFR recommande aux propriétaires d’un Phone (3a) (ou de l’un des modèles des marques également citées) de “se rapprocher de leur point de vente” pour définir avec lui les modalités de reprise de leur appareil. L’agence précise que ”les distributeurs doivent prendre les mesures de retrait et de rappel de leur propre initiative en cas d’inaction du fabricant”.
Ajoutons que l’ANFR mentionne également un smartphone très populaire, le Galaxy A55 de Samsung, dont elle relève notamment ”le défaut de marquage CE”. Ce smartphone, qui ”n’aurait jamais dû être mis sur le marché en France” selon ses termes, est en réalité une version internationale de l’appareil commercialisée non pas par Samsung, mais par le revendeur Valex, cité par l’ANFR. Votre Galaxy A55 acheté par les canaux classiques (revendeurs et opérateurs) n’est donc pas concerné par les mesures annoncées par l’agence.

articles.title: Descubre 3 formas de usar un kindle viejo de Amazon y convierte tu casa a inteligente
articles.text:
Un kindle antiguo, más allá de su función inicial como lector de libros electrónicos, puede transformarse en herramientas útiles y originales para el hogar. Existen diversas alternativas que permiten aprovechar la pantalla E-Ink y la conectividad Wi-Fi del dispositivo, logrando así funciones inesperadas como controlar la música, visualizar información relevante e incluso crear un reloj literario único.
Cómo transformar un kindle antiguo en controlador de música con Spotify
El kindle puede servir como centro de control para la reproducción de música si se emplea la función Spotify Connect. Para lograrlo, solo hace falta acceder al navegador integrado del dispositivo y abrir la página de Kindlify. El procedimiento consiste en iniciar sesión con la cuenta de Spotify y asegurarse de que el kindle esté conectado a la misma red Wi-Fi que el dispositivo principal que reproduce el contenido.
PUBLICIDAD
Este método no implica almacenar canciones ni instalar aplicaciones oficiales, sino que permite controlar la reproducción en tiempo real desde el kindle. Es posible pausar, reanudar y cambiar de pista, mientras se visualiza en la pantalla el contenido que está sonando en ese momento.
El sistema se basa en la conectividad entre dispositivos compatible con Spotify Connect, lo que facilita la gestión de la música desde distintos lugares de la casa. Esta solución permite aprovechar un e-reader fuera de su uso convencional y convertirlo en un accesorio práctico para quienes utilizan servicios de música en streaming.
PUBLICIDAD
Usar el kindle como panel inteligente para el hogar conectado
Una segunda alternativa consiste en transformar el kindle en una pantalla dedicada que muestre información relevante del hogar. Este proyecto implica un nivel de dificultad mayor, pues requiere configurar una página web personalizada y adaptar el formato del dispositivo, incluso recortando un marco específico si se desea un resultado más pulido.
El objetivo de este uso es aprovechar la pantalla de tinta electrónica para mostrar previsiones meteorológicas, eventos del calendario y listas de tareas que se actualizan en tiempo real.
PUBLICIDAD
La información proviene de servicios compatibles con aplicaciones externas, y se puede personalizar para que el kindle muestre los datos que resulten más útiles en la vida cotidiana. La versatilidad de este método reside en la posibilidad de integrar diferentes fuentes y adaptar el panel a las necesidades del usuario, convirtiendo un lector de libros en una pieza central de la automatización doméstica.
Convertir el kindle en un reloj literario para el hogar
El kindle puede también convertirse en un reloj de diseño original basado en citas literarias. Este proyecto mantiene la esencia del lector de libros, pero le da un giro novedoso: muestra en pantalla una cita diferente de una obra literaria para cada minuto del día, relacionada con la hora correspondiente.
PUBLICIDAD
El proceso requiere la selección y carga de imágenes, una para cada uno de los 1.440 minutos que tiene un día. Aunque la preparación de los archivos podría parecer compleja, ya existen recursos en línea que ofrecen tanto las imágenes como los elementos necesarios para instalar el reloj en el kindle.
Un aspecto llamativo de esta alternativa es que las citas aparecen sin indicar el título ni el autor, convirtiendo la consulta de la hora en un juego de reconocimiento literario. Si se desea conocer la fuente de la cita, basta con tocar la pantalla del dispositivo para revelar la información.
PUBLICIDAD
Este uso convierte el kindle en un objeto decorativo y funcional, que además invita a la reflexión y el entretenimiento para quienes disfrutan de la literatura y desean incorporar elementos originales a la decoración de su hogar.
Las tres propuestas permiten reutilizar un kindle viejo de formas creativas y útiles, adaptando el dispositivo a las tendencias de casas inteligentes. Cada proyecto varía en complejidad, desde la simple conexión con Spotify hasta la integración de paneles informativos o la creación de un reloj literario personalizado.
PUBLICIDAD
Estas alternativas demuestran que un lector de libros electrónicos puede tener una segunda vida en el entorno doméstico, añadiendo funciones prácticas y personalizadas sin necesidad de adquirir nuevos equipos.

articles.title: I stopped starting over in ChatGPT and the answers got much better
articles.text:
I stopped starting every ChatGPT conversation from scratch — these 5 simple changes made it much more useful
A little organization can give ChatGPT a real memory
One of the easiest ways to waste time with ChatGPT is to keep introducing yourself. You explain your project, your preferences, your goals and your writing style, get a useful answer, close the conversation and then repeat the whole process the next day.
There is a better approach. Rather than treating ChatGPT as a blank page every time you open it, think of it as a workspace that can be organized just like your computer. A few reusable prompts, a handful of reference documents and a little planning can dramatically reduce the amount of repetitive setup you do every week.
The best part is that none of these ideas require advanced prompt engineering or obscure features. They are simple habits that make ChatGPT spend less time learning about your task and more time actually helping you complete it.
1. Build a starter kit
Most people have a handful of requests they make over and over again. They ask ChatGPT to write in a particular tone, explain technical topics in plain English, or ensure everything has a citation. Instead of typing those instructions every time, save them as a reusable starter prompt.
Think about the jobs you repeat most often. If you regularly write certain kinds of emails, create one prompt that explains the tone, preferred length, and audience. If you frequently ask for meal ideas, save a prompt that includes your dietary preferences, budget, and the equipment you have in your kitchen. When you need help, paste the prompt into a new conversation before asking the real question.
The same approach works for hobbies. Someone learning French could create a starter prompt asking ChatGPT to correct mistakes gently while keeping the conversation moving. A keen gardener might save instructions explaining the local climate, soil type, and the plants already growing in the garden. Those details only need to be written once, but they improve every conversation that follows.
2. Build a reference library
One of the most overlooked ChatGPT features is the ability to work from documents you provide. You can create a small collection of files that explain the things you work on most often. Upload the relevant document at the beginning of a conversation and let ChatGPT use it as the foundation.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Keep a document listing your family's favorite meals, allergies and disliked ingredients, then upload it whenever you ask for a weekly meal plan. Store another file containing your packing checklist, travel preferences, and loyalty memberships so ChatGPT can help plan trips without needing the same information every time.
3. Treat ongoing projects like ongoing conversations
Many people instinctively click New Chat whenever they have another question for ChatGPT. That makes sense if today's topic has nothing to do with yesterday's. For projects that stretch over days or weeks, though, continuing the same conversation saves an enormous amount of time because all of the earlier decisions remain available.
Imagine planning a home office makeover. The first conversation might focus on furniture, the second on paint colors, and the third on lighting. By keeping everything together, ChatGPT already knows the size of the room, the budget, the style you like, and the desk you eventually chose. It can build on those decisions instead of asking you to repeat them.
The same habit works beautifully for learning new skills. If you are studying guitar, keep one conversation dedicated to practice. One day you ask about chord changes, the next you work on rhythm. Over time, the conversation becomes a record of your progress rather than a collection of disconnected lessons.
4. Give ChatGPT an example worth copying
ChatGPT usually produces better work when you show it what a good answer looks like. Instead of describing a tone as “friendly but professional,” paste in a paragraph, email, or product description that already sounds right and ask it to match the pacing, level of detail, and structure. This works especially well for recurring tasks such as newsletters, social posts, client updates or article introductions, where a vague style request can lead to something polished but strangely generic.
The example does not have to cover the same subject. A restaurant review can help shape the tone of a travel piece, while a strong project update can become the model for future internal messages. Be specific about what ChatGPT should imitate and what it should ignore, such as keeping the sentence length and warmth while avoiding the original wording or subject matter.
5. Ask for a second pass with a different job
A strong first draft often becomes much better when ChatGPT is given a new role for the revision. After it writes something, ask it to review the answer as an editor, skeptical reader, subject matter expert or member of the intended audience. Each perspective catches a different kind of weakness, from awkward phrasing to missing context or assumptions that only make sense to someone already familiar with the topic.
For example, after generating a travel itinerary, ask ChatGPT to review it as a parent traveling with a toddler and identify any unrealistic transitions. After drafting a business proposal, ask it to review the document as a cautious buyer who wants clearer costs and fewer vague promises. The second pass tends to be more useful when the reviewing role has a concrete reason to object.
None of these ideas make ChatGPT more intelligent. What they do is remove the unnecessary friction that creeps into everyday use. Instead of spending the first five minutes explaining who you are and what you need, you start much closer to the interesting part of the conversation. Once you stop rebuilding the same foundation every day, you can spend your time exploring better ideas instead of laying the same bricks over and over again.

articles.title: What was the first consumer gadget to feature a foldable display?
articles.text:
A little background
Ask most people to name the first folding-screen device and they will say Galaxy Fold. The real answer is a phone almost nobody outside China ever held: the Royole FlexPai, unveiled in Beijing on October 31, 2018, sold in a flash sale the following day, and shipped to buyers that December.
Royole was not a phone company. It was a Silicon Valley and Shenzhen display manufacturer that had been building ultra-thin flexible AMOLED panels since 2012, and the FlexPai existed largely to prove those panels could ship in a real product before Samsung Display or BOE beat it there.
The first consumer gadget with a foldable display wasn't made by Samsung
The spec sheet was serious enough: a 7.8-inch AMOLED at 1,920 x 1,440 in a 4:3 ratio, folding down to roughly 4 inches of usable screen, a Snapdragon 855, 6GB or 8GB of RAM, dual 16MP and 20MP cameras, and a hinge Royole rated for 200,000 folds. Pricing ran from 8,999 to 12,999 yuan, about $1,300 to $1,870 at the time.
It was also, by every account, rough. The FlexPai folded outward rather than inward, so the display was permanently exposed. It closed unevenly, leaving a visible wedge and a pronounced crease. Royole's Android 9 skin called "Water OS" frequently failed to reflow the UI when the device changed shape. Reviewers treated it as a proof of concept that had been rushed to market to win a race, which is exactly what it was.
Other early foldables...
Samsung's Galaxy Fold was announced in February 2019 and was supposed to arrive that April, but review units died within days after debris entered the hinge and testers peeled off what looked like a screen protector.
The relaunch finally happened on September 2019, in South Korea. Huawei's Mate X, revealed at MWC 2019 alongside a similar outward-folding design, slipped repeatedly and went on sale only in China on November 2019.
The ZTE Axon M was the trickiest distractor for our trivia. It shipped in October 2017, a full year before the FlexPai, and it folds. But it uses two separate rigid LCD panels joined by a mechanical hinge, with a thick seam down the middle, which makes it a dual-screen phone rather than a foldable-display one.
Flexible OLED reached consumers even earlier, in the curved Samsung Galaxy Round and LG G Flex of 2013, but those panels bent once at the factory and never moved again. A screen that folds and unfolds in the user's hands started with the FlexPai.

articles.title: Andrew Garfield deja clara su condición para volver como Spider-Man
articles.text:
Con el estreno de Spider-Man: Brand New Day, el superhéroe arácnido está más de moda que nunca. Tom Holland ha protagonizado su cuarta entrega en solitario, convirtiéndose en el actor con más películas en el papel del trepamuros. Pero antes que él vinieron los Spider-Man de Tobey Maguire y Andrew Garfield. Y este último ha confesado que no tiene la puerta cerrada a un regreso. Eso sí, bajo una condición innegociable.
En una entrevista concedida al podcast The Doscourse, de The Playlist, para promocionar su película El árbol muy muy lejano, Andrew Garfield se ha vuelto a pronunciar sobre su posible regreso como Spider-Man. El actor dejó atrás a su Peter Parker allá por 2014, aunque regresó en 2021 en No Way Home. Y dado el cariño que se le tiene entre el público, un nuevo retorno siempre está sobre la mesa. Pero no a cualquier precio.
"No lo sé. De verdad que no lo sé. Tendría que ser algo muy, muy peculiar. Tendría que ser muy extraño, y tendría que ser completamente poco convencional y casi… no diría aburrido, pero me gustaría que fuera totalmente inesperado. Como un género de Spider-Man que nunca hayas visto antes, que resulte muy fuera de lo común", señala Andrew Garfield. "Y ni siquiera sé qué podría ser eso", continúa, "quizás algo así como una película de viaje por carretera".
En definitiva, el intérprete solo estaría dispuesto a protagonizar una entrega de The Amazing Spider-Man si el filme se sale por completo de lo que entendemos por cine de superhéroes. Una propuesta muy difícil y arriesgada que es difícil que vea la luz verde. Aunque tratándose de un héroe tan popular como Spidey, no se puede descartar nada de cara a un futuro.
¿Andrew Garfield volverá como Spider-Man?
Lo cierto es que, al margen de esta inusual condición, hay bastantes posibilidades de que veamos a Andrew Garfield como Spider-Man de nuevo en el cine. Y es que Marvel está preparando Avengers: Secret Wars, que se estrenará en diciembre de 2027. En ella, la compañía espera reunir a una enorme cantidad de superhéroes del presente del UCM, pero también de franquicias anteriores.
Será el caso de los X-Men, que ya volverá en Avengers: Doomsday este mismo año. Y probablemente sea el caso de los Spider-Man de Tobey Maguire y Andrew Garfield, que volverían como Peter 2 y Peter 3 en esa entrega final de la Saga del Multiverso. Por ahora no están anunciados oficialmente, pero todos los rumores apuntan en la misma dirección.

articles.title: AI enthusiast unlocks and mods BIOS with Claude Code — AI defeats RSA-2048 signature checks and unlocks 55 hidden settings
articles.text:
AI enthusiast unlocks and mods BIOS with Claude Code — AI defeats RSA-2048 signature checks and unlocks 55 hidden settings
A new way to stop locked laptops from becoming eWaste is always welcome.
BIOS-locked laptops are sometimes sold at bargain prices due to the operational restrictions this kind of firmware security puts on the device. Can AI tools be used to bypass this security measure? The answer looks like a yes, as Reddit_2049 on the Claude AI subreddit recently shared the process that successfully unlocked their HP 15-dw1036ne.
A new owner of a BIOS-locked laptop will typically not be able to bypass a password or PIN at startup, nor be able to adjust any BIOS settings. It depends on what kind of lock has been implemented. There was a time when removing the CMOS could reset the BIOS and break these chains, but for a long time, laptop makers have had far stronger security.
The particular laptop model with a BIOS lock to bypass by the Redditor was the HP 15-dw1036ne, a 10th-gen Intel processor-packing laptop from the turn of the decade. This looks like a consumer laptop, so we reckon it will have had a power-on password set by the previous owner, which somehow didn’t get communicated to Reddit_2049 through the used/recycled electronics ownership chain. However, it isn’t explicitly stated what kind of BIOS lock faced the Redditor, so it could have been a BIOS admin lock. These locks aren’t as stringent or formidable as those possible with HP’s commercial laptops, which can even tie BIOS locks to the system TPM…
Back to the HP 15-dw1036ne unlock process, and it came with BIOS version F.68. The Redditor had access to a CH341A chip flasher and code disassembly tools, but said the system would throw up a ‘BIOS Corruption Detected’ message if any modification was detected. That’s a check that makes hacking it all the more difficult. This is where Claude Code stepped in.
Looking for previous examples and details of someone successfully unlocking this specific HP laptop’s BIOS was fruitless. So, Reddit_2049 asked Claude Code to pick through their backup BIOS dump and try to unlock it. Long story short, it worked.
Three levels of patches
The Redditor shared a few technical details about the three levels of patches that were required to unlock the BIOS. These include: finding the RSA-2048 DXE-FV signature check bypass, and 55 hidden setup fields, as well as revealing advanced BIOS configuration tabs. But most important to know is that Claude Code wrangled these bits and bytes, so Reddit_2049 now has a fully open BIOS on their HP laptop.
A Python script that completes the whole process on this particular HP laptop is shared at the bottom of the Reddit post. This will back up your current BIOS, implement all three patches, and leave your HP 15-dw1036ne unlocked.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Please be warned that this script might not work with your laptop, even if it's an HP, even if it’s a 15-dw1036ne, or even if there are other differences like board revision. However, this example shows that laptops with locked BIOS access/features and no specific known bypass method can now be fully unlocked thanks to AI.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Adieu les saccades : AMD prépare une évolution majeure de ses processeurs pour rendre vos jeux vraiment fluides
articles.text:
On juge souvent un processeur ou une carte graphique à son nombre d’images par seconde moyen. Sauf que ce chiffre ment un peu. Ce qui gâche vraiment une session de jeu, ce sont les chutes ponctuelles, ces instants où l’affichage saccade une fraction de seconde alors que la moyenne reste bonne. Les joueurs appellent ça les « 1 % lows ».
Le « 1 % low » mesure la vitesse d’affichage pendant le 1 % d’images le plus lent d’une partie. C’est là que se cachent les saccades qu’on sent manette en main. Et selon VideoCardz, c’est précisément ce phénomène que la future architecture Zen 6 d’AMD chercherait à améliorer, plutôt que de courir après quelques images de moyenne supplémentaires.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
Des réglages cœur par cœur pour lisser le jeu
D’après Tom’s Hardware, Zen 6 introduirait des contrôles orientés performance et une gestion plus fine, cœur par cœur, des budgets de chaleur et d’énergie. Au lieu d’appliquer les mêmes limites de température et de consommation à tous les cœurs en même temps, le processeur pourrait ajuster chacun individuellement. Un cœur qui gère la partie critique du jeu garderait sa fréquence quand les autres se calment, ce qui limiterait les à-coups.
C’est un changement d’approche. Ces dernières années, la bataille des processeurs de jeu s’est surtout jouée sur la moyenne d’images et sur le cache mémoire, avec les fameuses puces X3D d’AMD. S’attaquer directement aux microsaccades vise un défaut que les tests classiques mesurent mal mais que le joueur ressent tout de suite. Sur le papier, une partie plus régulière compte parfois plus qu’une moyenne un peu plus haute.
Reste que tout ceci relève encore de la fuite technique et qu’AMD n’a fait aucune annonce officielle. On sait déjà que la gamme Zen 6 s’annonce large, avec des configurations qui grimperaient jusqu’à 24 cœurs. Le calendrier, lui, est moins réjouissant pour les amateurs de jeu : les modèles les plus attendus par les joueurs seraient repoussés à 2027.
Si ces informations se confirment, Zen 6 pourrait devenir particulièrement intéressant pour qui joue sur PC et déteste les à-coups en pleine action. À voir sur pièces quand AMD dévoilera vraiment ses cartes, car un gain sur les 1 % lows se juge manette ou clavier / souris en main.
