articles.title: Taunted for driving, these six women now command Bihar’s Pink Buses
articles.text:
Taunted for driving, these six women now command Bihar’s Pink Buses
Meet Ragini, Anita, Baby, Gayatri, Aarti and Saraswati—six young women who overcame poverty and prejudice to become Bihar Pink Bus drivers.
Six young women, Ragini, Anita, Baby, Gayatri, Aarti and Saraswati, left behind social barriers, hardship and taunts to build a new identity as drivers of Bihar's Pink Buses. Their story shows that given the opportunity and the courage, daughters can take command of any steering wheel.
Seen from a distance, the Pink Bus on Bihar's roads looks much like any other city bus. The difference is its colour, but a far bigger change shows up in the driver's seat. Travelling with these young women are their families' hopes, their villages' changing outlook, and their own aspiration to build a better future.
Ragini Kumari, Anita Kumari, Baby Kumari, Gayatri Kumari, Aarti Kumari and Saraswati Kumari are the face of that change. Several come from the Mahadalit community, with fathers who work as daily-wage labourers and mothers who worked in fields and in other people's homes. One was mocked for her height; another was told that driving heavy vehicles is not a woman's job. Today these same women drive buses and trucks, challenging those very assumptions.
Ragini: past the taunts to the driver's seat
Twenty-one-year-old Ragini Kumari, from Alauddin Chak in Patna district's Punpun block, belongs to the Mahadalit Musahar community and is the first woman graduate in her large joint family. With the family's finances weak, her mother worked in fields and in other people's homes to keep things running, so for Ragini a job was also an attempt to change the family's situation.
Her schooling began with Nari Gunjan, and she later lived at the Prerna Hostel in Danapur. After graduation she prepared for competitive exams, but it was then that driving gave her life a new direction. With help from the Women and Child Development Corporation, she trained on light and then heavy vehicles at the Institute of Driving Training and Research (IDTR) in Aurangabad, carrying on despite mockery of her height and ability in the village.
"When I went to Aurangabad for training, people in the village said a lot to my parents," she says. "Someone asked whether the girl had run away; someone said, how will a girl drive a bus? I didn't let those words get to me. Nari Gunjan, Sudha didi and my mentors always kept my spirits up."
Her goal does not end at the wheel. She wants to make her family financially strong so her mother no longer has to labour, and then to pursue a PhD and become a professor.
Anita and Aarti: turning fear into strength
Twenty-two-year-old Anita Kumari's father is a daily-wage labourer, and when the chance came to train on heavy vehicles in Aurangabad, even arranging the cost of getting there was a challenge.
"When I first saw a heavy vehicle, I was afraid. Could I really drive it?" she says. "Even going for the training was a worry. But slowly I understood the vehicle and my fear disappeared. Given the chance and the right training, girls are behind in nothing."
Twenty-one-year-old Aarti Kumari, from Sikarhatta Khurd in Bhojpur district, joined Nari Gunjan in 2023, trained on light vehicles and then completed a month-long heavy-vehicle course in Aurangabad.
"At first I didn't even know whether I could drive such a big bus, and many in the village didn't believe it either," she says. "But my parents always stood by me. Pappu bhaiya and Sudha didi told me to learn instead of being afraid." She now wants other girls in her village to find the courage to make their own career decisions.
Baby and Gayatri: a new road to self-reliance
Twenty-two-year-old Baby Kumari, from Punpun Dehri, has been connected to Nari Gunjan since childhood and learned about the driving training while looking for work, completing light vehicles in 2023 and heavy vehicles in 2025. The real challenge waited outside the training centre, where her short height was mocked.
"When I told people I was learning to drive, many mocked my short height and asked how I would drive such a big vehicle," she says. "I heard taunts many times, but I didn't quit. My parents supported me, and Sudha didi and Pappu bhaiya kept encouraging me." For her, driving a Pink Bus is now a matter of self-respect.
Twenty-two-year-old Gayatri Kumari, from Paimar Ghat in Punpun block, also comes from the Mahadalit community. Educated at a Nari Gunjan centre, she completed Classes 10 and 12 and is now doing a BA. She trained on light vehicles in 2023 and heavy vehicles in 2025 before being selected as a Pink Bus driver.
"My bond with Nari Gunjan goes back to childhood, and that is where my education began," she says. "When the chance to learn driving came, my family stood by me. Today I am studying as well as handling the Pink Bus, and my mother is part of a women's band too. Seeing this change in our family, I feel that if women are given the chance, the thinking of an entire generation can change."
Saraswati: an identity built at the wheel
For 21-year-old Saraswati Kumari of Paimar Ghat, the Pink Bus is a journey of building her own identity. Connected to Nari Gunjan since childhood, she studied in the classes run in her village and later trained on light and heavy vehicles. At first she too held the notion so often heard in society, that driving such a large vehicle is a man's job, but the training changed that thinking. In the village she was advised to become a doctor or teacher; she took it as a challenge.
"The first time I went for training, I felt driving a bus was a boys' job and I wouldn't manage it," she says. "But the teachers boosted my morale. When I returned, people said a girl can't drive a bus. I thought, when others can learn, why can't I?"
The Pink Bus has become her identity. Her most special moments come when a woman passenger, seeing her at the wheel, says she too wants to learn to drive. "I feel our hard work is paving the way not only for us but for other girls as well," she says.
Bihar's Pink Bus service was launched to give women safe and convenient public transport, but an important part of the story reaches the women driving them. Commercial and heavy-vehicle driving has long been male-dominated, so these young women reaching the driver's seat is a small but significant part of a larger picture: women's participation in employment.
That participation has risen in recent years. According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation's (MoSPI) Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, the Labour Force Participation Rate for women aged 15 and above was 41.7 percent, up from 23.3 percent in 2017-18. Even so, their presence in traditionally male-dominated sectors such as transport remains limited.
By completing training, licensing and selection, these six women have made a place in a profession where, only a few years ago, even imagining an opportunity was difficult. Their identity is shaped not by hardship, taunts and lack of opportunity, but by their decision to overcome them. Mothers in particular have been central, having worked in fields and homes to fund their daughters' education; now those daughters are trying to change the family's financial picture.
On the roads of Patna, these women give no speeches each day; their presence says enough. Their journey does not end at the driver's seat. Perhaps the real journey begins right here, as daughters in Bihar no longer just choose their destination but take the steering wheel to get there themselves.

articles.title: Durante 20 años la solución a un Windows lento fue comprar más RAM. Microsoft admite que ahora le toca a él resolverlo
articles.text:
De ahorrar para comprar un PC Gaming a pedir presupuesto solo para un componente: el encarecimiento de la memoria RAM por el auge de los centros de datos ha hecho que renovar el PC sea Misión Imposible. Al menos para quienes no tenemos tanto dinero como Tom Cruise. Así que, si no hay forma de obtener mayores capacidades para los equipos, el paso lógico siguiente es ajustar el sistema para que funcione mejor con menos. Ese es el camino que se ha marcado Microsoft con Windows.
No nos quitamos de encima los 8 GB. Esta cifra parece anticuada, casi un dinosaurio en una época donde lo más óptimo es partir de 32 GB de memoria RAM. Dado que con solo usar el navegador web este se merienda gran parte de la tarta, convivir con menos a menudo supone lidiar con un sistema lento, inestable y, sobre todo, poco satisfactorio. Por eso Microsoft tiene planteada una meta: optimizar Windows para reducir sus requisitos de memoria.
A falta de más memoria, optimización. Los sistemas operativos, tanto de escritorio como móviles, se acostumbraron a que la solución para las apps más voraces fuese crecer en memoria RAM. Durante el tiempo que resultaba más o menos asequible esto tenía sentido, ahora ha dejado de tenerlo. Pavan Davuluri, actual presidente de la división de Windows y dispositivos, ha trazado un plan de cara a lo que queda de 2026 con cuatro áreas en la diana:
- Onboarding y configuración inicial de Windows.
- Optimización de memoria para 8 GB y superiores.
- Funciones de familia.
- Entrada por voz.
La que más ha llamado la atención es la de la memoria. Microsoft ya venía trabajando en la optimización del sistema, pero es ahora cuando le pone nombre y fecha. Davuluri no menciona en ningún momento el encarecimiento de la RAM, pero la conexión es más que plausible: con los precios de la DRAM disparados por [el cuello de botella que ha creado la IA en hardware doméstico](https://app.notion.com/p/ivanli/...), adelgazar el sistema deja de ser una mejora deseable para convertirse en la única salida.
La receta. Anunciar que optimizas un coloso como Windows está bien, el caso es saber la mejor manera de hacerlo. Microsoft no ha detallado cómo piensa recortar el consumo de memoria de Windows en los equipos de 8 GB, sí ha enumerado las tres vías en las que viene trabajando la eficiencia de memoria del sistema:
- Un asignador de memoria más eficiente con el que reducir la sobrecarga en aplicaciones y componentes.
- Un ajuste constante en el marco de desarrollo WinUI 3 para que las aplicaciones construidas sobre esta base consuman menos memoria por diseño.
- Reducción del consumo para los componentes de Chromium y WebView2 allí donde se integran en el sistema operativo.
Es razonable pensar que las anteriores vías son las mismas sobre las que Microsoft va a seguir trabajando. Es un trío que debería aportar una mayor experiencia con Windows a quienes deben ejecutarlo en equipos ajustados de memoria: desde PCs domésticos a los destinados a la enseñanza.
Falta lo importante: cuánto y cuándo. Microsoft no ha detallado los megas que la optimización podría ahorrar, tampoco una comparativa con el antes y el después de aplicar los cambios. Pavan Davuluri solo explicó que las mejoras han ido llegando a los Insiders durante los últimos meses y que empezarán a desplegarse de forma amplia en los PCs con Windows 11 a partir del otoño.
Hasta la optimización, y siempre que realmente sea efectiva, quien tenga 8 GB seguirá viendo cómo el sistema se lleva por delante una buena porción de esa memoria sin abrir nada. Y ahí está lo incómodo del asunto: durante años, la respuesta de la industria a un Windows pesado fue vender más RAM para alimentarlo. A él y a las aplicaciones, casi tan mal optimizadas como el propio sistema. Y ahora que la RAM es un componente de lujo, resulta que sí había margen para una operación bikini. Estuvo ahí todo el tiempo.

articles.title: Microsoft explique pourquoi il est si difficile de moderniser l'interface de Windows 11
articles.text:
Pourquoi les entrailles de Windows prennent-elles autant de temps à être modernisées ? C’est la question que Windows Central a eu l’occasion de poser — dans le contexte d’un échange plus largement consacré à l’interface de Windows 11 — au vice-président chargé de la conception et de la recherche pour Windows chez Microsoft : Marcus Ash.
L’intéressé s’est donc exprimé en détail sur les difficultés rencontrées par Microsoft pour réussir à remettre au goût du jour l’intégralité de Windows et notamment les éléments d’interface « Legacy » qui peuplent toujours les tréfonds de Windows 11.
Parmi eux, le Panneau de configuration. Sorte de baromètre des efforts de modernisation entrepris par Microsoft, ce panneau a commencé à être remanié il y a 13 ans, sous Windows 8… et le travail est encore loin d’être achevé, admet Marcus Ash.
Pourquoi ? Parce que Microsoft ne peut pas se précipiter et tout moderniser sans s’assurer au préalable que les nouvelles solutions assurent le même niveau de fonctionnalité que les anciennes.
Une modernisation très incrémentielle… pour de bonnes raisons
« C’est pour cela que des éléments comme le Panneau de configuration posent problème, car si un client dispose d’un pilote ou d’un élément qui dépend de cette fonctionnalité ‘Legacy’, nous devons simplement veiller à ne pas rompre cette promesse de compatibilité. Lorsque nous aurons enfin tout transféré dans les Paramètres, nous déprécierons alors les éléments du Panneau de configuration, par exemple, pour lesquels cette fonction n’est plus nécessaire, et nous pourrons la faire évoluer », explique Marcus Ash.
Le cadre de Microsoft indique néanmoins que la présence d’éléments « Legacy » hérités de vieilles versions de Windows dans Windows 11 rend l’OS de Microsoft plus solide en tant que plateforme. Il faut effectivement admettre qu’en la matière, Microsoft fait primer un niveau de compatibilité étendu sur la cohérence esthétique de son système d’exploitation.
« Il y aura des cas où, parce qu’un client souhaite disposer d’une fonctionnalité qui lui tient à cœur, nous devrons conserver certaines interfaces utilisateur ‘Legacy’, mais même dans ces situations, nous essayons de déterminer s’il existe des moyens, grâce à des outils et à de meilleures approches, de réduire progressivement ce phénomène au fil du temps. »
Autre moment intéressant de l’échange entre Windows Central et Marcus Ash : le passage où l’on apprend comment Microsoft détermine quels pans de l’interface doivent (ou peuvent) être modernisés en priorité.
La télémétrie à la rescousse
« Cela repose sur l’utilisation, les données télémétriques et les retours d’expérience. Nous nous demandons notamment : dans quels domaines estimons-nous que nos outils sont prêts à faire évoluer cette interface ? … Nous continuons simplement à analyser ces éléments et à veiller à ce qu’au fil du temps, la part d’interface utilisateur héritée que le client voit dans son expérience quotidienne ne cesse de diminuer. »
Ces efforts commencent à payer avec les dernières versions de Windows 11, qui ne recourent plus que très ponctuellement aux éléments « Legacy » du noyau Windows.
Et quant aux outils n’ayant toujours pas évolué d’un iota, comme l’éditeur de registre, patience : Microsoft se concentre évidemment sur les éléments les plus utilisés et visibles de Windows 11. Ces outils ne sont donc pas prioritaires, comme on pouvait s’en douter. Cela dit, Microsoft a semble-t-il commencé à se pencher sur cet épineux dossier.
« Je dirais que les éléments que nous examinons généralement sont ceux que les utilisateurs et les clients attendent le plus : l’Explorateur de fichiers et certaines des principales applications. Mais même pour des outils comme Regedit et certains autres, nous commençons déjà à nous pencher sur la question et à réfléchir à la manière d’aborder ce problème afin de respecter notre engagement en matière de compatibilité ET de moderniser ces infrastructures. »
Reste à savoir si tout sera enfin modernisé d’ici au lancement de Windows 12. Puisque ce dernier n’est visiblement pas près d’arriver, tous les espoirs sont permis.

articles.title: Buying crypto in Nigeria just got more expensive under new rules
articles.text:
Every time someone buys Bitcoin, the stablecoin USDT, or another cryptocurrency in Nigeria, the government will take a share of the transaction — and it wants that tax remitted in the same digital asset being traded.
New virtual asset tax guidelines issued by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) on Monday impose a 1.5% stamp duty on token-to-fiat and fiat-to-token transfers. Rather than deducting the levy from a buyer’s bank account, registered crypto exchanges and other virtual asset service providers (VASPs) must withhold the tax from the digital assets credited to a buyer’s wallet before remitting it to the government.
“Income tax deducted at source and stamp duty shall be remitted to the Service in the originating token of the transaction,” the tax authority said.
The guidelines represent Nigeria’s most comprehensive attempt yet to bring cryptocurrency transactions into the country’s tax system. In addition to introducing a 1.5% stamp duty on eligible virtual asset transactions, they effectively turn crypto exchanges into tax collectors by requiring them to deduct taxes in digital assets before users receive their tokens. The framework also clarifies how income tax, value-added tax (VAT), and stamp duty will apply to activities including trading, staking, mining, and other virtual asset transactions.
“These Guidelines are issued for the information and guidance of taxpayers, Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), Peer-to-Peer (P2P) marketplace operators, tax consultants, financial institutions, and all persons engaged in Virtual Assets (VA) activities,” the NRS wrote.
To illustrate how the levy works, the NRS noted: “User A pays ₦1,000,000 to acquire 1 BTC at a market price of ₦1,000,000 per BTC. Stamp duty at 1.5% = 0.015 BTC withheld from token credited to User A.”
“Net BTC credited to User A = 0.985 BTC. Seller receives ₦1,000,000 in full. VASP remits 0.015 BTC to NRS. User A later sells 0.985 BTC at ₦2,000,000 per BTC (proceeds = ₦1,970,000). User A receives ₦1,970,000 in full. Buyer receives 0.985 BTC less 1.5% stamp duty = 0.970225 BTC.”
The new rules go beyond the ₦50 ($0.037) stamp duty that already applies to electronic withdrawals of ₦10,000 ($7.33) and above. In January, exchanges such as Quidax notified users that the charge would apply to qualifying naira withdrawals under the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA) 2025.
“We’d like to share a quick update regarding recent changes under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and how they affect your Quidax withdrawals,” Quidax told customers in an email on January 15, 2026. “Going forward, a ₦50 stamp duty charge will apply to any withdrawal of ₦10,000 or more.”
The latest guidelines introduce a separate 1.5% stamp duty on eligible virtual asset transactions and extend to transactions facilitated through a VASP or other recognised intermediary, where the VASP or intermediary shall deduct and remit the applicable stamp duty. Where a virtual asset is used to settle a transaction that independently attracts stamp duty under the NTA, the applicable duty on the underlying instrument is also payable.
For crypto users, the practical effect means buying digital assets now becomes more expensive. Every eligible transaction now carries a 1.5% stamp duty, while users may also incur VAT on exchange service fees and income tax where gains arise, depending on the nature of the transaction.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks.

articles.title: Palantir shares jump 12% as revenue nearly doubles and guidance climbs again - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Palantir shares jump 12% as revenue nearly doubles and guidance climbs again
Shares in Palantir Technologies Inc. surged more than 12% in late trading today after the big data analytics company crushed second-quarter expectations and raised its full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter.
For its fiscal 2026 second quarter that ended on June 30, Palantir reported adjusted earnings per share of 41 cents, up from 16 cents per share in the same quarter of last year, on revenue of $1.935 billion, up 93% year-over-year. Both figures came in ahead of the 35 cents per share and revenue of $1.81 billion expected by analysts.
Notably, the 93% revenue increase topped the 85% increase posted in the first quarter, which had been the company’s previous record.
U.S. revenue grew 115%, to $1.573 billion. Commercial customers in the U.S. accounted for $764 million of that, a 149% rise. The government side of the domestic business reached $809 million, up 90%.
Deal counts kept climbing. Palantir closed 220 contracts worth at least $1 million during the quarter, among them 98 above $5 million and 73 above $10 million. Total contract value came in at $3.373 billion, up 49% year-over-year. U.S. commercial contract value hit a record $2.132 billion, a 153% increase. U.S. commercial remaining deal value, contracted revenue not yet recognized, ended June at $6.238 billion, up 124% year-over-year.
Net income attributable to common stockholders came in at $1.062 billion, more than triple the $326.7 million booked a year earlier. Adjusted operating income was $1.194 billion on a 62% margin. Unadjusted operating income of $912 million worked out to a 47% margin. Cash from operations reached $1.216 billion and adjusted free cash flow $1.220 billion.
The company ended the quarter with $9.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term U.S. Treasury securities. Its Rule of 40 score, the sum of revenue growth and adjusted operating margin, hit 155%.
“Demand for AI sovereignty has now been unleashed. And Palantir is the only company that has demonstrated it can transform tokens into actual economic value,” co-founder and Chief Executive Alex Karp said in the company’s earnings release. “This quarter was otherworldly.”
For the third quarter, Palantir guided to revenue of $2.160 billion to $2.164 billion, roughly 8% above analyst estimates, with adjusted operating income of $1.292 billion to $1.296 billion.
Full-year revenue guidance went up to between $8.150 billion and $8.158 billion, growth of about 82%. Three months ago, the company was pointing at $7.65 billion to $7.662 billion. U.S. commercial revenue is now expected to top $3.424 billion, a gain of at least 134%. Adjusted operating income guidance was lifted to $4.889 billion to $4.897 billion and adjusted free cash flow guidance to $4.5 billion to $4.7 billion.
Palantir shares had fallen about 40% from their fourth-quarter 2025 peak heading into the results, and options traders had positioned for a swing of 12% in either direction. Baird analyst William Power had a $200 price target on the stock heading into the report, calling it the ‘premier AI growth asset.’

articles.title: Lego deploys Hubble Space Telescope as detailed desktop model
articles.text:
For 35 years, the Hubble Space Telescope has looked out into the Universe. Now, Lego is inviting builders to look inward with its latest model of the orbiting observatory.
The new Lego Icons Hubble Space Telescope (set no. 11382) was released on August 1 for $140 at the toy company’s stores and its online shop. The 1,252-piece kit builds a 15-inch-long (38-cm) desktop model that is about twice as large as the previously released Lego Hubble models.
The Icons Hubble is the first to be sized in comparison to a Lego minifigure, such that the included astronaut provides a sense of scale for the telescope.
Of the previous three Hubble models, two were scaled to their companion orbiters: Lego Discovery Space Shuttle—STS-31, set 7470, from 2003 and Lego Icons NASA Space Shuttle Discovery, 10283, released in 2021. The third was a desktop model for the minifigure tribute to astronomer Nancy Grace Roman, the “Mother of Hubble,” included with the Women of NASA set, no. 21312, in 2017.
The real Hubble Space Telescope was launched on the space shuttle Discovery and deployed by the STS-31 crew in 1990. It is 43.5 feet long (13.2 meters), making the new Lego desktop model about 1:35 scale. (Lego minifigure scale is generally accepted to be between 1:35 and 1:45 scale, as the minifigures are not proportionally accurate.)
Open wide (field camera)
According to the set’s instruction book, in addition to being faithful to the overall shape and exterior details of the Hubble Space Telescope, the new Lego Icons model is the first to build representations of the science instruments and interior components that enable Hubble to operate in Earth orbit.
“In close collaboration with our partners at NASA and ESA, we’ve recreated authentic engineering details inside and out,” reads the designers’ introduction to the set in the book. “Each section of your model corresponds to real instruments that helped discover remarkable new information about our universe.”
The aperture door at the top of the telescope opens, affording a view of the secondary mirror assembly inside. Two panels along the upper and lower body of the Hubble can also be removed to expose the mirrors, as well as the central baffle that directs the light from stars and galaxies to the observatory’s instruments and primary mirror.

articles.title: Windows 11 vai rodar bem com 8 GB de RAM, promete Microsoft • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Windows 11 vai rodar bem com 8 GB de RAM, promete Microsoft
Aparentemente, atual cenário de escassez de memória fez Microsoft reconhecer que Windows 11 precisa ser otimizado para demandar menos RAM.
Hoje, é importante contar com pelo menos 16 GB de RAM para rodar o Windows 11 satisfatoriamente. Mas módulos de memória estão escassos no mercado. Aparentemente, esse cenário forçou a Microsoft a fazer uma promessa inesperada: otimizar o sistema operacional para trabalhar bem com 8 GB de RAM.
Não é que essa quantidade não seja suportada. Os requisitos de hardware do Windows 11 exigem pelo menos 4 GB de RAM, com o mínimo recomendado de 8 GB. Mas, para que você possa usar o sistema com risco reduzido de gargalos, o ideal são pelo menos 16 GB de memória — para jogos pesados ou tarefas muito exigentes, o mínimo pode ficar em 32 GB.
Até um passado recente, costumávamos resolver determinados problemas de desempenho no computador simplesmente aumentando a quantidade de RAM. Mas, com o atual cenário de escassez de memória, essa é uma decisão que precisa ser bem pensada.
Mas vai além. A própria indústria de PCs tem tido dificuldades para lançar modelos com quantidades mais generosas de memória RAM porque esse componente tem deixado os preços muito elevados. Uma abordagem paliativa tem sido a de lançar modelos mais acessíveis que, como tal, oferecem menos RAM. É nesse ponto que a medida anunciada pela Microsoft passa a fazer sentido.
Em março, a Microsoft havia prometido melhorar vários aspectos do Windows 11 para aprimorar a experiência do usuário com o sistema operacional. Recentemente, Pavan Davuluri, chefe da divisão Windows, deu continuidade a essa promessa.
Entre os avanços que o executivo destacou está justamente o da memória RAM:
Otimização de memória para 8 GB ou mais: redução do consumo de memória do Windows [11] para proporcionar uma experiência rápida e responsiva em todos os PCs que os clientes usam diariamente.
Pavan Davuluri, chefe da divisão Windows
Ainda não está claro como, exatamente, a Microsoft otimizará o consumo de RAM pelo Windows 11. Mas já há alguns esforços nesse sentido. Um exemplo recente: a companhia tem trabalhado para modernizar aplicativos nativos de modo a fazê-los justamente consumir menos RAM.
Isso será feito, em grande parte, por meio da atualização da WinUI, a biblioteca de interface gráfica que é usada no desenvolvimento de aplicativos e recursos modernos do Windows.
Para quando? A expectativa é a de que essa otimização, bem como outras mudanças no sistema operacional, cheguem aos usuários até o fim de 2026, embora me pareça que parte dos aprimoramentos só se tornará realidade no próximo ano.
Coincidência ou não, as promessas de Davuluri chegaram quase ao mesmo tempo em que Satya Nadella reafirmou o compromisso da Microsoft de melhorar o Windows 11.
A diferença é que a afirmação do CEO da companhia foi mais protocolar, afinal, foi dada durante uma conferência sobre os últimos resultados financeiros da Microsoft. Já Davuluri tratou dos aspectos técnicos com muito mais detalhes.

articles.title: La drástica decisión de Samsung con el Galaxy S27 Ultra para reducir costes
articles.text:
Los Galaxy S27 todavía están a varios meses de distancia, pero los rumores sobre los próximos buques insignia de Samsung son cosa prácticamente diaria. En esta oportunidad, un nuevo reporte del portal coreano ET News revela importantes novedades en las cámaras de los dispositivos, con un cambio drástico en el Galaxy S27 Ultra.
De acuerdo con el citado medio, Samsung eliminará una de las cámaras del Galaxy S27 Ultra. Si la noticia te suena un poco conocida es porque el dato ya lleva algún tiempo en circulación. A finales de abril pasado surgieron los primeros comentarios respecto de la presunta quita de uno de los sensores del modelo más premium de la gama, que la nueva publicación ratifica.
Tal y como se había comentado por entonces, el Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra diría adiós al teleobjetivo con zoom óptico de 3 aumentos. El fabricante coreano no lo reemplazaría, sino que directamente lo quitaría del móvil, que a partir de esta versión se lanzaría con tres cámaras en lugar de cuatro.
La información que suma el reporte que llega desde Corea del Sur es que la determinación sería pura y exclusivamente económica. Según parece, el objetivo de Samsung al eliminar el teleobjetivo 3x del Galaxy S27 Ultra es reducir costes, algo crucial en un momento en el que otros componentes como la RAM y el almacenamiento escasean y se venden a precios altísimos.
El Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra tendrá 3 cámaras para reducir costes
Quitar el teleobjetivo 3x del Galaxy S27 Ultra posiblemente sea la decisión de menor impacto para Samsung al reducir costes. Después de todo, es una cámara bastante criticada por sus limitaciones y falta de versatilidad. Además, el componente no desaparecería del catálogo de móviles de la marca, sino que se reubicaría en el nuevo modelo Pro.
Todo apunta a que la familia S27 se compondrá de cuatro modelos en lugar de tres, por lo que el reordenamiento de las cámaras también ayudaría a diferenciar los modelos de mayores prestaciones. De acuerdo con la más reciente filtración, la oferta de cámaras en los próximos buques insignia de Samsung sería la siguiente:
- Galaxy S27 y S27+: cámara principal de 50 megapíxeles, ultra gran angular de 12 megapíxeles y teleobjetivo de 10 megapíxeles.
- Galaxy S27 Pro: cámara principal de 200 megapíxeles, ultra gran angular de 50 megapíxeles y teleobjetivo de 10 megapíxeles con zoom óptico de 3 aumentos.
- Galaxy S27 Ultra: cámara principal de 200 megapíxeles, ultra gran angular de 50 megapíxeles y teleobjetivo de 10 megapíxeles con zoom óptico de 5 aumentos.
Todavía faltan varios meses para que el Galaxy S27 Ultra y sus hermanos lleguen al mercado. Si Samsung mantiene la estrategia de los últimos años, los modelos en cuestión deberían lanzarse en los primeros meses de 2027. Esto significa que hay tiempo de sobra para más rumores y filtraciones antes de su debut formal, como ya es costumbre de cada año.

articles.title: The studio behind Pokémon struggles to find its voice in Beast of Reincarnation
articles.text:
You have to imagine that the team at Game Freak is bursting with ideas. The studio puts out new mainline Pokémon adventures with a machinelike precision. But every so often it launches a curious experiment, whether it’s an action title about a militarized elephant or turning horse races into a card game, showing that it’s capable of more than the latest generation of pocket monsters. That’s part of what makes the idea of Beast of Reincarnation so enticing. Here is an established studio breaking free of the franchise it has become known for to make its take on a blockbuster action game. Unfortunately new ideas are in short supply in Beast, and aside from its slick action, there’s little that hasn’t been done before.
The studio behind Pokémon struggles to find its voice in Beast of Reincarnation
Game Freak’s new action game is full of ideas you’ve seen and played before.
Beast of Reincarnation takes place exactly 2,000 years in the future in a postapocalyptic vision of Japan that blends sci-fi and magic. Humans still exist, though many of them transferred their consciousness to robotic golems in order to survive the calamity that ruined the world. The real problem is that a mysterious blight has infected the landscape, turning wildlife into vicious, mutated monsters. Even worse: This seems to portend the return of the titular beast, a powerful creature that, as its name implies, appears to be immortal. You play as a wandering mercenary-type named Emma who has the ability to absorb the powers of fallen mutants, and soon she’s tasked with traversing the world to power up so that she can take down the beast for good.
It’s not a bad setup for an action game, as it gives you a reason to keep moving forward. Emma is constantly on the hunt for the next big creature that she can use to get stronger before taking on her final task. Beast of Reincarnation isn’t an open-world game, but instead is divided into a series of big locations that you travel between as the story progresses.
The standout feature of the game is its action. Emma is a speedy samurai type, wielding a blade and various bows. At first, Beast seems like Dark Souls or Elden Ring, a game built around dodging and parrying, with little room for error. But as you unlock new powers, it proves to be something a little different. Emma’s signature ability is that vines and plants can grow out of her hair. This sounds weird, but it’s also incredibly useful; she can build bridges to traverse big gaps, or use her hair like a grappling hook to reach locations up high. She also has an adorable and gigantic magical dog companion who follows her everywhere and provides a hand with combat and tedious chores like collecting loot.
Emma’s powers are especially helpful in battle. Slowly she gains abilities that let her zip around the battlefield, using her hair to quickly gain ground on an enemy, deliver an attack from above, or team up with her powerful pup for a devastating blow. Her hair can even improve your stealth: At one point I unlocked a skill that caused tall plants to sprout wherever I crouched, temporarily giving me some cover before delivering a silent kill. It takes a few hours for things to open up, but eventually Beast’s combat has plenty of room for freedom and creativity.
The same can’t be said for the rest of the experience. Initially, Beast’s postapocalyptic world is compelling because it’s full of mystery. You know almost nothing about the history of the world, but there are hints of interesting dynamics, like the human-infused machines and how they evolved differently from flesh-and-blood people. But Beast pushes the idea of mystery to a frustrating extreme. Everything in this game is mysterious: the landscape, Emma herself, her two human travel companions, her giant dog, the little girl that only Emma can see, the other wandering fighters she encounters in the world. I love a story that is full of secrets and intrigue, but I barely understood what I was even doing in Beast until at least a dozen hours into the game. It doesn’t help that the game hides explanations of many of its key elements in a tutorial menu. And when you do finally get answers to the big mysteries, they’re mostly underwhelming.
The story isn’t the only place that feels underdeveloped or uninspired. There are a number of gameplay elements — like the ability to grow your own food, and a weapon upgrade system — that are so simple that it’s easy to forget about them altogether. Meanwhile, the level design is incredibly straightforward, making exploration a bore, particularly when it comes to the dead-simple platforming sections. The game’s skill tree is even a literal tree.
But the real issue with Beast of Reincarnation is that it is full of ideas that already exist elsewhere. The story is like a watered-down version of Nier: Automata’s heartrending postapocalypse, while the boss battles feel ripped out of Monster Hunter (with designs straight from its contemporary Wild Hearts and one specific creature that looks identical to a Stranger Things demodog). Your mobile home base functions much like the one in Death Stranding — you can even shower — and it looks just like an AT-ST from Star Wars. Everywhere you go, there’s something from a different game or movie.
This is especially disappointing because there is so much potential in Beast of Reincarnation. Not only is the combat thrilling, but, as derivative as it is, the game still manages to create an incredible sense of melancholic moodiness through its sound and visuals. But it never delivers on that; I was excited to learn about the strange religions and customs that were developed by isolated groups of golem, for instance, but the revelations were all surface level and quickly brushed aside.
That sums up much of the Beast experience: There are flashes of excitement and intrigue, but mostly you’ve seen all of this before. At least there’s more Pokémon on the way.
Beast of Reincarnation launches on August 4th on the PS5, Xbox, and PC.

articles.title: Research Bits: Aug. 4
articles.text:
Stretchable electronics: Switchable analog, digital organic transistor; thread-based ICs; temporary e-tattoo electrodes.
Researchers from Pusan National University developed a stretchable organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) that can be reprogrammed to serve different purposes.
The device operates by moving ions through the conducting polymer PEDOT:PSS, which was modified with additives to improve electrical conductivity and improve its ability to stretch without degrading.
Changing the concentration of sodium chloride in the electrolyte alters how ions move through the transistor. High salt concentrations enabled rapid ON/OFF gating for digital logic computations, while lower salt concentrations produced an analog memory-like behavior that can act as an artificial synapse. The switching is reversible and is accompanied by the device changing color.
“The proposed platform is suitable for smart electronic skin, wearable health monitors, and soft bioelectronic implants, where a single stretchable device can both process and store physiological signals without added circuitry,” said Hyunseok Shim, an assistant professor in the School of Electronics and Electrical Engineering at Pusan National University, in a statement. “In the longer term, this work could lead to autonomous personalized therapeutics, such as dynamic compression bandages and electronic skins that respond to injury in real time, all monitored at a glance through a visible color change.”
As a proof of concept, the team built a wearable patch that senses inflammatory edema and skin temperature, then automatically tightens or loosens a compression band, reducing the risk of tissue damage. [1]
Researchers at Tufts University designed thread-based integrated circuits that can bend, coil, and stretch for wearable electronics or textiles.
The device uses thin threads coated with gold, to which flexible organic eutectogel-gated electrochemical transistors are attached. The deep eutectic solvents, or eutectogels, act as nonvolatile dielectrics that provide stable transistor performance without the need for encapsulation and avoid some of the challenges of hydrogels like drying out.
“By moving electronics from planar patches to free-form threads, we have opened a path toward wearable bioelectronics that are more like fibers than hardware,” said Sameer Sonkusale, a professor in the School of Engineering at Tufts, in a press release. “They will be soft, stretchable and able to follow the body’s shape rather than forcing the body to accommodate the device. They could even potentially be used like sutures to monitor processes inside the body.”
The researchers created several circuits to demonstrate the approach: a sensor signal amplifier, a wearable monitor that can be placed on the temple to detect blinking, and a device placed near the diaphragm to detect changes in breathing patterns and rates.
“The technology platform is still in early stages,” added Wenxin Zeng, Ph.D. candidate in electrical engineering at Tufts, in a press release. “But we expect to improve the speed and precision of fabrication, and the ability of the thread-based integrated circuits to carry out more complex functions.” [2]
Researchers from Penn State University developed a conductive ink that can be painted on the skin in various colors and patterns, creating temporary e-tattoos that act as electrodes to record electrical signals that indicate heart, muscle, and brain activity.
The ink is made from several different types of polymers mixed with acidic additives into a water-based solution, with a glue-like consistency when wet. It can be pigmented with food dyes to paint electrodes with personalized designs and can dry onto skin in less than 10 minutes. A porous, silver textile is attached to the skin’s surface with a portion of the paint and then connected to a larger module that transmits signals using Bluetooth.
The textile’s porous structure allows the electrodes to stretch to over 150% their original size without breaking. It also adheres better to skin, resulting in better conductivity particularly in the presence of hair or sweat, which can create challenges for typical electrodes.
In tests, the device tracked ECG readings over the course of 12 hours, during exercise, and enabled a user to control a robot prosthetic using muscle signals.
“Although we tested the daily use application over a 12-hour period, this is not the limit for these electrodes,” said Larry Cheng, professor of engineering science and mechanics at Penn State, in a press release. “The electrodes themselves can be washed away and easily reapplied. The big idea behind this is that in the future, you could potentially have a more expensive sensing module that remains separate from the system, but the electrodes themselves can be disposable. A single bottle of ink could provide enough material to paint multiple electrodes over the course of several days or a week.”
The team plans to continue developing the electrodes to potentially enable more advanced health sensing of biomarkers like cortisol or glucose. [3]
[1] H. Kim, T. Kim, Y. Kim, et al. Fully Stretchable Ionically Tunable Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Wearable Adaptive Logic Bioelectronics. ACS Nano (2026) 20 (26): 18883–18899. https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.6c05309
[2] W. Zeng, R. E. Owyeung, N. I. Hossain, et al. Free-Form Three-Dimensional Integrated Circuits on a Thread Using Organic Eutectogel-Gated Electrochemical Transistors. ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces (2026) 18 (21): 30211–30226. https://doi.org/10.1021/acsami.5c25103
[3] W. Zhang, X. Xin, Y. Wang, et al. Paintable on-skin dry electrodes with robust skin and device connection for wireless sensing and human–machine interfaces, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 123 (29) e2615835123, (2026). https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2615835123

articles.title: Shigeru Miyamoto révèle que le B-Dash de Super Mario Bros était un bug de collision
articles.text:
Père, entre autres, de Mario, Shigeru Miyamoto a une tonne d’anecdotes à raconter. Et, justement, il en a partagé une croustillante à propos du plombier à l’occasion d’un entretien paru dans le magazine Casa Brutus (via NintendoEverything le 1er août 2026). Elle concerne l’un des mouvements les plus iconiques de Mario : le B-Dash.
Depuis le tout premier jeu paru sur NES dans les années 80, Mario est capable de sprinter. Cette capacité lui ouvre la porte à d’autres mouvements intéressants, comme des sauts plus hauts et plus longs ou, encore, la capacité de « survoler » des petits vides, sans oublier l’impact sur le speedrunning. Cette aptitude, assez impressionnante en jeu, était en réalité un bug à l’origine. Bug que Shigeru Miyamoto a préféré conserver, sachant que le B-Dash existe encore dans les jeux Mario 2D les plus récents (comme Super Mario Bros. Wonder).
Le B-Dash de Mario était un bug
Shigeru Miyamoto révèle : « Vous connaissez le B-Dash de Mario, n’est-ce pas ? Si vous maintenez le bouton B enfoncé tout en courant, il peut franchir de petits trous sans tomber — c’est une petite triche. À vrai dire, c’était en réalité un bug causé par une détection de collision avec le sol défectueuse. Quand le programmeur s’en est rendu compte, il a dit : ‘Pardon ? Il n’est pas tombé !’ et a voulu le corriger. Mais je lui ai dit : ‘Non, non ! C’est amusant s’il peut franchir les trous en sprintant — laissons ça comme ça !’ Alors nous l’avons gardé. »
Le B-Dash est tellement devenu légendaire qu’il existe un kart B Dasher dans Mario Kart DS, en référence à cette aptitude, et que l’expression est devenue courante parmi les joueuses et les joueurs japonais (en lien avec la capacité de sprinter ou, plus littéralement, la fameuse expression « piquer un sprint »). Il y a même eu un groupe de pop B-Dash, créé en 1997 et séparé en 2017. Le terme B-Dash est donc très répandu au Japon.
À noter que Super Mario Bros. a eu d’autres problèmes techniques ayant abouti à des mécaniques phares de la saga. Outre le B-Dash, Shigeru Miyamoto raconte que le bloc caché est lié à « un bug qui faisait apparaître des pièces dans les airs alors qu’il n’y avait rien à la base ». On imagine qu’il y a bien d’autres bugs devenus des opportunités de gameplay, surtout en provenance d’une saga aussi incroyable et riche comme Mario.

articles.title: Egyptian CNC startup Simplex expands to 10th of Ramadan City with $50m facility - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Simplex, which specialises in computer numerical control (CNC) machine manufacturing, has officially inaugurated its latest industrial expansion in 10th of Ramadan City, with a 40,000 square metre facility costing US$50 million.
Computer numerical control (CNC) is a manufacturing method that automates the control, movement and precision of machine tools through the use of preprogrammed computer software, which is embedded inside the tools.
A graduate of the Flat6Labs accelerator programme, Simplex specialises in manufacturing CNC machines, and provides advanced technological solutions that meet the needs of customers in various industrial sectors. It has successfully built a strong reputation in regional and global markets.
The ceremony brought His Excellency Dr. Ahmed Kouchouk, Minister of Finance; and a lot of investors; alongside elite international partners, diplomats, and senior government representatives. They were received by the co-founders of Simplex, Eng. Ahmed Shaaban and Eng. Mohamed Mansour.
Attendees toured the facility, showcasing Simplex’s growth journey as a leader in localizing CNC machinery manufacturing. The tour included the official ribbon-cutting for the new company’s second factory followed by a comprehensive walkthrough of its assembly divisions, production lines, and advanced technologies.
Aligning with its regional growth strategy, Simplex signed new partnership and agency agreements in both Jordan and Kuwait, reflecting the accelerating footprint of Egyptian engineering products and solutions in Arab markets.
“This celebration stands as a testament to what Egyptian youth can accomplish when given the opportunity and support. Simplex began as a graduation project and has evolved into an enterprise exporting to 34 countries, proving that Egyptian industrial innovation can compete on the global stage,” Shaaban said.

articles.title: EV maker Ather Energy Q1 losses narrow by 71% to Rs 51 crore
articles.text:
EV maker Ather Energy Q1 losses narrow by 71% to Rs 51 Cr
Ather said it is seeing strong tailwinds due to policy support and consumer demand. The company delivered 83,173 units during the quarter, up 80.5% YoY.
Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy’s consolidated net loss narrowed by 71% to Rs 51 crore for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 of FY27) from Rs 178 crore a year ago. It reported a consolidated total income of Rs 1,260 crore for the quarter, up by 87.2% YoY, thanks to a growing contribution from non-vehicle revenue including software subscriptions, charging, accessories, spares, and service.
The quarter also saw consolidated EBITDA turn positive at Rs 9 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with an EBITDA loss of Rs 106 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the company statement. Ather said it delivered 83,173 units during the quarter, up 80.5% YoY.
"We continued to see strong demand across our portfolio, as structural tailwinds from both policy support and shifting customer sentiment translated into a massive upsurge for our products, with demand far outstripping supply. This gives us confidence that the market continues to expand,” said Tarun Mehta, Co-founder and CEO, Ather Energy.
“In the coming months, we are particularly excited about our new product on the EL platform, commencing production alongside the scale-up of our new factory at AURIC. Together, they position us well for the next phase of Ather's growth,” he added.
Ather's Factory 3.0 at AURIC in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar’s Phase 1, with an annual production capacity of 500,000 units, is expected to start production during Q3 FY27. Upon completion of Phase 1 and 2 at AURIC, Ather's total installed annual production capacity across its manufacturing facilities will reach 1.42 million electric two-wheelers.
The company also added that the demand for electric vehicles has increased over the last quarter, with industry registrations increasing 68% YoY to approximately 525,000 units, per Vahan data. EV penetration also crossed 10% for the first time in June 2026.

articles.title: Cybersecurity And IT Support For Productive, Protected Workdays - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Importance of Cybersecurity in Modern Work Environments
In today’s digital-centric business landscape, cybersecurity is no longer a luxury but a necessity. Organizations of all sizes face an increasing risk of cyber threats that can disrupt operations, compromise sensitive data, and cause significant financial losses. According to a recent report, cybercrime damages are expected to reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, up from $3 trillion in 2015, highlighting the exponential growth of this threat. This staggering figure reflects the urgency for businesses to strengthen their defenses against cyberattacks.
The consequences of inadequate cybersecurity are severe. Data breaches can lead to loss of customer trust, legal penalties, and irreparable damage to a company’s reputation. Furthermore, cyberattacks often result in operational downtime, which directly impacts productivity and revenue. In fact, the average cost of a data breach globally reached $4.35 million in 2022, emphasizing the financial stakes involved in protecting digital assets.
For businesses to maintain productive and protected workdays, safeguarding IT infrastructure against evolving cyber risks is critical. This involves not only implementing robust cybersecurity measures but also ensuring that IT support is readily available to address issues promptly and effectively. Proactive management of IT systems helps prevent downtime and data breaches, enhancing overall business continuity and resilience.
Integrating Cybersecurity and IT Support for Optimal Performance
A seamless integration of cybersecurity protocols with comprehensive IT support services is essential for sustaining business productivity. Cybersecurity tools such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and endpoint protection software serve as the first line of defense. However, without expert IT support to monitor, update, and troubleshoot these technologies, organizations remain vulnerable.
Many companies choose to discuss with Bryley Systems to leverage specialized knowledge and tailored cybersecurity strategies. These partnerships enable businesses to stay ahead of threats by adopting the latest security frameworks and best practices. Moreover, a dedicated IT support team can swiftly respond to incidents, minimizing the impact of any security breach or technical glitch.
Effective IT support goes beyond reactive problem solving; it includes ongoing system maintenance, vulnerability assessments, and compliance management. For example, ensuring that software patches and security updates are applied promptly can close exploitable gaps before attackers can take advantage. IT support teams also help enforce cybersecurity policies, such as strong password management and access controls, which are vital for protecting sensitive information.
The Role of IT Support in Enhancing Cybersecurity Posture
IT support teams play a pivotal role in maintaining a secure and efficient technological environment. They conduct regular system audits, apply critical patches, and ensure that all devices comply with security policies. According to a study, 60% of small businesses that experience a cyberattack go out of business within six months, underscoring the importance of ongoing IT support. This statistic highlights how devastating cyber incidents can be without proper IT defense and response.
Outsourcing technology supported by ChaceTech offers businesses access to experienced professionals who can manage complex IT infrastructures while implementing strong cybersecurity measures. This approach not only reduces the risk of cyber incidents but also alleviates the burden on internal staff, allowing them to focus on core business functions. External IT support providers often bring expertise in the latest cybersecurity technologies and threat intelligence, which smaller or resource-constrained companies might lack.
In addition, IT support teams assist with disaster recovery planning and execution. In the event of a cyberattack or system failure, having a tested backup and recovery plan can mean the difference between a brief interruption and prolonged downtime. Regular backups and data recovery drills ensure that businesses can quickly restore operations and minimize losses.
Best Practices for Cybersecurity and IT Support Collaboration
To maximize the benefits of cybersecurity and IT support, organizations should adhere to several best practices:
– Regular Training and Awareness: Employees are often the weakest link in cybersecurity. Regular training ensures staff recognize phishing attempts and understand security protocols. In fact, 91% of successful cyberattacks begin with a phishing email, making employee vigilance crucial.
– Comprehensive Incident Response Plans: Having a well-defined plan allows quick and coordinated action in the event of a cyberattack. This includes clear roles, communication strategies, and mitigation steps to reduce damage.
– Continuous Monitoring and Updates: Cyber threats evolve rapidly. Constant system monitoring and timely updates keep defenses strong. Employing tools like Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) can provide real-time threat detection and response.
– Data Backup and Recovery Solutions: Reliable backups ensure that data can be restored quickly after an incident, minimizing downtime. Ideally, backups should be stored securely offsite or in the cloud to protect against ransomware attacks.
These practices, combined with expert IT support, create a resilient security posture that supports uninterrupted productivity. Collaboration between cybersecurity specialists and IT support teams ensures that preventive and corrective measures are aligned, reducing vulnerabilities.
Leveraging Technology to Support Remote and Hybrid Work
The rise of remote and hybrid work models has introduced new cybersecurity challenges. Employees accessing corporate networks from various locations and devices increase the attack surface for cybercriminals. As a result, organizations need to implement secure remote access solutions such as virtual private networks (VPNs), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and endpoint security.
According to Gartner, by 2024, 70% of organizations will have adopted a hybrid work model, necessitating robust IT support to manage and secure diverse work environments. This shift demands flexible, scalable cybersecurity strategies that accommodate remote access without compromising security.
Businesses that can ensure their remote workforce remains productive and protected through continuous monitoring, security updates, and rapid technical assistance. Securing remote endpoints, enforcing strong authentication methods, and educating employees about safe remote work practices are vital components of this approach.
Moreover, IT support extends beyond security to include ensuring that remote employees have reliable access to necessary applications and data. Prompt resolution of technical issues reduces downtime and frustration, helping maintain high levels of productivity even outside the traditional office setting.
The Economic Impact of Cybersecurity and IT Support Investments
Investing in cybersecurity and IT support is not merely a cost center but a strategic business decision that can yield significant returns. According to a report by Accenture, companies that implement mature cybersecurity practices can reduce the cost of cybercrime by up to 72%. This demonstrates that proactive security and IT management can save organizations millions by preventing breaches and minimizing recovery expenses.
Furthermore, a secure IT environment contributes to customer confidence and competitive advantage. Clients and partners increasingly demand assurance that their data is protected, making cybersecurity a key factor in business reputation and growth. Organizations with strong cybersecurity and IT support frameworks are better positioned to comply with regulatory requirements, avoiding fines and legal repercussions.
Conclusion
Cybersecurity and IT support are inseparable components of a productive and secure workplace. As cyber threats become more sophisticated, organizations must prioritize both preventive security measures and responsive support services. Partnering with experienced providers and adhering to best practices ensures that businesses can operate smoothly, protect their data, and maintain customer trust.
By investing in a robust cybersecurity framework coupled with reliable IT support, companies can confidently navigate the complexities of today’s digital world while fostering a productive and protected work environment. This dual approach not only safeguards critical assets but also empowers employees to work efficiently without fear of disruption or compromise. In an era where cyber risks continue to escalate, the integration of cybersecurity and IT support remains a cornerstone of sustainable business success.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : vers un prix de départ à 1 729 €, soit le tarif de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max en version 512 Go
articles.text:
iPhone 18 Pro : vers un prix de départ à 1 729 €, soit le tarif de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max en version 512 Go
Enlisée dans une pénurie de mémoire mondiale, Apple n’aurait pas le choix de rehausser le prix des iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max, pulvérisant le plafond par rapport à ses prédécesseurs, les iPhone 17 Pro.
Les rumeurs autour du prix des iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max s’affolent, alors qu’Apple a déjà rehaussé sa grille tarifaire sur les iPhone 17 au Japon. La pénurie de mémoire forcerait en effet l’entreprise à étendre cette hausse à travers le monde pour sa future génération, qui débuterait au prix de 1 729 € dans le pire des cas (identique à l’iPhone 17 Pro Max avec 512 Go), soit 400 € de plus que pour l’iPhone 17 Pro.
Apple iPhone 17 Pro
De +330 € à +400 €, les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max deviennent encore plus inaccessibles
Jeff Pu vient d’ajouter son grain de sel autour du prix des prochains smartphones Pro d’Apple. D’après lui, ils subiront une augmentation tarifaire comprise entre 250 et 300 dollars aux États-Unis, et ce, à cause de la pénurie de mémoire. En appliquant la logique de conversion d'Apple, cela se traduirait par une hausse vertigineuse allant de 330 à 400 euros sur le marché européen. Pour imager la chose, sachez que l’iPhone 18 Pro coûterait dans le pire des cas le prix d’un iPhone 17 Pro Max en version 512 Go, soit 1 729 € au lieu des traditionnels 1 329 € du 17 Pro en 256 Go.
Une flambée des prix inédite dans la continuité de la hausse récemment appliquée aux Mac et iPad dans le monde, ou encore plus récemment aux iPhone 17 au Japon. Elle s’explique par l'explosion du coût des composants (surtout pour la mémoire), directement liée au développement massif des infrastructures liées à l'intelligence artificielle.
Apple doit par exemple absorber les augmentations tarifaires liées à sa nouvelle puce A20 Pro gravée en 2 nanomètres par TSMC, qui pourrait coûter jusqu'à 280 $ (au lieu de 85 à 90 $ pour l’A19 Pro). Ensuite, le prix de la mémoire vive LPDDR5X (avec 12 Go de RAM désormais facturés autour de 145 $) et du stockage NAND a quasiment triplé. Si on ajoute à cela les nouveautés majeures, dont l'intégration d'un objectif à ouverture variable, la facture des composants s’alourdit à vue d’œil pour Apple, qui devra répercuter la hausse sur le prix de vente final payé par les consommateurs.
À noter, d’autres informateurs vont dans le même sens, le Wall Street Journal évoquant aussi un prix de départ de 1 399 $ pour l’iPhone 18 Pro, alors que Counterpoint Research planche sur des coûts de fabrication bondissant de 300 $ par rapport aux iPhone 17 Pro.
Face à cette situation, l’analyste Jeff Pu alerte sur une possible “incertitude de la demande” à la sortie des prochains iPhone. Il a d’ailleurs d’ores et déjà dégradé la recommandation de l'action Apple, conseillant plutôt de conserver ses parts au lieu d’en acheter de nouvelles pour l’instant.
Alors que Tim Cook a gardé le silence sur le sujet lors des derniers résultats financiers, il incombera probablement à John Ternus, le nouveau PDG de la marque à la rentrée 2026, d'annoncer la douloureuse nouvelle d’une hausse tarifaire sur les iPhone 18 Pro lors de la keynote de septembre. Le fameux événement dévoilera au passage le tout premier iPhone pliant de la firme à la pomme, qui devrait allègrement dépasser les 2 000 $.

articles.title: Rusia lleva tiempo intentando bloquear a los satélites Starlink desde tierra. Ahora ha decidido apuntar directamente al cielo
articles.text:
Países como Rusia o China llevan tiempo queriendo desarrollar sistemas que permitan deshabilitar los satélites Starlink de SpaceX, pues su constelación supone una gran ventaja en el frente de batalla. Rusia, por lo pronto, ya tiene su “Starlink Killer”, ya que ha mostrado por primera vez las capacidades de su sistema Volna Kupol Garant ("Ola Cúpula Garante"). En vez de interferir en las antenas terrestres de los usuarios, este sistema promete apuntar directamente a los satélites en órbita para saturar sus receptores y dejarlos temporalmente "sordos".
Qué es exactamente. Se trata de un equipo desarrollado por la empresa rusa Russkiy Kupol, con sede en Crimea. Según Dmitry Kuzyakin , diseñador jefe del Centro de Soluciones Integradas No Tripuladas, el sistema emite un haz de radio de alta frecuencia y muy estrecho que sobrecarga las antenas receptoras de los satélites Starlink que se encuentren situados sobre la zona de operación. Esto impide que los satélites puedan captar las señales enviadas desde los terminales en tierra.
Cómo funciona. Los satélites de Starlink orbitan a unos 500 kilómetros de altura y reciben las señales de los usuarios en la banda de 14 a 14,5 GHz, dividida en ocho canales de 62,5 MHz cada uno. Desde el medio local 1.ru aseguran que el sistema concentra ocho antenas direccionales, una por canal, apuntando todas ellas a un mismo satélite para saturar sus receptores.
Serhii Beskrestnov, experto en radiocomunicaciones y asesor del Ministerio de Defensa de Ucrania, asegura que los rusos habrían tomado ocho antenas parabólicas apuntadas al satélite, cada una emitiendo interferencias en su propio canal, hasta dejarlo "sordo".
No destruye, pero deja fuera de juego. Rusia insiste en que no se trata de un arma antisatélite convencional, ya que no daña físicamente el satélite. "Volna no destruye físicamente la nave espacial, pero mientras dura la 'iluminación', bloquea la capacidad de un satélite concreto para dar servicio a los terminales terrestres", cuenta Kuzyakin. El efecto, además, dura algo más que el tiempo de operación de este sistema, pues el propio diseñador reconoce que los satélites afectados necesitan varios minutos adicionales para recuperar la normalidad una vez cesa la interferencia.
El despliegue sobre el terreno. Físicamente, el sistema se compone de seis módulos remolcados, cada uno con dos antenas orientables protegidas por radomos, lo que le da cierta flexibilidad para operar desde distintas posiciones. Según los datos difundidos por distintos medios, el radio de alcance seria de varios kilómetros cuadrados, con un peso total del equipo de unos 120 kilogramos por unidad y un único operador necesario para su manejo, aunque se pueden controlar en remoto.
Mucho coste para poco alcance. Beskrestnov asegura que el sistema tiene sus limitaciones. Una de las más gordas es que cada equipo solo puede interferir a un satélite Starlink a la vez, y la constelación cuenta ya con más de 10.000 satélites activos, con varias decenas sobrevolando constantemente cada punto del frente y relevándose cada pocos minutos. Además, el coste de cada unidad, según el propio Beskrestnov, ascendería hasta los 1,5 millones de dólares.
Es fácil de detectar y destruir. Beskrestnov también apunta que SpaceX detecta casi al instante las interferencias en sus canales de comunicación, y que las numerosas antenas activas del sistema, junto con su considerable tamaño, lo hacen muy visible para los satélites de reconocimiento electrónico de los países aliados de Ucrania. De hecho, según Militarnyi, el 15 de junio el Regimiento 422 de Sistemas No Tripulados y el Centro de Operaciones Especiales "A" del Servicio de Seguridad de Ucrania (SBU) localizaron y destruyeron con drones uno de estos sistemas en el sur del país, alcanzando varios de sus seis vehículos desplegados.
A falta de pan... Pese a sus limitaciones, Rusia parece decidida a multiplicar su despliegue. Y es que según recoge TSN, la escalada en el uso de estos equipos coincidiría con los ataques ucranianos de medio alcance contra nudos logísticos rusos, lo que sugiere que Moscú los emplea como respuesta ante la falta de alternativas eficaces contra los drones que dependen de Starlink para operar.

articles.title: Alibaba debuts Qwen3.8-Max model with 2.4T parameters - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Alibaba debuts Qwen3.8-Max model with 2.4T parameters
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. today debuted a new addition to its Qwen series of open-source large language models.
Qwen3.8-Max is the Chinese e-commerce giant’s most capable LLM to date. It features 2.4 trillion parameters, about seven times more than the Qwen3.5 model that Alibaba released in February. The LLM activates 95 billion of its parameters when answering a query.
Qwen3.8-Max supports prompts with up to 1 million tokens worth of data. According to Alibaba, that enables the model to analyze more than 200 pages of text or about 100 hours of footage per request. Prompt responses contain up to 131,000 tokens.
Alibaba hasn’t yet shared a detailed overview of Qwen3.8-Max’s architecture. Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6, the previous two entries in the model lineup, shared certain technical properties including a so-called Gated DeltaNet attention mechanism. It’s possible Alibaba’s newest LLM also uses the technology.
An LLM’s attention mechanism is a software module it uses to interpret prompts. The module ingests the inputted text, identifies the most important parts and prioritizes them during processing. Gated DeltaNet is a variation of the technology that was introduced by Nvidia Corp. researchers last year.
Linear scale
A standard attention mechanism scales quadratically, which means that doubling the size of a prompt quadruples the amount of memory and computing power needed to process it. A Gated DeltaNet module, in contrast, scales linearly. Its processor and memory requirements don’t increase as fast as prompt size grows, which reduces LLM hardware usage.
Gated DeltaNet is not the only implementation of attention that offers linear scaling. What sets it apart is the use of two data processing techniques known as the gated update rule and the delta rule. According to Nvidia, these techniques make LLMs with linear-scaling attention mechanisms better at processing long prompts.
Alibaba evaluated Qwen3.8-Max’s capabilities across multiple tests ahead of its debut today. According to the company, the model successfully completed a 16-day coding project without human input. In another test, Qwen3.8-Max performed a chip design optimization task that comprised over 500 steps.
The model scored 1,668 points on a benchmark called Frontend Code Arena that measures LLMs’ interface development skills. That puts it just 37 points behind the most advanced configuration of Claude Opus 5, Anthropic PBC’s latest LLM. Qwen3.8-Max outperformed more than a dozen other frontier models including Meta Platforms Inc.’s flagship Muse Spark 1.1.
The model is available via Alibaba’s cloud platform on launch. The company plans to open-source it next week along with a smaller, more hardware-efficient version called Qwen3.8-27B.
