articles.title: Prime Video : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en août 2026
articles.text:
Prime Video : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en août 2026
Que voir sur Prime Video en août 2026 si on est fan de séries ? Découvrez la sélection des meilleures fictions sérielles du service selon Les Numériques pour ce mois-ci.
En quête de divertissement sériel en ce mois d'août 2026 ? Direction le service de streaming Prime Video car vous trouverez forcément de quoi occuper vos soirées dans le catalogue de la plateforme de SVOD d'Amazon, qui compte en effet plus de 1200 séries.
Vous êtes perdus parmi les séries disponibles sur le service ? Pas de panique, Les Numériques a fait le tri et a sélectionné pour vous, comme le mois dernier, les 10 meilleures séries à ne pas manquer sur Prime Video en août 2026.
Quelles sont les meilleures séries à voir sur Prime Video en août 2026 ?
Ride or Die
Cette série suit deux meilleures amies, Debbie Claybourne et Judith Burton, qui pensaient tout savoir l'une de l'autre — jusqu'à ce qu'il s'avère que Judith est une tueuse à gages internationale. Lorsqu'une mystérieuse figure du passé de Judith refait surface et qu'un contrat tourne terriblement mal, leurs vies basculent et elles se retrouvent contraintes de prendre la fuite ensemble. S'engage alors une course contre la montre et un périple à travers l'Europe, avec à leurs trousses les forces de l'ordre, des tueurs d'élite et des criminels particulièrement dangereux.
Portée par les excellentes Octavia Spencer (La couleur des sentiments) et Hannah Waddingham (Ted Lasso), cette série pleine d'action et d'humour est surtout une jolie histoire d'amitié, dont les épisodes sont particulièrement rythmés et ne laissent aucune place à l'ennui. Sans être révolutionnaire, l'intrigue est prenante et la série entraîne ses spectateurs dans des péripéties divertissantes à souhait.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
The Five-Star Weekend
Hollis Shaw, une célèbre influenceuse culinaire connue pour ses délicieuses recettes, son goût impeccable et son comportement chaleureux, est dévastée par un deuil. Son incapacité à aller de l'avant fait apparaître des fissures dans sa vie parfaite : son mariage tendu, sa relation compliquée avec sa fille et sa quête croissante de validation de la part de ses followers. Pour surmonter son chagrin et se retrouver, Hollis invite quatre amis de différents chapitres de sa vie pour un week-end à Nantucket, où des vérités cachées émergent et où les relations évoluent dans le luxe côtier.
Cette série portée par Jennifer Garner, Regina Hall, Chloë Sevigny, D'Arcy Carden et Gemma Chan est adaptée du roman best-seller de Elin Hilderbrand et offre une histoire captivante sur fond d'amitié et de découverte de soi au milieu des jolis paysages de Nantucket. Les actrices sont au top, l'intrigue touchante, et la bande-son entraînante, alors tous les ingrédients sont réunis pour passer un bon moment.
À découvrir sur Prime Video dès le 21 août.
- Regardez le générique de la série :
Reacher
Ancienne recrue de l'armée américaine, Jack Reacher s'est retiré de la police militaire. Son voyage à travers le pays l'amène à s'impliquer dans de périlleuses enquêtes.
Si elle n'est clairement pas du goût de la rédaction, la série Reacher pourra toutefois plaire aux fans d'enquête et du genre policier, et à ceux qui aiment les justiciers baraqués. Une série à la hauteur d'un téléfilm d'après-midi qui fascine pourtant, notamment en raison de son personnage principal, montagne de muscles absurde. Pas désagréable en soi, Reacher saura contenter les spectateurs en quête de divertissement léger. Et ça tombe bien, puisque sa saison 4 arrive en août sur Prime Video.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Elle
Elle suit Elle Woods avant qu’elle ne se retrouve comme un poisson hors de l’eau à Harvard. Nous la rencontrons en 1995, alors qu'elle est un poisson dans les eaux tumultueuses du lycée, où elle fait face à des amitiés compliquées, une romance interdite et des choix vestimentaires discutables. À travers tout cela, Elle s'appuie sur sa famille et tisse un lien encore plus fort avec sa mère, prouvant qu'elles peuvent surmonter tout ce que la vie leur réserve tant qu'elles sont là l'une pour l'autre. À chaque défi qu'elle relève, Elle se rapproche de plus en plus de la Elle Woods que nous connaissons et aimons aujourd'hui.
Cette série préquelle des films La Revanche d'un Blonde avec Reese Witherspoon est portée par la pétillante Lexi Minetree dans le rôle-titre. On retrouve ainsi le personnage d'Elle Woods au lycée, et elle s'avère aussi drôle et attachante que sa future version. La série n'a rien de révolutionnaire mais elle fera passé un moment divertissant aux fans de La Revanche d'une Blonde et invite ceux qui ne connaissent pas encore Elle Woods à découvrir son univers plein de rose et de bonne volonté.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
La Légende de Vox Machina
Ils sont tapageurs, ils sont hétéroclites, ce sont des inadaptés devenus des mercenaires à louer. Vox Machina est plus intéressé par l'argent facile et la bière bon marché que par la protection du royaume. Mais lorsque ledit royaume est menacé par le mal, cet équipage bruyant se rend compte qu'il est le seul capable de rétablir la justice.
Les fans de Donjons et Dragons et de Critical Role seront enchantés par cette série qui reprend la première campagne de cette troupe d’acteurs adeptes du fameux jeu de rôle. Ceux qui ne savent pas ce que tout cela veut dire découvriront quant à eux une série d’animation fantastique pleines d’aventures, de personnages attachants et amusants, et seront embarqués dans un récit captivant.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Off Campus
Les aventures d’une équipe d’élite de hockey sur glace et des femmes qui partagent leur vie, alors qu’ils sont confrontés à l’amour, aux chagrins et à la découverte de soi, forgeant des amitiés profondes et des liens durables tout en surmontant la transition vers l’âge adulte.
Cette série pour jeunes adultes inspirée des romans à succès signés Elle Kennedy est bien moins superficielle qu'elle en a l'air. Sur fond de la romance sexy et pleine d’humour entre Hannah, une auteure-compositrice discrète, et Garrett, la star de l’équipe de hockey de l’université de Briar, le show explore en réalité des thématiques intéressantes et nécessaires sur la place cruciale de la confiance dans les relations amoureuses. Ajoutez à cela une bande-son entraînante et de jeunes acteurs au top, et vous obtenez un binge watch parfait pour l'été.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Invincible
Après avoir découvert que son père est le super-héros le plus puissant du monde, un ado développe lui aussi des pouvoirs et décide de suivre les traces de son géniteur.
Créée par Robert Kirkman (The Walking Dead), et dans l'esprit gore et corrosif de The Boys, Invincible est une variation qui plaira assurément aux fans du genre super-héroïque. Loin de s'arrêter là, la série se révèle plus touchante et intelligente qu'elle n'en a l'air, et nous offre une belle réflexion sur la famille et le poids de l'héritage. Dotée d'un joli casting vocal (Steven Yeun, J.K. Simmons, Sandra Oh), Invincible a déjà quatre saisons à retrouver sur Prime Video.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la saison 4 :
Spider-Noir
Spider-Noir
Prime Video
- Date de sortie
- 27/05/2026
- Genre
- Action, Fantastique, Epouvante-horreur, Policier
- Durée
- 45 min
- Episodes
- 8
Ben Reilly, un détective privé vieillissant et malchanceux dans le New York des années 1930, est forcé de se confronter à son passé en tant qu'unique super-héros de la ville. Dans le passé, Ben Reilly était le super-héros connu sous le nom de "L'Araignée". Après un drame personnel, il a abandonné son alter ego héroïque. Seule une affaire extraordinaire pouvait pousser ce détective privé malchanceux à abandonner sa vie d'homme ordinaire et à revêtir à nouveau son masque.
Spider-Noir est une véritable bouffée d'air frais pour la franchise Spider-Man de Sony. En embrassant pleinement son concept de polar pulp et rétro, la série de Prime Video offre une œuvre singulière, formellement superbe et portée par un Nicolas Cage qui cabotine avec un plaisir communicatif. Malgré quelques baisses de rythme et une proposition clivante qui ne fera pas l'unanimité, ce voyage dans le New York des années 1930 est une vraie réussite. Nous vous conseillons la version en noir & blanc pour savourer pleinement cette proposition atypique.
- Regardez une bande-annonce de la série :
The Good Wife
L'épouse d'un homme politique voit sa vie bouleversée par l'incarcération de son mari à la suite d'un scandale sexuel et une affaire de corruption largement relayés par les médias. Dépassant la trahison et l'humiliation publique, Alicia Florrick décide de reprendre sa carrière d'avocate après une pause de 13 ans loin des tribunaux.
Cette excellente série du duo Robert et Michelle King, portée par la fantastique Julianna Margulies mais aussi Josh Charles, Christine Baranski et Matt Czuchry, a récemment débarqué dans son intégralité sur le service de streaming d'Amazon. En sept saisons, ce drame sur fond de droit et de politique a démontré sa capacité à allier écriture intelligente et personnages brillamment développés. À ne pas manquer !
- Regardez une bande-annonce de la série :
Good Omens
Adaptée du roman de Terry Pratchett et Neil Gaiman (De bons présages), cette série met en scène un duo improbable, un Ange exigeant et un Démon qui vit en liberté. Ils ont pris goût à la vie sur Terre et sont obligés de former une alliance pour arrêter Armageddon.
Portée par les excellents Michael Sheen et David Tennant, Good Omens s’impose comme une comédie fantastique solide, au casting particulièrement inspiré. Entre satire de la fin du monde et humour très britannique, la série développe un univers singulier, aussi accessible qu’attachant. Malgré quelques longueurs, l’ensemble convainc grâce à une écriture soignée, une réalisation appliquée et un duo d’acteurs au charisme et à la complicité indéniables.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :

articles.title: Les AirPods avec caméras auraient enfin une date de sortie, et elle est proche
articles.text:
Après des mois d’attente, la sortie des AirPods avec caméras semble enfin se préciser. En effet, selon Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple aurait décidé de lancer le produit en septembre prochain, aux côtés des iPhone 18. Les AirPods avec caméras sont prêts depuis maintenant des mois et Siri AI a été déployé auprès du grand public. L’entreprise à la pomme n’a plus de raison de retarder le lancement de ce produit très attendu.
Les AirPods avec caméras pourraient sortir dès septembre
La sortie des AirPods équipés de caméras ne se sera pas faite sans embûche. Pour rappel, l’appareil est prêt depuis des mois, mais Siri AI, soit son cerveau, ne l’était pas. Apple a donc dû attendre la mise à niveau de Siri avant de considérer sérieusement toute commercialisation. Cependant, l’intelligence artificielle d’Apple boostée par Gemini est maintenant opérationnelle et une date de commercialisation semble désormais se préciser. En effet, selon les informations de Mark Gurman, Apple prévoirait de présenter ses AirPods avec caméras en septembre prochain, soit en même temps que les iPhone 18. La commercialisation de ces écouteurs de nouvelle génération pourrait donc avoir lieu quelques semaines plus tard.
Deux modèles ont été repérés
Toujours selon Gurman, deux modèles d’AirPods avec caméra ont été repérés. Le premier porte le nom de code B790, tandis que le second est identifié sous le nom de code B798. À l’heure actuelle, nous ne savons pas quelle est la différence entre ces deux modèles. Il pourrait s’agir d’un modèle standard et d’un modèle premium. Une autre hypothèse est que l’entreprise a développé plusieurs variantes du produit et qu’elle n’en gardera au final qu’une seule.
Quoi qu’il en soit, l’attente semble toucher à sa fin. Comme nous l’avons précisé précédemment, Apple n’a maintenant plus de raison de retarder le lancement de ses AirPods avec caméras. La conception du produit est maintenant terminée depuis des mois et Siri AI a été déployé auprès du grand public. En revanche, il reste à voir si certaines fonctionnalités de Siri AI intégrées aux AirPods avec caméras ne seront pas bloquées en Europe, comme cela pourrait être le cas avec la nouvelle gamme domotique d’Apple.
Pour rappel, les AirPods avec caméras ne sont pas conçus pour prendre des photos et des vidéos, comme le feraient des lunettes connectées. Les caméras, intégrées aux tiges des écouteurs, captureront uniquement des images en basse résolution afin de fournir à l’intelligence artificielle une compréhension visuelle de l’environnement en temps réel. Leur design devrait être proche des AirPods 4. Les seules différences notables seraient des tiges légèrement plus longues pour embarquer les différents capteurs et un indicateur LED qui signale le transfert de données vers le cloud. Rendez-vous donc en septembre pour découvrir ce nouveau produit d’Apple. Du moins, on l’espère.

articles.title: Dozens of police officers accused of using license plate cameras to track women
articles.text:
TL;DR: An investigation has revealed a growing number of police officers using license-plate reader systems to track women they knew personally, turning a tool sold for crime fighting into one that could also enable stalking and surveillance. The problem is not limited to one department or one state. It is showing up wherever these systems are widely deployed and lightly checked.
The main tool being misused is Flock Safety, a network of roadside cameras that scan and catalog billions of license plates each month. The firm says its network spans more than 6,000 communities, with devices designed to capture plates in difficult conditions, including at night and in heavy rain, using computer vision. The result is a searchable, time-stamped record of vehicle locations that officers can query without a warrant.
The technical capabilities are straightforward but powerful. Cameras feed plate data into a centralized system, where officers can search by plate number or, using newer "vehicle fingerprint" tools, by characteristics such as color or bumper stickers.
Alerts can be set through "hot lists," notifying users when a vehicle appears anywhere in the network. The infrastructure is distributed – solar-powered cameras connected via cellular networks – making it easy to deploy across cities, suburbs and private properties.
That accessibility, combined with minimal friction in running searches, has created what investigators describe as a gap between capability and oversight. According to the Washington Post's review of police and court records, at least 50 officers nationwide have been accused of or charged with misusing license-plate reader systems, often to track women in their personal lives. In 46 of those cases, Flock's system was involved.
In one case in Georgia, a police chief used the system to repeatedly search for a woman's vehicle, logging hundreds of queries over more than a year. After confronting him, she learned he had relied on the camera network to monitor her movements. "It's a camera system that reads tags," he wrote in a message. He later added, "Don't worry I'm not tracking you or some weird stalker s--t."
Audit logs – one of the system's built-in accountability features – ultimately revealed the extent of the searches. Those logs have become a central mechanism for detecting misuse, but they are typically reviewed only after complaints or internal investigations. Some departments make them available through public records requests, while others do not, limiting visibility into how often the tools are used or abused.
Flock has emphasized that misuse represents a small fraction of overall activity and points to logging and auditing as safeguards. "We're not going to change humans, and humans make bad decisions," CEO Garrett Langley told the Washington Post. "What we can do is make sure that they know if you use this tool, you will be held accountable."
The company recently introduced a voluntary feature that scans for suspicious query patterns, such as repeated searches for the same vehicle or activity outside an officer's working hours.
However, critics argue that optional safeguards and decentralized policy decisions leave too much room for abuse. Police agencies set their own rules for access and use, and in many jurisdictions there is no requirement to tie a search to a case number or active investigation. With no comprehensive federal framework governing license-plate reader use, standards vary widely across the roughly 18,000 law enforcement agencies in the country.
Privacy advocates say the underlying issue is not just misconduct but the design of the system itself. The ability to reconstruct a person's movements – where they shop, seek medical care or spend time – creates a detailed behavioral profile that can be accessed with little immediate oversight. "Flock has already claimed that they have oversight, that they have guardrails, and we still see these kinds of abuses," said Eva Galperin of the Electronic Frontier Foundation.
Law enforcement officials and consultants counter that tighter restrictions could undermine a tool they view as transformative. Langley has described license-plate readers as critical infrastructure for modern policing, citing their role in criminal investigations and recoveries. In a public talk, he recalled a police chief describing the technology as "as transformational as DNA."
The tension reflects a broader shift in policing technology, where systems built for scale – large datasets, cross-agency sharing, AI-assisted search – are outpacing governance models designed for smaller, more localized tools. In several documented cases, officers continued to access license-plate databases even after concerns were raised internally.
Flock is facing growing pushback from communities concerned about privacy and other issues. In Roseville, California, an internal police review found more than 1,000 false positives from the system over two years.
Nevertheless, many city officials remain enthusiastic about the network, even as privacy concerns continue to grow. For people who learn they've been tracked, often only after the fact, the experience shows just how hidden these systems can be. Cameras mounted on utility poles or roadside fixtures continuously collect data, while access remains largely confined to law enforcement systems. As one victim put it after learning how often her vehicle had been queried, "He watched every single move I made."

articles.title: Exclusive: Terra Security's Prevention writes the firewall rules to block proven exploits - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Terra Security’s Prevention writes the firewall rules to block proven exploits
Offensive security startup Terra Security Inc. today launched Prevention, a feature that writes the firewall rules needed to block an attack its artificial intelligence agents have already proven works.
Prevention is available now. Terra built it for the gap between a confirmed finding and a deployed code fix, a stretch that can run for weeks while a patch waits on release cycles and change-management approval. Attackers do not wait that long. Known vulnerabilities are being weaponized within minutes of disclosure.
Pentest reports have long closed with a mitigation section telling the customer to update a web application firewall, tune a firewall, adjust segmentation or change a configuration. Terra says nobody acts on that advice because it never specifies which rule to write or whether that rule would stop the exploit sitting in the report.
When the platform confirms a finding is exploitable, its agents run the customer’s existing compensating controls against that specific attack path to see whether they hold. Where they do not, Terra generates a targeted WAF or firewall rule and validates it against the exploit. The security team then deploys it. Sensitive changes in production require a human sign-off.
“Finding an exploitable risk is only half the job,” said Gal Malachi, co-founder and chief technology officer at Terra Security. “The hardest part is the stretch between proving it and fixing it, and adversaries can now exploit vulnerabilities in minutes. Defenders get time to remediate properly without leaving the door open.”
Rules generated by Prevention move through the same exploit, guidance and retest cycle Terra already applies everywhere else on the platform. The company claims no other agentic offensive security platform acts on the risks it proves exploitable.
Founded in 2024, Terra sells an AI-native offensive security platform. Swarms of trained AI agents probe customer environments under human supervision, and what they find is ranked by whether it can actually be exploited rather than by severity score alone. Web applications, APIs, mobile and internal apps, AI systems, networks and cloud environments are all in scope. Fortune 500 organizations are among its customers, according to the company.
The platform picked up network infrastructure testing in May, when Terra added continuous exploitation validation for network gear to the web application and AI system testing it already offered. The startup also won CrowdStrike Holdings Inc.’s Cybersecurity Startup Accelerator prize in September.
Terra is a venture capital-backed startup that raised $38 million in venture capital funding, including $30 million in a Series A round led by Felicis Ventures Management Company in September.
Shahar Peled, co-founder and chief executive, and Anna Sarnek, vice president of business and strategy at Terra, spoke with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, in June and discussed how the company uses agentic AI to find risks before attackers do.

articles.title: The $60 million startup tackling Africa's travel payments problem | TechCabal How African hotels can reduce international payment costs
articles.text:
Every year, international travellers spend billions of dollars on African safaris, luxury lodges and holiday experiences. Yet before much of that money reaches the businesses providing those experiences, a portion is lost to payment processing fees, foreign exchange charges and the cost of moving money across borders.
For African tourism operators, getting paid can be surprisingly expensive.
TurnStay, a South African fintech that helps travel businesses accept payments from international guests, believes that problem has been overlooked for too long.
Alon Stern, TurnStay’s chief executive officer (CEO) and co-founder, said the three-year-old startup processed over R1 billion ($60.6 million) in travel payments during the first six months of 2026. The company provides payment infrastructure for hotels, safari lodges, tour operators and villa agencies, helping them reduce the cost of accepting international bookings.
The milestone underscores a broader challenge facing Africa’s tourism sector. While many operators compete for the same global travellers as hotels and tour companies elsewhere in the world, they often pay significantly more simply to receive payment. Card network fees, foreign exchange spreads, cross-border acquiring costs, and can collectively consume a meaningful share of booking revenue, eroding margins and reducing the amount of tourism income that ultimately remains on the continent.
“Getting paid can be expensive in the travel industry, and for a long time African merchants have carried a much heavier cost than their overseas counterparts for doing exactly the same job,” said Stern.
He stated that traditional payment processing for international travel bookings can cost African merchants as much as 8% of a transaction. By combining a merchant-of-record model with modern payment rails, including stablecoins for cross-border settlement, TurnStay says it can reduce fees to as little as 1.6%.
“The less merchants pay in fees, the more money stays in Africa,” Stern said. “That’s the philosophy behind everything we build. The experiences African travel businesses offer are already world-class. We think the payment infrastructure behind them should be too.”
Rather than relying solely on traditional banking infrastructure, TurnStay uses digital payment rails to move money across borders faster and at lower cost before settling funds with merchants.
“Global platforms have used this model for years,” stated Stern. “But what we have done is bring that same infrastructure to African travel merchants directly, so a lodge or tour operator doesn’t have to be the size of Airbnb to access it.”
The company counts luxury hospitality brands including Singita, Londolozi, Safari.com and The Capital among its customers, with operations expanding beyond South Africa into Kenya, Tanzania, Botswana and Mauritius.
TurnStay raised a $300,000 pre-seed round in 2024 followed by a $2 million seed round in 2025 and is now preparing for a Series A fundraising round to accelerate its pan-African expansion.
For Stern, the company’s rapid growth is less about payment volumes than correcting a structural imbalance in Africa’s tourism economy.
“Three years ago there were two of us and an idea,” he said. “Now we’re processing over a billion rand every six months for some of the best-known names in African travel, and we have just begun.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: SpaceX is set to acquire 130,000 acres of marshland in southern Louisiana
articles.text:
SpaceX and the state of Louisiana are close to finalizing a deal for the launch company to acquire about 130,000 acres along the northern coast of the Gulf of Mexico.
There have been persistent rumors about such an agreement for months, but now The Times-Picayune | The New Orleans Advocate reports that Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry is expected to announce the agreement later this month.
The deal would give SpaceX control of an 18-mile stretch of marshland southwest of Lafayette. The site, known as Pecan Island, became available as part of a legal settlement that resolves dozens of lawsuits that blame ExxonMobil for pollution and coastal land loss, the newspaper reports.
No Louisiana officials publicly commented on the deal. Nor did SpaceX. In May, however, the company said in response to rumors about the Louisiana site on X, “It’s no secret that we intend to launch Starship a lot, targeting thousands of flights per year. That cadence will require the ability to launch from many different locations, so we are constantly exploring to find viable sites to expand Starship operations in the future, both domestically and internationally.”
Plenty of incentives
Adding fuel to the rumors was the passage of bills by the Louisiana Legislature earlier this year that included a package of incentives for aerospace companies, including liability protections and property tax breaks.
According to the Louisiana newspaper, the agreement with SpaceX will include provisions for coastal restoration and preservation of the sensitive marshland along the northern Gulf Coast, which is important for wildlife and also acts as a buffer for hurricanes that regularly impact the region.
So why would SpaceX be interested in a remote, marshy location in southern Louisiana?
Lots of reasons to like Louisiana
If the company is to fulfill its ambitions to launch thousands of Starship rockets a year to build a massive constellation of orbital data centers, among other purposes, it needs more launch sites. And there are limited expanses of undeveloped coastal locations along the Gulf of Mexico and southern Atlantic Ocean in the United States.

articles.title: UK AI chip startup OLIX raises €270.5 million at €2.8 billion valuation just two years after its founding | EU-Startups
articles.text:
OLIX, a London-based AI chip startup building the infrastructure for frontier AI inference, today announced a €270.5 million ($312 million) Series B financing round at a €2.8 billion ($3.3 billion) valuation, two years after it was founded.
The round included Fundomo, Arm and Hudson River Trading, alongside angel investors including Reed Hastings, the co-founder of Netflix, with existing investors all increasing their commitments.
Alongside the round, OLIX has appointed Professor Nick McKeown to its board of directors. He is Professor Emeritus of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering at Stanford University and winner of the 2025 Marconi Prize. The company has also appointed former Wise executive Matt Briers as Chief Financial Officer.
Founded in London in 2024, OLIX designs every part of its systems: the chips, the lasers and the network that connects them.
OLIX believes the industry’s approach to building AI inference hardware is reaching its efficiency limits. “A datacenter is a factory whose product is the token. Producing a single token takes hundreds of operations, each placing different demands on hardware. Any other factory would give each stage a machine built for it. Instead, the token factory runs every stage on the same general-purpose chip. Each new chip generation has improved by pushing single-chip specifications higher: an even better generalist but never a specialist,” the startup explained.
The company claims that its systems are built on the belief that using specialised chips for each stage of the token production process will unlock a step change in AI performance and cost. It states that in OLIX’s X-1 platform, models are fully unrolled across a large number of chips, creating a production line which allows each chip to focus on a single part of the model.
As AI model architectures are rapidly evolving, each chip retains a flexible compute fabric and does not hard-code or bake-in a particular model’s architecture.
The company highlighted that the system is built around a novel “slow and wide” optical interconnect that moves data directly between chips using light instead of copper, at ultra-low latency and energy cost. This is made possible by rack-scale codesign across every part of the link. Workloads are scheduled across racks by a fully deterministic compiler.
OLIX believes this will make existing frontier AI more affordable and abundant, and more importantly, unlock the deployment of far more powerful models in the future.
DX-1 is the first chip OLIX is developing within the X-1 platform, its decode accelerator, designed for the stage where a model reasons and generates its output. The company reports that for 100B parameter size models, DX-1 can achieve Pareto-optimal inference performance, delivering simultaneously over 10,000 Tokens per second per user. It achieves this at higher output token throughput per watt than general-purpose chips running large batch sizes. The architecture scales performantly to models 10 trillion parameters and above in size thanks to OLIX’s multi-rack scale-up domain architecture.
DX-1 holds a model in fast on-chip memory, SRAM, for higher energy efficiency and lower latency. The design uses no advanced packaging and no high-bandwidth memory, the components the industry is in the shortest supply of, and is designed to be able to scale volumes in spite of the supply chain shortages across the industry.
The company plans to use this funding to deliver DX-1 to OLIX’s first customers by H2 2027, and the build-out of the wider custom silicon platform behind it, together with the manufacturing and supply chain commitments that scaling frontier inference hardware requires. OLIX is hiring across silicon, photonics, compiler and systems engineering in London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco.

articles.title: CXMT Reportedly Plans Second Fab in Beijing to Boost DRAM Output
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
CXMT Reportedly Plans Second Fab in Beijing to Boost DRAM Output
Chinese memory maker CXMT is planning a second DRAM fab in Beijing amid high demand for its memory products. According to Reuters, the Chinese memory giant is considering building this second fab and is already in talks to secure funding for the project. As CXMT aims to boost its manufacturing output, measured in DRAM wafers per month (WPM), the company needs to secure new funding and is reportedly backed by the local government to increase production. While the project details are currently unknown, building a modern DRAM fab can cost over $10 billion, meaning CXMT will likely require significant funds to get started.
Currently, CXMT operates two 12-inch fabs, one in Hefei and one in Beijing, with each fab having an output of about 100,000 WPM. This means the current output capacity is around 200,000 wafers per month, with plans to triple that number to an astonishing 600,000 WPM when the Shanghai and Hefei plants are completed and fully operational. We have already reported that CXMT will end the year 2026 with about 350,000 WPM of DRAM output, just behind Micron's 375,000 DRAM WPM output.Although building a modern semiconductor plant takes years, CXMT is leading the industry in the speed of construction. Cleanrooms, where actual DRAM is manufactured away from any debris, are being built by CXMT in just 12 months, while the rest of the industry takes roughly two years. This is a significant speedup compared to the rest of the industry, as the entire supply chain is struggling to meet the massive demand driven by the AI data center buildout. CXMT's added capacity is likely to have a positive impact on the overall supply chain, but it will mostly be consumed by Chinese hyperscalers and AI labs for domestic demand.

articles.title: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
articles.text:
The European Union has ushered in some additional rules that aim to make it easier for people to identify chatbots and AI deepfakes online. The new transparency obligations under the bloc’s landmark AI Act came into effect on August 2nd, requiring companies to disclose when people are interacting with AI models, and if content has been generated or altered by them.
Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
Tech companies could face fines if they don’t meet new requirements for AI transparency.
The transparency rules differ between providers (companies that develop and market AI systems) and deployers (platforms and services that use those AI systems), though some companies like Meta and SpaceXAI are classified as both.
Providers must design AI systems to explicitly notify users when they’re dealing with AI instead of a human, “unless this is obvious,” and include machine-readable marks on synthetic audio, image, video, and text so that it can be detected as artificially generated or manipulated. Likewise, deployers are required to label any AI-generated or manipulated image, audio, and video deepfake content that’s designed to look real.
“The rapid development of generative and interactive AI systems is making it increasingly difficult to distinguish AI interactions and AI-generated content from human-created and authentic content,” the European Commission said in its transparency guidelines. “People should know when they are interacting with AI or exposed to AI-generated content. This will help them make informed decisions, calibrate their trust and reliance on AI and avoid misinformation or deception.”
The Commission has also developed a set of AI disclosure labels that tech platforms can adopt in accordance with the AI Act rules, alongside examples of when they should be used. These mirror similar labels that have already been introduced by TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook. The EU-made icons have been introduced to prevent platforms from having to design their own, and while the EU examples are optional to use, the Commission pointedly notes that its labeling requirements “are not.”
Companies that fail to comply with these new transparency rules risk facing fines of up to €15 million (about $17.2 million), or 3 percent of their global annual turnover. While the new transparency rules are enforceable immediately for new AI systems, any models and services that launched before August 2nd have a four-month grace period until December 2nd to comply.

articles.title: Amazon y Henry Cavill preparan una serie animada de 'Warhammer 40k'
articles.text:
Amazon MGM Studios y Henry Cavill siguen firmes con su intención de adaptar el universo Wharhammer 40k al mundo del cine y las series. Según reporta Variety, el estudio y el actor se encuentran a la cabeza de un nuevo proyecto de animación basado en la franquicia para Prime Video.
Pese a que todavía no se han brindado demasiados detalles sobre la propuesta, sí se menciona que será una serie que servirá como spin-off del episodio de Warhammer 40k que se incluyó en la antología animada Secret Level.
Respecto de la trama, todavía no hay grandes novedades. Solamente se ha mencionado que será una historia expandida que se enfocará en los Vigías de la Muerte (conocidos como Deathwatch en inglés), el cuerpo de Marines Espaciales más letal.
Vale mencionar que la serie animada de Warhammer 40k se produce en paralelo con la película live-action que también involucra a Henry Cavill, aunque no solo como productor ejecutivo, sino también como protagonista. Dicho proyecto lleva varios años en desarrollo y sus pormenores son todavía un misterio.
Una serie animada de Warhammer 40k llegará a Prime Video de la mano de Henry Cavill
Warhammer 40k fue uno de los títulos elegidos para la antología Secret Level, que se lanzó en Prime Video a finales de 2024. La propiedad intelectual de Games Workshop protagonizó el quinto episodio, que resultó ser de los más aclamados por el público. La animación del capítulo en cuestión estuvo a cargo de Blur Studio, que ahora tomará la responsabilidad de desarrollar la nueva serie animada al completo.
Tim Miller, fundador de Blur Studio y responsable de Secret Level, producirá la serie animada de Warhammer 40k junto con Henry Cavill. Por su parte, Dave Wilson será el creador y director del nuevo proyecto, y trabajará en conjunto con el guionista John Orloff, responsable de escribir la aclamada Band of Brothers (HBO).
Wilson dirigió el episodio de Secret Level dedicado a Warhammer 40k, de modo que ya tiene una idea de cómo llevar la franquicia a un proyecto audiovisual de este tipo. Cavill, por su parte, es un gran fanático del juego de Games Workshop y manifestó durante años su interés por llevarlo al cine y las series.
Warhammer 40k nació como un juego de mesa de guerra a finales de los ochenta, con figuras en miniatura que los propios jugadores deben armar y pintar. El formato original de la propuesta continúa vigente y ha cultivado una muy amplia base de fanáticos, pero la franquicia también ha dado el salto al mundo de los videojuegos, con decenas de adaptaciones entre las que destacan las de la subsaga Space Marine.

articles.title: PNLD Breach Exposes U.K. Police and Government Contact Details on Dark Web
articles.text:
The Police National Legal Database (PNLD) has confirmed that police, government and customer contact information was compromised and published on the dark web.
The data included names, organisations and work email addresses belonging to police officers, police staff, criminal justice professionals, government partners and customers.
The incident, identified on July 26, also exposed some names and email addresses belonging to people who had submitted questions through Ask the Police. That exposure could make phishing messages targeting named officers appear more convincing, according to UK government guidance.
PNLD said, "There is no evidence to suggest that passwords or other security credentials have been compromised." The service provides legal information, products and services to UK police forces and criminal justice organisations. It is not the Police National Computer or the Police National Database, is not a crime-recording system, and does not hold confidential information about victims, witnesses or offenders.
PNLD says it contacted all affected organisations and provided them with further information and guidance. Affected Ask the Police users have already received an email with more information and guidance. It notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and is working with the National Crime Agency (NCA) and specialist cybersecurity organisations.
As of August 3, 2026, it had not publicly disclosed how many people were affected, when the intrusion began, how long access lasted, or how much information was taken.
PNLD's official breach notice describes the exposed fields but provides no victim total. PNLD reported 108,429 police registrations and support for all 43 Home Office police forces in its 2025-26 annual summary. That is a user-base figure, not a breach-victim count.
PNLD said in its 2023-24 annual summary that the database uses Microsoft Power Platform technology. The Hacker News confirmed on August 3, 2026, that the breach-notice page referenced assets hosted on Microsoft's content.powerapps.com domain. That corroborates the platform connection but does not show how the attacker obtained the data.
VenariX reviewed samples associated with 11 of ExfilSquad's 15 claimed victims and found Dataverse-consistent structures across all 11. In the Houston case, it confirmed that a public portal returned records without authentication and that those records were consistent with data published by the group.
VenariX assessed the likely campaign-level path as a public Power Pages site with broad Anonymous Users access to Dataverse tables. The path also required an enabled Power Pages Web API or legacy OData feed.
Microsoft's documentation says granting the Anonymous Users role access to a table makes its data visible to anyone visiting the site. Its Web API documentation says the /_api interface follows the table permissions attached to each web role.
VenariX said the evidence "does not yet confirm that every organization was affected through an exposed Power Apps portal or the same configuration issue." As of August 3, 2026, neither PNLD's notice nor VenariX's report identified a PNLD-specific endpoint, permission setting, API route, or supporting log.
At this stage, the Power Pages link remains a hypothesis to test rather than an explanation of the PNLD breach.
Microsoft provides a tenant-level governance control that blocks unauthenticated users from reading Dataverse data while still allowing public form submissions.
VenariX recommends that Power Pages operators also review Anonymous Users table permissions, Web API settings, and legacy OData feeds, then validate access from an unauthenticated browser session. Those measures address the configuration pattern identified by VenariX, not a confirmed PNLD root cause.
ExfilSquad listed PNLD on its leak site on July 26, but PNLD has not attributed the incident to the group. VenariX found no evidence of ransomware deployment, malware use, lateral movement or exploitation of a software vulnerability in the campaign material it examined.
PNLD has not publicly disclosed the exact access route, the number of unique people affected or the full volume of data published.

articles.title: I tested the first AI spotting scope for birders — here's my verdict
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The GoBirding Vision Master is a novel idea, and when its on-device bird identification works, it's a treat. But sluggish autofocus, stabilization that struggles at full zoom — even on a tripod, odd-looking colors, and unusual bokeh hold back the image quality, while the companion app feels distinctly unfinished (something I hope will be remedied by the time it goes on sale). At $999 (approx. £749 / AU$1,439), it's a steep ask for a device with this many rough edges, even accounting for the fact that there's little else quite like it on the market. If you're a keen spotter able to grab one for an early-bird (no pun intended) price, however, you may feel like you've got your money's worth.
Pros
- ++Innovative all-in-one scope, camera and app ecosystem
- +On-device AI identification works well in good conditions
- +Useful second-screening for sharing views with others
Cons
- -Autofocus is sluggish and often unreliable
- -Stabilization struggles at higher zoom levels
- -Odd-looking colors and unusual angular bokeh
Why you can trust TechRadar
GoBirding Vision Master: One-minute review
Bird-spotting scopes have remained stubbornly analog for a very long time: you point some glass at a distant feathered friend, squint, and hope you remembered your spotter's guide. The GoBirding Vision Master Smart AI Spotting Scope, or the APL-ETF-M1 to give it its slightly snappier model name, wants to drag that experience kicking and screaming into the smartphone era.
It does so by squeezing a 4K camera, on-device AI bird identification and smartphone-friendly connectivity into a 30x optical zoom scope. It's certainly an ambitious concept; and after spending a few weeks testing it, I came away impressed in some ways and frustrated in others.
The build quality is a positive: the scope feels solid rather than plasticky, and the design manages to be fairly discreet too. At 932g with the tripod mount attached, it's not a lightweight in absolute terms, but it's manageable enough for a session in the field. The front and eyepiece caps, though, have an annoying habit of working themselves loose when the scope is packed away in a bag — worth knowing if you're the sort who likes to keep your gear spotless.
The headline feature — AI bird identification — works, but with caveats. GoBirding claims the M1 can ID over 1,500 species offline, and over 10,000 when connected to the internet via your smartphone, and in practice it correctly called out everything from common cormorants and herring gulls to species I hadn't heard of, like the water pipit. It's less confident with distant or backlit subjects, though, and it drew a blank on a peregrine falcon I spotted, likely because the bird was too well camouflaged against its perch for the system to extract enough detail; you need a clean, in-focus shot for reliable results, and that's not always easy to get.
Which brings me to the scope's chief weakness: autofocus. It's sluggish, and for fast or skittish birds, I found myself reaching for manual focus. It's a similar story with the image stabilization; GoBirding recommends a tripod over handheld use, and having tried both, I heartily agree. Mounted up, footage steadies out nicely; handheld, especially at higher magnifications, it completely fails to remain level.
Image quality itself is a mixed bag. 4K/30fps video looks reasonably sharp at native zoom, but push into the digital range beyond 30x and detail falls off fast. Colors also tend toward the oversaturated — skies in particular can look implausibly turquoise — and the bokeh has an odd, angular quality unlike anything I've seen from a superzoom camera, more chain-link fence than creamy blur.
The companion app is spotty too. Second-screening — letting someone else see what you're viewing through the scope on their phone — works well, and is genuinely useful for shared birding trips. But other features feel unfinished: the app never once managed to log my location correctly, defaulting instead to a spot on the equator, and it doesn't automatically record the time or place of AI-identified sightings, which feels like a missed opportunity given how central data-logging is to the scope's appeal.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Pricing, like a skittish sparrow, remains something of a moving target. GoBirding has confirmed an official retail price of $999, with Kickstarter backers able to secure an Early Bird unit for significantly less depending on tier; there will also be an as-yet-unspecified Super Early Bird VIP discount available too. The Kickstarter campaign is expected to arrive around August 20, with shipping to follow in batches after that — but I should caution that all of this remains subject to change.
GoBirding Vision Master: Price and availability
- Official retail price set to be $999 (about £750 / AU$1,450)
- Kickstarter Early Bird pricing from $649 (about £490 / AU$940)
- Kickstarter campaign expected to launch around August 20, 2026
The M1 isn't on sale yet. GoBirding's Kickstarter campaign is expected to launch around August 20, 2026, offering backers an Early Bird price from $649 to $699 depending on tier. That's well below the $999 official retail price, which will apply once the M1 reaches general sale. A further Super Early Bird VIP discount has also been promised, though GoBirding hasn't yet specified the terms.
GoBirding hasn't published official GBP or AUD pricing, so the conversions above are calculated at current exchange rates rather than confirmed figures. Production is reportedly already underway, with shipping to begin shortly after the Kickstarter campaign wraps and orders are confirmed. There's no word yet on wider retail availability beyond that, however.
At $999, the M1 sits close in price to premium bridge cameras like the Nikon Coolpix P1100, but well below high-end AI optics like the Swarovski AX Visio. My gut feeling is that it's a rather steep price to pay for a scope that doesn't feel completely finished in terms of features and has some image-quality issues, but given that there's not really anything else like it on the market, it's hard to say what something like this should cost.
GoBirding Vision Master: Specs
| Leica SL3-P specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Zoom: | 30x optical, up to 120x hybrid | 
| Sensor: | 1/2.7-inch CMOS | 
| Video: | Up to 4K/30fps; 1080p/120fps | 
| Viewfinder: | 1080p Micro OLED, 0.49-inch | 
| Stabilization: | OIS (optical image stabilization) | 
| Storage: | microSD, up to 512GB (not included) | 
| Battery life: | Around 6 hours of continuous use | 
| Waterproofing: | IP65 | 
| Dimensions: | 11.7 x 3.22 x 4.3 inches / 297.6 x 82 x 110mm | 
| Weight: | 32.8oz / 932g (inc tripod mount) | 
GoBirding Vision Master: Design
- Solid, weatherproof IP65 build
- Tripod-ready straight out of the box
- Weighs around 32.8oz / 930g
Picking up the M1, the first thing I noticed was the heft-to-size ratio — it's a dense, reassuringly solid object, rather than something that feels hollow or plasticky. The forest-green and gunmetal-grey colorway feels like an appropriate choice for a birding tool, and should blend into foliage far better than a garish action-cam-orange scope would.
The controls are nicely tactile and have a rubbery finish, which suits outdoor use: there's a push-pull zoom joystick (which can be tilted left and right to manually focus), a dedicated AI recognition button, and separate stills/video capture controls, and they're all operable by feel alone, which is helpful when you're trying to keep your eyes on a parakeet rather than the top of the scope. The eyepiece itself houses a 1080p micro-OLED display, is angled nicely for extended viewing sessions, and can be twisted to adjust focus. As a glasses wearer, I found it comfortable and easy to get a nice sharp view.
A pull-out rubber flap protects the microSD slot and USB-C port. I found that I wasn't able to transfer videos and images over to my MacBook Air via USB (the scope didn't show up as an openable drive in Finder) so I had to pop out the card, put it in a card reader and do it that way. Also, my sample didn't come with a microSD card, so you may need to buy one if you don't already have one going spare.
A tripod mount is attached to the underside, and given how much GoBirding leans on tripod use for its stabilization claims (more on that in the Performance section below), it's good that they haven't made you buy one separately or hunt for a compatible adapter. The mount can be removed by loosening a nut if you want to slim things down a bit and shoot handheld, but I kept it attached the whole time I was testing.
In the box you get a drawstring storage bag, a microfiber cleaning cloth, and protective push-on rubber caps for both the front element and the eyepiece. The caps are a nice idea in theory, but in practice they had an irritating habit of working themselves loose while the scope was in my backpack.
GoBirding Vision Master: Performance
- AI recognition impresses more often than it disappoints
- Autofocus is the scope's biggest let-down
- Image quality is solid in good light, shakier elsewhere
The M1's AI bird identification is simple to use — you just tap the AI button to toggle on a red box indicator, then center the bird within the box until the name appears on-screen — and mostly delivers on its promise. GoBirding claims 1,500 species identifiable offline and over 10,000 via the companion app, and across my testing it correctly called out common species like cormorants, rock pigeons and herring gulls, alongside less familiar ones — the water pipit, Caspian gull and great black-backed gull all got flagged, the latter two of which I'd wrongly assumed were regular herring gulls. I also tested it on a batch of still photos, and it was accurate the vast majority of the time, with only the occasional misidentification.
It's not infallible, though. The system needs a clean, sharply-focused subject to work with, so extreme-range or backlit birds (reduced to little more than silhouettes) routinely trip it up. It also failed to recognize a peregrine falcon I spotted perched on a distant church tower, most likely due to both the range and because its plumage blended in too well with the stonework for the AI to extract meaningful detail.
Autofocus isn't a strong point. It's noticeably sluggish and inaccurate, and for anything fast-moving or skittish I found manual focus the faster and more reliable option. Combine that with image stabilization that GoBirding itself admits works best with a tripod, and handheld shooting at higher magnifications becomes frustrating. Mounted up, footage steadies out nicely, but when you're shooting freehand, especially at the long end of that zoom range, you'll struggle to keep it level. Even when using a tripod, I found it almost impossible to get steady footage at 120x zoom.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Image quality is a mixed bag, and here the small 1/2.7-inch CMOS sensor is a limiting factor throughout. In good light, 4K/30fps footage and 8MP stills at native zoom look reasonably crisp, but push into the digital zoom range beyond 30x and detail falls away quickly, as you'd expect from a sensor this size.
Colors also look oversaturated by default — skies in particular can be implausibly turquoise — and bokeh has an odd, angular character, more chain-link fence than the smooth, attractive background blur you'd get from a larger-sensor camera.
Should you buy the GoBirding Vision Master?
Buy it if...
You want bird identification without a guide
The on-device recognition system works well enough to speed up confirming species in the field — arguably a handier trick than raw zoom power alone.
You mainly shoot from a tripod
Mount it up and the M1's stabilization and AI accuracy improve, and that ambitious zoom range becomes an asset instead of a challenge.
Don't buy it if...
You need it to work handheld
Stabilization struggles without a tripod, especially at higher magnifications — a real problem for a device that claims to offer grab-and-go convenience.
You're fussy about image quality
The small sensor, inaccurate color metering and unusual angular bokeh mean this won't satisfy anyone used to a proper superzoom camera or a dedicated wildlife lens.
Also consider
CoolPix P1100
If reach matters more than AI cleverness, the Coolpix P1100 goes further than the M1: its 125x optical zoom stretches to a 3000mm-equivalent focal length, more than double the M1's maximum. It's a conventional superzoom camera rather than a purpose-built birding tool, so you won't get on-device species recognition, and its small 1/2.3-inch sensor means image quality has its own well-documented limitations in anything but good light.
Read our Nikon P1000 review
Sony RX10 V
A very different proposition, the RX10 V pairs a much larger 1-inch sensor with a 24-600mm lens, and delivers image quality and autofocus performance that the M1 simply can't touch. Its 25x optical zoom falls well short of the M1's reach, and there's no AI bird identification here, but if outright photographic quality is your priority over specialized birding features, it's in a different league. It costs well over twice as much as the M1, though.
Read our Sony RX10 V review
How I tested the GoBirding Vision Master
- Tested over several weeks in several locations including a country park, the seafront, and a local churchyard
- Shot in a range of light conditions during the UK summer
- Tested handheld and tripod-mounted
I spent several weeks testing a review sample of the GoBirding Vision Master supplied to me by the manufacturers, across a range of locations near my home, aiming to put its birding-specific features through their paces in the kind of everyday settings a typical user would actually experience.
A local country park with a birding hide, and my town's seafront gave me a good mix of woodland, marshland and open-water species to test the AI recognition on. A nearby churchyard, home to a resident family of peregrine falcons, gave me the chance to test the M1 against a truly challenging subject: a stealthy bird of prey that spends much of its time perched high and partially obscured.
Across all locations, I tested both handheld and tripod-mounted use. I used the on-device AI identification extensively in the field, and separately tested it against a batch of still photos to assess accuracy outside of live conditions.
All shooting was carried out during a hot, dry summer spell, so while I can vouch for the M1's performance in strong sunlight, I wasn't able to test its weatherproofing in wet or cold weather.
First reviewed July 2026
Sam has been writing about tech and digital culture for over 20 years, starting off in video games journalism before branching out into the wonderful worlds of consumer electronics, streaming entertainment and photography. Over the years he has written for Wired, Stuff, GQ, T3, Trusted Reviews and PC Zone, and now lives on the Kent coast in the UK – the ideal place for a camera reviewer to ply their trade.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 30, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 3, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, August 3, 2026.
Games long forgotten through time is getting a revival by one intrepid individual even as companies continue to raise funding, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
Featured stories
Vinita Sidhartha is on a curious quest to revive the games people played
Vinita’s unending fascination for traditional Indian games is the fuel that keeps Kreeda going. The Chennai-based organisation is dedicated to researching, documenting, and promoting the rich heritage of Indian games.
Snabbit says it has surpassed 1,15,000 jobs a day
Bengaluru-based on-demand home services platform Snabbit said it has crossed 1,15,000 fulfilled jobs a day. This milestone, the company noted, reflects not only the rising demand for on-demand domestic services but also its improving financial discipline as it scales. It also said the latest milestone comes only months after it surpassed 50,000 daily jobs and 1 million monthly jobs.
MobiKwik swings to net profit of Rs 7.6 Cr in Q1 FY27
Fintech company MobiKwik swung into profit for the first quarter of 2026-27, driven by strong growth in its payments business, improved lending profitability and continued focus on cost efficiency. The company reported a net profit of Rs 7.6 crore for the first quarter of FY27 as compared to a loss of Rs 42 crore a year ago. MobiKwik said it has now registered profitability for three consecutive quarters.
Funding news
ideaForge secures Rs 151 Cr from govt's RDI scheme
Leading drone manufacturer ideaForge Technology has secured a letter of intent for up to Rs 151 crore in long-term debt financing under the Government of India's Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) scheme to develop YETI, a heavy-lift autonomous aerial platform designed for operations in extreme terrains and high-altitude environments.
Kaapi Machines raises Rs 50 Cr from Sedna HoReCa
Kaapi Machines, a coffee equipment and service provider based in Bengaluru, has raised Rs 50 crore in equity funding from Sedna HoReCa, a PE-backed B2B solutions provider for the HoReCa segment (hotels, restaurants and cafes/catering).
RoadGrid secures Rs 13 crore TDB support for EV charger manufacturing
RoadGrid India has secured Rs 13 crore in financial assistance from the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology, for its Rs 27.5 crore project to establish a manufacturing and assembly facility for its patented Universal EV Charger. The upcoming plant, expected to begin commercial production in March 2027, will have an annual capacity of 2,000 chargers and generate over 100 direct jobs.
RoadGrid's charger integrates a 140 kW dual DC charging system with CCS2 and Type 6 connectors, along with AC charging capability, enabling charging across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial EVs on a single platform. The project aims to accelerate EV adoption by offering interoperable charging infrastructure developed using indigenous technology.
Quest Global makes investment in Lavni Ventures Fund II
Quest Global Engineering Services has announced a strategic investment in Lavni Ventures Fund II. A statement said the commitment is among the fund’s largest to date, signalling a deepening partnership between two organisations committed to advancing deep-tech innovations in sectors that include climate, energy, and health.
Lavni Ventures backs early-stage, deep-tech startups building science-led solutions. Quest Global views its commitment to Lavni Ventures Fund II as a strategic step toward advancing its innovation agenda and supporting the next generation of deep-tech solutions. In addition to capital, the Lavni Ventures portfolio companies will have access to Quest Global’s engineering expertise and technical mentorship, as well as opportunities to engage with its global enterprise ecosystem to validate and scale innovative solutions.
Yuvraj Singh joins stealth healthcare startup UN:BLOC as investor
Former Indian cricketer Yuvraj Singh has joined UN:BLOC, a new healthcare venture founded by entrepreneur Deepak Sahni, as an investor and member of its founding team.
The move marks their second entrepreneurial association after Yuvraj backed Sahni's previous venture, Healthians, during its early stages. UN:BLOC is currently operating in stealth mode, with details of its products and business model yet to be disclosed.
Yuvraj said he decided to back the company after understanding the scale of the healthcare challenges it aims to address and its potential to improve millions of lives. Sahni described Yuvraj's return as an early supporter as a significant milestone for the venture.
Other news
Anicut Capital, Chennai Angels partner to boost startup investments
Alternative asset manager Anicut Capital and angel investment network The Chennai Angels (TCA) have partnered to strengthen early-stage startup funding through a Category I Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) structure. The partnership aims to provide startups with institutional-grade capital while simplifying equity management through a single-investor cap table structure.
Anicut Capital manages over Rs 4,500 crore in assets across seven funds and has backed more than 200 companies. TCA, founded in 2007, has over 150 investors and has invested more than ₹200 crore across 99 startups. The collaboration seeks to combine TCA's deal sourcing capabilities with Anicut's investment management expertise to improve access to growth capital for startups.
Freshworks named leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for ITSM
Freshworks Inc. has been recognised as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for IT Service Management (ITSM) Platforms, reflecting its focus on AI-powered service operations. The company said the recognition comes as enterprises increasingly seek intelligent service management capabilities beyond traditional ticketing systems.
Freshworks CEO Dennis Woodside said the recognition highlights the company's commitment to building Freshservice into an AI-powered platform that combines service management with infrastructure and asset intelligence. Gartner's return to publishing the ITSM Magic Quadrant also signals the evolution of the market, driven by AI adoption and changing enterprise requirements for governance, automation and operational efficiency.
ICRA upgrades Groww's rating to AA with stable outlook
ICRA has upgraded the long-term rating of Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd, the parent company of investment platform Groww, to AA (Stable) from AA- (Stable), citing improvements in market position, capitalisation, profitability and liquidity.
The rating agency said Groww has remained India's largest stockbroker by active NSE clients for around 11 consecutive quarters, with a market share of about 29% as of June 2026. ICRA also highlighted the company's strengthened balance sheet following its $202 million Series F funding in 2025 and IPO proceeds of around ₹1,060 crore. Groww reported a consolidated tangible net worth of ₹8,413 crore as of March 31, 2026, while maintaining strong profitability despite regulatory changes.
Pegasystems expands university partnerships to build AI talent
Pegasystems Inc. has expanded its University Academic Program (UAP) by partnering with additional Indian universities to strengthen education in agentic AI, generative AI and enterprise automation. VEMU Technical University has joined the programme, while existing collaborations with the University of Engineering & Management (UEM), Kolkata, and Woxsen University have been expanded.
The initiative aims to train faculty and students in Pega technologies, creating a pipeline of industry-ready talent. The programme currently covers 23 universities, with plans to add another 30-40 institutions this year. Each 1.5-year cohort trains around 40-50 students, with several universities integrating the programme as a credit-based course in their engineering curricula.
QNu Labs, SRMIST launch quantum communications training initiative
QNu Labs, a sovereign quantum cybersecurity company incubated at IIT Madras Research Park, has partnered with SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) to train and certify its first batch of faculty in professional quantum communication courses. The collaboration also includes the establishment of a dedicated Quantum Communications Lab equipped with industry-grade quantum-safe products.
The initiative aims to strengthen faculty expertise, enabling universities to scale quantum education and produce industry-ready professionals. The lab will provide students and researchers with hands-on access to technologies already deployed across India's defence and banking sectors. The programme aligns with the National Quantum Mission's objective of building indigenous quantum technologies and skilled talent.
Licious partners with MoEngage for AI-driven customer engagement
Direct-to-consumer meat and seafood brand Licious has partnered with customer engagement platform MoEngage to strengthen AI-powered personalisation across its digital ecosystem. The collaboration is aimed at enhancing customer experience, driving repeat purchases and supporting the company's omnichannel expansion strategy.
Licious plans to use AI-driven insights based on customer preferences, regional tastes and location data to deliver personalised interactions throughout the purchase journey. The platform will help the company engage new customers while reactivating existing users through tailored product recommendations. The company said the initiative builds on its presence across online, quick commerce and offline retail channels as it seeks to deepen customer loyalty.
Safer Internet India launches online shopping safety handbook
Safer Internet India (SII) has launched Your Guide to Safe Online Shopping, a consumer handbook designed to help shoppers identify and avoid online frauds and scams. Commissioned by Amazon under its Mission GraHAQ initiative, the handbook offers practical guidance on safe online shopping practices and consumer protection.
Built around the themes of informed, alert and empowered consumers, the handbook covers common online shopping scams, consumer rights, grievance redressal mechanisms and measures to enhance digital safety. Mission GraHAQ, launched in 2022, has reached millions of consumers through awareness campaigns, digital outreach and partnerships promoting safe online shopping, payment security and fraud prevention across India.
Nemetschek India, CADD Centre launch AI-enabled BIM courses
Nemetschek India has partnered with CADD Centre to introduce a portfolio of AI-enabled Building Information Modelling (BIM) certification programmes aimed at developing digitally skilled professionals for the architecture, engineering and construction sector. The courses will cover technologies including Archicad, Solibri and Bluebeam.
The learning portfolio includes executive diploma, master certificate and specialised certification programmes integrating AI with BIM workflows. Initially launched across select CADD Centre locations in Chennai, Bengaluru and Pune, the courses will later expand across its wider network and be offered through the CloudKampus online platform. The initiative targets students, architects, engineers and working professionals seeking industry-focused digital construction skills.
Anaptyss launches employee innovation and IP incubation programme
AI-first managed services company Anaptyss has launched IGNITE, an enterprise-wide employee innovation and intellectual property incubation programme aimed at converting employee ideas into customer solutions, commercial value and patents. The initiative establishes a structured framework for idea generation, co-creation with customers and development of intellectual property.
Employees can participate through three tracks—IdeaLab, Co-Create and Patent Path—covering process improvements, customer-led innovation and patent creation. The programme includes leadership mentorship, executive sponsorship, milestone-based rewards and funding for prototype development and patent filing. Anaptyss said IGNITE is designed to institutionalise innovation as a core business capability while encouraging employees to contribute directly to the company's long-term growth and technology portfolio.
FarmerChat crosses 10 lakh users
Digital Green India has announced that FarmerChat, the multilingual, AI-powered farming advisory assistant it deploys, has crossed 10 lakh users in India since its launch in October 2024. Available in five languages, FarmerChat offers timely, context-aware guidance across a farmer's decisions, from crop and pest management to livestock care and weather, even in low-connectivity environments.
FarmerChat answers field-level questions across the farming cycle: crop planning, pest and disease management, livestock care, weather forecasts, and inputs. Building on this momentum, Digital Green India aims to add another 35 lakh farmers to the platform by 2028 — deepening women farmers' participation, driving adoption of climate-smart practices, and improving household incomes. In India, FarmerChat has already answered over 30 lakh queries, with women making up around 45% of its users.
Karnataka IT dept signs MoU with FICCI FLO Bengaluru
The Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, government of Karnataka, through the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with FICCI FLO Bengaluru and the FLO Bengaluru Industrial Park Association to strengthen support for women entrepreneurs across startups and manufacturing.
The partnership aims to create greater opportunities for women entrepreneurs by enhancing access to government programmes, mentorship, funding, industry connect and manufacturing infrastructure. The MoU aims to strengthen support for women entrepreneurs across startups, technology and manufacturing. Facilitate greater participation of women-led startups in flagship government programmes, Support women-led manufacturing enterprises through the FLO Bengaluru Industrial Park by facilitating access to industrial infrastructure, statutory approvals and government schemes.

articles.title: Grab 32GB of Corsair DDR5 for an effective $230 right now in this 9950X3D combo deal — Newegg RAM bundle ships with 16-core AMD X3D chip alongside an MSI X870E board and a free 240mm cooler for $1,308

Grab 32GB of Corsair DDR5 for an effective $230 right now in this 9950X3D combo deal — Newegg RAM bundle ships with 16-core AMD X3D chip alongside an MSI X870E board and a free 240mm cooler for $1,308
A powerful bundle to bring the cost of DDR5 memory down
RAM bundles are becoming one of the best ways to upgrade or build a new PC, as they help to bring down the effective cost for new memory modules compared to buying RAM separately. This powerhouse Newegg bundle is no exception, featuring the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, an MSI MPG X870E motherboard, and 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5 RAM for $1,308.99.
● Check out this deal on Newegg
This bundle saves you $259.99 compared to buying each part individually but, more importantly, it means you're effectively paying just $230 for the RAM, compared to its $489.99 list price. That's also a huge drop of $150 compared to the nearest, cheapest equivalent RAM kit on the market right now, and doesn't factor in the additional free $70 MSI cooler you're getting with this bundle, too.
A powerhouse bundle for gaming that ships with the 16-core AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi ATX motherboard, and 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM.
Also included, for free, is an MSI MAG 240mm AIO cooler worth $72. The bundle makes the effective RAM cost just $230 right now.
The RAM isn't the only thing that stands out with this kit combo, however, as you're getting the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D for your next gaming PC with this deal. This Zen 5 CPU has 16 cores and 32 threads and ships with a huge 128MB of L3 cache capacity. It's built using the second generation of AMD's V-Cache technology, with a redesigned stacking layout that allows for better thermal performance. The extra cache means that the CPU isn't forced to drop back and use the slower system RAM as often, helping to ensure better and more consistent frame rates, especially in CPU-hungry games like Cyberpunk 2077.
The CPU benchmark data shows that the 9950X3D can match the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D's performance for gaming, especially when using AMD's Precision Boost Overdrive overclocking. It also has the advantage of unleashing its full 16 cores for multi-threaded performance when you need it to.
