articles.title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Could Let Model Repositories Execute Arbitrary Code
articles.text:
Three high-severity security flaws have been disclosed in Hugging Face's Diffusers library that could allow crafted model repositories to stealthily execute arbitrary code on machines that load it, opening the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain to security risk.
"These vulnerabilities are bypassing trust_remote_code, the safeguard designed to stop unreviewed code from running in the custom pipelines loading process," Zafran Labs researchers Gal Zaban and Ido Shani said in an analysis published last week.
The shortcomings have been collectively named FaceHugger.
With Hugging Face becoming the "GitHub of the AI era" and its libraries and repositories prevalent in enterprise environments, vulnerabilities in libraries like Diffusers can grant attackers extensive access owing to how the library is embedded into production pipelines, CI/CD systems, and container images.
Diffusers is a Python package that serves as a library of state-of-the-art (SOTA) pretrained diffusion models for generating videos, images, and audio. According to statistics shared on pepy.tech, the package has been downloaded more than 8.1 million times in July 2026.
One of the key capabilities of the library is to locally load a model from a Hugging Face hub repository via the DiffusionPipeline API, which, in turn, makes use of a configuration file to initialize specific pipeline and component classes, along with custom pipeline code.
The "trust_remote_code" parameter in Diffusers is a security safeguard that controls whether custom Python code hosted inside a model repository is allowed to execute during "from_pretrained()" loading. Setting it to "True" permits custom code execution, while "False" or omitting it blocks unverified code from running.
"The root cause of all different RCE variants [...] is that the trust check lives entirely in the first phase," Zafran explained. "Therefore, any method that makes the loader see custom code that the gate did not, allows bypassing the trust_remote_code mechanism."
Each variant has been traced back to a case of Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU), with the model download designed as two sequential, non-atomic HTTP requests instead of one a "single atomic operation" and the "trust_remote_code" security gate configured to run only against the first.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-44827 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A code injection vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be loaded through the custom_pipeline flow from a Hub repository by means of a crafted pipeline with the name "None.py" despite passing trust_remote_code=False (or omitting it, which is the default).
- CVE-2026-45804 (CVSS score: 7.5) - A race condition vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be introduced to a repository by modifying the configuration between the hf_hub_download and snapshot_download HTTP calls to the Hub, leading to code execution.
- CVE-2026-44513 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A code injection vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be loaded through the custom_pipeline flow from a Hub repository despite passing trust_remote_code=False (or omitting it).
Following responsible disclosure, the vulnerabilities were addressed in Diffusers version 0.38.0, released in early May 2026. Any user who invokes "DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained" with custom pipelines is impacted.
"The underlying problem is that artifacts pulled from AI repositories are frequently treated as passive data, when configuration files, loaders, and custom pipeline code can quietly cross into executable code and turn a routine model load into an initial-access vector," the researchers added.
If immediate patching is not an option, the project maintainers have recommended the following workarounds -
- Only call from_pretrained with pretrained_model_name_or_path, custom_pipeline, and local snapshot directories from fully trusted sources that have been audited.
- Do not pass custom_pipeline= pointing at a Hub repository different from the primary pretrained_model_name_or_path before reading its pipeline.py.
- Before calling from_pretrained on a local snapshot, inspect the snapshot for unexpected *.py files, especially under component subdirectories (unet/, scheduler/, etc.) and at the snapshot root.
"These vulnerabilities underscore the critical need to treat AI model repositories as untrusted code, particularly as enterprise reliance on platforms like Hugging Face continues to grow," Zafran said. "A routine model download can easily become a vector for arbitrary code execution if security boundaries like trust_remote_code are bypassed."

articles.title: Palworld’s expanding to mobile with a new MMORPG
articles.text:
After its 1.0 launch last month, Palworld is coming to iOS and Android with a new open-world MMORPG launching later this year, Polygon reports. Garena, the developer behind the new game, says in its announcement that Palworld Online “reimagines the depth, freedom, and scale of the original PC survival creature-collecting title for mobile.”
Palworld’s expanding to mobile with a new MMORPG
Palworld Online will expand on the original game with a new setting and new story elements.
The core features of the new mobile game sound a lot like the original Palworld, with crafting, creature collecting, and multiplayer options for co-op, PvP, and PvE. Garena says it will introduce a “new narrative setting with original story elements,” and “expand the narrative with new side stories created exclusively for this version.” It will also have a “streamlined, touch-friendly interface with optional one-tap controls” to handle base management on different sized mobile screens.
Palworld Online doesn’t have a specific release date yet, but if it does come out this year, it could arrive before the Palfarm spin-off Pocketpair announced last year, which also doesn’t have a release date yet.

Nasa-Rover Curiosity entdeckt ein Meer an mysteriösen Wabenstrukturen auf dem Mars
articles.text:
Mars-Geheimnisse: Nasa-Rover Curiosity entdeckt ein Meer an unerklärlichen Wabenstrukturen
Der Nasa-Rover Curiosity hat Strukturen auf dem Marsboden entdeckt, die an Waben von Honigbienen erinnern. Diese Formationen werden als polygonale Brüche bezeichnet und haben jeweils einen Durchmesser von vier bis acht Zentimetern. Auf der Erde entstehen solche wabenartigen Strukturen etwa durch thermische Kontraktionen.
Nasa-Rover Curiosity unterwegs im Valle Grande
Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass der Rover Curiosity diese seltsamen Strukturen auf dem Mars beobachtet hat. Laut Nasa wurden jedoch noch nie so viele der polygonalen Brüche wie jetzt an einem Ort entdeckt.
Der Rover hat sie im Marstal „Valle Grande“ entdeckt und ein 360 Grad-Panorama aufgenommen – die polygonalen Formen erstrecken sich in alle Richtungen, so weit der Rover blicken kann. „Wir haben durch die Augen von Curiosity schon viele faszinierende Landschaften gesehen, aber dieses Meer aus Polygonen hat uns den Atem geraubt“, sagt Ashwin Vasavada, Projektwissenschaftler der Curiosity-Mission.
Forscher müssen noch herausfinden, was die polygonalen Brüche verursacht
Forschende wissen bisher nicht, was die wabenartigen Strukturen auf dem Mars verursacht. Einige der Polygone, die die Mission in der Vergangenheit entdeckt hat, sind eindeutig als Schlammrisse zu erkennen, wobei verschiedene Prozesse zu ihrer wabenartigen Struktur beitragen könnten. Eine Theorie von Forschenden ist, dass zum Beispiel Temperaturwechsel zwischen warm und kalt dafür verantwortlich sind.
Noch fehlen jedoch eindeutige Beweise, die die Herkunft der seltsamen Strukturen erklären. Darüber kann bislang also nur spekuliert werden. Der neueste Fund des Nasa-Rovers könnte die Wissenschaftler:innen ein Stück näher an die Erklärung bringen. „Wir haben ihre Formen und ihre chemische Zusammensetzung sorgfältig vermessen und hoffen, dass die Daten Hinweise darauf liefern, wie diese Strukturen entstanden sind“, sagt Vasavada von der Nasa.
Auf der Suche nach Leben auf dem Mars
Im Laufe seiner Mission auf dem Mars hat der Curiosity Schwefelkristalle, Meteoriten und eine Vielzahl geologischer Merkmale entdeckt. Außerdem konnten Wissenschaftler:innen durch die Mission schon feststellen, dass der Mars in seiner frühen Geschichte viel feuchter war und er die chemischen Bedingungen sowie Nährstoffe bot, die mikrobielles Leben ermöglichten.
Bei der Erforschung des Planeten stoßen Wissenschaftler:innen immer wieder auf Hinweise für Leben, oder vergangenes Leben, auf dem Mars. Ein Forschungsteam der University of Arkansas hat im vergangenen Jahr etwa „starke Hinweise“ darauf gefunden, dass es auf dem Mars mal einen großen Ozean gegeben hat.
Der Mars hält immer wieder Überraschungen bereit. Eine Raumsonde der Europäischen Weltraumorganisation Esa, entdeckte kürzlich einen Ausschnitt des Kaiser-Krater-Bodens, der scheinbar von metallisch schimmernden Wellen bedeckt ist.

articles.title: Egypt’s PraxiLabs named winner of Visa’s “She’s Next” programme - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup PraxiLabs has been selected as winner of Visa’s “She’s Next” programme, taking home US$20,000 in prize money.
“She’s Next”, delivered in collaboration with CIB Business Banking and Shark Tank, is designed to empower women entrepreneurs and accelerate business growth through access to training, mentorship, visibility, and funding.
This year’s edition attracted more than 2,500 applications from women-led businesses, after which nine finalists were selected to pitch their businesses to a distinguished panel of experts and investors.
PraxiLabs, which has developed an interactive virtual lab for science education, was named overall winner, securing US$20,000 in prize money. Sustainable fashion brand Up-Fuse was second, banking US$15,000, and prop-tech startup Kennah third, winning US$10,000.
Over the past months, participants in the programme benefited from specialised training and mentorship sessions focused on strengthening business models, improving pitch readiness, leveraging digital tools and emerging technologies, and preparing for sustainable growth. The winners were recognised for their innovative business models, strong growth potential, and ability to address real market needs.
“This year’s winners reflect the creativity, ambition, and resilience of women entrepreneurs in Egypt. Through She’s Next, Visa is proud to support women-led businesses with the tools, resources, funding, and networks they need to grow, scale, and create lasting impact. We believe that when women entrepreneurs are empowered, they not only grow their own businesses, but also contribute to stronger communities and a more inclusive economy,” said Malak El Baba, vice president and country manager for Visa in Egypt, Libya, and Sudan.

articles.title: Operation Sindoor architect AK Bharti signs off after 39 years
articles.text:
Operation Sindoor architect AK Bharti signs off after 39 years
Air Marshal A.K. Bharti retired on 31 July 2026 after a distinguished career spanning frontline fighter operations, strategic appointments and a defining role in Operation Sindoor.
Air Marshal AK Bharti, the officer who became the public face of the Indian Air Force during Operation Sindoor, retired on 31 July 2026 after 39 years in uniform. He spent his last morning in service at the National War Memorial in New Delhi, laying a wreath for soldiers who never got a retirement of their own. He stepped down as Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, a post held since 1 June 2025, and was succeeded by Air Marshal Tejpal Singh on 1 August 2026.
The man nobody had heard of
Until the second week of May 2025, Awadhesh Kumar Bharti was a name known inside Air Headquarters and almost nowhere else. That changed on 11 May, when he sat at the National Media Centre in New Delhi alongside Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai and Vice Admiral AN Pramod for the first joint briefing on Operation Sindoor. He spoke in short sentences, declined to guess at figures he could not confirm, and recited a couplet from the Ramcharitmanas from memory to explain the shift in India's posture. The lines describe Lord Ram's patience with the sea running out after three days, after which he lifts his bow.
He was born in Jhunni Kala village in Bihar's Purnea district, to Jiwachh Lal Yadav, who worked in the finance department of the Kosi Irrigation Projects, and Urmila Devi. In 1977 he was one of 140 boys admitted to Sainik School Tilaiya. Six years later, 28 of that batch cleared the National Defence Academy examination. He was among them. At the NDA he won the President's Silver Medal and set a cross country record that stood for years, which is where the nickname Galloping Horse came from. At the Air Force Academy, Dundigal, he finished first in overall merit and took the Sword of Honour.
Four thousand hours and a Sukhoi squadron
Commissioned into the fighter stream on 13 June 1987, Bharti logged more than 4,000 hours across the MiG-21, MiG-29, Su-30MKI and Su-30MKM. He qualified as a Fighter Combat Leader and earned three stars for accident free flying. He was Flight Commander of No. 24 Squadron before taking command of No. 30 Squadron in August 2005, a tenure to September 2007 that placed him at the centre of operationalising the Su-30MKI's weapon systems. Under his command the squadron took part in exercises including Gagan Shakti, Indradhanush 2006 and Garuda 2007. He later commanded a frontline fighter base at Lohegaon, and as Air Attaché in Malaysia trained Malaysian pilots on the Su-30MKM.
The staff appointments mattered as much. At Strategic Forces Command and then Air Headquarters, he held jobs concerned with how India would fight rather than how it trains. Promoted to Air Marshal on 1 September 2023, he became Senior Air Staff Officer at Central Air Command in Prayagraj, and took over as Director General of Air Operations in October 2024.
What does the Director General of Air Operations actually do
The DGAO sits at Air Headquarters and owns the air operations brief for the entire service: target sets, force allocation, tasking across commands and the air defence picture over Indian territory.
A political decision to strike is not a flying programme. Somebody has to convert intent into aircraft, weapons, routes, timings and the defensive cover that brings crews home. That conversion happens at the DGAO's desk, which is also why offence and air defence sit under the same appointment.
Fifteen days, then nine targets
Operation Sindoor followed the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025, in which 26 civilians were killed. Fifteen days later, in the early hours of 7 May, India struck nine terrorist sites in Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir, including facilities at Bahawalpur and Muridke. When Pakistan retaliated, the IAF shifted to military targets while the air defence network absorbed drones and missiles.
Asked at the briefings what weapons had been used and what damage they had caused, Bharti said only that the methods chosen had produced the desired effects on enemy targets. On Pakistani aircraft, he said their planes had been prevented from crossing, that a few had been brought down, and that all Indian pilots were back home. He credited the Integrated Air Command and Control System and indigenous platforms such as Akash, and tied that capability to a decade of sustained budgetary backing. Pakistan has disputed Indian accounts of the exchange.
He was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal in 2008, the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal on Republic Day 2024, and the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal, the highest of India's wartime distinguished service awards, in the honours list announced on 14 August 2025.
What he leaves behind
As Deputy Chief, Bharti spent his final year pushing indigenisation harder than the timelines were comfortable with. At an industry event in September 2025, he told manufacturers that even 99% indigenous content counts for little if critical components remain import dependent, and that innovation needed to move off cruise setting. That argument, more than any single operation, is the brief his successor inherits, at a moment when the IAF is chasing squadron strength, an indigenous engine and the AMCA programme at once. The campaign made his name. The procurement fight will decide whether its lessons hold.

articles.title: ExfilSquad hackers leak info of over 100,000 UK police officers, staff
articles.text:
A cyberattack on the U.K.'s Police National Legal Database (PNLD) has compromised contact data of more than 100,000 police officers and other criminal justice professionals.
The intrusion was detected on Sunday, July 26, and was later claimed by the ExfilSquad data extortion group, which alleges it stole 135,000 contact records.
PNLD is an online legal resource service that has been used for more than 30 years by the 43 Home Office police forces in England and Wales, as well as the British Transport Police.
PNLD also operates ‘Ask the Police,’ a public-facing website with answers to hundreds of common policing and legal questions.
In a statement today, the service says that the breach exposed the full names, organizations, and email addresses of police officers, staff, criminal justice professionals, and government partners.
Also considered compromised are the names and email addresses of Ask the Police users who submitted a question through the platform.
The incident is now being investigated with assistance from cybersecurity experts and the National Crime Agency (NCA). No evidence has been found that passwords or other security credentials have been compromised.
PNLD does not hold confidential information relating to victims, witnesses, or offenders, and says no such data was impacted.
“All affected organizations were contacted in the days following the incident and provided with further information and guidance. The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) has also been notified,” PNLD says.
ExfilSquad claims 135,000 records
The ExfilSquad data extortion group claimed responsibility for the attack on PNLD and published sample data to support its claims. The threat actor also demanded a ransom in exchange for not releasing the remaining stolen data.
ExfilSquad claims to have stolen 1.9 GB of data from PNLD, including approximately 135,000 records. According to the group, the data consists of information belonging to 114,000 PNLD subscribers and 21,000 Ask the Police users.
ExfilSquad is the same threat actor that recently claimed an attack on American semiconductor company Analog Devices.
PNLD has confirmed the breach and publication of contact details but has not publicly attributed the intrusion or disclosed how attackers gained access.
BleepingComputer has contacted PNLD to ask for more details about the incident and will update the article when we receive a reply.

articles.title: Microsoft Releases TypeScript 7.0 with a Native Go Compiler, Delivering 10x Faster Builds
articles.text:
Microsoft has released TypeScript 7.0, the first stable version of the language to ship its long-in-development native compiler, a faithful port of the toolset from TypeScript into Go that the team says typically delivers speedups of between 8x and 12x on full builds.
The project began as an experimental native port first announced in March 2025, and had been available to the community as the @typescript/native-preview package, which reached over 8.5 million weekly downloads.
With 7.0, nightly builds move back under the standard typescript package on the next tag, and the new tsc executable installs the usual way:
npm install -D typescript
Microsoft published build times against real codebases to back the numbers. On the VS Code source, a full build fell from 125.7 seconds on TypeScript 6 to 10.6 seconds, an 11.9x improvement, while aggregate memory use dropped by around 18 percent. Editors benefit too, because the new tooling is built on the Language Server Protocol and uses multiple threads. Opening a file with an error in the VS Code codebase previously took about 17.5 seconds, and now takes under 1.3 seconds.
Teams testing early releases reported similar gains. Slack engineers said the change brought CI type-checking from about 7.5 minutes to 1.25 minutes, and Vanta reported positive results too:
Our tsgo adoption at Vanta has been pretty high-impact. Everything is so, so much faster now.
Parallelism can be tuned with the new --checkers and --builders flags, or switched off entirely with --singleThreaded for constrained environments.
TypeScript 7.0 ships without a stable programmatic API, which the team expects to land in 7.1, so tools like typescript-eslint and the framework tooling for Vue, Svelte, Astro, MDX and Angular cannot use it yet.
On a Hacker News thread, one developer shared the numbers, and offered congraduations to the team and their migration:
The speed up numbers based on their testing:
Codebase TypeScript 6 TypeScript 7 Speedup vscode 125.7s 10.6s 11.9x sentry 139.8s 15.7s 8.9x bluesky 24.3s 2.8s 8.7x playwright 12.8s 1.47s 8.7x tldraw 11.2s 1.46s 7.7x Congratulations to the team for pulling off this feat while doing a responsible migration
Elsewhere a commenter on the blog noted that projects using webpack loaders will need to wait:
I’m excited to upgrade all my projects to use TypeScript 7, but most of them use webpack, and there seems to be no API surface in the 7.0 release for webpack loaders to utilize.
I’ll sadly have to wait for 7.1.
That side-by-side path is central to migration. Microsoft published a compatibility package, @typescript/typescript6, that provides a tsc6 binary and re-exports the 6.0 API so existing tooling keeps working, wired up through npm aliases.
TypeScript 7.0 also turns 6.0's deprecations into hard errors, with strict and esnext now the defaults, so the team recommends adopting TypeScript 6.0 first to smooth the jump. Detailed behavioural differences are tracked in the project's CHANGES.md.
Unlike faster tools such as esbuild, swc and Biome, which strip or transpile types without checking them, TypeScript 7.0 keeps full type-checking while closing much of the speed gap. The team says feature work resumes now that the port has shipped, with new releases expected every three to four months and 7.1 focused on the API the wider ecosystem is waiting on.
TypeScript is an open-source programming language developed and maintained by Microsoft, distributed under the Apache 2.0 license. It builds on JavaScript by adding optional static typing, making it easier to catch errors early and build large-scale applications with confidence.

articles.title: Airtel chases Kenya's small businesses with merchant wallet
articles.text:
Airtel Money Kenya is targeting small businesses with a new digital wallet as it seeks to deepen customer engagement after increasing its share of Kenya’s mobile money market to 10.9%, signalling a new phase in its challenge to Safaricom’s M-PESA.
The launch of Bizna Wallet on Monday comes as merchant payments emerge as one of the fastest-growing segments of Kenya’s mobile money market.
Safaricom, which dominates the sector, more than doubled the number of merchants using Pochi la Biashara to 2.1 million in the year ended March, while revenue from the product rose 86% to KES 4 billion ($31 million). The figures suggest merchant services are becoming a meaningful growth engine, creating an opening for rivals that have spent years focused primarily on attracting new users.
Airtel’s customer base has expanded steadily through lower transfer costs, broader agent coverage and partnerships with banks.
According to the company, Airtel Money now serves more than six million customers through a network of 270,000 agents and over two million merchant outlets.
The challenge has now shifted from persuading customers to open wallets to making Airtel Money an integral part of how they run their businesses.
Competing for merchant payments
Bizna Wallet targets Kenya’s informal economy, where many traders still receive customer payments through personal mobile money wallets. The product provides a dedicated wallet for business income, allowing merchants to separate business earnings from household spending without opening another account.
Micro, small and medium enterprises employ more than 14.9 million people, contribute between 30% and 34% of Kenya’s gross domestic product and account for more than 90% of private businesses, according to a 2026 study by Strathmore University Business School.
Many of those businesses, from market traders and neighbourhood shops to salons and boda boda riders, depend on mobile money to receive payments. Yet many continue to use personal wallets, making it more difficult to separate business income from household expenses, track cash flow and maintain accurate records.
“Our entrepreneurs need more than just a platform to send and receive money,” Acting Airtel Money Kenya managing director Michael Bonke said. “They need a financial solution that will help them manage their day-to-day business activities.”
Airtel said customers will not pay fees when transferring money into a Bizna Wallet, a pricing decision that could encourage broader adoption among small businesses.
The product closely resembles Safaricom’s Pochi la Biashara, underscoring how merchant services have become the next battleground in Kenya’s mobile money market. Whereas earlier competition centred on transaction pricing and customer acquisition, the focus is increasingly shifting towards boosting transaction volumes and merchant activity.
Platform overhaul lays the groundwork
Bonke devoted much of the launch to discussing Airtel Money’s technology rather than the product itself, pointing to a recent upgrade of the company’s core payments platform.
“We’ve recently upgraded our Airtel Money system to allow us to have a faster go-to-market,” he said.
According to Airtel, the investment has enabled Airtel to introduce products and partnerships at a quicker pace while improving reliability and security. In recent months, the investment has seen Airtel deepen integrations with banks, retailers and government agencies, allowing customers to move money between Airtel Money and all major Kenyan banks. Bizna Wallet is one of the first products built on that upgraded infrastructure.
Airtel paired the launch with changes to its loyalty programme, replacing airtime rewards with cashback paid directly into customers’ Airtel Money wallets. Eligible transactions, including person-to-person transfers, merchant payments and bill payments, will now return 50% of transaction fees as cash instead of airtime.
“As I begin this new chapter as CEO of Airtel Kenya, I am honoured that one of my first engagements is the launch of Airtel Money Business Wallet and the 50% cashback programme,” chief executive Djibril Tobe said. “They reflect our commitment to empowering Kenyan businesses and advancing financial inclusion.”
The cashback programme gives customers a reason to leave money inside Airtel Money and continue transacting instead of immediately converting rewards into airtime or cashing out.
Safaricom still commands the vast majority of Kenya’s mobile money market, but the rapid growth of its merchant business has highlighted where the sector’s next expansion opportunity lies.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Un fragmento de cohete de SpaceX va a estrellarse contra la Luna este miércoles. Y los científicos están encantados
articles.text:
A los humanos no nos gustan los objetos que impactan sobre la Tierra, pero los que chocan con la Luna son un caramelito para la ciencia. No suponen un riesgo para nuestro planeta (deberían ser objetos enormes para que así fuera) y nos dan información muy interesante. No hay más que ver el caso del asteroide 2024 YR4, que durante mucho tiempo se pensó que podría chocar con la Tierra en 2028. Los últimos cálculos eliminan esa posibilidad, pero sí que siguen manteniendo la Luna dentro de la franja de impacto posible. Esto, lejos de ser tan preocupante como era el posible impacto con la Tierra, brinda a los astrónomos la posibilidad de estudiar un impacto conocido sobre nuestro satélite. Pero, en realidad, no habrá que esperar hasta 2028. Este mismo miércoles tendrá lugar el impacto en la Luna de la etapa superior de un cohete de SpaceX. Eso también puede darnos datos muy interesantes.
Un cohete de SpaceX muy conocido. El objeto que impactará con la Luna el próximo miércoles, 5 de agosto, a las 8:44 (hora peninsular española) es la etapa superior de un Falcon 9 que se lanzó en enero de 2025 con dos módulos lunares a bordo: el Blue Ghost, de Firefly Aerospace, y el Hakuto-R MIssion 2, de la compañía japonesa ispace. Tras liberar ambas cargas útiles sin problema, el propulsor del cohete aterrizó de nuevo en la Tierra, mientras que la etapa superior quedó libre en el espacio. Todo esto es el proceso normal de cualquier cohete reutilizable de SpaceX. Normalmente, se hace un seguimiento de la etapa superior, que o se convierte en basura espacial o acaba reentrando en nuestro planeta. Pero, en este caso, dicho seguimiento ha mostrado un final diferente: la etapa superior chocará con la Luna.
Las predicciones. Los primeros cálculos sobre el futuro impacto apuntan a que este debe producirse cerca de los cráteres Einstein y Bell, en el extremo lunar occidental. La columna de eyección, que se producirá inmediatamente después, podría llegar a medir entre 75 y 100 kilómetros de altura, generando un brillo que contrastaría con la oscuridad en torno a nuestro satélite. Por eso, los científicos que han analizado el suceso creen que podrá verse tanto con telescopios espaciales como terrestres. Incluso los aficionados podrán verlo con un telescopio suficientemente sensible.
Lo que nos enseña este impacto. Más allá de un curioso espectáculo, el impacto de este cohete de SpaceX sobre la Luna puede dar información muy importante a los científicos. Para empezar, servirá para probar los sistemas que ya hay en la Luna de análisis de actividad sísmica. Estos están diseñados para, en caso de detectarse un temblor muy grande, identificar su origen. Dado que en este caso el origen ya se conoce y estará perfectamente monitorizado, se podrá comprobar si estos sistemas están bien calibrados.
Por otro lado, se espera que las partículas liberadas por el choque del cohete de SpaceX viajen incluso a 1.000 kilómetros de distancia. Es importante estudiar cómo se comportan, ya que, en un futuro, si se produce un impacto parecido con astronautas trabajando sobre la Luna, podría suponer un peligro para ellos. Es importante monitorizar estos eventos sin humanos pululando aún por nuestro satélite. En el futuro, cuando se construyan bases lunares, será muy habitual que haya personas trabajando en ellas, por lo que es importante predecir el comportamiento de cualquier impacto para que estas estén a salvo.
No se puede saber todo. Según ha explicado a Space uno de los científicos que han analizado el comportamiento del cohete de SpaceX, William Jo, los cálculos pueden ser excesivamente optimistas. Quizás la columna no sea ni tan alta ni tan brillante. Pero está claro que la información que nos aporte seguirá siendo muy útil de cara a la futura colonización lunar. Por eso hay tantos ojos puestos en ese cohete jubilado que se dirige poco a poco hacia una muerte anunciada sobre la Luna. No es óptimo que impacte con la Luna, pues es una clara muestra de los riesgos que supone la basura espacial, pero al menos nos ayuda a prepararnos para cuando otro trozo de chatarra impacte sin avisar.

articles.title: Microsoft teams revoit le design de son interface pour éviter les clics accidentels
articles.text:
Jusqu’à présent, Microsoft Teams ne brillait pas vraiment par l’efficacité de son interface. Trop encombrée, celle-ci conduisait souvent à des erreurs de clic de la part des utilisateurs, provoquant, par exemple, des partages d’écran accidentels, ou des départs involontaires de réunions. Pour éviter ces erreurs de clics, Microsoft a revu et optimisé l’interface de Teams pour corriger ces problèmes.
Des changements majeurs dans l’interface
Pour commencer, Microsoft a mené une réorganisation des commandes principales de la réunion. Celles-ci ont été repositionnées en haut au centre de l’écran.
L’équipe en charge du design de l’interface a par ailleurs modifié le bouton permettant de quitter une réunion en cours. Auparavant, celui-ci était situé à côté des options de partage et des boutons permettant de gérer l’activation de la caméra et du micro. Désormais, le bouton pour quitter une réunion prend place tout à droite de la fenêtre pour éviter de cliquer dessus accidentellement alors que vous souhaitiez simplement activer ou désactiver votre caméra ou votre micro.
Microsoft a également procédé à un nettoyage en règle des fonctionnalités proposées par défaut dans l’interface de Teams. Pour désencombrer la barre d’outils principale, les fonctions les moins utilisées ont été migrées dans un menu déroulant. Vous y retrouverez ainsi la fonction d’enregistrement et de sous-titrage, les notes de réunion et les salles pour petits groupes, ou encore les sondages, le tableau blanc, Planner, ou encore YouTube.
Plus de contrôle pour l’IA
Microsoft en a également profité pour proposer une importante nouveauté concernant la gestion de l’intelligence artificielle dans l’application. Vous pouvez dorénavant désactiver toutes les fonctionnalités d’IA, comme Copilot, Facilitator ou Récap, en un clic en cours de réunion. Bonne nouvelle, ce réglage reste accessible même si vous utilisez une machine administrée, notamment en entreprise. Vous n’aurez donc besoin d’aucune autorisation pour y accéder.
Le déploiement de cette nouvelle interface est en cours et devrait se faire de manière progressive. Il devrait toutefois arriver chez tous les utilisateurs dans le courant du mois d’août.

articles.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI
articles.text:
At a glance
- Orchard is an open-source framework for scalable and cost-effective agentic AI research, built around Orchard Env, a reusable environment service for training and evaluating agents across task domains.
- The same Orchard infrastructure supports software-engineering, web-navigation, and personal-assistant agents, and can train them directly inside real deployment harnesses such as Codex, OpenClaw, and ZeroClaw—letting researchers reuse environments, data pipelines, and evaluation workflows across tasks.
- Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw demonstrate that relatively small open-weight models can achieve strong results on complex real-world tasks. For example, Orchard-SWE reaches 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified—73.0% with value-model reranking—using only about 3 billion active parameters, approaching frontier systems using more than 10 times larger models.
Alongside the models and workflows, the project releases training data and evaluation methods intended to help the broader research community build and study open agentic systems. Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving beyond static question-answering toward autonomous agents that can plan, reason, and act across complex, multistep environments. These systems can fix bugs in complex codebases, navigate the web on a user’s behalf, and manage workflows involving calendars and email.
While there is excitement around agentic AI’s capabilities, the research community faces a persistent bottleneck. Building state-of-the-art agentic systems often requires proprietary infrastructure, including custom sandboxes, closed training pipelines, and proprietary datasets that most researchers and practitioners cannot access or reproduce.
To address this gap, we introduce Orchard (opens in new tab), an open-source framework for scalable agentic modeling. At the center of Orchard is Orchard Env, a lightweight, Kubernetes environment that provides reusable isolated components for running and building agents at scale—from collecting training data to reinforcement learning rollouts and evaluation.
Unlike many existing frameworks, Orchard Env is designed to support different agent systems and task types without modification. The same service can support software-engineering agents, web-browsing agents, and personal-assistant agents across domains.
To demonstrate this approach, we are releasing three domain-specific training recipes—Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw. (opens in new tab) We are also releasing the training data and evaluation methods used to build them.
Environment layer that scales across types of tasks
The central idea behind Orchard is that the runtime environment should be a standalone, reusable service rather than infrastructure embedded inside a specific training framework. Orchard Env’s Kubernetes foundation enables it to create, manage, and remove thousands of isolated components in parallel.
The system is designed to work across tasks like coding, web browsing, using tools. It is also designed to work across different agent systems, along with stages of the training and evaluation process, including data distillation and reinforcement learning rollouts.
This flexibility makes Orchard practical at a research scale. Teams can introduce new benchmarks, agent systems, or training algorithms without rebuilding the underlying infrastructure from scratch.
Orchard also makes it possible to train agents inside any harness. Today’s most capable agents rarely run as a bare model. They operate through sophisticated harnesses—such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw—that manage multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and connections to external systems. Open training tools usually cannot handle these stateful, multi-process harnesses, forcing researchers to train on a simplified stand-in and then deploy in the real setting, which creates a mismatch. Orchard closes this gap: a lightweight proxy records the harness’s own model calls as training data while each rollout runs in its own container, so an agent can be trained end-to-end directly in the harness that it will be deployed with—OpenClaw, Codex, ZeroClaw, or others—and across several harnesses.
Orchard-SWE: Advancing open-source software engineering agents
Software engineering is one of the most demanding settings for autonomous agents. It requires multi-step reasoning over real codebases, tool use, and the ability to recover from mistakes. Orchard-SWE is our training workflow for this domain. It is built using the Mini-SWE-Agent framework, designed to autonomously solve software engineering tasks, and evaluated on the widely used SWE-bench Verified benchmark, which tests a model’s ability to navigate, diagnose, and repair real-world codebases.
To train the system, we distilled 107,000 agent interactions from two advanced open-weight models (MiniMax-M2.5 and Qwen3.5-397B) covering a broad range of GitHub Issues. The training process uses credit-assignment supervised fine-tuning: rather than discarding attempts where the agent failed to fully resolve an issue, the system learns from the productive portions of those partial attempts, expanding the amount of useful training data available to the model.
Reinforcement learning comes next, but its feedback is sparse—an agent usually learns only whether its final patch passed or failed the hidden tests. We start with Balanced Adaptive Rollout, designed to make the most of these infrequent success signals, and then add two “dense reward” techniques for richer guidance: on-policy distillation, in which a stronger teacher model scores the agent’s decisions step by step, and a process reward model, in which an AI judge rewards sound problem-solving process—writing tests that reproduce the bug, verifying the fix, and checking that existing behavior still works—independent of whether the final tests passed.
Finally, we train a value model on past rollouts to rerank candidate solutions. Reinforcement learning generates many practice trajectories that are normally discarded; instead, trajectories from 20 prior experiments train a compact 4-billion-parameter value model that recognizes high-quality solutions, and at problem-solving time it scores several candidate answers and picks the best one. Together, these techniques take Orchard-SWE from a 61.4% baseline on SWE-bench Verified to 69.1% with Balanced Adaptive Rollout and 69.7% with the dense-reward techniques—a new state of the art among open-source models of comparable size (roughly 3 billion active parameters)—rising to 73% with value-model reranking, approaching frontier systems more than 10 times larger, as shown in Figure 1.
Orchard-GUI: A lightweight browser agent for real-world web tasks
Web navigation presents a different set of challenges. Agents must interpret visual layouts, interact with dynamic interfaces, and complete open-ended tasks described only in natural language.
Orchard-GUI trains a 4-billion-parameter vision-language model as a browser agent using a relatively small amount of supervision: 400 distilled demonstrations combined with 2,200 open-ended training tasks. Despite this limited training data, the resulting model achieves strong results across several web-navigation benchmarks: 74.1% on WebVoyager, 67.0% on Online-Mind2Web, and 64.0% on DeepShop, for an average of 68.4%, as shown in Figure 1.
These results place Orchard-GUI among the strongest open-source web agents to date while remaining competitive with larger proprietary models. The results also suggest that with the right training approach and environment, small open models can perform well on real-world web tasks.
Orchard-Claw: Personal assistant agents for everyday productivity
Many of the most impactful agentic applications involve everyday productivity tasks, including reading and drafting emails, managing calendars, searching for information, and coordinating across tools. Orchard-Claw focuses on personal-assistant tasks by training an agent on just 200 synthetic tasks. Evaluated on Claw-Eval, a benchmark covering realistic productivity workflows, it successfully completes 59.6% of tasks when given up to three attempts. That increases to 73.9% when paired with the stronger ZeroClaw agent system.
Because Orchard can train agents directly inside real deployment harnesses, Orchard-Claw is trained across several of them—including ReACT, ZeroClaw, OpenClaw, and Codex—rather than a single simplified loop. Training inside these real harnesses substantially improves the agent’s reliability; under the Codex harness, for example, its success rate rises from 18.6% for the untrained model to 51.5% after Orchard training.
Implications and the road ahead
Orchard’s results reinforce a broader point: the environment layer matters. By making the underlying infrastructure open, lightweight, and reusable, Orchard lowers the cost of agentic AI research. Teams no longer need to build custom isolated environments from scratch or depend on proprietary cloud services. The same Orchard Env can be used to generate training data, run reinforcement learning rollouts, and evaluate final models without rebuilding the system each time.
Looking ahead, we see reusing training experience as a promising direction toward cumulative agent learning. Instead of discarding trajectories once a training run finishes, we treat them as persistent assets—for example, distilling them into reusable value models. This enables agentic experience to accumulate over time, allowing each new generation of agents to inherit and extend the knowledge acquired by previous ones, rather than starting from scratch.
The data efficiency demonstrated by Orchard-GUI suggests that larger-scale web agents could be trained without requiring large amounts of manually created training data. By releasing the complete Orchard stack, including the environment service, training pipelines, and training datasets, we hope to help the broader research community build more capable open agents more quickly.
Acknowledgements
We thank the teams at Microsoft Research and collaborating institutions for their contributions to Orchard, as well as the open-source community whose benchmarks and tools made this research possible.

articles.title: Samsung lança alto-falantes Music Studio no Brasil; veja modelos e preços • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung lança alto-falantes Music Studio no Brasil; veja modelos e preços
Samsung finalmente anunciou caixas de som Music Studio 7 e Music Studio 5 no mercado brasileiro. Primeiro modelo tem som de 3.1.1 canais; segundo chama a atenção pelo design.
Resumo
- Samsung lançou oficialmente os alto-falantes Music Studio 7 e Music Studio 5 no Brasil, com preços a partir de R$ 1.599;
- Music Studio 7 oferece áudio de 3.1.1 canais, Controle Dinâmico de Graves e conexões HDMI eARC, Wi-Fi e Bluetooth, por R$ 2.499;
- já Music Studio 5 tem áudio de 2.0 canais, woofer de 4 polegadas e dois tweeters, e custa R$ 1.599.
Dois alto-falantes da Samsung estão chegando oficialmente ao Brasil: os modelos Music Studio 7 e Music Studio 5. O primeiro tem um design mais tradicional, mas oferece mais recursos. O segundo é mais compacto e ousa no visual. Os preços sugeridos partem de R$ 1.599.
Demorou um pouco para as duas caixas de som serem lançadas no mercado brasileiro, afinal, tanto a Music Studio 7 quanto a Music Studio 5 foram homologadas pela Anatel em março de 2026. Lá fora, a Music Studio 7 e a Music Studio 5 foram anunciadas no final do ano passado.
Mas a Samsung dá a entender que a espera no Brasil valeu a pena:
Com a linha Music Studio, ampliamos nosso portfólio de áudio com uma nova categoria de produtos que combina alta qualidade sonora, design e inteligência. Pensamos em um dispositivo extremamente versátil, que pode acompanhar o consumidor em diferentes ambientes da casa, funcionar de forma independente ou integrado à TV e ainda fazer parte de todo o ecossistema conectado da Samsung.
Edson Santana, gerente de produtos de áudio da Samsung Brasil
Entre os recursos que os dois modelos trazem em comum estão tecnologias como Dolby Atmos, Eclipsa Audio e SpaceFit Sound Pro. Outra tecnologia é a Q-Symphony, que permite que os dois alto-falantes sejam sincronizados com bastante precisão a TVs compatíveis da Samsung.
O que a caixa Samsung Music Studio 7 oferece?
Com design retangular, remetendo às caixas de som tradicionais, a Samsung Music Studio 7 (LS70H) tem o áudio de 3.1.1 canais como destaque. Graças aos alto-falantes esquerdo, frontal, direito e superior, o equipamento pode distribuir o som para a frente, para as laterais e para cima, permitindo uma percepção espacial precisa do áudio, de acordo com a Samsung.
A novidade oferece ainda Controle Dinâmico de Graves (usa IA para reproduzir frequências mais graves sem causar distorção), processa áudio de até 24 bits/96 kHz (Hi-Resolution Audio) e suporta frequências de até 35 kHz para alcançar “nuances sutis”.
No aspecto da conectividade, o destaque vai para as conexões HDMI eARC, que possibilitam reproduções com formatos Surround 3D sem atrasos. Wi-Fi e Bluetooth também estão presentes.
O que há de legal na Samsung Music Studio 5?
A caixa Samsung Music Studio 5 (LS50H) é mais compacta (mas só um pouco), e atrai os olhares por ser arredondada em cima e ter linhas retas na parte inferior. É o modelo mais “diferentão” da dupla.
Em termos de recursos, a Music Studio 5 trabalha com áudio de 2.0 canais. Ela é equipada com woofer de 4 polegadas e dois tweeters. A função Controle Dinâmico de Graves também está presente aqui, bem como a conectividade Bluetooth e Wi-Fi.
Quais os preços da linha Samsung Music Studio?
Os dois alto-falantes começam a ser vendidos nesta semana no Brasil. No site da Samsung, os preços oficiais são os seguintes (sem considerar descontos ou promoções):
- Samsung Music Studio 7: R$ 2.499
- Samsung Music Studio 5: R$ 1.599

articles.title: Hay que hablar sobre el iPhone 18, porque todo apunta a que Apple no lo va a lanzar en septiembre
articles.text:
Apple está preparando el mayor cambio en el lanzamiento del iPhone desde 2011. Llevamos varias semanas escuchando rumores y viendo filtraciones de cada vez más expertos de la industria, y todo apunta a que podría ser una previsión bastante precisa. Tal y como lees en el título: la compañía de Cupertino no lanzaría el iPhone 18 en septiembre. Es lo esperado y lo que todo el mundo quiere, pero este año las cosas podrían ser diferentes por culpa de otros modelos que van a entrar en el catálogo.
Por supuesto, Apple no ha comentado nada de forma oficial. La información proviene de filtradores tan importantes como Jeff Pu o Wayne Ma, quienes apuntan a que la cadena de suministro de Apple no está preparando el modelo base para un lanzamiento en septiembre como nos tiene acostumbrados desde hace más de una década. Y es ahí donde está la clave: el modelo base es el iPhone 18, pero no el iPhone 18 Pro.
¿Qué modelos de iPhone se lanzarían en septiembre? Si hacemos caso a estos rumores, Apple presentará varios móviles nuevos el mes que viene, pero restaría uno importante a la ecuación. Lo que se dice en estos momentos es que el próximo gran cambio de la Apple Store lucirá tal que así cuando la compañía abra las reservas.
- iPhone 18 Pro
- iPhone 18 Pro Max
- iPhone Fold (plegable)
Esta estrategia tiene un objetivo claro: dar protagonismo a los modelos más avanzados y no saturar la Apple Store con demasiados dispositivos nuevos. El iPhone 17 seguiría estando disponible como el modelo básico más actual. De esta manera, septiembre se convertiría en un lanzamiento enfocado en todos los que van a por los iPhone más potentes y avanzados.
¿Cuándo se lanzará el iPhone 18? ¿Apple saltará directamente al iPhone 19?
Como decimos, por ahora son solo rumores y filtraciones, por lo que no hay nada 100% claro. Lo que dicen los expertos con (supuesta) información proveniente de China es que Apple retrasaría el lanzamiento del iPhone 18 hasta marzo de 2027. Lo lanzaría junto con el iPhone 18e, convirtiendo el inicio del segundo trimestre en la época para comprar los nuevos iPhone básicos.
Es algo bastante raro y una teoría que muchos filtradores importantes no apoyan, pero cada vez parece haber más evidencias que respaldan esta teoría. De esta forma, quien compró un iPhone 17 en septiembre de 2025 seguirá teniendo el modelo base más avanzado durante 6 meses más.
Y, por supuesto, si esta información acaba siendo cierta, es de esperar que durante los próximos años Apple siga una estrategia similar, lanzando el modelo base y la versión 'e' a principios de primavera y dejando los modelos avanzados para septiembre.
Una estrategia que, por otro lado, le daría más relevancia a la compañía, le permitiría diversificar más los picos de ventas a lo largo del año y hacer que la época veraniega no sea un valle en las cifras por culpa de los modelos próximos.
¿Cuánta verdad hay en estas palabras? Por ahora es muy difícil saberlo, aunque de ser ciertas, estaríamos ante uno de los cambios más relevantes por parte de Apple con la generación de los iPhone 18.

articles.title: Ghana’s Swiftway is a digital freight forwarding platform built for African businesses - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ghanaian startup Swiftway is a digital freight forwarding platform built for African businesses, handling the full process of air and sea freight, customs clearance, and haulage across corridors including China, the UK, US, Turkey, and Dubai.
Launched in June 2025 by Abubakar Sadick Fuseini and Suleiman Abubakar Sadique, Swiftway allows business owners in Accra to ship goods internationally, and vice versa, without having to navigate a maze of brokers, paperwork, and hidden charges.
“We do that for them, end-to-end,” Fuseini told Disrupt Africa.
The freight forwarding industry in Africa has two dominant players – informal brokers who are opaque and unreliable, and large multinationals like DHL Global Forwarding and Bolloré, which are simply too expensive for most SMEs.
“Nobody was building a transparent, tech-enabled solution specifically for the African SME importer. That is the gap we are filling. Globally, Flexport is doing something similar, but they have no meaningful focus on the African market. We are building for this market from the inside,” said Fuseini.
Fully-bootstrapped since launch, Swiftway has already onboarded over 540 active businesses and built a waitlist of more than 19,000 registered users.
“That kind of organic demand tells us the problem is real and the appetite is there. Growth has come primarily through digital channels Meta ads and WhatsApp, with strong word of mouth driving a significant portion of new clients,” Fuseini said.
Swiftway is currently closing a US$100,000 pre-seed round, and already serves clients importing primarily from China, the UK, and US. It is actively expanding into Nigeria through on-the-ground logistics partnerships.
“We have signed enterprise agreements with clients operating across West Africa. The vision is to become the leading digital freight forwarder across the West African corridor over the next three years,” Fuseini said.
Swiftway earns a service fee on every shipment covering its freight forwarding margin, customs clearance fees, and haulage coordination.
“For larger enterprise clients, we operate on volume-based agreements. We have billed approximately US$71,000 in revenue since launch, while remaining fully bootstrapped,” said Fuseini.
“We are reinvesting aggressively into growth right now, but the unit economics are healthy and improving as our volumes scale.”

articles.title: Google picks 20 AI startups for 2026 Play Accelerator India cohort
articles.text:
Google picks 20 AI startups for 2026 Play Accelerator India cohort
Google has selected 20 AI-powered Indian startups for its 2026 Google Play Accelerator India, offering three months of equity-free mentorship on AI, security, app quality, growth and monetisation to support global expansion.
Google has selected 20 AI-powered Indian startups for the 2026 cohort of Google Play Accelerator India, expanding support for app developers as artificial intelligence becomes central to India’s fast-growing digital economy.
The three-month, equity-free programme is designed to help startups improve app quality, integrate AI responsibly, strengthen security, grow their user base, and build sustainable revenue models.
The latest cohort spans education, healthcare, gaming, agriculture, finance, ecommerce, productivity, lifestyle, and entertainment.
Google said the selected companies are building AI-driven products that address practical problems, ranging from helping farmers and improving access to chronic healthcare to supporting exam preparation, sports coaching, and digital payments.
“India’s next wave of app innovation is being built with AI at the centre,” said Aditya Swamy, Managing Director, Google Play Partnerships. “The 2026 cohort reflects the ambition of Indian startups to build trusted, useful products for India and the world.”
The selected startups include healthcare platforms such as HeyDoc AI and MrMed, education-focused firms including UrbanPro and Lingopanda, gaming companies such as ChennaiGames and MetaShot, agritech startup Kisanwala and fintech ventures including Swipe and Zet.
Google said the programme combines expertise from Google Play and the wider Google technology stack to help founders develop products that can scale both within India and internationally.
“Over the next three months, we will work closely with these founders on product quality, responsible AI integration, security, growth, and monetization, helping them strengthen their apps for users in India and global markets,” noted Paul Ravindranath, Regional Lead, Developer and Startup Programs at Google.
The announcement comes as large tech firms intensify their efforts to support AI startups. They are expanding accelerator programmes, cloud credits, and developer tools to attract early-stage companies building AI applications.
Google has been widening its support for the startup ecosystem through the Google for Startups Accelerator. Recent announcements at Google I-O Connect India highlight new AI capabilities, developer tools, and infrastructure aimed at helping Indian companies build and deploy AI more securely and at scale.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: AMD Helios Architecture Deep Dive: The Power of AMD's Hardware Combined
articles.text:
Of all the product announcements made at this year’s AMD Advancing AI event, by far the most high-profile was the semi-formal launch of AMD’s Helios rack. The pride and joy of the company, Helios is a culmination of multiple AMD technologies, CPU, GPU, and DPU/NIC, along with its ZT Systems engineering, into a single product in order to build a computing appliance that can operate at a scale beyond what a single server can do. Or, as it has since been coined, rackscale systems.
Increasingly serving as the backbone of datacenter AI hardware, rackscale systems have come to the fore as AI workloads are too large for a single server, both in terms of processing power and memory capacity. The next step beyond a single server, then, is that rackscale systems are all about clustering multiple servers, and multiple types of servers, to function as a single coherent machine. It is a computing paradigm that, in part, has helped put AMD rival NVIDIA in GPU computing space.
The technology principles behind a rackscale system are reasonably straightforward, and simpler supercomputer clusters have existed long before them. Still, the execution needed to make a rackscale system work is another matter. A rackscale AI system not only needs CPUs and GPUs to orchestrate and process data, but they need a high-performance fabric to link those systems together. In that respect, the biggest advances in making rackscale systems a reality have been adding those kinds of fabrics to GPUs and then designing networking hardware to extend (scale up) those fabrics to connect to the other nodes within a rack.
After acquiring Pensando in 2022, four years later, all of the pieces are finally in place for AMD to strike out in the world with its first true rackscale system, Helios. The combination of AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice” CPUs, Instinct MI455X GPUs, and Pensando NICs/DPUs, Helios is the flagship technological achievement for AMD. The resulting significance of Helios to AMD on both a technical and a business level is difficult to overstate, and fittingly, the company has been promoting it for over a year now.
At long last, Helios and its constituent parts are now in production. And with that, AMD is giving Helios its day in the sun at Advancing AI with the deepest dive yet on Helios’s scale-up architecture. So let us jump in and see what makes Helios fly.
AMD Helios By the Numbers
We will start with a high-level overview of Helios’s hardware specifications.
Looking at the state of Helios a year after AMD first announced the rack, the shipping specifications for the system ended up being remarkably close to AMD’s original projections. The 72 GPU systems will offer 2.9 EFLOPS of peak MXFP4 compute performance. With those GPUs paired up with 432GB of HBM4 memory offering 23.3TB/second of memory bandwidth each, the cumulative rackscale system offers 31TB of HBM4 memory with a total memory bandwidth of 1.7PB/second.
That latter specification is also the starkest difference from AMD’s original projections: the bandwidth per MI455X GPU (and thus the whole rack) is about 21% higher than AMD originally planned. With memory bandwidth remaining one of the major bottlenecks in AI inference, any improvement will be most welcome by AMD and its customers alike.
Meanwhile, on the networking side, the rackscale system features a series of network connections for both scale-up networking within a Helios rack and scale-out networking for clustering multiple Helios racks if needed. The scale-up domain offers a massive 260TB/second of cumulative network bandwidth between the nodes, while the scaling-out domain offers a more modest 43TB/second of bandwidth beyond a Helios rack. In a historical context, those are huge numbers from a single rack.
Okay, I’ll bite. How do you apply 690 lbs of insertion force? Gigantic insertion levers on each card? A giant mallet? Only hiring olympic-grade weightlifters as datacenter techs? Some sort of powered switch lifter that then rams things into place somehow without knocking other racks around in the process?
Scott – a lever.

articles.title: Alibaba's AI coded for 16 days straight and every commit is on GitHub
articles.text:
Alibaba’s AI coded for 16 days straight and every commit is on GitHub
Alibaba has launched Qwen3.8-Max, a multimodal model with 2.4 trillion parameters and built for complicated tasks that may take several days to complete. Now available through QwenCloud and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, it’s priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.
Qwen3.8-Max builds on the Qwen3.5 architecture and uses a sparse mixture-of-experts design with hybrid attention. Although the model contains 2.4 trillion parameters in total, it activates approximately 95 billion for each token.
The mixture-of-experts architecture draws on the parts of the model needed for each task — instead of running all 2.4 trillion parameters every time. According to the company, the model weights will be published on Hugging Face and ModelScope next week, making it the first Qwen-Max model released with downloadable weights.
The model’s mixture-of-experts architecture draws on the parts of the model needed for each task, which still leaves developers with an enormous model to host.
How the harness works
Even with only 95 billion parameters active at once, the full weights must be stored and distributed across multiple high-memory GPU nodes. In practice, that puts self-hosting beyond the reach of most developers and makes Qwen3.8-Max a more realistic option for large organizations and inference providers with the infrastructure to run it.
quot
Qwen3.8-Max is a realistic option for large organizations and inference providers with the infrastructure to run it.
This brings Alibaba close to Moonshot AI’s new Kimi K3, which has 2.8 trillion parameters. Alibaba holds a 36% stake in Moonshot AI, so these are not fully independent rivals. Kimi K3 topped Arena’s frontend coding leaderboard within hours of its debut, and demand overwhelmed Moonshot’s GPU capacity so fast that the company had to pause new subscriptions. Kimi K3’s open-weight release ran into exactly this problem: Demand blew past GPU capacity within 48 hours, and the model’s 2.8T parameters made self-hosting impractical for all but the largest shops. Qwen3.8-Max now enters the same race.
Other long-running demos
According to Alibaba’s tests, Qwen3.8-Max spent 16 days building a command-line app, took five days to reproduce a research paper’s results, and improved a chip design after about 500 iterations. Alibaba has not released enough information for outside researchers to verify these results.
Alibaba’s most ambitious software demo had Qwen3.8-Max spend 16 days building “oh-my-cli” on its own. During that time, it made 265 commits and opened 127 pull requests as it worked through 151 GitHub issues. The repository and its audit trail are public under qwen-code-dev-bot/oh-my-cli, so developers do not have to rely solely on Alibaba’s account of what happened.
The difference between the model and its harness is key for long-running jobs.
The difference between the model and its harness is key for long-running jobs. The model decides what to do next, but the system around it handles everything else. These parts can decide if an agent runs for 16 days or fails after just 16 minutes.
That infrastructure layer is what Anthropic acquired the CI/CD startup Mendral to build out, and it’s the same lesson GoDaddy learned when it opened its registrar to AI agents; the guardrails had to come first.
Alibaba says it trained Qwen3.8-Max on complicated projects that an agent might actually encounter. The model performed similarly when tested with QwenWork, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes.
The company has published guides showing developers how to connect it to those tools. Developers should soon be able to put that claim to the test. Model Studio works with the OpenAI and Anthropic API formats, so teams can bring Qwen3.8-Max into coding tools they already use without rebuilding their setup from scratch.
Context window limits
In one experiment, the model was given the paper “Unified Data Selection for LLM Reasoning” without any code. Alibaba says the agent wrote about 7,600 lines of code, started 33 GPU training jobs, and reproduced the paper’s six main results. It also tested 18 more ideas and improved the reported AIME24 result by 2.7 points.
In another test, Qwen3.8-Max optimized a cryptographic circuit over about 500 iterations. Alibaba says the model cut the design from 8,298 logic gates to 678. After running it through OpenROAD, an open-source chip design tool, the physical area dropped by 81%.
This was not a one-shot coding test. The agent had to inspect each result and use it to decide what to try next. But even a million-token context window can only take an agent so far. Developers will want to see whether Qwen3.8-Max can remember earlier decisions and instructions as a project grows.
Sending nearly one million tokens at every step would cause other problems — and as the economics of agentic AI have shown, cheaper per-token pricing does not automatically translate to cheaper projects when autonomous agents are consuming tokens at rates that dwarf human-supervised sessions.
But even a million-token context window can only take an agent so far. Developers will want to see whether Qwen3.8-Max can remember earlier decisions and instructions as a project grows.
Benchmarks need outside verification
Alibaba’s internal benchmarks show Qwen3.8-Max performing close to models from Anthropic and OpenAI. According to Alibaba, it scored 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, compared to 88.8 for OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol (max). Independent runs of the same benchmark produce somewhat different scores for both models, so these figures may shift once outside labs repeat the tests. It also placed fifth in Text Arena and second in Vision Arena. In Alibaba’s own comparison table covering 31 tests, the model leads in six; Claude Fable 5 or GPT-5.6 Sol comes out ahead in most of the rest.
These results make Qwen3.8-Max a strong contender, but they do not yet prove the model can maintain production software on its own for weeks. Once Alibaba releases the weights, developers can find out how well Qwen3.8-Max works outside the company’s own setup. If its performance drops when it is moved to different infrastructure or connected to other coding tools, that will tell us far more than its place on a leaderboard.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy A57, A37 et A27 : quel modèle choisir en 2026 ?
articles.text:
Les excellentes performances de Samsung depuis près de 10 ans dans l’industrie du smartphone doivent moins à ses très voyants Galaxy S26 et autres smartphones premium, qu’à ses Galaxy A. Mais sont-ils encore des valeurs sûres ? Et surtout, lequel faut-il choisir parmi les trois modèles ?
Afin de vous aider à vous y retrouver, voici un rapide guide des principales différences entre les trois modèles. Pour rappel, nous avons cette année droit aux :
- Samsung Galaxy A57 ;
- Samsung Galaxy A37 ;
- Samsung Galaxy A27.
Design : plus c’est haut de gamme, plus c’est léger
Commençons par le design. De prime abord, les trois appareils se ressemblent beaucoup. Ils partagent une même philosophie de design : un écran plat, des bords plats, un bloc photo en vertical en forme de pilule avec trois appareils photo et une légère bosse pour accueillir les boutons et faciliter la prise en main.
Mais comme souvent, le diable est dans les détails. L’idée est simple : plus vous monterez en gamme, plus vous aurez un produit fin et léger, et donc plus agréable à manier. Le A57 démarre à 179 g, suivi de très loin par les 196 g et 200 g de ses deux compères. Niveau finesse rebelote, le A57 profite de 6,9 mm d’épaisseur contre 7,4 pour le A37 et 7,8 pour le A27.
Le A27 dégraisse pas mal
Mais ce n’est pas tout. À mesure que l’on descend en gamme, les bordures autour de l’écran vont tendre à s’agrandir. Le A57 possède un ratio d’écran proche des 90 %, le A37 tombe à 86,9 et, si le A27 possède un même ratio, il intègre tout de même un menton un peu plus proéminent et le contour noir autour de la caméra selfie prend plus de place.
Si les trois appareils possèdent un dos en verre, ce qui est une bonne chose, ainsi qu’un verre Corning Gorilla Glass Victus+ en façade, seul le A57 intègre des tranches en métal. Les deux autres optent pour le plastique.
Pour ce qui est de la résistance à l’eau, tous ne sont pas logés à la même enseigne. Le Galaxy A57 et le A37 sont tous deux étanches (IP68), lorsque le A27 est simplement résistant aux éclaboussures (IP64). Pour terminer la liste des petites concessions du A27, celui-ci en possède encore deux très importantes : il n’a qu’un seul haut-parleur, lui interdisant la stéréo, et le capteur d’empreinte n’est pas niché sous l’écran, comme pour ses camarades, mais sur le côté.
Écran : assez peu de différences
Pour l’écran, ce n’est pas compliqué, vous aurez le droit à une dalle de 6,7 pouces Full HD en OLED et 120 Hz (non adaptatif) à chaque fois.
Si l’on s’en réfère aux mesures du 01lab, effectuées grâce à notre sonde colorimétrique et le logiciel Calman Ultimate, les écrans proposent des performances de luminosité très proches.
En revanche, la calibration par défaut n’est pas du tout la même. Si la balance des blancs est mieux réglée sur le A57, il affiche une plus grande dérive colorimétrique que son comparse, le A37.
Logiciel : One UI pendant 6 ans
Là-dessus encore, il n’y a pas vraiment match, les trois appareils sont livrés avec One UI, la surcouche de Samsung, et bénéficient d’une même durée de mise à jour de 6 ans.
Photo : une montée en gamme progressive
Pour justifier la montée en gamme, rien de mieux que la photographie, qui reste encore le grand marqueur différentiant entre les appareils les plus chers et les plus accessibles. Les trois smartphones ici présents possèdent trois modules photo, mais la montée en gamme est nette.
On commence avec le Galaxy A27. Celui-ci possède un grand angle de 50 Mpx ouvrant à f/1.8 avec un capteur de type 1/2,76 pouce. Il est accompagné d’un ultra-grand-angle avec capteur de 8 Mpx de type 1/5 pouce, ce qui est vraiment minuscule, ainsi qu’un capteur macro de 2 Mpx bien inutile.
Dès le A37, la montée en gamme est marquée, puisqu’on passe à un capteur de 50 Mpx, plus grand, puisqu’il est de type 1/1.56 pouce (plus le chiffre à droite est petit, plus grand est le capteur). L’ultra grand angle est aussi un peu mieux avec 8 Mpx sur un capteur plus grand là aussi, de type 1/4 pouce. Le macro, toujours peu utile, s’améliore néanmoins et passe à 5 Mpx.
Quant au Galaxy A57, il part sur les mêmes bases que son prédécesseur, le A37, mais améliore un brin le capteur de son ultra grand-angle, passant à 12 Mpx pour une taille de type 1/3,06 pouce, plus grand donc.
Performances : de plus en plus musclé et connecté
Voici les configurations des trois appareils :
- A57 : Exynos 1680 (4 nm) CPU Octa-core (1×2.9 GHz Cortex-720 & 4×2.6 GHz Cortex-720 & 3×1.95 GHz Cortex-520) ;
- A37 : Exynos 1480 (4 nm) CPU Octa-core (4×2.75 GHz Cortex-A78 & 4×2.0 GHz Cortex-A55) ;
- A27 : Qualcomm SM6475-AB Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 (4 nm) CPU Octa-core (4×2.4 GHz Cortex-A78 & 4×1.8 GHz Cortex-A55).
Cela se traduit assez logiquement par un gain en performance non négligeable d’un modèle à l’autre, que ce soit sur la partie CPU ou GPU, comme le montre notre graphique ci-dessous.
Concernant la RAM et le stockage, le A27 est le moins bien loti, puisqu’il est le seul à démarrer en 6 Go de RAM + 128 Go de stockage, contre 8 + 256 coté A37 et A57.
Réseaux
Les puces gèrent également la partie réseau, et là-dessus encore, des différences sont à noter. Le A27 est compatible WiFi 5, un standard un peu vieillissant. Le A37 passe au WiFi 6 et seul le A57 profite du WiFi 6E. Pour le Bluetooth, même rengaine, on démarre par du Bluetooth 5.1, pour passer sur du 5.3 puis du 6.0.
Concernant la connectivité 5G, les trois téléphones en sont pourvus, mais une nuance importante est à souligner. Les A57 et A37 intègrent l’eSIM, en plus d’être compatible double SIM. Le A27, s’il en est dépourvu, se venge, si l’on peut dire, avec le support d’une carte micro SD.
Batterie : même capacité ne dit pas même batterie
Les trois modèles possèdent une batterie de la même capacité, 5000 mAh. Côté charge, les A57 et A37 supportent jusqu’à 45 W lorsque le A27 monte à 25 W.
Malgré cette proximité en termes de taille de batterie, attendez-vous à des différences importantes en terme d’autonomie.
Comme le démontre notre protocole maison, le Galaxy A57, sans doute grâce à sa puce plus performante, ou encore à sa meilleure gestion de la chauffe, parvient à grappiller presque 2 h d’usage en plus, pour arriver à un score honorable de 18 h 12 d’usage en continu. Vous pouvez vous attendre à tenir la journée sans trop forcer.
Prix des Galaxy A
L’ultime différence, la voici, le prix. Le Galaxy A57 démarre à 529 euros, lorsque le Galaxy A37 débute à 459 euros. 90 euros plus bas, vous trouverez le Galaxy A27 et ses 369 euros.
Comme nous l’avons démontré dans cet article, la différence de prix se justifie systématiquement par une montée en gamme entre ces trois appareils. À notre avis, cette année, le plus équilibré des trois est sans aucun doute le Galaxy A37.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : le retour de Tom Bombadil dans la saison 3 pose un vaste défi narratif pour la série
articles.text:
Il y a les évidences, comme Sauron, Elrond ou Galadriel, personnages-clés de la série télévisée Les Anneaux de pouvoir (Rings of Power). Il y a aussi les surprises attendues, à l’image de Celeborn, un Elfe de premier plan qui va enfin faire ses débuts avec la saison 3. Ou les annonces stupéfiantes, en témoigne le casting de Simon Pegg pour faire la voix du… balrog.
Il y a aussi les inévitables nouveaux, tels Andrew Richardson (Anárion), Eddie Marsan (Thraïn), Zubin Varla (Khamûl l’Oriental) et Adam Young (Marnûkh). Ces quatre-là incarneront respectivement un Humain (le fils cadet d’Elendil), un seigneur nain, un futur Nazgûl et un orc. Et puis il y a les personnages délicats à manipuler, mais qui reviennent quand même.
Un personnage surpuissant nommé Tom Bombadil
C’est typiquement le cas de Tom Bombadil. Comme on peut le remarquer, le casting officiel des Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 recense Rory Kinnear parmi les acteurs et actrices qui reviennent. La présence du comédien britannique avait été officialisée en 2023 par Amazon Studios pour interpréter le mystérieux mais sympathique Tom Bombadil dans la saison 2.
Rory Kinnear avait laissé une bonne impression en tant que Tom Bombadil. Le problème, c’est la spécificité même de son personnage. Si J. R. R. Tolkien n’a jamais très clairement défini la nature de Tom Bombadil, on devine qu’il est peut-être l’un des personnages les plus puissants, voire le protagoniste le plus puissant de toute la Terre du Milieu.
Dans la série, Tom Bombadil s’est décrit comme « l’Aîné », affirmant qu’il était « là bien avant la rivière et les arbres », qu’il se souvenait « de la première pluie et du premier gland de chêne ». Surtout, il dit avoir « connu l’obscurité sous les étoiles, quand le monde n’avait encore rien à craindre ». Bref, il est dans ce monde depuis des éons.
Son identité est manifestement surnaturelle, donc. Et parmi les théories qui circulent autour de lui, on retrouve l’hypothèse d’une entité angélique (un peu comme Gandalf, Sauron ou Saroumane), voire divine (avec les Valar, qui sont les maîtres des entités angéliques). On dit même qu’il serait un écho d’Eru Ilúvatar, la divinité suprême.
Pourquoi ne se dresse-t-il pas contre Sauron ?
Le problème avec une telle description, c’est qu’elle peut être handicapante pour le scénario. Comment un être que l’on suppose (ou que l’on présente comme) aussi puissant ne s’élève-t-il pas pour s’opposer aux sombres desseins de Sauron dans la Terre du Milieu ? Qui plus est avec le caractère agréable et positif dont il fait preuve.
En somme, il représente un peu la même difficulté que les fameux aigles qui sont venus en aide à Gandalf (quand il était emprisonné à Isengard) ou bien à Frodon et Sam pour les extirper de la Montagne du Destin, au Mordor, lors de la guerre de l’Anneau. Ce sont des créatures si puissantes que leur existence même pose un souci à la narration.
Dans le cas des aigles, ceux-ci auraient pu largement faciliter le voyage de la communauté de l’Anneau, en transportant l’artefact maudit au cœur du volcan. Et pour ce qui est de Tom Bombadil, il aurait aussi pu intervenir pour sauver les peuples de la Terre du Milieu, au lieu de rester à s’occuper de son petit lopin de terre.
Il est vrai que Tolkien avait lui-même neutralisé par avance tout risque de deus ex machina en glissant lors du Conseil d’Elrond la possibilité de lui confier l’Anneau, avant que l’idée ne soit écartée. Gandalf avait alors dit que Bombadil n’a aucun pouvoir face à Sauron en dehors de ses terres et qu’il égarerait l’Anneau par pur désintérêt.
Reste désormais à voir si les showrunners d’Amazon sauront faire preuve de la même finesse. Tout le défi de cette saison 3 sera de laisser à « l’Aîné » sa place de figure mystique et bienveillante, sans jamais en faire un sauveur trop facile.
