articles.title: Beast of Reincarnation revived my love for Game Freak
articles.text:
On December 25, 1999, I woke up that Christmas morning, opened my gifts, and found not only a purple Game Boy Color, but also my first-ever video game, Pokémon Silver. Since that day, I’ve played many Pokémon games (Pokémon Yellow, Crystal, Sapphire, Emerald, Diamond, Platinum, Black, White 2, X, Moon, Ultra Sun, Sword, Violet, Fire Red, Heart Gold, Omega Ruby, and Legends: Arceus) so you can call me a pretty big fan — I even have HM04 tattooed on my chest (only real nerds know).
And while Pokémon Heart Gold is probably my favourite game ever, I have seen the pitfalls of the series, like Pokémon Sapphire having too much water, Scarlet having too many issues at launch, and Legends: Z-A wasn’t my cup of tea at all.
This was a lot of exposition to say when Pokémon game developer Game Freak made another game; I just had to get my hands on it. That game, Beast of Reincarnation, is absolutely fantastic, and though it’s not completely flawless, I enjoyed the 30ish-hour campaign and would definitely recommend it.
Not a difficult beast to tame
I would call Beast of Reincarnation a soulslite, a term used to describe a game with soulslike elements but far more forgiving. While Game Freak warned me that it’d be difficult, on the “Normal” mode, I found the game far easier than soulslikes such as Dark Souls, Lies of P or the game that I feel it has most in common with, Sekiro. In fact, this title feels heavily inspired by that FromSoftware game, as you can see that throughout the game’s main combat mechanic, parrying. Although parry windows are far more generous, and so are most aspects of the game. For instance, when you die, you don’t need to go back and collect any souls; enemies are easier to read with more wind-up time, and you have best boy Koo by your side with clever mechanics that can shift the tides of battle.
Speaking of Koo, the wolf turned malefect (the term for creatures affected by the blight that’s changing the world), he might be the best partner character I’ve had the pleasure of teaming up with – but I’ll explain why later.
But my point is, if you’re worried Beast of Reincarnation might be too difficult, if you were able to finish a FromSoftware game, you should have no problem here. And if you haven’t, I’d still give it a shot considering there’s an easy mode.
Sort of like Spider-Man
Beast of Reincarnation has two gameplay elements that I’ve been absolutely loving: traversal and combat. The protagonist, Emma, is seemingly like Koo, another malefect, who’s able to use her root-like hair to traverse the world. Pressing ‘jump’ twice raises Emma higher, like one of the coolest double jumps ever, as roots come up from the ground to give her more leverage. She can grapple to far-away destinations by using her hair as some sort of branch-like chain and can even use her hair to make a bridge of roots to help cross distances.
The traversal in this game is so unique, and while playing, I even compared it to Marvel’s Spider–Man. One section has you grappling around oversized trees, and it felt epic. You can’t cling to any surface, and you only tether when the icon appears, but it’s everywhere.
The blade is sharp…
And traversal can help emphasize Emma’s combat abilities. For instance, if you level up Emma’s hair-bridge ability and aim it towards an enemy, a giant flower will emerge from the ground that you can grapple to, double jump, and execute an enemy from above.
Emma and Koo have some very cool combat potentials; Beast of Reincarnation has literal skill trees for both characters, allowing you to pick and choose which abilities you want to level up. Emma has several perks that can be picked up as well to enhance her hair, range and sword abilities. Emma’s sword combat is very interesting, and there are several very easy combos to master.
On PlayStation, pressing ‘R1’ initiates a sword swing, and pressing ‘Square’ activates the ability. So if you’ve swung your sword twice and press Square, it’ll activate an ability; maybe a giant flower will spring up from the ground, or a swamp bog will emerge from your feet. Each swing of your sword will initiate a different ability that Square can activate, and there will be a pop-up to indicate what ability you’ll use when you press Square. It’s very intuitive and looks pretty cool when you’re fighting enemies. And the more you level up, fight bosses and gain powers, the more combos you can chain in combat. Eventually, you’ll be popping different plants out of the ground and moving your sword at insane speeds; it looks pretty fancy and very inspired by anime.
Emma pretty much feels like a character from the anime Demon Slayer swinging her sword in the coolest ways possible, and that’s only the tip of it.
…but so are Koo’s fangs
Koo brings a whole other element to combat. So while you’re controlling Emma fighting enemies, you’ll need to be both cutting away normally so you can build energy to use the above-mentioned sword techniques and then parrying as well so you’re able to build up Koo’s FP gauge. Once Koo has enough FP for the ability you want, press ‘Triangle’ (on PS5), and the world will slow down, like bullet time, and you’re able to choose the best ability for whoever you’re fighting against. In this game, you have to consider things like type advantages and resistances, and how to best build the numerous status effects the game has, while also wrecking the enemy’s stamina gauge so you can stagger them and devastate their health. You can also unlock six slots (through leveling up) that let you pick from a list of ‘Mods’ that enable Koo to perform passive abilities. For instance, Koo can summon a garden of flowers to heal you, throw fire bombs at the enemy or use special bite attacks that can build status effects. I eventually started relying on Koo to heal me a lot during combat, without me having to tell him to heal me. I’d expect him to build the ‘rooting’ status effect that would build roots around an enemy’s feet, trapping them, or expect him to use a howling ability that would increase my strength. Having both passive and active abilities for your side character is pretty cool, and even cooler because he’s a beautiful wolf that can shoot blazing seeds at your enemies.
Other aspects of the game I really enjoy include both the visuals and the music. I loved the background music during battles, and when you’re travelling the world, it’s calm and relaxing. And visually, Beast of Reincarnation is stunning, from the world to the gruesome bosses affected by the blight to Koo and Emma herself; I couldn’t get over how appealing everything looked. Though I did notice some texture pop-in once in a while (I am playing on base PS5), so some things would at first look a little smudgy – like Clair Obscur, and then details and proper textures would take a few seconds to catch up. Game Freak released a patch a few hours ahead of publishing this review, which helps performance, but I haven’t gotten the chance to check it out. But I didn’t experience any actual problems while playing.
Not without its flaws
I thoroughly enjoyed Beast of Reincarnation, but it wasn’t perfect. For instance, a larger variety of enemies would have been nice. By the end of the 30-hour campaign, I was getting tired of seeing the same robots and blight-infected beasts. Even some of the bosses double up, which is a little annoying. I think the last 10 hours I started noticing some doubling up and started getting annoyed by some of the enemy types. New areas bring different enemies, or stronger versions of previously fought ones, but even that gets a little tiring after your first combat with them.
I also understood the story (for the most part), but I definitely wasn’t playing the game for its story. It felt like a convoluted anime, and a far wilder version of Horizon Zero Dawn as Emma and Koo discover what happened to the world 2000 years ago (the game is set in the year 4026), the cause of the blight, and learn more about themselves. Seriously, there is a story here; parts of it are interesting, doing far better than most souls-esque games, but I was far more interested in finding and killing the next boss.
Other parts of Beast of Reincarnation were interesting, like the different regions based on apocalyptic Japan. Some were more forestial, others mountainous, another region was full of desiccated buildings, and dungeons to explore. I was expecting more variations, but it was fine, and I enjoyed exploring each section – the game has various sections to explore, instead of being a fully open world title. But some of these sections felt pretty large, while others were small. You can’t ride around on Koo, but a mount isn’t necessary; none of the sections were that big.
Time to put away the Pokéball
Beast of Reincarnation wasn’t perfect, but the title’s combat was fun, engaging and has an anime undertone that I love, and the traversal mechanics were top-notch. Seeing some of the bosses for the first time was exhilarating, and the title is beautiful with flashy swordplay, beautiful scenery, and grotesque monsters. And I was absolutely laughing when a boss falls in battle and then ‘evolves’ and comes back even stronger – like she literally says ‘it’s evolving’ like it’s Pokémon; now that’s hilarious.
Game Freak should consider hanging up Pokémon, take all the money it’s earned and focus on this game, possible DLCs and sequels or even other adventures. Because I definitely had a lot more fun playing Beast of Reincarnation than any Game Freak Pokémon game in years.
Worth mentioning, I didn’t rush through the game. I spent a lot of time exploring in the first half, but halfway through I was having more fun killing bosses, so I spent less time exploring and getting through it. Plus, I wanted to make sure I completed the title before writing the review; I’m in NG+ spending even more time in each region.

articles.title: Adieu le lecteur disque ? Microsoft veut convertir vos jeux Xbox physiques en licences PC
articles.text:
C’est un nouveau bouleversement qui se profile pour les joueurs Xbox. Après avoir officialisé l’extension de son programme de rétrocompatibilité au PC avec l’arrivée des jeux de la première Xbox, Microsoft préparerait désormais l’intégration du catalogue Xbox 360. Les joueurs pourraient techniquement se retrouver avec plus de 2 000 titres sur PC.
Selon les informations rapportées par The Verge, cette initiative s’inscrirait dans la nouvelle stratégie du programme de rétrocompatibilité porté par l’arrivée de la nouvelle Xbox Helix.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
    Pour aller plus loin
            L’arrivée de jeux Xbox originaux sur PC ouvre la voie aux jeux Xbox 360 sur Windows
            
Un calendrier encore lointain
Selon The Verge, les développeurs de jeux Xbox 360 peuvent choisir de rendre leurs jeux rétrocompatibles et pourront fixer leurs prix ainsi que leur disponibilité sur le Game Pass. Une fonctionnalité qui ne devrait toutefois pas voir le jour avant 2027 ou 2028.
De son côté, le nouveau programme de rétrocompatibilité Xbox serait attendu dès octobre 2026.
Du physique au numérique
Dans le sillon de cette nouvelle stratégie, la note interne donne un calendrier prévisionnel pour le déploiement de la fonctionnalité « Disc-to-Digital ». Celle-ci permettrait aux possesseurs de jeux physiques de convertir leurs disques en licences numériques.
Une fois activé, le système permettrait à un joueur d’insérer un jeu Xbox One ou Xbox Series dans la console associée afin d’obtenir une licence numérique du titre. Cette dernière pourrait ensuite être utilisée sur l’ensemble de ses consoles Xbox compatibles. Le dispositif prendrait également en compte les échanges et la revente de disques. En cas de cession du jeu physique, le propriétaire initial perdrait l’accès à la version numérique associée.
Initialement prévue pour entrer en phase bêta en juillet, puis bénéficier d’un lancement généralisé en août, la fonctionnalité aurait finalement été repoussée. Reste désormais à savoir si Microsoft conservera une disponibilité générale dans les mois à venir ou si ce report entraînera un nouveau calendrier de déploiement.

articles.title: Votre PC Intel Panther Lake sera bientôt plus endurant sous Linux
articles.text:
Attendu dans le courant du mois d’août, Linux 7.3 donnera à Intel l’occasion d’améliorer la maîtrise énergétique de ses derniers processeurs Panther Lake (Core Ultra de série 3). On apprend en effet de VideoCardz que la firme prépare, pour la prochaine version de Linux, une nouvelle fonctionnalité d’économie d’énergie destinée aux iGPU Xe3.
Dans le détail, ce nouveau mode d’économie d’énergie permettra aux solutions Core Ultra de série 3 (ainsi qu’aux SoC Intel attendus par la suite) de réduire la fréquence de certains sous-systèmes propres à l’iGPU lorsque l’écran nécessite peu de bande passante mémoire.
Un changement qui n’aura pas de conséquences sur la qualité d’affichage ou les performances.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
Éviter le superflu pour préserver l’autonomie
Comme le résume le site spécialisé, le moteur d’affichage intégré aux processeurs Intel lit les images finalisées dans la mémoire système avant de les transmettre à l’écran d’un ordinateur portable ou à un moniteur externe ; et si le processeur doit effectivement veiller à ce que son architecture mémoire fonctionne à une vitesse suffisante pour gérer ce trafic, une fréquence standard plus basse peut la plupart du temps offrir une bande passante supérieure aux besoins, réels, des configurations d’affichage.
En d’autres termes, ce nouveau mode voué à Linux devrait permettre d’éviter le superflu, en ajoutant un nouveau point de fonctionnement QGV réglé à 20 Go/s. Le nouveau pilote peut alors sélectionner ce seuil lorsque le débit lié aux données d’affichage est en dessous de 20 Go/s.
Une manière efficace d’économiser de la batterie sans nuire aux performances graphiques, puisque cette limite n’est appliquée que dans certains contextes d’affichage et d’alimentation.
Deux bémols toutefois : cette nouveauté ne bénéficiera pas aux puces équipées de parties graphiques plus anciennes que les nouveaux iGPU Xe3 d’Intel. A priori, les précédentes générations de processeurs mobiles Intel (Meteor Lake ou Lunar Lake, par exemple) ne seront donc pas concernées.
Par ailleurs, Intel n’a pas encore donné de détails concernant les gains potentiels en termes d’autonomie. Il faudra donc attendre le déploiement de Linux 7.3 sur nos distributions pour le savoir.
Quoi qu’il en soit, cette nouveauté est particulièrement bienvenue en pleine période de lancement de celui qui est, pour l’instant, le meilleur PC portable Linux justement équipé d’un processeur Intel Panther Lake : le Framework Laptop 13 Pro.

articles.title: Problemas em Plutão! Parte do planeta anão estaria colapsando
articles.text:
A atmosfera de Plutão pode estar começando a desaparecer à medida que o planeta anão segue sua lenta trajetória para regiões cada vez mais frias e distantes do Sistema Solar. Um novo estudo identificou os primeiros indícios de uma queda significativa na pressão atmosférica, sugerindo que os gases ao redor do corpo celeste podem estar congelando sobre sua superfície.
A pesquisa foi conduzida por cientistas liderados por Amanda Sickafoose, do Planetary Science Institute, e publicada na revista Planetary Science Journal.
Plutão está se afastando cada vez mais do Sol
Plutão percorre uma órbita bastante elíptica ao redor do Sol. Até o ano de 2114, continuará se afastando da estrela, alcançando regiões ainda mais frias antes de iniciar o caminho de volta.
Segundo os pesquisadores, este é o primeiro deslocamento de Plutão para essas regiões externas desde sua descoberta, em 1930.
À medida que a temperatura diminui, a atmosfera do planeta anão pode congelar gradualmente e se depositar sobre a superfície na forma de gelo.
Primeiros sinais de mudança
- A equipe analisou observações realizadas entre 2017 e 2023 para acompanhar a evolução da atmosfera de Plutão;
- Os dados mostram que, entre a histórica passagem da sonda New Horizons, em 2015, e parte de 2021, a pressão atmosférica permaneceu praticamente estável;
- Entretanto, entre meados de 2021 e julho de 2023, os pesquisadores registraram uma redução de aproximadamente 16% na pressão da atmosfera;
- Os modelos utilizados no estudo consideram uma atmosfera rica em névoa, como a observada pela New Horizons durante seu sobrevoo;
- Segundo os autores, essa queda pode representar os primeiros sinais de um processo de colapso atmosférico.
Como cientistas estudam uma atmosfera tão distante
Nenhuma espaçonave está atualmente próxima de Plutão para acompanhar diretamente sua atmosfera. Além disso, mesmo os telescópios mais avançados enxergam o planeta anão apenas como um pequeno ponto luminoso.
Para contornar essa limitação, os pesquisadores utilizam um fenômeno chamado ocultação. Nesses eventos, Plutão passa exatamente na frente de uma estrela vista da Terra. Conforme a estrela desaparece atrás do planeta anão, sua luz atravessa a atmosfera de Plutão antes de ser bloqueada.
Ao medir cuidadosamente como esse brilho diminui e reaparece, os cientistas conseguem calcular características da atmosfera, como sua pressão e densidade.
Desde 2017, a equipe observou dez ocultações estelares. Em quatro delas, o mesmo evento pôde ser registrado simultaneamente por observatórios diferentes, permitindo comparar medições e analisar diferentes regiões da atmosfera.
“Fico constantemente impressionada com o fato de que a simples técnica de observar uma estrela escurecer e reaparecer nos permite estudar uma atmosfera extremamente fina — com apenas alguns milionésimos da densidade da atmosfera terrestre — em um mundo com cerca de dois terços do tamanho da nossa Lua e localizado 30 vezes mais distante do Sol”, afirmou Sickafoose.
Atmosfera e superfície estão diretamente ligadas
A atmosfera de Plutão é composta principalmente por nitrogênio, além de metano e monóxido de carbono. Esses compostos podem formar uma névoa que envolve o planeta anão.
Segundo os pesquisadores, à medida que a pressão atmosférica diminui, essa névoa tende a ficar menos densa e se concentrar em altitudes mais baixas.
Os cientistas destacam que o comportamento da atmosfera está intimamente relacionado ao gelo presente na superfície de Plutão, embora muitos detalhes dessa interação ainda não sejam totalmente compreendidos.
Observações continuarão nas próximas décadas
Para os autores, ainda são necessários muitos anos de observações para confirmar definitivamente se a atmosfera de Plutão entrou em um processo permanente de colapso.
“Estamos em um momento particularmente interessante para Plutão. Nosso trabalho sugere que a atmosfera começou recentemente a perder pressão. Espero que possamos obter mais dados nos próximos anos e décadas para confirmar ou refutar essa tendência”, disse Sickafoose.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Introducing the Billable Usage API: programmatic cost visibility for Cloudflare
articles.text:
Introducing the Billable Usage API: programmatic cost visibility for Cloudflare
Agents Week is about the shift already underway: agents write code, deploy Workers, and provision infrastructure on your behalf. That shift changes what you need to see. If a program is spending money in your Cloudflare account, you need to know what it's spending; throughout the day, per product, in a shape another program can consume. The dashboard is the right answer for humans. It's not the right answer for automation.
So we're launching a new Billable Usage API for self-serve accounts: a single endpoint that returns your account's usage and cost, broken down by product and by service period. It covers every usage-based Cloudflare product on the account, including Workers, R2, D1, Workers AI, Vectorize, Images, and Stream, all with one call. And if you already work in a FinOps toolchain, the column names should look familiar.
curl https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/billable-usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"curl "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/billable-usage?from=2026-02-01&to=2026-02-15" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"
You'll get back an HTTP 200 OK with Content-Type: application/json and the usage rows in the response body. Today, usage and cost data are updated daily while we work towards providing more real time data. 
What comes back
Each row in the response is one charge period for one product on your account.
- ServiceName andServiceFamilyName — which product ("Workers Standard" under the "Workers" family, "R2 Storage" under "R2", etc.).
- ChargePeriodStart /ChargePeriodEnd — the window this row covers.
- PricingQuantity andConsumedUnit — how much you used, in the unit of measure we bill on (GB-months, GB-seconds, requests, etc.).
- ContractedCost — what that period cost, inBillingCurrency .
- CumulatedPricingQuantity andCumulatedContractedCost — running totals for the billing period.
- ZoneId /ZoneName — when the usage is attributed to a specific zone.
Most of these map directly to columns in the FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS), so if your team is already ingesting FOCUS data from another provider, the names and semantics should be familiar:
| Cloudflare field | FOCUS column | Notes | 
|---|---|---|
| BillingCurrency | BillingCurrency | Exact match. | 
| BillingPeriodStart | BillingPeriodStart | Exact match. | 
| ChargePeriodStart /ChargePeriodEnd | ChargePeriodStart /ChargePeriodEnd | Exact match. | 
| ServiceName | ServiceName | Exact match. | 
| ConsumedQuantity /ConsumedUnit | ConsumedQuantity /ConsumedUnit | Exact match. | 
| PricingQuantity | PricingQuantity | Exact match. | 
| ContractedCost | ContractedCost | Exact match. | 
| ServiceFamilyName | (close to ServiceCategory ) | Cloudflare-native grouping; FOCUS uses a controlled vocabulary. | 
| CumulatedContractedCost | (derived) | Convenience field — FOCUS treats cumulation as a query concern. | 
| ZoneId /ZoneName | (close to ResourceId /ResourceName ) | Zone-scoped identifier where applicable. | 
Responses use the standard Cloudflare API envelope — result is an array of rows, one per product per charge period, alongside success, errors, and messages.
{
  "result": [
    {
      "BillingCurrency": "USD",
      "BillingPeriodStart": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
      "ChargePeriodStart": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
      "ChargePeriodEnd": "2025-02-28T23:59:59Z",
      "ServiceName": "Workers Standard",
      "ServiceFamilyName": "Workers",
      "ConsumedQuantity": 150000,
      "ConsumedUnit": "GB-months",
      "ContractedCost": 0.75,
      "CumulatedContractedCost": 2.25
    }
  ],
  "success": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messages": []
}
Where we are on FOCUS
Matching FOCUS naming was a deliberate choice. AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, and a growing list of SaaS providers already publish FOCUS formatted exports, and every serious cost-management tool speaks to it. That said, we're not yet claiming full conformance: a handful of columns the spec requires aren't in the payload today. Getting there is on our roadmap. Consider this the first step: familiar shape now, full conformance next.
Cloudflare spend, next to the rest of your cloud spend: our partnership with Vantage
We've partnered with Vantage on a native Cloudflare integration. Vantage is an infrastructure cost management platform that ingests cost and usage data from more than 30 providers, across AI, Cloud and SaaS providers, and brings it into a single view for reporting, allocation, and optimization. With this integration, your usage flows into the same Cost Reports, Budgets, and Cost Alerts you already use for the rest of your infrastructure.
Vantage connects to Cloudflare using a read-only API token with Billing Read access. Once connected, Vantage pulls your Billable Usage data daily and breaks it down by product (such as Workers and R2), zone, and account, so you can see which products drive your spend and attribute it to the teams and services behind it.
A few of the workflows this integration supports:
- Cross-provider allocation. Group Cloudflare spend by product, zone, and account, then use Virtual Tags to allocate by team or product line alongside your AWS, Azure, and other provider costs, all in a single report.
- Anomaly detection. Vantage Cost Alerts monitor every connected provider and notify you via Slack or E-Mail when spend deviates from its baseline, so a change in Workers or R2 spend surfaces the same way it does for any other provider.
- FinOps agents and MCP. Ask the in-console Vantage FinOps agent a question such as "What was our biggest cost driver last week across every provider?", or query the same data from Claude or ChatGPT through Vantage's hosted MCP server. Cloudflare spend is included alongside your other connected providers.
Connect your Cloudflare account in the Vantage console, and your costs appear next to everything else you run. There are no manual exports, no invoice uploads, and no separate dashboard to maintain.
This FOCUS standardized API also works with other Fintech tooling.
Why we built this
Agents do more than write code. They deploy Workers, provision R2 buckets, and manage D1 databases. When you grant programmatic access to your Cloudflare account, you need programmatic visibility into what it's costing you. Not at the end of the month, but throughout the day, by product, in a shape a program can actually consume.
The Billable Usage API is that shape. And customers have been asking us for programmatic usage for years. Finance teams want to pull spend into their own systems and attribute cost back to internal projects, teams, and even their end customers. Developers want a curl they can drop in a script. Every one of those workflows used to involve a screenshot or a manual export. Now it's an HTTP call, or a configuration in Vantage.
What's next
- Finer-grained time windows. Today the API returns charge-period rows, which for most products is daily. We're looking at more real time breakdowns for the products where it makes sense.
- Forecasting. CumulatedContractedCost tells you where your spend is in the current billing cycle. We want to help you predict where you're going to end up. And not just at the account level, but the product level.
- Enterprise coverage. This first release is self-serve only. An equivalent experience for Enterprise contracts is in the works.
Try it
The endpoint is live today for all self-serve accounts. Grab an API token with the Billing Read permission, point your curl at it, and you'll get back your current billing period broken down by product. Full reference is available on the Cloudflare API docs. To see it alongside the rest of your cloud spend, connect your Cloudflare account in the Vantage console.
Cloudflare has spent years making it easy to run more of your stack on our network. It's time we made it just as easy to see what that's costing you — on Cloudflare, and everywhere else.

articles.title: ¿Se pueden controlar todos tus dispositivos solo con la voz? He pasado un día intentándolo
articles.text:
¿Se pueden controlar todos tus dispositivos solo con la voz? He pasado un día intentándolo
Los populares asistentes por voz de Google y Amazon permiten controlar luces, enchufes, aires acondicionados, televisores...
“Alexa, apaga las luces”. “Hey Google, pon música”. La promesa de controlar la casa con la voz llevaba años entre nosotros, pero ¿es real?, ¿hasta qué punto podemos prescindir del móvil, los interruptores o las apps? Lo cierto es que, gracias a la evolución que han experimentado los asistentes inteligentes, la popularidad de estándares como Matter y la inteligencia artificial, el control por voz se ha ampliado a muchísimos dispositivos y con mayores posibilidades: luces, enchufes, termostatos, televisores, aspiradores… incluso se pueden crear rutinas automatizadas.
Para comprobar si realmente usar solo la voz para controlar nuestros equipos es una opción a día de hoy, he pasado un día entero intentando interactuar con ellos únicamente mediante comandos de voz, utilizando uno de los nuevos altavoces Google Home Speaker y un Amazon Echo con Alexa+. En este sentido, es importante saber que, para usar la voz con eficacia, lo primero que hay que hacer es configurar previamente todo desde las apps.
Por la mañana: la voz como despertador
Mi día empieza con la alarma sonando en el altavoz y apagándola por la voz. Luego, le pido que suba la persiana de la ventana de mi habitación, que tiene instalado un kit que la convierte en inteligente, que encienda las luces, me haga un resumen de las noticias y me informe del estado del tráfico. A continuación, le digo que la cafetera me vaya preparando un café. Eso sí, para ello he necesitado una cafetera conectada (y no hay muchas): pido al asistente que la encienda, que lo prepare a mi gusto –como está programado en la app– y puedo preguntar si ya está listo.
Hasta aquí la experiencia es fluida. Los asistentes han mejorado en comprensión contextual: no hace falta dar órdenes robóticas: “enciende la luz del salón” funciona igual que “da la luz”, siempre que el sistema sepa dónde estás. Este tipo de procesamiento del lenguaje natural es uno de los avances más visibles en los últimos años.
A lo largo de la mañana, las órdenes por voz demuestran su utilidad en tareas repetitivas. Crear rutinas —por ejemplo, que al decir “me voy” se apaguen luces y se active la alarma— simplifica la gestión del hogar. Tanto Alexa como Google Home permiten configurar estas secuencias desde sus apps; y, una vez creadas, se ejecutan con una simple frase.
También controlo el entretenimiento musical sin tocar nada: cambiar canciones, ajustar el volumen, reproducir podcasts… Funciona bien en servicios integrados, pero falla si lo que pedimos es ambiguo. Me explico: decir “pon algo relajante” puede dar resultados impredecibles. En este sentido, la voz sigue siendo menos precisa que una interfaz visual cuando no se tiene claro qué se quiere.
Además, como los altavoces que he probado integran asistentes inteligentes, aprovecho para hacer algunas consultas: ideas para una receta de donuts saludables, cuál es el mejor momento para reservar entradas para visitar algunos monumentos en nuestro destino vacacional…
Llega la tarde y empiezan las limitaciones
A medida que avanza el día, los límites se hacen más evidentes. Gestionar dispositivos como cámaras de seguridad o configuraciones avanzadas del aire acondicionado resulta más sencillo desde la app. La voz permite acciones básicas (“muestra la cámara”, “baja la temperatura”), pero no navegar por opciones detalladas.
También he notado problemas de reconocimiento de la voz en entornos ruidosos o cuando hablan varias personas. Aunque los asistentes han mejorado en identificación de voces, no siempre aciertan, especialmente en hogares con varios usuarios — o niños hablando alto de fondo—.
Al final del día, la voz vuelve a brillar, mejorando en comodidad: me meto en la cama y pido al altavoz que apague todas las luces y programe la alarma para despertarme mañana. Son acciones sencillas, repetitivas y perfectamente adaptadas al uso sin pantallas ni botones.
¿Se puede vivir solo con la voz?
Entonces, ¿se puede vivir sólo con la voz? La respuesta es no; al menos, no todavía. El control por voz funciona especialmente bien en tres escenarios: acciones simples y repetitivas (encender luces, reproducir música), automatizaciones previamente configuradas (rutinas) y situaciones donde usar las manos es incómodo (cocinar, estar en la cama).
Sin embargo, sigue teniendo limitaciones claras. Una de las más importantes es que la configuración inicial sigue dependiendo totalmente de la app. Además, hay falta de precisión en tareas complejas, el ruido en la casa afecta y todavía se nota compatibilidad desigual entre dispositivos. En otras palabras, por ahora la voz no sustituye a la interfaz táctil, sino que la complementa.

articles.title: How to Run Isolated Tenant Kubernetes Clusters on Shared GPU Infrastructure | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Running a dedicated Kubernetes cluster per team often results in more isolation than an organization requires. While one cluster can be successfully shared across many teams, the coordination costs increase as the number of teams grows. Challenges include conflicting CRD versions, overlapping RBAC, and no clean way to carve GPU capacity into team-level budgets. At a certain scale, teams might start asking for their own clusters just to regain autonomy.
This post provides a pattern that preserves team autonomy without splitting the hardware. This solution involves a single control plane cluster with a GPU pool, GPU sharing with per-team quotas, and isolated Kubernetes control plane per team including an API server, controller, data store, syncer, and scheduler. This can be achieved using two open source tools: KAI Scheduler and vCluster.
Follow along with the tutorial steps and you’ll have three teams running real GPU Kubernetes pods in their own tenant clusters, all sharing a single physical GPU. You’ll also be able to verify that each team only sees their own workloads.
Tutorial prerequisites and notes
To keep the process reproducible for users that have limited resources, this tutorial uses a cluster with one NVIDIA L40S GPU and three teams sharing fractions of it. This makes the moving parts easy to see and try. The process works the same way on a larger cluster with hundreds of GPU nodes and dozens of teams. You can scale the node pool, the queue hierarchy, and the number of tenant clusters.
KAI Scheduler is a robust, efficient, and scalable topology-aware Kubernetes scheduler that was purpose-built for optimizing GPU resource allocation for AI workloads. It’s designed to manage large-scale GPU clusters, including thousands of nodes, and a high throughput of workloads. With KAI Scheduler, you can dynamically allocate GPU resources to workloads. It can run alongside the default kube-scheduler. Any pod with schedulerName: kai-scheduler is handled by KAI Scheduler. Everything else goes through the usual kube-scheduler process. 
The vCluster Kubernetes platform provisions fully isolated tenant clusters on your infrastructure or directly on bare metal. Each tenant cluster gets its own API server, custom resource definitions (CRDs), and role-based access control (RBAC), indistinguishable from a dedicated Kubernetes cluster, while sharing the underlying nodes and hardware. The virtualized control plane is invisible to tenants: no shared control plane nodes, no in-cluster agent pods, and no lateral path between environments. That makes vCluster a natural fit for GPU infrastructure where teams need their own clean cluster experience without splitting the hardware.
The vCluster shared-nodes model is used for this tutorial, so teams share the GPU node while each gets its own isolated control plane, the right fit for trusted internal teams. For untrusted tenants needing node-, network-, and storage-level separation, the same pattern extends to vCluster private nodes.
The example in this post uses three teams: NLP Team, Vision Team, and Recommender System Team. The NLP Team wants to install their own CRDs. The Vision Team wants cluster-admin to debug scheduling. The Recommender Team is on a different Kubeflow version. Nobody wants to share a kubectl context and accidentally break one another’s environments.
Using vCluster, each team gets their own isolated control plane, RBAC, namespaces, and CRDs. They can each have cluster-admin access. Underneath, all tenant clusters share the same nodes and GPUs.
Demo environment
This demo runs on an NVIDIA Brev GPU instance on Nebius with:
- One NVIDIA L40S, 40 vCPUs, 160 GiB RAM, 256 GiB disk (48 GB VRAM)
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- MicroK8s v1.36.2 – Kubernetes was preconfigured by Brev, including the MicroK8s gpu addon, which pre-installs the NVIDIA GPU Operator into the gpu-operator-resources namespace
- KAI Scheduler v0.16.4
- vCluster CLI 0.35.1
Note: For different setups, the cluster-creation and GPU Operator install steps will differ on GKE/EKS/AKS/vanilla k8s/k3s. Step 3 (KAI Scheduler) onward is identical on any Kubernetes that has the NVIDIA GPU Operator running with Container Device Interface (CDI) enabled.
Step 1: Local tooling
Install standalone kubectl and helm to avoid prefixing every command with microk8s. Then wire up a kubeconfig and pin MicroK8s so snap doesn’t auto-upgrade the control plane during the demo.
sudo snap refresh --hold microk8s
sudo snap install kubectl --classic --channel=1.35/stable
sudo snap install helm --classic
mkdir -p ~/.kube
sudo microk8s config > ~/.kube/config
sudo chown $USER:$USER ~/.kube/config
chmod 600 ~/.kube/config
Next, make sure the required MicroK8s addons are enabled:
microk8s enable dns
microk8s enable hostpath-storage    # vCluster needs PVCs
Then verify:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get storageclass
NAME             STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION                CONTAINER-RUNTIME
brev-8dq0cch1j   Ready    <none>   57d   v1.36.2   10.0.0.20     <none>        Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS   6.11.0-1016-nvidia (amd64)   containerd://2.2.3
NAME                          PROVISIONER            RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
microk8s-hostpath (default)   microk8s.io/hostpath   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   false                  20m
Step 2: Add the Helm repo
Add the NVIDIA Helm repo:
helm repo add nvidia https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia
helm repo update
Step 3: Confirm the GPU Operator
kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator-resources
NAME                                                         READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
gpu-feature-discovery-wpcjm                                  1/1     Running     0          8m
gpu-operator-57d75775c8-npjzz                                1/1     Running     0          9m
gpu-operator-node-feature-discovery-...                      1/1     Running     0          9m
nvidia-container-toolkit-daemonset-ft4hb                     1/1     Running     0          8m
nvidia-cuda-validator-8vqdv                                  0/1     Completed   0          8m
nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-l6fj6                         1/1     Running     0          8m
nvidia-operator-validator-cdnmj                              1/1     Running     0          8m
If you’re using an older GPU Operator, upgrade in place to 26.3.x:
helm upgrade gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator \
   -n gpu-operator-resources \
   --version v26.3.3 \
   --reset-then-reuse-values
If needed, install NVIDIA GPU Operator directly:
helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator \
    -n gpu-operator-resources --create-namespace \
    --version v26.3.3 \
    --set driver.enabled=false \
    --set operator.defaultRuntime=containerd \
    --set toolkit.env[0].name=CONTAINERD_CONFIG \
    --set toolkit.env[0].value=/var/snap/microk8s/current/args/containerd.toml \
    --set toolkit.env[1].name=CONTAINERD_SOCKET \
    --set toolkit.env[1].value=/var/snap/microk8s/common/run/containerd.sock \
    --set-string toolkit.env[2].name=CONTAINERD_SET_AS_DEFAULT \
    --set-string toolkit.env[2].value=1
Step 4: Install KAI Scheduler
Next, install the KAI Scheduler:
helm upgrade -i kai-scheduler \
  oci://ghcr.io/kai-scheduler/kai-scheduler/kai-scheduler \
  -n kai-scheduler --create-namespace \
  --version v0.16.4 \
  --set "global.gpuSharing=true"
Then verify:
kubectl get pods -n kai-scheduler
NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
admission-57556f949-sp98t                1/1     Running   0          47s
binder-66785d8dd9-9frgk                  1/1     Running   0          46s
kai-operator-6fdf595c4d-292d7            1/1     Running   0          52s
kai-scheduler-default-6bb667b767-vq2q4   1/1     Running   0          46s
pod-grouper-84dfc7759b-v5qtb             1/1     Running   0          47s
podgroup-controller-5878f48dbb-v7wcn     1/1     Running   0          47s
queue-controller-7796bb8984-hdn5r        1/1     Running   0          46s
Step 5: Define team queues
KAI Scheduler uses a Queue CRD to model an org → team hierarchy. This step involves creating one parent (ml-org, with a total budget of one GPU) and three child queues. Each is guaranteed 0.33 of the GPU and allowed to increase to the full GPU when others are idle. 
Save the following as create-queues.yaml:
apiVersion: scheduling.run.ai/v2
kind: Queue
metadata:
  name: ml-org
spec:
  resources:
    gpu: { quota: 1, limit: -1, overQuotaWeight: 1 }
---
apiVersion: scheduling.run.ai/v2
kind: Queue
metadata:
  name: team-nlp
spec:
  parentQueue: ml-org
  priority: 100
  resources:
    gpu: { quota: 0.33, limit: 1, overQuotaWeight: 1 }
---
apiVersion: scheduling.run.ai/v2
kind: Queue
metadata:
  name: team-vision
spec:
  parentQueue: ml-org
  priority: 100
  resources:
    gpu: { quota: 0.33, limit: 1, overQuotaWeight: 1 }
---
apiVersion: scheduling.run.ai/v2
kind: Queue
metadata:
  name: team-recommender
spec:
  parentQueue: ml-org
  priority: 100
  resources:
    gpu: { quota: 0.33, limit: 1, overQuotaWeight: 1 }
Here, quota is the guaranteed minimum, limit is the maximum allowed, and overQuotaWeight controls how surplus is split.
Next, apply and list:
kubectl apply -f create-queues.yaml
kubectl get queues
queue.scheduling.run.ai/ml-org created
queue.scheduling.run.ai/team-nlp created
queue.scheduling.run.ai/team-vision created
queue.scheduling.run.ai/team-recommender created
NAME                   PRIORITY   PARENT                 CHILDREN                                        DISPLAYNAME
default-parent-queue                                     ["default-queue"]
default-queue                     default-parent-queue
ml-org                                                   ["team-nlp","team-vision","team-recommender"]
team-nlp               100        ml-org
team-recommender       100        ml-org
team-vision            100        ml-org
Note that default-parent-queue and default-queue are created automatically by KAI Scheduler on first install. They are the fallback queue for any pod that doesn’t specify one.
Step 6: Spin up a vCluster per team
Next, install the vCluster CLI:
curl -L -o vcluster "https://github.com/loft-sh/vcluster/releases/latest/download/vcluster-linux-amd64"
sudo install -m 755 vcluster /usr/local/bin/vcluster
rm vcluster
vcluster --version
vcluster version 0.35.1
Define the vCluster config. The critical setting is setOwner: false. The KAI Scheduler pod-grouper walks ownership chains (Job → Pod, Deployment → ReplicaSet → Pod) to auto-group workloads. Disabling vCluster owner rewriting allows KAI Scheduler to see the real hierarchy.
cat > vcluster.yaml <<'EOF'
experimental:
  syncSettings:
    setOwner: false 
sync:
  fromHost:
    nodes:
      enabled: true
      selector:
        all: true
EOF
Then create one vCluster per team:
vcluster create team-nlp          --values vcluster.yaml --connect=false
vcluster create team-vision       --values vcluster.yaml --connect=false
vcluster create team-recommender  --values vcluster.yaml --connect=false
Verify that all three vClusters are running:
vcluster list
        NAME       |         NAMESPACE         | STATUS  | VERSION | CONNECTED | AGE
  -------------------+---------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-------
    team-nlp         | vcluster-team-nlp         | Running | 0.35.1  |           | 102s
    team-recommender | vcluster-team-recommender | Running | 0.35.1  |           | 88s
    team-vision      | vcluster-team-vision      | Running | 0.35.1  |           | 93s
Each team sees the real nodes, including the GPU node:
vcluster connect team-nlp -- kubectl get nodes
19:09:22 done vCluster is up and running
NAME             STATUS   ROLES    AGE     VERSION
brev-8dq0cch1j   Ready    <none>   6m20s   v1.36.2
Step 7: Deploy a workload from each team
Each team deploys their GPU workload from their own vCluster. The pod spec is simple, with three fields telling KAI Scheduler what to do:
vcluster connect team-nlp -- kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nlp-sentiment-model
  labels:
    kai.scheduler/queue: team-nlp # Which team 
  annotations:
    gpu-fraction: "0.33"          # How much GPU
spec:
  schedulerName: kai-scheduler.   # Use KAI, not default
  tolerations:
    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
    - name: nlp-inference
      image: nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base-ubuntu22.04
      command: ["bash", "-c", "nvidia-smi; sleep infinity"]
  nodeSelector:
    nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
EOF
19:13:34 done vCluster is up and running
pod/nlp-sentiment-model created
Do the same to deploy from each team, changing the queue name.
Now, verify:
NAMESPACE                   NAME                                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE    IP             NODE
vcluster-team-nlp           nlp-sentiment-model-x-default-x-team-nlp         1/1     Running   0          110s   10.1.171.180   brev-8dq0cch1j
vcluster-team-recommender   recommender-model-x-default-x-team-recommender   1/1     Running   0          6s     10.1.171.187   brev-8dq0cch1j
vcluster-team-vision        vision-classifier-model-x-default-x-team-vision  1/1     Running   0          14s    10.1.171.145   brev-8dq0cch1j
Three pods, three different vcluster-team-* namespaces, all running on the same physical node brev-8dq0cch1j. 
Each team sees only their own pod from inside their vCluster:
vcluster connect team-nlp         -- kubectl get pods -o wide
vcluster connect team-vision      -- kubectl get pods -o wide
vcluster connect team-recommender -- kubectl get pods -o wide
NAME                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP             NODE             NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
nlp-sentiment-model   1/1     Running   0          3m11s   10.1.171.180   brev-8dq0cch1j   <none>           <none>
NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP             NODE             NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
vision-classifier-model   1/1     Running   0          3m59s   10.1.171.145   brev-8dq0cch1j   <none>           <none>
NAME                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP             NODE             NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
recommender-model   1/1     Running   0          2m45s   10.1.171.187   brev-8dq0cch1j   <none>           <none>
Finally, the queue confirms the allocation. You can check all three at the same time:
kubectl describe queue team-nlp         | grep -A4 Status
kubectl describe queue team-vision      | grep -A4 Status
kubectl describe queue team-recommender | grep -A4 Status
You will see the same result for all:
Status:
  Allocated:
    nvidia.com/gpu:  330m
  Requested:
    nvidia.com/gpu:  330m
Note that KAI Scheduler handles scheduling—which pods land on which GPU and in what proportion. It does not enforce GPU memory isolation at the hardware level when GPU sharing is used. Applications need to respect their memory amount (for example, setting –gpu-memory-utilization in vLLM).
Under the hood, the GPU time-slices between CUDA contexts from each pod at kernel boundaries. For hard memory isolation on supported hardware, NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) provides hardware-level partitioning, which can be scheduled by KAI Scheduler as well.
Get started running isolated tenant Kubernetes clusters
KAI Scheduler decides fairly who gets GPU slices and schedules them as a group using GPU sharing and DRA Driver support, hierarchical queues with guaranteed quotas plus over-quota capabilities, gang scheduling, and topology awareness. Once AI workload scheduling is solved, teams want their own clusters. vCluster gives each team its own isolated Kubernetes control plane without the cost of separate infrastructure.
Together, KAI Scheduler and vCluster provide a dedicated cluster experience for three teams with zero waste on a single GPU. The answer isn’t always more GPUs, but better utilization of infrastructure.
Ready to get started? Check out KAI Scheduler, vCluster, and NVIDIA GPU Operator on GitHub.
Learn more about KAI Scheduler and vCluster integration at KubeCon 2026 North America, November 9-12.

articles.title: Gemini Spark Skills are getting easier to make, and Canadians can try it soon
articles.text:
Google is preparing to bring full Gemini Spark Skill management directly to the Gemini app on Android.
To add some context, Google’s Gemini-powered autonomous agent previously restricted full Skill management to the Gemini website, with mobile users only able to make conversational edits to an existing Skill file. Previously, mobile users could not create or organize these Skill files from scratch.
Now, in Google app v17.45.14, Android Authority spotted evidence that Google would soon give mobile users the same controls as the web interface.
Basically, Android app users will be able to access a dedicated Skills section within the top-right overflow menu within the Gemini app. This menu displays a full Skill management page that includes recommended Skills and active/inactive Skills across your platforms.
If you tap the add button (the plus sign in the corner), a small popup will appear with two distinct Skill creation paths: Create with Gemini and Create manually. Clicking Create with Gemini opens a guided setup where you can use natural language to describe your goal, and Gemini uses conversational prompts to draft the Skill for you. Creating the Skill manually will give you a bare-bones editor that gives you full control over the Skill name, description, and some custom instructions.
Now, this comes after Gemini Spark’s debut at Google I/O, but it didn’t launch in Canada initially. However, a blog post from Google a few days ago detailed that Spark would be rolling out to Canadians over the coming weeks, which comes at a perfect time with this new feature on the horizon.
Source: Android Authority

articles.title: DeepSeek's smaller model just outperformed its own flagship
articles.text:
DeepSeek’s smaller model just outperformed its own flagship
DeepSeek has launched DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, delivering a significant boost in agent performance without changing the model’s core architecture.
Following an announcement last week, the company made the update available as a public beta through DeepSeek’s API, and the open weights were published on Hugging Face under the MIT license later the same day.
Although the model itself hasn’t changed, DeepSeek says additional post-training is responsible for the performance gains, showing that meaningful improvements don’t always require a larger model.
DeepSeek’s decision to release the production-ready weights under a permissive license gives organizations much more control over how they deploy and customize the model.
Although the model itself hasn’t changed, DeepSeek says additional post-training is responsible for the performance gains, showing that meaningful improvements don’t always require a larger model.
Same architecture, better results
DeepSeek says V4-Flash-0731 uses the same architecture as the preview release, with 284 billion total parameters and 13 billion activated parameters per token.
This is much smaller than V4-Pro, which has 1.6 trillion total parameters and 49 billion activated parameters. For companies running agents at scale, the activated-parameter gap translates directly into inference cost — though model price alone doesn’t tell the full story.
Even though it is still the smaller model, DeepSeek says the updated Flash version now beats the earlier V4-Pro preview on several agent-focused benchmarks.
The company reported 82.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 54.4 on DeepSWE, and 70.3 on Toolathlon-Verified.
Benchmark claims under scrutiny
Early independent testing by Artificial Analysis found a lower Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 79%, which suggests that DeepSeek’s reported numbers may not always match independent results.
DeepSeek also shared results from several internal tests, though they have not yet been independently verified. If those results hold up, they add to growing evidence that companies can get more performance out of existing models through post-training instead of simply making them larger.
Open weights, full control
The MIT license means organizations aren’t limited to using DeepSeek through its hosted API. The release adds to a trend towards open-weight models closing the gap with proprietary alternatives. That flexibility is paired with support for tools many developers already use. V4-Flash now supports the Responses API for building AI agents and multi-step workflows, and DeepSeek has published instructions for integrating the model into Codex-based development workflows.
Familiar APIs, lower switching costs
For teams already using OpenAI-style APIs, that lowers the barrier to trying another model because they can evaluate it without making major changes to their existing setup.
The V4 technical report also covers inference improvements, like speculative decoding with DeepSeek’s DSpark framework, which are designed to make serving more efficient. When combined with self-hosted deployments, these features give infrastructure teams more ways to adjust performance for their own production needs.
This release reflects that companies are now finding new ways to improve model effectiveness without making models larger, and they’re competing on how those models are delivered. While many AI vendors focus on hosted APIs, DeepSeek continues to publish downloadable weights that organizations can run on their own infrastructure. Support for familiar API formats also makes it easier for teams to test open-weight models without revamping present workflows.
Companies are finding new ways to improve model effectiveness without making models larger, and they’re increasingly competing on how those models are delivered.

articles.title: Xbox : Microsoft augmente encore les prix en Europe, la Series S désormais au prix de lancement de la Series X
articles.text:
Que nous ayons été prévenus en amont ne change rien à l'affaire : la nouvelle augmentation des consoles Microsoft fait très mal.
La politique tarifaire de Microsoft continue de faire grincer des dents. Après plusieurs hausses successives, les consoles Xbox Series voient une nouvelle fois leurs prix grimper en Europe. Résultat : la Xbox Series S d'entrée de gamme est désormais vendue 499,99 €, soit le prix auquel la Xbox Series X avait été lancée en 2020.
Sponsorisé
Vous conservez l’électricité solaire produite en trop pendant la journée pour la réutiliser lorsque vos besoins augmentent.
Sponsorisé
Une inflation qui ne s'arrête plus
Les joueurs européens devront une nouvelle fois mettre la main au portefeuille. Microsoft a officialisé la nouvelle augmentation des prix de l'ensemble de sa gamme Xbox Series qui avait déjà été évoquée en juin dernier.
Comme prévu, cette augmentation concerne toutes les consoles Xbox Series et tous les marchés européens, que ce soit l'Allemagne, la France ou le Royaume-Uni, pour n'en citer que certains des plus importants. La hausse est plus particulièrement observable sur les modèles considérés comme les plus accessibles, traditionnellement présentés comme la porte d'entrée vers l'écosystème Xbox.
Le cas de la Xbox Series S 512 Go illustre parfaitement cette évolution. Commercialisée à 299,99 € lors de son lancement en novembre 2020, puis progressivement revalorisée au fil des années, elle atteint désormais les 499,99 €. Un montant symbolique puisqu'il correspond exactement au prix de lancement de la Xbox Series X – la console haut de gamme de Microsoft – il y a près de six ans. Avouez que le symbole est fort.
Microsoft invoque le coût des composants
Cette Xbox Series X augmente pour sa part de 200 € par rapport à ce prix de lancement. Elle se trouve aujourd'hui facturée 749,99 € dans sa version sans lecteur optique et 799,99 € avec lecteur optique.
Pour justifier cette nouvelle révision tarifaire, Microsoft met en avant la flambée persistante des coûts des composants, notamment de la mémoire vive et du stockage en mémoire flash. Une pression qui touche l'ensemble de l'industrie électronique, portée par une demande toujours plus forte en puces destinées aux infrastructures dédiées à l'intelligence artificielle.
Cette nouvelle hausse intervient alors que les consoles de salon suivent une trajectoire inhabituelle. Là où les prix avaient historiquement tendance à diminuer au fil des années, les PlayStation et autres Xbox Series enchaînent au contraire les revalorisations. Les consoles de Sony ont déjà connu des augmentations assez similaires et le prix de la Switch 2 de Nintendo devrait être réévalué en septembre prochain.

articles.title: Index Ventures raises €1.7 billion, bringing total investing capital to nearly €3 billion | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Index Ventures, the global venture capital firm, has raised approximately €1.7 billion ($2 billion), bringing its total investing capital to nearly €3 billion ($3.5 billion) across all stages: Seed, venture, and growth.
The capital comprises a €346.9 million ($400 million) Seed fund, a €780.4 million ($900 million) venture fund, and an additional €607.01 million ($700 million) committed to the firm’s existing growth fund. This latest addition increased its €1.3 billion ($1.5 billion) 2024 fund to €1.9 billion ($2.2 billion).
“They’ll enable us to keep doing what we’ve always done, backing exceptional founders from first check to the public markets and beyond, across the ten-hour time zone that runs from Tel Aviv to San Francisco, in every cycle,” the firm mentioned in its blog post.
Founded in 1996, Index Ventures is marking its 30th anniversary with the fundraise. The firm backs “exceptional entrepreneurs”. It claims that it works with entrepreneurs and their companies at every stage, whether Seed, venture, or growth, and across every sector. Its portfolio companies are supported by an experienced team of investors, strategists, and a global network.
Its portfolio companies include Adyen, Datadog, Figma, Revolut, Robinhood, Roblox, Scale AI and cybersecurity company Wiz.
Index Ventures was an early investor in Wiz, which Google agreed to acquire for $32 billion in March 2025. Google completed the acquisition in 2026.
Explaining the rationale behind the timing of this raise, the firm mentioned, “This moment feels right for it. AI is putting the power to build into more hands than ever before, accelerating the time from idea to product, and opening entire industries to disruption, from infrastructure and cybersecurity to fintech, healthcare, productivity and consumer.”
Index Ventures has remained active across Europe in recent months, backing companies spanning artificial intelligence, FinTech and healthcare. Its 2026 investments include London-based Marker, Conduct, Inherent, Scope, Adfin, Granola and Ineffable Intelligence, alongside Paris-based Parallel and Uncovr. The firm has also continued backing established portfolio companies, participating in Alan’s €480 million Series G and Wonderful’s approximately €130 million Series B.

Galaxy A57 5G despenca de preço em oferta histórica com cupom na Amazon
Galaxy A57 (128 GB) tem tela Super AMOLED+ e câmera principal de 50 MP; celular da Samsung atinge menor preço histórico no Pix com cupom em oferta do 8.8
O Galaxy A57 de 128 GB está por R$ 1.599 no Pix com cupom SMART200 na Amazon. O smartphone da Samsung com câmera de 50 MP e tela Super AMOLED+ de 120 Hz atinge o menor preço histórico com desconto de 56% sobre o original de R$ 3.599.
Não perca a chance de adquirir um dos melhores celulares do mercado no precinho nesta oferta em alusão ao 8.8, data em que o varejo oferece diversas condições especiais.
O Galaxy A57 se destaca por sua nova tela Super AMOLED+ de 6,7″, uma evolução sutil ao Super AMOLED com melhor qualidade de imagem, aliada à taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de até 1.900 nits. Tal combinação entrega cores vibrantes, alta fluidez e garantia de visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
No desempenho, o chip Exynos 1680 e os 8 GB de RAM permitem a execução de apps em multitarefa e games, além de algumas funções da suíte Galaxy AI. Os 128 GB de espaço interno podem ser expandidos com planos de armazenamento na nuvem.
O kit de câmeras de um dos melhores celulares de 2026 inclui wide de 50 MP com OIS e ultrawide de 12 MP, ambas captam belas cenas em ambientes abertos, a lente macro de 5 MP para aproximações de elementos pequenos e o sensor frontal de 12 MP. Todas filmam em 4K.
O corpo de alumínio do A57 conta com o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+ na traseira e sobre a tela para proporcionar resistência a pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção adicional em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 5.000 mAh resiste até dois dias de uso, segundo a Samsung. O carregamento rápido de 45 W via cabo USB-C permite injetar uma carga de 60% em 30 minutos, evitando que o usuário seja pego de surpresa sem energia.
O Galaxy A57 de 128 GB (R$ 1.599 no Pix com cupom SMART200) traz conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC. Além disso, roda Android 16 e tem promessa de receber seis atualizações do sistema operacional.

articles.title: Busha Expands Its Innovation Portfolio with the Launch of Licensed Prediction Market, Signal by Busha - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
LAGOS, Nigeria — As prediction markets gain global recognition as tools for forecasting trends across business, politics, technology and sports, Busha today announced the launch of Signal by Busha, a prediction market licensed by the Lagos State Lottery and Gaming Authority.
Available immediately as a web platform, Signal by Busha is accessible to existing Busha users using their current Busha accounts. New users can get started by creating a Busha account before connecting it to Signal. Users fund their Signal wallets directly from their Busha wallets using supported balances, including Naira, stablecoins, and other cryptocurrencies available within the Busha app.
At launch, users can trade in markets across sports, crypto, culture, politics, economics, and trending topics, with additional categories expected over time. Rather than simply placing one-off predictions, users can buy and sell positions throughout the life of a market, allowing them to adjust their exposure as new information becomes available. Markets are settled using official event sources wherever available, while an internal resolution team determines outcomes for markets that do not have a single authoritative source, operating strictly in accordance with Busha’s publicly available, transparent market resolution policies and consumer protection guidelines. Once a market is resolved, eligible payouts are automatically credited to users’ Signal wallets, and funds can be withdrawn to their Busha wallets.
Globally, prediction markets are gaining recognition as a complementary forecasting tool for businesses, researchers, analysts, and policymakers. Unlike opinion polls, which capture sentiment at a single point in time, or sentiment analysis, which reflects how people feel, prediction markets aggregate what participants are willing to back with conviction. As trading activity evolves, market prices continuously update to reflect changing expectations, creating a real-time signal that can sit alongside traditional research and forecasting methods.
“Markets have always been powerful information systems,” said Olaoluwa Samuel-Biyi, co-founder of Busha. “When people put their conviction behind a prediction, they collectively generate valuable signals about where they believe the future is headed. Signal by Busha is designed to surface those insights in real time, giving individuals, businesses, and researchers a new lens for understanding markets and emerging trends. We believe prediction markets will become an increasingly important complement to traditional research, and we want African users to participate in that evolution through a trusted, regulated platform.”
For Busha, the launch represents another step in the company’s evolution from a digital asset platform to a broader technology company that builds products at the intersection of finance, information, and emerging technology.
“From inception, our vision has been to build technology that gives Africans access to the financial tools shaping the future,” said Michael Adeyeri, co-founder and CEO of Busha. “We started by making digital assets more accessible. Today, we are building products across savings, payments, global money movement, and now prediction markets. Signal by Busha reflects our belief that technology can do more than help people transact, it can also help them make better-informed decisions by harnessing collective intelligence in real time. By expanding beyond saving, investing, and digital assets into forecasting and market predictions, we are continuing to redefine what a modern African financial technology company can build.”
The launch builds on a period of rapid product expansion for Busha. Over the past six months, the company introduced Busha 3.0, a redesigned all-in-one money app with high-yield savings products, expanded into enterprise financial infrastructure through Busha Business, enabling stablecoin-powered cross-border payments for businesses, and is soon to launch stablecoin-backed virtual Visa cards that allow users to spend directly from their digital asset and fiat balances.
With Signal by Busha, the company is extending its innovation portfolio beyond financial services into technology-powered forecasting and market intelligence. The launch reinforces the company’s commitment to building innovative technologies that help Africans make smarter decisions, move money more efficiently, and engage with the future through trusted, regulated products.
###
About Busha
Busha is a Pan-African digital asset exchange and one of Nigeria’s first SEC-licensed digital asset platforms. Operating across Nigeria and Kenya, Busha provides consumers and businesses with access to traditional savings, crypto trading, crypto-backed loans, and stablecoin-powered business infrastructure. Through Busha Business, companies, fintechs, and developers access licensed payment infrastructure for cross-border payments, stablecoin treasury, merchant payments, and API integration. Trusted for its compliance-first approach, deep liquidity, and exceptional user experience, Busha is at the forefront of driving responsible innovation in Africa’s digital financial ecosystem.

articles.title: Meshy 3D Agent: 3D-Modelle per Chat erstellen – ohne CAD-Software
articles.text:
KI-Agenten erobern die 3D-Welt – aber das eigentliche Problem ist ein anderes
Erst Code, dann Text, Bilder, Musik: KI-Agenten haben zuletzt eine kreative Disziplin nach der anderen übernommen. 3D galt lange als zu sperrig – zu viel Geometrie, Topologie und Textur für einen einzelnen Prompt. Mit dem Meshy 3D Agent soll auch diese Hürde fallen: Man beschreibt, was man will, und führt ein Gespräch, bis das Modell steht. Das klingt nach dem nächsten Hype – ist aber der falsche Reflex. Denn ein 3D-Objekt zu erzeugen, war selten das Problem. Die eigentliche Frage lautet: Lässt sich das Ergebnis auch benutzen?
Wie 3D bisher entstand
Klassisch entsteht ein 3D-Modell von Hand – in Spezialsoftware wie Blender, Maya oder ZBrush. Das ist ein Handwerk mit langer Lernkurve; wer es nicht beherrscht, vergibt jeden Auftrag nach außen. Die erste Generation von KI-Werkzeugen verkürzte das drastisch: Aus einem Prompt entsteht in Sekunden ein Modell. Doch das blieb meist ein Schuss ins Blaue – ein Prompt, ein Ergebnis, das man danach selbst nachbessert. Genau hier setzt der dialogbasierte Ansatz an.
Warum ein Dialog mehr ist als ein weiterer Generator
Der Meshy 3D Agent dreht dieses Prinzip um: Er schlägt Richtungen vor, erzeugt mehrere Varianten, verfeinert auf Zuruf und behält den Kontext. Statt zu raten, näherst du dich Schritt für Schritt einem nutzbaren Modell. Nach Angaben von Meshy ist es der erste vollständig dialogbasierte, mehrstufige Agent speziell für die 3D-Erstellung. Seit Kurzem steht er allen Nutzerinnen und Nutzern offen, zuvor lief er als Beta für zahlende Accounts.
Ein Praxisbeispiel: ein komplettes Set in einem Chat
Wie das praktisch aussieht, zeigt ein Beispiel aus der Spieleentwicklung. Ausgangspunkt ist ein einziges Referenzbild einer Szene – etwa eine Retro-Arcade-Kulisse mit Gebäuden, tropischen Pflanzen und Fahrzeugen. Im Chat löst der Entwickler die einzelnen Elemente heraus, erzeugt sie nacheinander in 3D und hält sie im selben Stil. Das Ergebnis ist kein zusammengewürfelter Haufen, sondern ein Set, das zusammengehört. Per Export wandern die fertigen Objekte nach Blender, wo die Szene entsteht. Genau das ist der Unterschied zu einem einzelnen Generator: nicht ein hübsches Modell, sondern ein stimmiges Set – in einem Durchgang, ohne zwölf Einzelteile mühsam aufeinander abzustimmen.
Was herauskommt – und in welchem Format
Nach Angaben von Meshy haben bis Juli 2026 mehr als 12 Millionen registrierte Nutzer über 100 Millionen 3D-Modelle auf der Plattform erstellt, die laut SimilarWeb gemessen am Web-Traffic die Nummer eins ihrer Kategorie ist. Das Unternehmen hat soeben eine Series-B-Finanzierungsrunde über 400 Millionen US-Dollar abgeschlossen – bei einer Bewertung von 1,5 Milliarden US-Dollar.
Als Eingabe reicht, was ohnehin da ist: ein Satz, ein Foto, eine Skizze. Ein texturiertes Modell entsteht laut Anbieter in rund einer Minute und lässt sich in acht Formaten exportieren (FBX, OBJ, GLB, USDZ, STL, BLEND, 3MF, DXF) – direkt in Engines wie Unity, Unreal oder Godot, in Blender und Maya. Für den 3D-Druck gibt der Agent wasserdichte STL- und 3MF-Dateien aus und prüft die Druckbarkeit vor dem Slicen; in Meshys eigenen Tests bestehen rund 97 Prozent der figurenartigen Modelle die Slicer-Prüfung in Bambu Studio. Die Übergabe an Slicer wie OrcaSlicer, Cura oder Creality Print erfolgt direkt.
Für Entwickler: Schnittstelle statt Oberfläche
Auch in eigene Workflows lässt sich der Agent einbinden: über eine REST-API, SDKs für Python und Node.js sowie offizielle Skill-Dateien für die Programmierassistenten Cursor und Claude Code. Ein KI-Assistent kann die 3D-Erzeugung damit direkt aufrufen – als Teil der Pipeline, nicht als isolierter Schritt.
Wofür sich das lohnt – und für wen
Der eigentliche Hebel ist nicht das einzelne Modell, sondern wer 3D überhaupt erstellen kann – und das betrifft nicht nur Spielestudios. Im Produktdesign verkürzt sich der Weg von der Skizze zum Prototyp, im Marketing entstehen 3D-Assets ohne eigene Pipeline. Wichtig bleibt: Der Agent nimmt die Fleißarbeit ab, Auswahl und kreatives Urteil bleiben beim Team.
Wo der Agent (noch) an Grenzen stößt
Ehrlich bleibt: Am stärksten ist die KI bei organischen Formen, Figuren und einzelnen Objekten. Bei präzisen geometrischen oder mechanischen Teilen mit engen Toleranzen wird es schwierig – generierte Kanten wirken oft weicher, als es eine Passung verträgt; hier bleibt klassische CAD-Software die bessere Wahl. Sehr feine Strukturen unter einem Millimeter, etwa dünne Antennen, können beim Druck brechen. Exakte Maße liefert er nicht von sich aus – sie müssen im Slicer nachgezogen werden. Und: Neue Modelle erzeugt er, vorhandene texturiert er neu – die Geometrie einer bestehenden 3D-Datei bearbeitet er nicht.
Lohnt sich der Test?
Wer das selbst beurteilen will, testet mit der Art von Objekt, die man wirklich braucht – nicht mit dem Vorzeige-Drachen, sondern dem eigenen Anwendungsfall. Weil die Generierung eine Zufallskomponente hat, lohnt es sich, mehrere Varianten zu erzeugen und die sauberste zu nehmen – und das Ergebnis vor Produktion oder Druck einmal durch Slicer oder Engine laufen zu lassen. Unterm Strich verschiebt der dialogbasierte Ansatz spürbar, was ohne Spezialsoftware möglich ist. Für Teams, die schnell von der Idee zum nutzbaren Modell kommen wollen, ist er einen Test wert. Ausprobieren lässt er sich bei Meshy.
